              "patch": "Index: lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts\n===================================================================\n--- lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts\t\n+++ lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts\t\n@@ -1,811 +1,875 @@\n /**\n  * Outline: plan a course's scenes from the requirements, the material and\n  * the research, streaming each scene outline as the model writes it. The\n  * logic of 1.1.x's POST /api/generate/scene-outlines-stream; a run streams\n  * the step's events to the browser.\n  *\n  * Interactive mode and the server-enabled task engine mode keep their own\n  * prompt templates; standard generation is byte-identical to the generation\n  * package's outline prompt. The stream is retried on the same model, then\n  * once on the stage's fallback model, and every retry is reported as an event.\n  */\n import { attachedModelFallback } from '@/lib/ai/model-fallbacks';\n import { streamLLM } from '@/lib/ai/llm';\n import {\n   resolveFallbackModel,\n   shouldFallbackFor,\n   logFallbackFired,\n } from '@/lib/server/llm-fallback';\n import { buildPrompt, PROMPT_IDS } from '@/lib/prompts';\n import {\n   formatImageDescription,\n   formatImagePlaceholder,\n   buildVisionUserContent,\n   buildOutlinePrompt,\n   uniquifyMediaElementIds,\n   formatTeacherPersonaForPrompt,\n } from '@openmaic/generation';\n import type { AgentInfo } from '@openmaic/generation';\n import { DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE } from '@openmaic/generation';\n+import {\n+  formatDesignDirective,\n+  normalizeDesignDirective,\n+  type DesignDirective,\n+} from '@openmaic/generation';\n import { MAX_PDF_CONTENT_CHARS, MAX_VISION_IMAGES } from '@/lib/constants/generation';\n import { MAX_OUTLINE_SCENES } from '@/lib/server/generation/outline-schema';\n import { nanoid } from 'nanoid';\n import type {\n   UserRequirements,\n   PdfImage,\n   SceneOutline,\n   ImageMapping,\n } from '@/lib/types/generation';\n import { resolveServerGenerationCapabilities } from '@/lib/server/generation-capabilities';\n import {\n   isNonRetryableHostFailure,\n   isProviderQuotaRefusal,\n } from '@/lib/server/generation-run-hooks/runtime';\n import { sortDocumentImagesForVision } from '@/lib/document/bundle';\n import { resolveVocationalActive } from '@/lib/config/feature-flags';\n \n import {\n   StepAbortedError,\n   StepRefusal,\n   type OwnerStepContext,\n   type StepContext,\n   type StepLanguageModel,\n   type WorkspaceStepContext,\n } from './context';\n \n const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 2;\n // Hard ceiling on the accumulated stream buffer. Legitimate outline JSON is\n // small (tens of KB); anything past this is a runaway/degenerate generation\n // and must not be allowed to grow the heap unbounded.\n const MAX_OUTLINE_STREAM_BYTES = 512 * 1024;\n \n /**\n  * Extract the languageDirective from the streamed wrapper JSON.\n  * Matches `\"languageDirective\":\"<value>\"` in partial JSON like:\n  *   {\"languageDirective\":\"Teach in English...\",\"outlines\":[...\n  */\n function extractLanguageDirective(buffer: string): string | null {\n   // The directive is the first key of the wrapper object, so it can only ever\n   // appear in the head of the buffer. Bound the scan to keep this O(1) per\n   // streamed chunk — it is called on the full, growing buffer on every chunk,\n   // which is otherwise O(n²) over the stream.\n   const head = buffer.length > 8192 ? buffer.slice(0, 8192) : buffer;\n   const match = head.match(/\"languageDirective\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/);\n   if (!match) return null;\n   try {\n     return JSON.parse(`\"${match[1]}\"`);\n   } catch {\n     return match[1];\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * Extract the courseTitle from the streamed wrapper JSON.\n  * Same head-bound scan as `extractLanguageDirective` — the title is a\n  * top-level key near the start of the wrapper object, so it only appears in\n  * the buffer head. Returns the decoded title, or null if not yet streamed.\n  */\n const COURSE_TITLE_RE = /\"courseTitle\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/;\n \n // Normalize a captured title identically to the non-streaming parser\n // (@openmaic/generation outline parser): ignore whitespace-only titles and cap\n // length defensively so a hallucinating model cannot push a blank or unbounded\n // value into the stage name. Returning null lets callers fall back / keep scanning.\n function normalizeStreamedTitle(raw: string): string | null {\n   let title: string;\n   try {\n     title = JSON.parse(`\"${raw}\"`);\n   } catch {\n     title = raw;\n   }\n   const normalized = title.trim();\n   return normalized ? normalized.slice(0, 120) : null;\n }\n \n function extractCourseTitle(buffer: string): string | null {\n   const head = buffer.length > 8192 ? buffer.slice(0, 8192) : buffer;\n   const match = head.match(COURSE_TITLE_RE);\n   return match ? normalizeStreamedTitle(match[1]) : null;\n }\n \n /**\n+ * Extract the designDirective from the streamed wrapper JSON. Unlike the two\n+ * string directives above, the directive is an object, so it is recovered by\n+ * a balanced-brace scan (string-aware) starting at its key. The scan re-runs\n+ * per chunk until found; it is bounded to the 16 KB head, where the wrapper\n+ * directives live — normal shape is `\"designDirective\":{...},\"outlines\":[`.\n+ */\n+const DESIGN_DIRECTIVE_KEY_RE = /\"designDirective\"\\s*:\\s*\\{/;\n+\n+function extractDesignDirective(buffer: string): DesignDirective | null {\n+  const head = buffer.length > 16384 ? buffer.slice(0, 16384) : buffer;\n+  const match = head.match(DESIGN_DIRECTIVE_KEY_RE);\n+  if (!match) return null;\n+  let depth = 0;\n+  let inString = false;\n+  let escaped = false;\n+  for (let i = match.index + match[0].length - 1; i < head.length; i++) {\n+    const char = head[i];\n+    if (escaped) {\n+      escaped = false;\n+      continue;\n+    }\n+    if (char === '\\\\' && inString) {\n+      escaped = true;\n+      continue;\n+    }\n+    if (char === '\"') inString = !inString;\n+    if (inString) continue;\n+    if (char === '{') depth++;\n+    else if (char === '}') {\n+      depth--;\n+      if (depth === 0) {\n+        try {\n+          const raw: unknown = JSON.parse(head.substring(match.index + match[0].length - 1, i + 1));\n+          return normalizeDesignDirective(raw);\n+        } catch {\n+          return null;\n+        }\n+      }\n+    }\n+  }\n+  return null; // Object not complete in the head yet — scan again next chunk.\n+}\n+\n+/**\n  * Full-buffer fallback, run once after the stream completes: recovers a title\n  * the model emitted after the `outlines` array or beyond the 8KB head window —\n  * cases the head-bound `extractCourseTitle` scan would miss. Only invoked when\n  * the streaming scan produced nothing, so the extra full-buffer regex is paid once.\n  */\n function extractCourseTitleFromComplete(buffer: string): string | null {\n   const match = buffer.match(COURSE_TITLE_RE);\n   return match ? normalizeStreamedTitle(match[1]) : null;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Incremental JSON array parser.\n  * Extracts complete top-level objects from a partially-streamed JSON array,\n  * resuming from `scanFrom` (an index into `buffer`) so the growing buffer is\n  * scanned only ONCE across the whole stream — O(n) total instead of O(n²).\n  * Supports both a flat array `[{...},{...}]` and a wrapper object\n  * `{\"languageDirective\":\"...\",\"outlines\":[{...},{...}]}`, with or without a\n  * markdown ```json fence (the array is located by content, not by stripping).\n  * Returns newly found objects plus the index to resume scanning from next time.\n  */\n function extractNewOutlines(\n   buffer: string,\n   scanFrom: number,\n ): { outlines: SceneOutline[]; scanFrom: number } {\n   const results: SceneOutline[] = [];\n \n   let i: number;\n   if (scanFrom > 0) {\n     // Resume just past the last fully-parsed object (between array elements,\n     // so not inside a string and at brace depth 0).\n     i = scanFrom;\n   } else {\n     // Locate the outlines array opening once.\n     const outlinesKeyIdx = buffer.indexOf('\"outlines\"');\n     const arrayStart =\n       outlinesKeyIdx >= 0 ? buffer.indexOf('[', outlinesKeyIdx) : buffer.indexOf('[');\n     if (arrayStart === -1) return { outlines: results, scanFrom: 0 };\n     i = arrayStart + 1;\n   }\n \n   let depth = 0;\n   let objectStart = -1;\n   let inString = false;\n   let escaped = false;\n   let consumed = i; // index just past the last fully-parsed object\n \n   for (; i < buffer.length; i++) {\n     const char = buffer[i];\n \n     if (escaped) {\n       escaped = false;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (char === '\\\\' && inString) {\n       escaped = true;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (char === '\"') {\n       inString = !inString;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (inString) continue;\n \n     if (char === '{') {\n       if (depth === 0) objectStart = i;\n       depth++;\n     } else if (char === '}') {\n       depth--;\n       if (depth === 0 && objectStart >= 0) {\n         try {\n           results.push(JSON.parse(buffer.substring(objectStart, i + 1)));\n         } catch {\n           // Incomplete or invalid JSON — skip\n         }\n         objectStart = -1;\n         consumed = i + 1;\n       }\n     }\n   }\n \n   return { outlines: results, scanFrom: consumed };\n }\n \n function normalizeTaskEngineProceduralOutline(\n   outline: SceneOutline,\n   requirement: string,\n ): SceneOutline {\n   const widgetOutline = outline.widgetOutline ?? {};\n \n   return {\n     ...outline,\n     type: 'interactive',\n     widgetType: 'procedural-skill',\n     widgetOutline: {\n       ...widgetOutline,\n       procedureType: widgetOutline.procedureType ?? 'inspection',\n       task: widgetOutline.task || requirement,\n       tools:\n         widgetOutline.tools && widgetOutline.tools.length > 0\n           ? widgetOutline.tools\n           : ['required PPE', 'task checklist'],\n       steps:\n         widgetOutline.steps && widgetOutline.steps.length > 0\n           ? widgetOutline.steps\n           : ['Confirm task conditions', 'Select required tools', 'Complete safety check'],\n       successCriteria:\n         widgetOutline.successCriteria && widgetOutline.successCriteria.length > 0\n           ? y: number; z: number };\n   rotation?: { x: number; y: number; z: number };\n   scale?: number | { x: number; y: number; z: number };\n   material?: {\n     type: 'basic' | 'lambert' | 'phong' | 'standard' | 'emissive';\n     color?: string;\n     emissive?: string;\n     wireframe?: boolean;\n     transparent?: boolean;\n     opacity?: number;\n   };\n   // For animated objects\n   animation?: {\n     type: 'orbit' | 'rotate' | 'bounce' | 'pulse';\n     speed?: number;\n     axis?: 'x' | 'y' | 'z';\n   };\n   // For hierarchical objects\n   children?: Visualization3DObject[];\n }\n \n export interface Visualization3DInteraction {\n   type: 'orbit' | 'zoom' | 'pan' | 'slider' | 'button' | 'toggle';\n   target?: string; // Object ID or 'camera'\n   label?: string;\n   param?: string;\n   min?: number;\n   max?: number;\n   default?: number;\n   step?: number;\n }\n \n export interface Visualization3DConfig extends WidgetConfigBase {\n   type: 'visualization3d';\n   visualizationType: 'molecular' | 'solar' | 'anatomy' | 'geometry' | 'physics' | 'custom';\n   description: string;\n   objects: Visualization3DObject[];\n   interactions?: Visualization3DInteraction[];\n   camera?: {\n     position?: { x: number; y: number; z: number };\n     target?: { x: number; y: number; z: number };\n     fov?: number;\n   };\n   lighting?: {\n     ambient?: { color?: string; intensity?: number };\n     directional?: Array<{\n       color?: string;\n       intensity?: number;\n       position?: { x: number; y: number; z: number };\n     }>;\n     point?: Array<{\n       color?: string;\n       intensity?: number;\n       position?: { x: number; y: number; z: number };\n     }>;\n   };\n   presets?: Array<{\n     name: string;\n     description?: string;\n     state: Record<string, unknown>;\n   }>;\n }\n \n // ==================== Procedural Skill Widget ====================\n \n export interface ProceduralSkillStep {\n   id: string;\n   title: string;\n   description: string;\n   tools?: string[];\n   successCriteria?: string[];\n }\n \n export interface ProceduralSkillConfig extends WidgetConfigBase {\n   type: 'procedural-skill';\n   task: string;\n   description: string;\n   tools?: string[];\n   steps: ProceduralSkillStep[];\n   successCriteria?: string[];\n }\n \n+// ==================== Animation Explainer Widget ====================\n+\n+/**\n+ * Motion-graphic explainer: a deterministic code-animation scene (GSAP/\n+ * CSS vector graphics) that plays itself — the lesson's opening \"trailer\".\n+ */\n+export interface AnimationExplainerConfig extends WidgetConfigBase {\n+  type: 'animation-explainer';\n+  concept: string;\n+  description: string;\n+  /** Ordered named beats of the animation (p0, p1, ... p_N markers). */\n+  beats?: Array<{ id: string; label: string }>;\n+  mood?: string;\n+}\n+\n // ==================== Union Types ====================\n \n export type WidgetConfig =\n   | SimulationConfig\n   | DiagramConfig\n   | CodeConfig\n   | GameConfig\n   | Visualization3DConfig\n-  | ProceduralSkillConfig;\n+  | ProceduralSkillConfig\n+  | AnimationExplainerConfig;\n",

              "file": "packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/interactive.ts",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/interactive.ts\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/interactive.ts\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/interactive.ts\t\n@@ -1,78 +1,80 @@\n /** Interactive scene content and its dependency-free widget extension point. */\n \n /** Every widget kind produced by the interactive-content pipeline. */\n export type WidgetType =\n   | 'simulation'\n   | 'diagram'\n   | 'code'\n   | 'game'\n   | 'visualization3d'\n-  | 'procedural-skill';\n+  | 'procedural-skill'\n+  | 'animation-explainer';\n \n /** Frozen set of every valid {@link WidgetType}. */\n export const WIDGET_TYPES = [\n   'simulation',\n   'diagram',\n   'code',\n   'game',\n   'visualization3d',\n   'procedural-skill',\n+  'animation-explainer',\n ] as const satisfies readonly WidgetType[];\n \n // Compile-time exhaustiveness in both directions: `satisfies` above rejects an\n // invalid tuple entry, while this assertion rejects a missing union member.\n type _WidgetTypesExhaustive = [WidgetType] extends [(typeof WIDGET_TYPES)[number]] ? true : never;\n const _widgetTypesExhaustive: _WidgetTypesExhaustive = true;\n void _widgetTypesExhaustive;\n \n /** Narrow an unknown value to a valid {@link WidgetType}. */\n export function isWidgetType(value: unknown): value is WidgetType {\n   return typeof value === 'string' && (WIDGET_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(value);\n }\n \n /**\n  * Minimal contract shared by every widget configuration. The contract names\n  * only `type`; every other widget-config member belongs to the app domain.\n  */\n export interface WidgetConfigBase {\n   type: WidgetType;\n   [key: string]: unknown;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Interactive web content.\n  *\n  * `html` is a complete HTML document rendered via iframe `srcDoc`; `url` is a\n  * `src` fallback used only when `html` is absent. `url` is optional because\n  * producers historically wrote `url: ''` when no fallback existed. The\n  * validators require at least one of `html` or `url` to be present as a string,\n  * a disjunction intentionally not expressed by the generated schema.\n  */\n export type InteractiveContent<TWidgetConfig extends WidgetConfigBase = WidgetConfigBase> = {\n   type: 'interactive';\n   url?: string;\n   html?: string;\n   widgetType?: WidgetType;\n   widgetConfig?: TWidgetConfig;\n };\n \n /** Cheap structural guard for {@link InteractiveContent}. */\n export function isInteractiveContent(value: unknown): value is InteractiveContent {\n   if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) return false;\n   const content = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n   if (content.type !== 'interactive') return false;\n   if (typeof content.html !== 'string' && typeof content.url !== 'string') return false;\n   if (content.url !== undefined && typeof content.url !== 'string') return false;\n   if (content.html !== undefined && typeof content.html !== 'string') return false;\n   if (content.widgetType !== undefined && !isWidgetType(content.widgetType)) return false;\n   if (content.widgetConfig !== undefined) {\n     if (\n       typeof content.widgetConfig !== 'object' ||\n       content.widgetConfig === null ||\n       Array.isArray(content.widgetConfig)\n     )\n       return false;\n     if (!isWidgetType((content.widgetConfig as Record<string, unknown>).type)) return false;\n   }\n   return true;\n }\n",
              "additions": 3,
              "deletions": 1,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/snippets/widget-visual-polish.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/snippets/widget-visual-polish.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/snippets/widget-visual-polish.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/snippets/widget-visual-polish.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@\n+## Visual Quality Standard for ALL Interactive Widgets (shared)\n+\n+A widget that \"works\" but looks like a 2005 dashboard fails this pipeline as much as a widget that crashes. Apply the course design directive (see \"Design Directive\" in the user prompt) to every widget.\n+\n+### Palette discipline\n+\n+- Use those exact colors from the design directive for: page/canvas background, primary accents, text, and semantic states. Do not invent new hues per element.\n+- One background treatment across all views; one accent hue doing the highlighting. 60% neutral / 30% secondary / 10% accent, never the accent everywhere.\n+- Text contrast: body text ≥ 4.5:1 against its actual background (count tint overlays). Never light text on mid-tone backgrounds. If uncertain, darken the surface, not the text.\n+- On dark surfaces, never full-screen linear gradients (they band); use a solid base + one or two radial gradient glows at 12–25% opacity. Tint neutrals (like #1a1f2e, #e8ecf4) toward the accent hue — dead pure grays look undesigned.\n+\n+### Layout & depth\n+\n+- Largest-to-smallest hierarchy is visible in 2 seconds: one hero element (number, headline, chart) per view; labels < 16px only for metadata.\n+- Cards use 12–20px radii, 2–4px borders or soft shadows — web UI values are invisible at classroom projection distance, so scale up: body text ≥ 16px on mobile-safe layouts, ≥ 20px on main surfaces, padding ≥ 24px between zones.\n+- Every scene (state) needs at least two focal points the eye can travel between — a single floating text block is a failure.\n+- Backgrounds are never empty: add 2–5 subtle decorative layers (accent-tinted radial glow, oversized faded keyword at 3–8% opacity, hairline grid, muted panel) so whitespace looks intentional.\n+- Icons: use inline SVG (project/stroke style, 2px round-cap strokes, viewBox 0 0 24 24). No emoji as primary info — emoji only inside achievement/reward badges.\n+\n+### Motion has meaning\n+\n+- Decorative elements get one ambient animation (breathing glow, slow drift, gentle rotation) so nothing reads static; shared across them is fine.\n+- State changes animate ~200–300ms `ease-out` (entrances), `ease-in` (exits); reveal beats stagger children 50–120ms apart. Springs for direct manipulation only.\n+- Numbers count up to their value (~0.8–1.2s, `power2.out`) when they enter; progress bars/donuts draw when revealed, not before.\n+- No animation is longer than 600ms except cinematic reveals the directive's motionPersonality explicitly asks for. \"The best motion is barely noticeable.\"\n+- All motion must be deterministic: no `Date.now()` state in published observations, no unseeded randomness inside rendered results. Randomness is allowed only for generated practice content, and then through a seeded helper.\n+\n+### States, feedback & safety\n+\n+- Every control gives feedback within 100ms (hover/active/pressed/disabled states defined in CSS).\n+- Loading/empty/error states exist and use the same palette (spinner or skeleton bars, not invented colors).\n+- Failure feedback is supporting, never guilt-tripping: green = correct/done, amber = check again, red = unsafe/wrong.\n+- Mobile safety: 44px min touch targets, collapsible panels, no horizontal scroll, canvas resizes with container.\n",
              "additions": 33,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@\n+/**\n+ * Per-course visual design directive: the shared design language every scene\n+ * of one course generates under (palette, mood, motion personality). Inferred\n+ * once by the outline stage from the requirement, materials and research\n+ * context, then threaded through slide, quiz and widget content generation so\n+ * a course never again defaults to one shared \"PowerPoint blue\" look.\n+ */\n+\n+export interface DesignDirective {\n+  /** One line describing the intended visual mood, e.g. \"cinematic dark-mode physics lab\". */\n+  concept: string;\n+  /**\n+   * 2-5 hex colors, first entry intended as the base/background or darkest\n+   * neutral, last as the accent. All scene generation uses only these.\n+   */\n+  palette: string[];\n+  /** Whether scene backgrounds lean dark or light. */\n+  background: 'dark' | 'light';\n+  /**\n+   * Tween voice for motion: playful / premium / energetic / calm /\n+   * storytelling. Widgets and (when supported) slide animation cues read it.\n+   */\n+  motionPersonality:\n+    | 'playful'\n+    | 'premium'\n+    | 'energetic'\n+    | 'calm'\n+    | 'storytelling';\n+}\n+\n+const HEX_COLOR_RE = /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/;\n+const PERSONALITIES: DesignDirective['motionPersonality'][] = [\n+  'playful',\n+  'premium',\n+  'energetic',\n+  'calm',\n+  'storytelling',\n+];\n+\n+function clampText(value: unknown, maxLength: number): string | undefined {\n+  if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined;\n+  const trimmed = value.trim();\n+  return trimmed ? trimmed.slice(0, maxLength) : undefined;\n+}\n+\n+/**\n+ * Validate and normalize a model-provided design directive. Returns null when\n+ * the value is absent or wholly unusable (callers fall back to their own\n+ * defaults rather than failing generation over styling).\n+ */\n+export function normalizeDesignDirective(\n+  value: unknown,\n+): DesignDirective | null {\n+  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {\n+    return null;\n+  }\n+  const raw = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n+\n+  const concept = clampText(raw.concept, 200);\n+  const conceptFromStyle =\n+    concept ??\n+    (typeof raw.style === 'string' && raw.style.trim()\n+      ? clampText(raw.style, 200)\n+      : undefined);\n+\n+  const palette = Array.isArray(raw.palette)\n+    ? raw.palette\n+        .filter(\n+          (entry): entry is string => typeof entry === 'string' && HEX_COLOR_RE.test(entry.trim()),\n+        )\n+        .map((entry) => entry.trim().toLowerCase())\n+        .filter((entry, index, list) => list.indexOf(entry) === index)\n+        .slice(0, 5)\n+    : [];\n+\n+  const background =\n+    raw.background === 'dark' || raw.background === 'light' ? raw.background : undefined;\n+\n+  const personality = PERSONALITIES.find((candidate) => candidate === raw.motionPersonality);\n+\n+  const directive: DesignDirective = {\n+    ...(conceptFromStyle ? { concept: conceptFromStyle } : { concept: '' }),\n+    ...(palette.length > 0 ? { palette } : { palette: [] }),\n+    ...(background ? { background } : { background: 'dark' }),\n+    ...(personality ? { motionPersonality: personality } : { motionPersonality: 'calm' }),\n+  };\n+\n+  // Wholly unusable (nothing but defaults): treat as absent so the prompt\n+  // falls back to self-selection instead of asserting an empty directive.\n+  if (!conceptFromStyle && palette.length === 0 && !background && !personality) {\n+    return null;\n+  }\n+  return directive;\n+}\n+\n+/** The fallback used when the outline stage produced no usable directive. */\n+export const FALLBACK_DESIGN_DIRECTIVE: DesignDirective = {\n+  concept: '',\n+  palette: [],\n+  background: 'dark',\n+  motionPersonality: 'calm',\n+};\n+\n+/**\n+ * Render a directive into the text block scene prompts consume. Always\n+ * non-empty: without a directive it instructs the model to design one\n+ * coherent system itself, appended by the scene-generation context.\n+ */\n+export function formatDesignDirective(directive: DesignDirective | null | undefined): string {\n+  if (!directive) {\n+    return 'None. Before writing any scene: declare ONE coherent design system yourself (background mode, text color, one accent hue, motion personality) that suits the topic, and apply it consistently across every scene you generate this course.';\n+  }\n+  const lines: string[] = [];\n+  if (directive.concept) lines.push(`- Visual mood: ${directive.concept}`);\n+  if (directive.palette.length > 0) {\n+    lines.push(`- Palette (use ONLY these hexes): ${directive.palette.join(', ')}`);\n+  }\n+  lines.push(`- Background mode: ${directive.background}`);\n+  lines.push(`- Motion personality: ${directive.motionPersonality}`);\n+  return lines.join('\\n');\n+}\n",
              "additions": 121,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },

              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/src/outline-generator.ts\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/src/outline-generator.ts\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/src/outline-generator.ts\t\n@@ -1,236 +1,254 @@\n /**\n  * Stage 1: Generate scene outlines from user requirements.\n  * Also contains outline fallback logic.\n  */\n \n import { nanoid } from 'nanoid';\n import { MAX_PDF_CONTENT_CHARS, MAX_VISION_IMAGES } from './constants.js';\n import { parseJsonResponse } from './json-repair.js';\n import { noopGenerationLogger, type GenerationLogger } from './logger.js';\n import {\n   formatImageDescription,\n   formatImagePlaceholder,\n   sortDocumentImagesForVision,\n } from './outline-formatters.js';\n import { uniquifyMediaElementIds } from './outline-media.js';\n+import { normalizeDesignDirective } from type { AICallFn, GenerationResult } from './pipeline-types.js';\n import { buildPrompt, PROMPT_IDS } from './prompts/index.js';\n \n export const DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE =\n   'Teach in the language that matches the user requirement.';\n \n export interface OutlinePromptContext {\n   pdfText?: string;\n   pdfImages?: PdfImage[];\n   visionEnabled?: boolean;\n   imageMapping?: ImageMapping;\n   imageGenerationEnabled?: boolean;\n   videoGenerationEnabled?: boolean;\n   researchContext?: string;\n   teacherContext?: string;\n }\n \n export interface OutlineGenerationOptions extends Omit<\n   OutlinePromptContext,\n   'pdfText' | 'pdfImages'\n > {\n   logger?: GenerationLogger;\n }\n \n export interface OutlineFallbackOptions {\n   allowProceduralSkill?: boolean;\n   logger?: GenerationLogger;\n }\n \n function buildAvailableImages(\n   pdfImages: PdfImage[] | undefined,\n   context: OutlinePromptContext,\n ): { availableImagesText: string; visionImages?: Array<{ id: string; src: string }> } {\n   let availableImagesText = 'No images available';\n   let visionImages: Array<{ id: string; src: string }> | undefined;\n \n   if (pdfImages && pdfImages.length > 0) {\n     if (context.visionEnabled && context.imageMapping) {\n       const sortedImages = sortDocumentImagesForVision(pdfImages);\n       const allWithSrc = sortedImages.filter((image) => context.imageMapping![image.id]);\n       const visionSlice = allWithSrc.slice(0, MAX_VISION_IMAGES);\n       const textOnlySlice = allWithSrc.slice(MAX_VISION_IMAGES);\n       const noSrcImages = sortedImages.filter((image) => !context.imageMapping![image.id]);\n \n       const visionDescriptions = visionSlice.map((image) => formatImagePlaceholder(image));\n       const textDescriptions = [...textOnlySlice, ...noSrcImages].map((image) =>\n         formatImageDescription(image),\n       );\n       availableImagesText = [...visionDescriptions, ...textDescriptions].join('\\n');\n \n       visionImages = visionSlice.map((image) => ({\n         id: image.id,\n         src: context.imageMapping![image.id],\n         width: image.width,\n         height: image.height,\n       }));\n     } else {\n       availableImagesText = pdfImages.map((image) => formatImageDescription(image)).join('\\n');\n     }\n   }\n \n   return { availableImagesText, visionImages };\n }\n \n /** Build the byte-stable system and user prompts for outline generation. */\n export function buildOutlinePrompt(\n   requirements: UserRequirements,\n   context: OutlinePromptContext = {},\n ): { system: string; user: string } {\n   const { pdfText, pdfImages } = context;\n   const { availableImagesText } = buildAvailableImages(pdfImages, context);\n \n   const userProfileText =\n     requirements.userNickname || requirements.userBio\n       ? `## Student Profile\\n\\nStudent: ${requirements.userNickname || 'Unknown'}${requirements.userBio ? ` — ${requirements.userBio}` : ''}\\n\\nConsider this student's background when designing the course. log.debug(`Got ${generatedQuestions.length} questions for: ${outline.title}`);\n \n   // Ensure each question has an ID and normalize options format.\n   // Plain strings become letter/content pairs. Object fields stay as written.\n   const questions: QuizQuestion[] = generatedQuestions.map((q) => {\n     const isText = q.type === 'short_answer';\n     const options = isText ? undefined : normalizeQuizOptions(q.options);\n     return {\n       ...q,\n       id: q.id || `q_${nanoid(8)}`,\n       options,\n       answer: isText\n         ? undefined\n         : normalizeQuizAnswer(q as unknown as Record<string, unknown>, options),\n       hasAnswer: isText ? false : true,\n     };\n   });\n \n   const contractFailure = findQuizOptionsContractFailure(questions);\n   if (contractFailure) {\n     log.error(`Quiz option contract failed for \"${outline.title}\": ${contractFailure}`);\n     onFailure?.({ code: 'invalid-model-output' });\n     return null;\n   }\n \n   return { questions };\n }\n \n const QUIZ_OPTION_VALUE = /^[A-Z]$/;\n \n /**\n  * Reason a built quiz breaks the choice-option contract, or null when it holds.\n  *\n  * Choice questions (everything except `short_answer`) need a non-empty option\n  * list whose `value`s are single ASCII letters A-Z, and every answer entry\n  * must equal one of those values exactly. Short-answer questions are skipped.\n  */\n export function findQuizOptionsContractFailure(questions: readonly QuizQuestion[]): string | null {\n   for (let index = 0; index < questions.length; index += 1) {\n     const question = questions[index];\n     if (!question || question.type === 'short_answer') continue;\n \n     const where = question.id ? `question ${index + 1} (${question.id})` : `question ${index + 1}`;\n     const options = question.options;\n     if (!options || options.length === 0) {\n       return `${where}: choice question has no options`;\n     }\n \n     const optionValues = new Set<string>();\n \n     for (let optionIndex = 0; optionIndex < options.length; optionIndex += 1) {\n       const value = options[optionIndex]?.value;\n       if (typeof value !== 'string' || !QUIZ_OPTION_VALUE.test(value)) {\n         const shown = JSON.stringify(value);\n         return `${where}: option ${optionIndex + 1} value ${shown} is not a single letter A-Z`;\n       }\n \n       if (optionValues.has(value)) {\n         return `${where}: option ${optionIndex + 1} repeats value ${JSON.stringify(value)}`;\n       }\n \n       optionValues.add(value);\n     }\n \n     const answer = question.answer;\n     if (!answer || answer.length === 0) {\n       return `${where}: answer key does not reference an option value`;\n     }\n \n     for (const entry of answer) {\n       if (!optionValues.has(entry)) {\n         return `${where}: answer ${JSON.stringify(entry)} does not match an option value`;\n       }\n     }\n   }\n \n   return null;\n }\n \n type NormalizedQuizOption = { value: string; label: string };\n \n /**\n  * Normalize quiz options from AI response.\n  * AI may generate plain strings [\"OptionA\", \"OptionB\"] or QuizOption objects.\n  * Plain strings become { value: \"A\", label: \"OptionA\" }. Object `value` and\n  * `label` are kept as provided — a letter in `label` with content in `value`\n  * is not swapped.\n  */\n export function normalizeQuizOptions(\n   options: unknown[] | undefined,\n ): NormalizedQuizOption[] | undefined {\n   if (!options || !Array.isArray(options)) return undefined;\n \n   return options.map((opt, index) => {\n     const letter = String.fromCharCode(65 + index); // A, B, C, D...\n \n     if (typeof opt === 'string') {\n       return { value: letter, label: opt };\n     }\n \n     if (typeof opt === 'object' && opt !== null) {\n       const obj = opt as Record<string, unknown>;\n       return {\n         value: typeof obj.value === 'string' ? obj.value : letter,\n         label: typeof obj.label === 'string' ? obj.label : String(obj.value || obj.text || letter),\n       };\n     }\n \n     return { value: letter, label: String(opt) };\n   });\n }\n \n /**\n  * Normalize quiz answer from AI response.\n  * AI may generate correctAnswer as string or string[], under various field names.\n  * This normalizes to string[] format matching option values.\n  *\n  * The LLM writes the answer key inconsistently, as option CONTENT (\"(6, 2)\")\n  * or as a LETTER (\"A\"). project topic without inventing any.)',\n   ]\n     .filter(Boolean)\n     .join('\\n');\n }\n \n /**\n  * Step 3.2: Generate Actions based on content and script\n  */\n export async function log.info(\n       `[Actions Gen] Interactive \"${outline.title}\": hasHtml=${hasHtml}, widgetType=${hasHtml ? content.widgetType : 'N/A'}`,\n     );\n   }\n \n   if (outline.type === 'slide' && '...' : ''}\"`;\n       } else if (el.type === 'chart' && 'chartType' in el) {\n         summary = `Chart type: ${el.chartType}`;\n       } else if (el.type === 'image') {\n         summary = 'Image element';\n       } else if (el.type === 'shape' && 'shapeName' in el) {\n         summary = `Shape: ${el.shapeName || 'unknown'}`;\n       } else if (el.type === 'latex' && 'latex' in el) {\n         summary = `Formula: ${((el.latex as string) || '').substring(0, 30)}`;\n       } else {\n         summary = `${el.type} element`;\n       }\n       return `- id: \"${el.id}\", type: \"${el.type}\", ${summary}`;\n     })\n     .join('\\n');\n }\n \n /**\n  * Format question list for AI reference\n  */\n function formatQuestionsForPrompt(questions: QuizQuestion[]): string {\n   return questions\n     .map((q, i) => {\n       const optionsText = q.options\n         ? `Options: ${q.options.map((o) => `${o.value}. ${o.label}`).join(', ')}`\n         : '';\n       return `Q${i + 1} (${q.type}): ${q.question}\\n${optionsText}`;\n     })\n     .join('\\n\\n');\n }\n \n /**\n  * Process and validate Actions\n  */\n function processActions(\n   actions: Action[],\n   elements: PPTElement[],\n   agents?: AgentInfo[],\n   log: GenerationLogger = noopGenerationLogger,\n ): Action[] {\n   const elementIds = new Set(elements.map((el) => el.id));\n   const agentIds = new Set(agents?.map((a) => a.id) || []);\n   const studentAgents = agents?.filter((a) => a.role === 'student') || [];\n   const nonTeacherAgents = agents?.filter((a) => a.role !== 'teacher') || [];\n \n   return actions.map((action) => {\n     // Ensure each action has an ID\n     const processedAction: Action = {\n       ...action,\n       id: action.id || `action_${nanoid(8)}`,\n     };\n \n     // Validate spotlight elementId\n     if (processedAction.type === 'spotlight') {\n       const spotlightAction = processedAction;\n       if (!spotlightAction.elementId || !elementIds.has(spotlightAction.elementId)) {\n         // If elementId is invalid, try selecting the first element\n         if (elements.length > 0) {\n           spotlightAction.elementId = elements[0].id;\n           log.warn(\n             `Invalid elementId, falling back to first element: ${spotlightAction.elementId}`,\n           );\n         }\n       }\n     }\n \n     // Validate/fill discussion agentId\n     if (processedAction.type === 'discussion' && agents && agents.length > 0) {\n       if (processedAction.agentId && agentIds.has(processedAction.agentId)) {\n         // agentId valid — keep it\n       } else {\n         // agentId missing or invalid — pick a random student, or non-teacher, or skip\n         const pool = studentAgents.length > 0 ? studentAgents : nonTeacherAgents;\n         if (pool.length > 0) {\n           const picked = pool[Math.floor(Math.random() * pool.length)];\n           log.warn(\n             `Discussion agentId \"${processedAction.agentId || '(none)'}\" invalid, assigned: ${picked.id} (${picked.name})`,\n           );\n           processedAction.agentId = picked.id;\n         }\n       }\n     }\n \n     return processedAction;\n   });\n }\n \n /**\n  * Generate default slide Actions (fallback)\n  */\n function generateDefaultSlideActions(outline: SceneOutline, elements: PPTElement[]): Action[] {\n   const actions: Action[] = [];\n \n   // Add spotlight for text elements\n   const textElements = elements.filter((el) => el.type === 'text');\n   if (textElements.length > 0) {\n     actions.push({\n       id: `action_${nanoid(8)}`,\n       type: 'spotlight',\n       title: '聚焦重点',\n       elementId: textElements[0].id,\n     });\n   }\n \n   // Add opening speech based on key points\n   const speechText = outline.keyPoints?.length\n     ?               "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@\n+# Motion-Graphic Explainer Generator (Course Intro \"Trailer\")\n+\n+Generate a self-contained HTML motion-graphic explainer — a cinematic, animated opening scene for an online course, in the style of premium product-launch motion graphics (kinetic typography, hero stats, icon choreography, SVG path draws).\n+\n+**This is the FIRST scene of the course: its job is to HOOK the learner in 20–45 seconds and make them want to continue.** Motion is the message; there is no narrator audio inside the widget — the teacher (outside the iframe) narrates over it.\n+\n+## Story Shape (4 phases — follow exactly)\n+\n+Build ONE master timeline with 4 labeled phases. Each phase is one idea. Total on-screen duration 25–45 s:\n+\n+| Phase | Label | Duration | Job |\n+|---|---|---|---|\n+| 1. HOOK | `p0` | 6–10 s | Open with the question, paradox, or stakes of the topic. A *wait, what?* moment — never \"Welcome to course X\". One bold statement, a moving visual, an intriguing number. |\n+| 2. TEASE | `p1` | 7–12 s | Sketch the territory the course covers: 3–4 keyword cards or icons snap/chase in, a comparison or a map of the problem space. Sets expectation, not detail. |\n+| 3. SPARK | `p2` | 8–14 s | The signature visual moment: one idea animated beautifully — the concept as a moving infographic (orbit, build-up, transformation, count-up, path draw). This is the beat people remember. |\n+| 4. TITLE | `p3` | 5–8 s | Course title lockup: assemble/inch to final position, then everything settles into a calm LOOPING ambient state (breathing glow, drifting particles) for as long as the scene stays open. |\n+\n+**Content rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE):**\n+- Ground EVERYTHING in the topic from Scene Information. Real keywords, real numbers (mark hypothetical ones as \"example\"), real terminology in the course language.\n+- Max ~2-8 words per card; readable in 1.5 s. The learner reads while the teacher speaks.\n+- No fake claims about the course (\"best course ever\", fake student counts). No teacher identity. Captions in the teaching language (per `languageDirective`) — including proper names kept in their original script.\n+- No photographic assets, no external images (except CDNs listed below). Everything is CSS/SVG/typography. This keeps generation cheap and offline-safe.\n+\n+## Master Design Skill (motion doctrine — read carefully)\n+\n+### Easing is emotion, not technique\n+\n+- `.out` eases for entrances (starts fast, decelerates — confident). `.in` for exits. `.inOut` for repositioning. Sine for ambient loops. **Linear only for rotation, ticks, progress** — never for spatial movement.\n+- Durations: micro (0.15–0.3s) = energy; standard (0.3–0.5s) = professional; slow (0.5–0.8s) = gravity; very slow (0.8–1.6s) = cinematic. Vary: the slowest tween in a phase should be ≥ 3× the fastest. Never default everything to one duration.\n+- Exits are 30–50% FASTER than entrances. Overshoot-and-settle (`back.out(1.4)`) for playful entries; `expo.out` for confident reveals; `elastic.out(1, 0.5)` sparingly.\n+\n+### Choreography\n+\n+- Stagger children 60–140ms apart; keep a whole stagger sequence under 500ms. The element that moves FIRST reads as most important — lead with the hero.\n+- One ambient motion per phase (breathing glow, slow drift, subtle scale) — attached to the seekable timeline, never a bare `gsap.to()` outside it.\n+- Vary entrance directions across elements (from left / from right / scale-up / blur-in / letter-spacing). Repeating `y:30 + fade` for everything is a failure.\n+- Scene structure per phase: **build** (elements enter, first 30%) → **breathe** (hold, ambient alive, middle 40%) → **resolve** (exit or hand off, last 30%). No dead air, no abrupt stops.\n+- Never run two independent tweens on the SAME element+property concurrently; if one element needs an entrance AND a continuous motion, combine in a single `fromTo()` or nest (parent gets entrance, child gets the loop).\n+- Prefer `tl.fromTo()` over `tl.from()` — deterministic under phase seeking.\n+\n+### Kinetic typography (main technique toolbox)\n+\n+| Effect | How |\n+|---|---|\n+| Sequential word reveal | Words pop one-by-one, 80–150ms apart, slight overshoot |\n+| Expressive scale | The KEY word jumps to 130–160% scale + accent color, others dim |\n+| Typewriter / mask reveal | Clip-path inset or width reveal left→right |\n+| Gradient-text sweep | Shimmering gradient across large headline (sparingly) |\n+| Letter-spacing settle | Wide tracking → tight tracking as word lands |\n+| 3D flip / rotate entrance | `rotationX/Y` with `transformPerspective: 1200` |\n+| Path draw | SVG `strokeDashoffset` to 0 over 0.6–1.2s (logos, arrows, connectors) |\n+| Count-up | Number for 0→target, ~1s, `power2.out`, snap:true integers |\n+| Progress bar / donut fill | scaleX or stroke draw when revealed |\n+\n+### Composition (frames are scenes, not web pages)\n+\n+- Fill the stage: hero text spans 60–80% of width, entrance padding 60–140px.\n+- ≥ 2 focal points per phase so the eye travels; anchor content to edges or split into zones — not everything centered-floating.\n+- ≥ 3 layers per phase: background treatment (radial accent glow, oversized ghost word at 3–8% opacity, subtle grid/panel) + midground content + foreground accents (hairline rules that `scaleX` from 0, index labels, tick marks).\n+- Scale: headlines 56–120px (weight 700–900, tight tracking); key words 34–48px; labels 16–22px; borders 2–4px; decorative opacity 12–25%. Use `clamp()` and `vw/vmin` units so it scales inside any iframe size.\n+\n+## Design Directive\n+\n+The Scene Information contains a **Design Directive** (palette, mood, motion personality). It is LAW:\n+\n+- Background is the directive's `background` mode (dark builds feel cinematic; light builds need bold 2px+ structural elements and full-saturation accent hits to avoid the blank-slide feel).\n+- Use the directive's `palette` hexes only. Map: `palette[0]` → base/background or the darkest neutral, then text/high-contrast neutrals stay within ±10 lightness of the palette's neutrals; the accent (brightest/most saturated) is the 10% — HOOK keyword, hero number, draw strokes, glow.\n+- `motionPersonality` sets the tween voice: `playful` → overshoot/elastic, 20–30% exaggeration; `premium` → slow calm eases, zero overshoot, generous whitespace; `energetic` → fast cuts, hard snaps, high stagger; `calm` → long holds, gentle sine ambient; `storytelling` → front-load the SPARK phase.\n+- If the directive is missing or incomplete, choose ONE coherent system yourself (declare bg / text / accent before writing CSS), and keep it across every phase.\n+\n+**Do NOT:** gradient text everywhere, cyan-on-dark cliché, neon-on-neon, pure `#000`/`#fff`, identical repeated cards, more than one gradient text effect per phase. Tint neutrals toward the palette.\n+\n+## Technical Contract (MANDATORY)\n+\n+### 1. Deterministic timeline\n+\n+```html\n+<!DOCTYPE html>\n+<html>\n+<head>\n+  <!-- GSAP via CDN (same allowance as 3D widgets) -->\n+  <script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js\"></script>\n+  <style> /* all custom CSS inline, fonts = system stacks only */ </style>\n+</head>\n+<body>\n+  <div id=\"experiment\"> <!-- the whole scene inside this wrapper -->\n+    ...\n+    <script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\"> ... </script>\n+    <script> /* all JS */ </script>\n+  </div>\n+</body>\n+</html>\n+```\n+\n+- ONE master timeline: `const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: false })` with **labels `p0`…`p3`** at each phase boundary.\n+- Total active timeline ~25–45 s. After the TITLE phase, append a repeating ambient block: `tl.to(..., { ..., repeat: -1 }, 'amb')` is FORBIDDEN on the master (it would stall phase seeking) — instead build a separate `ambientTl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true, repeat: -1 })` and start it when the master completes (`tl.eventCallback('onComplete', () => ambientTl.play())`). Ambient changes nothing that phases depend on.\n+- **No `Date.now()` for animation state, no `Math.random()` inside the timeline** (seeded jitter in decorative particles is allowed: `gsap.utils.random` with a fixed seed or precomputed offsets). Everything visible must be a pure function of timeline position so Replay and phase-seek are exact.\n+- Fallback without network: wrap usage — if `typeof gsap === 'undefined'`, add class `no-anim` to `<body>`. CSS: `.no-anim [data-step]{opacity:1;transform:none}` and skip timeline creation. Content must be fully readable, statically laid out, with the HTML static fallback (a static poster) — never a blank iframe.\n+- No audio, no video tags, no fetch(), no localStorage, no timers/runnning loops outside the timelines.\n+\n+### 2. Phase control API (REQUIRED)\n+\n+Expose a global so the platform and the phase dots can drive the story:\n+\n+```javascript\n+window.setExplainerPhase = function (phase) {\n+  // phase is 'p0'..'p3' (or number index)\n+  ambientTl.pause();\n+  tl.seek(phase, false);\n+  tl.play();\n+};\n+window.explainerGetState = function () {\n+  return { phase: currentPhase(), progress: tl.totalProgress() };\n+};\n+```\n+\n+- On `message` events, honor `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with `state.phase` → `window.setExplainerPhase(state.phase)`. Also accept `{ state: { replay: true } }` → restart (`tl.restart()`).\n+- In-iframe controls (always visible, small, bottom-center): phase dots `#phase-dots` (button per phase, `id=\"phase-dot-p0\"` etc., current highlighted) + a replay button `id=\"replay-btn\"`. Clicking → `setExplainerPhase` / restart. 44px touch targets.\n+\n+### 3. Observation contract\n+\n+{{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n+\n+For this widget publish:\n+```json\n+{ \"summary\": \"Phase 2 (Spark): the solar system race is animating\", \"state\": { \"phase\": \"p2\", \"phaseIndex\": 2 }, \"beats\": [ {\"id\":\"p0\",\"label\":\"Hook\"}, ... ] }\n+```\n+Publish on load, on every phase change (`tl.call(publishCurrentState, [], tl, 'p1')` at each label) and after any seek. Include the phase label list once in `state.beats`.\n+\n+### 4. widget-config (widget-config REQUIRED)\n+\n+```json\n+{\n+  \"type\": \"animation-explainer\",\n+  \"concept\": \"<topic concept>\",\n+  \"description\": \"<what this animation covers>\",\n+  \"beats\": [{ \"id\": \"p0\", \"label\": \"Hook name\" }, { \"id\": \"p1\", \"label\": \"...\" }, { \"id\": \"p2\", \"label\": \"...\" }, { \"id\": \"p3\", \"label\": \"Title\" }],\n+  \"mood\": \"<motionPersonality>\"\n+}\n+```\n+\n+### 5. Robustness (cheap-model safety net)\n+\n+- Script at end of body; all setup inside one IIFE or DOMContentLoaded; **no top-level `await`**; syntax must be ES5-safe-ish (no optional chaining needed) so the validator never rejects it.\n+- SVG: inline only, `viewBox` set, no external URLs. Animate with GSAP (`strokeDashoffset`, `scale`, `opacity`), never CSS `@keyframes` conflicts with GSAP on the same element.\n+- No duplicated documents: exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>`; output the document once.\n+- Keep total output < ~25 KB of CSS + ~15 KB of JS. Leverage CSS custom properties for the palette.\n+\n+## Output Format (CRITICAL)\n+\n+Return ONLY one complete HTML document, no markdown fences, no prose.\n+\n+## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n+\n+- [ ] 4 phases with labels p0–p3 present in the master timeline; total 25–45 s\n+- [ ] HOOK is a question/stakes/paradox grounded in THIS topic — not a welcome slide\n+- [ ] Real topic keywords and (example-safe) numbers; the course language is used\n+- [ ] Palette = the design directive; bg mode respected; one accent discipline; contrast ≥ 4.5:1\n+- [ ] ≥ 3 entrance easing values; ≥ 3 entrance directions; stagger ≤ 500ms; exits faster than entrances\n+- [ ] Background decoration ≥ 3 treatments across phases (glow, ghost type, rules/grid)\n+- [ ] `window.setExplainerPhase` + `SET_WIDGET_STATE` routing + `#phase-dots` + `#replay-btn` work\n+- [ ] `data-maic-observation` publishes phase on load and at every phase label\n+- [ ] widget-config JSON: type `animation-explainer`, `beats` matches phase labels\n+- [ ] Offline/static fallback (`no-anim`) leaves content readable; no blank screen\n+- [ ] Deterministic: replay produces the exact same animation\n",
              "additions": 165,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },

              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/user.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/user.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/user.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@\n+Create the opening MOTION-GRAPHIC EXPLAINER for: {{title}}\n+\n+## Concept\n+\n+{{concept}}\n+\n+## what to cover (from the course planner)\n+\n+{{description}}\n+\n+## Key Points\n+\n+{{keyPoints}}\n+\n+## Story Beats\n+\n+{{beats}}\n+\n+## Mood\n+\n+{{mood}}\n+\n+## Design Directive\n+\n+{{designDirective}}\n+\n+## Language\n+\n+{{languageDirective}}\n+\n+---\n+\n+Generate the complete HTML motion graphic (the \"course trailer\"):\n+\n+- Build phase 1 (HOOK) around the FIRST key point or the topic's central paradox — give the viewer a reason to care in the first 6 seconds.\n+- Phase 2 (TEASE) visualizes the main key points as 3-4 keyword/icon cards.\n+- Phase 3 (SPARK) is the signature animated infographic tied to this exact topic's core mechanism (count-up, orbit, transformation, path draw, comparison).\n+- Phase 4 (TITLE) locks in the course title \"{{title}}\" and settles into an ambient loop.\n+- Apply the Design Directive palette strictly; follow the mood for easing and pacing.\n+- All text in the teaching language.\n+- Include: `window.setExplainerPhase`, `SET_WIDGET_STATE` listener (`phase` + `replay`), phase dots + replay button, `data-maic-observation` with phase state, and the `widget-config` JSON with `beats` matching your phase labels.\n+- Deterministic GSAP master timeline (labels p0-p3), total 25-45 s, ambient loop after completion. Static fallback if GSAP is missing.\n+\n+Return ONLY the HTML document.\n",

href=\"#-agent-workbench-integration\">OpenClaw</a>\n42: </p>\n43: \n44: ## 🗞️ News\n45: \n46: - **2026-10-04** — [v1.2.0-rc.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.2.0-rc.1) (pre-release): **server-first.** Until 1.1.x, the browser drove course generation step by step and kept courses, keys and model settings itself, so closing the tab stopped a course halfway, every browser had to be configured on its own, and the headless API ran a separate pipeline. In 1.2.0 the server owns all of it: generation runs on the server and survives closed tabs and restarts, models are configured once in `openmaic.yml` (with defaults, locks and an option to forbid user keys), materials are parsed as soon as they are attached, and the web app and the API share one pipeline. It needs PostgreSQL and a long-running server; Vercel deployments stay on [1.1.x](#vercel-deployment-up-to-11x). Read the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) before upgrading.\n47: - **2026-09-28** — [v1.1.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.1.2): security — provider requests connect only to validated addresses and refuse redirects ([GHSA-g87c-cm4q-cw5x](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/security/advisories/GHSA-g87c-cm4q-cw5x)).\n48: - **2026-09-27** — [v1.1.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.1.1): security — hardened MinerU Cloud parsing ([GHSA-cpjc-vgjh-c5jp](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/security/advisories/GHSA-cpjc-vgjh-c5jp)).\n49: - **2026-09-24** — [v1.1.0](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.1.0): agentic classroom chat (ask about any slide element, interactive, or whiteboard drawing); settings rebuilt around the course workflow; Token Plan connections.\n50: - **2026-09-15** — [v1.0.3](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.0.3): security — access-code tokens expire, render-service network policy, pinned audio connections, Next.js RCE patch.\n51: - **2026-09-14** — [v1.0.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.0.2): security — SSRF and DNS-rebinding fixes, classroom overwrite fix.\n52: - **2026-09-06** — [v1.0.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.0.1): security and stability; tightens two defaults.\n53: - **2026-08-27** — **v1.0.0**: agent workbench, durable sessions, reusable skills, session materials, provider-neutral capabilities.\n54: \n55: <details>\n56: <summary>Earlier releases</summary>\n57: \n58: - **2026-08-14** — [v0.3.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.3.2): video export hardening, server-backed persistence and asset registry, `@openmaic/generation`, four new locales, FunASR.\n59: - **2026-07-21** — [v0.3.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.3.1): one-click MP4 export, direct slide editing, smarter \"Edit with AI\", expanded document parsing.\n60: - **2026-06-28** — [v0.3.0](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.3.0): PBL v2, \"Edit with AI\" editor agent, `@openmaic/*` SDKs on npm, relicensed to MIT.\n61: - **2026-06-02** — [v0.2.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.2.2): MAIC Editor Pro Mode, editable outlines, offline classroom export.\n62: - **2026-04-26** — [v0.2.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.2.1): VoxCPM2 TTS with voice cloning, per-model thinking config, course completion page.\n63: - **2026-04-20** — **v0.2.0**: Deep Interactive Mode — 3D, simulations, games, mind maps, online programming.\n64: - **2026-04-14** — [v0.1.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.1.1): language inference, ACCESS_CODE, classroom ZIP export/import, Ollama.\n65: - **2026-03-26** — [v0.1.0](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.1.0): discussion TTS, immersive mode, keyboard shortcuts.\n66: \n67: </details>\n68: \n69: Full history in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).\n70: \n71: ## 📖 Overview\n72: \n73: **OpenMAIC** (Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom) is an open-source AI platform that turns any topic or document into a rich, interactive classroom experience. Powered by multi-agent orchestration, it generates slides, quizzes, interactive simulations, and project-based learning activities — all delivered by AI teachers and AI classmates who can speak, draw on a whiteboard, and engage in real-time discussions with you. The built-in OpenMAIC Skill works with [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) as well as agent workbenches such as Codex, DeepSeek, and WorkBuddy, so you can generate classrooms from messaging apps like Feishu, Slack, or Telegram, or right inside your IDE.\n74: \n75: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f3f1e5f-1468-4e93-8054-afeeea683a61\n76: \n77: ### Highlights\n78: \n79: - **One-click lesson generation** — Describe a topic or attach your materials; the AI builds a full lesson in minutes\n80: - **Multi-agent classroom** — AI teachers and peers lecture, discuss, and interact with you in real time\n81: - **Rich scene types** — Slides, quizzes, interactive HTML simulations, and project-based learning (PBL)\n82: - **Whiteboard & TTS** — Agents draw diagrams, write formulas, and explain out loud\n83: - **Export anywhere** — Download editable `.pptx` slides or interactive `.html` pages\n84: - **[Agent workbench integration](#-agent-workbench-integration)** — The OpenMAIC Skill supports OpenClaw, Codex, DeepSeek, WorkBuddy, and more — generate classrooms from Feishu, Slack, Telegram, 20+ messaging apps, or your IDE\n85: \n86: ## 🚀 Quick Start\n87: \n88: ### Prerequisites\n89: \n90: - **Node.js** >= 22.19\n91: - **pnpm** >= 10\n92: - **PostgreSQL** 16 — courses are stored on the server. For local development\n93:   `pnpm db:up` starts one in Docker for you.\n94: \n95: ### 1. Clone & Install\n96: \n97: ```bash\n98: git clone https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC.git\n99: cd OpenMAIC\n100: pnpm install\n101: ```\n102: \n103: ### 2. Configure\n104: \n105: ```bash\n106: cp .env.example .env.local            # API keys and server options\n107: cp openmaic.example.yml openmaic.yml  # which models the server uses\n108: ```\n109: \n110: The copied example needs only `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env.local` (or change its provider to one you have a key for); everything else in it is commented out until you want it. `openmaic.yml` declares **providers** (accounts the server can call) and gives each **slot** (a use of AI: the outline, slide content, text to speech, web search, …) a model. Keys stay in `.env.local` and are referenced as `${VAR}`:\n111: \n112: ```yaml\n113: providers:\n114:   openai:\n115:     preset: openai\n116:     apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}      # OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... in .env.local\n117:   anthropic:\n118:     preset: anthropic\n119:     apiKey: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}\n120: \n121: slots:\n122:   llm: openai:gpt-5.5              # the default chat model\n123:   course.outline: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6\n124:   video: null                      # turn a capability off\n125: ```\n126: \n127: The slots you write are the server's defaults; users can change them, or connect services of their own, in the app's model settings unless you `lock` them or set `allowUserKeys: false`. The server validates the file at startup and names every mistake by its field (or, for broken YAML, its line).\n128: \n129: | To learn about | Read |\n130: | --- | --- |\n131: | Slots, presets, fallbacks, `lock`, `allowUserKeys`, `OPENMAIC_SECRET_KEY` | [Configuration](packages/docs/content/docs/configuration.mdx) |\n132: | Every provider preset and model ID | [Supported models](packages/docs/content/docs/supported-models.mdx) |\n133: | Upgrading: provider variables, `server-providers.yml`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` and `MODEL_FALLBACK` still work without `openmaic.yml`; `MODEL_ROUTES` must become slots | [Migrating from the legacy configuration](packages/docs/content/docs/configuration.mdx#migrating-from-the-legacy-configuration) |\n134: \n135: **Providers:** OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, MiniMax, Grok (xAI), OpenRouter, OpenCode, TokenDance, Doubao, Tencent Hunyuan/TokenHub, Xiaomi MiMo, GLM (Zhipu), Ollama, [Lemonade](#lemonade-local-ai) and [FunASR](#funasr-local-asr) (local), and any OpenAI-compatible API.\n136: \n137: > [!TIP]\n138: > **Recommended setup:** OpenMAIC is at its best with every modality turned on — generated illustrations, narration, video clips, and web-grounded research. The least friction is a single key that covers all of them (see the token plan examples below), with a fast long-context model such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash` as the default.\n139: \n140: <details>\n141: <summary><b>More examples</b>: token plans, Xiaomi MiMo and GLM, Amazon Bedrock</summary>\n142: \n143: Token plan quick example (one key for chat, image, video, TTS and web search; `tokendance` works the same way):\n144: \n145: ```yaml\n146: providers:\n147:   minimax:\n148:     preset: minimax\n149:     apiKey: ${MINIMAX_API_KEY}\n150: \n\n(Showing lines 1-150 of 1061. Use offset=151 to continue.)\n</content>",

href=\"#-agent-workbench-integration\">OpenClaw</a>\n</p>\n\n## 🗞️ News\n\n- **2026-10-04** — [v1.2.0-rc.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.2.0-rc.1) (pre-release): **server-first.** Until 1.1.x, the browser drove course generation step by step and kept courses, keys and model settings itself, so closing the tab stopped a course halfway, every browser had to be configured on its own, and the headless API ran a separate pipeline. In 1.2.0 the server owns all of it: generation runs on the server and survives closed tabs and restarts, models are configured once in `openmaic.yml` (with defaults, locks and an option to forbid user keys), materials are parsed as soon as they are attached, and the web app and the API share one pipeline. It needs PostgreSQL and a long-running server; Vercel deployments stay on [1.1.x](#vercel-deployment-up-to-11x). Read the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) before upgrading.\n- **2026-09-28** — [v1.1.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.1.2): security — provider requests connect only to validated addresses and refuse redirects ([GHSA-g87c-cm4q-cw5x](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/security/advisories/GHSA-g87c-cm4q-cw5x)).\n- **2026-09-27** — [v1.1.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.1.1): security — hardened MinerU Cloud parsing ([GHSA-cpjc-vgjh-c5jp](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/security/advisories/GHSA-cpjc-vgjh-c5jp)).\n- **2026-09-24** — [v1.1.0](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.1.0): agentic classroom chat (ask about any slide element, interactive, or whiteboard drawing); settings rebuilt around the course workflow; Token Plan connections.\n- **2026-09-15** — [v1.0.3](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.0.3): security — access-code tokens expire, render-service network policy, pinned audio connections, Next.js RCE patch.\n- **2026-09-14** — [v1.0.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.0.2): security — SSRF and DNS-rebinding fixes, classroom overwrite fix.\n- **2026-09-06** — [v1.0.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v1.0.1): security and stability; tightens two defaults.\n- **2026-08-27** — **v1.0.0**: agent workbench, durable sessions, reusable skills, session materials, provider-neutral capabilities.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Earlier releases</summary>\n\n- **2026-08-14** — [v0.3.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.3.2): video export hardening, server-backed persistence and asset registry, `@openmaic/generation`, four new locales, FunASR.\n- **2026-07-21** — [v0.3.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.3.1): one-click MP4 export, direct slide editing, smarter \"Edit with AI\", expanded document parsing.\n- **2026-06-28** — [v0.3.0](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.3.0): PBL v2, \"Edit with AI\" editor agent, `@openmaic/*` SDKs on npm, relicensed to MIT.\n- **2026-06-02** — [v0.2.2](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.2.2): MAIC Editor Pro Mode, editable outlines, offline classroom export.\n- **2026-04-26** — [v0.2.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.2.1): VoxCPM2 TTS with voice cloning, per-model thinking config, course completion page.\n- **2026-04-20** — **v0.2.0**: Deep Interactive Mode — 3D, simulations, games, mind maps, online programming.\n- **2026-04-14** — [v0.1.1](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.1.1): language inference, ACCESS_CODE, classroom ZIP export/import, Ollama.\n- **2026-03-26** — [v0.1.0](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/releases/tag/v0.1.0): discussion TTS, immersive mode, keyboard shortcuts.\n\n</details>\n\nFull history in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).\n\n## 📖 Overview\n\n**OpenMAIC** (Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom) is an open-source AI platform that turns any topic or document into a rich, interactive classroom experience. Powered by multi-agent orchestration, it generates slides, quizzes, interactive simulations, and project-based learning activities — all delivered by AI teachers and AI classmates who can speak, draw on a whiteboard, and engage in real-time discussions with you. The built-in OpenMAIC Skill works with [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) as well as agent workbenches such as Codex, DeepSeek, and WorkBuddy, so you can generate classrooms from messaging apps like Feishu, Slack, or Telegram, or right inside your IDE.\n\nhttps://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f3f1e5f-1468-4e93-8054-afeeea683a61\n\n### Highlights\n\n- **One-click lesson generation** — Describe a topic or attach your materials; the AI builds a full lesson in minutes\n- **Multi-agent classroom** — AI teachers and peers lecture, discuss, and interact with you in real time\n- **Rich scene types** — Slides, quizzes, interactive HTML simulations, and project-based learning (PBL)\n- **Whiteboard & TTS** — Agents draw diagrams, write formulas, and explain out loud\n- **Export anywhere** — Download editable `.pptx` slides or interactive `.html` pages\n- **[Agent workbench integration](#-agent-workbench-integration)** — The OpenMAIC Skill supports OpenClaw, Codex, DeepSeek, WorkBuddy, and more — generate classrooms from Feishu, Slack, Telegram, 20+ messaging apps, or your IDE\n\n## 🚀 Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- **Node.js** >= 22.19\n- **pnpm** >= 10\n- **PostgreSQL** 16 — courses are stored on the server. For local development\n  `pnpm db:up` starts one in Docker for you.\n\n### 1. Clone & Install\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC.git\ncd OpenMAIC\npnpm install\n```\n\n### 2. Configure\n\n```bash\ncp .env.example .env.local            # API keys and server options\ncp openmaic.example.yml openmaic.yml  # which models the server uses\n```\n\nThe copied example needs only `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env.local` (or change its provider to one you have a key for); everything else in it is commented out until you want it. `openmaic.yml` declares **providers** (accounts the server can call) and gives each **slot** (a use of AI: the outline, slide content, text to speech, web search, …) a model. Keys stay in `.env.local` and are referenced as `${VAR}`:\n\n```yaml\nproviders:\n  openai:\n    preset: openai\n    apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}      # OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... in .env.local\n  anthropic:\n    preset: anthropic\n    apiKey: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}\n\nslots:\n  llm: openai:gpt-5.5              # the default chat model\n  course.outline: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6\n  video: null                      # turn a capability off\n```\n\nThe slots you write are the server's defaults; users can change them, or connect services of their own, in the app's model settings unless you `lock` them or set `allowUserKeys: false`. The server validates the file at startup and names every mistake by its field (or, for broken YAML, its line).\n\n| To learn about | Read |\n| --- | --- |\n| Slots, presets, fallbacks, `lock`, `allowUserKeys`, `OPENMAIC_SECRET_KEY` | [Configuration](packages/docs/content/docs/configuration.mdx) |\n| Every provider preset and model ID | [Supported models](packages/docs/content/docs/supported-models.mdx) |\n| Upgrading: provider variables, `server-providers.yml`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` and `MODEL_FALLBACK` still work without `openmaic.yml`; `MODEL_ROUTES` must become slots | [Migrating from the legacy configuration](packages/docs/content/docs/configuration.mdx#migrating-from-the-legacy-configuration) |\n\n**Providers:** OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, MiniMax, Grok (xAI), OpenRouter, OpenCode, TokenDance, Doubao, Tencent Hunyuan/TokenHub, Xiaomi MiMo, GLM (Zhipu), Ollama, [Lemonade](#lemonade-local-ai) and [FunASR](#funasr-local-asr) (local), and any OpenAI-compatible API.\n\n> [!TIP]\n> **Recommended setup:** OpenMAIC is at its best with every modality turned on — generated illustrations, narration, video clips, and web-grounded research. The least friction is a single key that covers all of them (see the token plan examples below), with a fast long-context model such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash` as the default.\n\n<details>\n<summary><b>More examples</b>: token plans, Xiaomi MiMo and GLM, Amazon Bedrock</summary>\n\nToken plan quick example (one key for chat, image, video, TTS and web search; `tokendance` works the same way):\n\n```yaml\nproviders:\n  minimax:\n    preset: minimax\n    apiKey: ${MINIMAX_API_KEY}\n",

Here is the full report.\n\n---\n\n# OpenMAIC Lesson Generation Pipeline — Research Report\n\n## 1. Architecture overview\n\nGeneration is a package (`@openmaic/generation`) plus an app-side server pipeline (`lib/server/generation/`).\n\n**Package stage functions** (in `/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/packages/@openmaic/generation/src/`):\n\n| File | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `outline-generator.ts` | **Stage 1** — requirements → scene outlines (`generateSceneOutlinesFromRequirements`). Builds prompt via `buildOutlinePrompt`, returns `{languageDirective, courseTitle, outlines}`, applies `applyOutlineFallbacks` (interactive-without-widget → slide; procedural-skill-disabled → diagram) |\n| `scene-generator.ts` | **Stage 2a** — outline → scene content (`generateSceneContent`: slide / quiz / interactive-widget / PBL) and **Stage 2b** — content → teaching actions (`generateSceneActions`). Also contains `resolveImageIds`, `fixElementDefaults`, LaTeX→KaTeX rendering, HTML extraction, element inventory extraction |\n| `scene-builder.ts` | Assembles the final `CompleteScene` (`buildCompleteScene`), minting the default slide **theme** |\n| `scene-types.ts` | Pre-assembly payload types (`GeneratedSlideContent`, `GeneratedInteractiveContent`, …) |\n| `prompt-formatters.ts` | Context builders: `buildCourseContext` (position in course), `formatAgentsForPrompt`, `formatTeacherPersonaForPrompt`, `buildLanguageText`, vision image attachment array |\n\n**Prompt system**: actual prompt *text* lives in the package's `templates/<id>/system.md` + `user.md` (26 files), composed with `snippets/*.md` (9 files) via `{{snippet:…}}`, `{{#if flag}}…{{/if}}`, `{{variable}}` — handled by `src/prompts/loader.ts` (`src/prompts/index.ts` lists the 13 prompt IDs).\n\n**App engine** (`lib/server/generation/run/engine.ts`, `steps/*.ts`, `run/media.ts`): sequences research → material-analysis → outline → agents → per-scene (content → actions → narration) → media lane, persisting scenes and media assets, with outline confirmation, retries, and asset placement.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Prompt file inventory (exact paths and purpose)\n\n### Package templates — `/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/`\n\n| Path | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `requirements-to-outlines/system.md` + `user.md` | Stage-1 course planner. Infers topic/audience/duration/language from the user's free-text requirement; emits `languageDirective`, `courseTitle` (≤30 chars), and a `SceneOutline[]`. Defines scene types, widget-type selection table, PBL config, media-request (`mediaGenerations`) guidance, chart/table keyPoint conventions. **Default assumption: \"Visual Style: Professional\"** — but nothing downstream consumes this; outlines carry no style field |\n| `slide-content/system.md` + `user.md` | **The main slide-design prompt** (detailed excerpts below). Teaches the LLM the JSON element schema, canvas geometry, layout math. Strictly bounded: no global theme variables, no color palette directive, no animation instructions |\n| `quiz-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Quiz generator: JSON array of questions (`single`/`multiple`/`short_answer`), strict `value`=letter A–Z / `label`=content contract, difficulty table, `analysis` + `points` required |\n| `simulation-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Interactive widget #1 — self-contained HTML canvas simulation (rigid-body/slider demos). Mobile-safe layouts, reset state machine, visible animation, postMessage listener, embedded `widget-config` JSON |\n| `diagram-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Interactive widget #2 — SVG flowchart/mindmap with reveal order, node/edge geometry code, high-contrast spec |\n| `code-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Interactive widget #3 — Pyodide/JS code playground (stdout capture pattern, test cases, progressive hints) |\n| `game-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Interactive widget #4 — \"GAMES, NOT QUIZZES\"; physics/action games, fair-start rules, inline `onclick`, custom CSS over Tailwind |\n| `visualization3d-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Interactive widget #5 — Three.js scenes with CDN importmap, lighting minimums (ambient ≥0.5, background `#0a0a1a` not pure black), mandatory zoom buttons, procedural planet textures |\n| `procedural-skill-content/system.md` + `user.md` | Interactive widget #6 (vocational) — stateful step/consequence practice widget with stable `#step-N-control` selectors, `#feedback-panel`, `resetState()` |\n| `slide-actions/system.md` + `user.md` | Generates the teaching order over generated slide elements: `spotlight`/`laser`/`play_video`/`discussion` actions interleaved with teacher speech; strict same-session continuity rules, TTS-readability |\n| `quiz-actions/system.md` + `user.md` | 1–2 text-only teacher opening lines; answer-safety rules (never hint answers) |\n| `interactive-actions/system.md` + `user.md` | Teacher actions driving the widget iframe: `widget_highlight`, `widget_setState`, `widget_annotation`, `widget_reveal`, picking selectors from the **Element Inventory** |\n| `pbl-actions/system.md` + `user.md` | Speech introducing the PBL project, grounded in generated milestones How user topic/context is injected\n\n**Stage 1 (outline)** — `buildOutlinePrompt` (`outline-generator.ts` 82–117) + `requirements-to-outlines/user.md`:\n- `{{requirement}}` — the user's raw free-text topic (\"## User Requirements\").\n- `{{pdfContent}}` — upload text truncated to `MAX_PDF_CONTENT_CHARS = 50_000` chars.\n- `{{availableImages}}` — PDF-image descriptions/placeholders (vision slice ≤ `MAX_VISION_IMAGES = 20` images attached via `buildVisionUserContent`, interleaved text+images with dimensions: \"… (important for layout decisions)\").\n- `{{researchContext}}` — web-search results (\"reference specific findings and sources\").\n- `{{userProfile}}` — built inline (`outline-generator.ts` 89–92): `\"## Student Profile\\n\\nStudent: <nickname> — <bio>\\n\\nConsider this student's background when designing the course. IMPORTANT: The teacher's name and identity must NOT appear on the slides … Slides should read as neutral, professional visual aids.\"*\n- The model must infer and emit `languageDirective` (teaching-language rules) and `courseTitle`.\n\n**Stage 2a (scene content)** — important finding: the raw user requirement is **not** re-injected for slides.
