Scene types that exist\n\nFour scene **types** (`SceneOutline.type`, outline prompt: \"\\\"slide\\\" (presentation), \\\"quiz\\\" (assessment), \\\"interactive\\\" (interactive visualization), and \\\"pbl\\\" (project-based learning) are supported\"):\n\n1. **slide** — static PPTist-style canvas (elements above), spotlight/laser/play_video/discussion actions.\n2. **quiz** — single/multiple/short_answer questions with points + analysis.\n3. **interactive** — self-contained HTML in an iframe, with 6 widget types (`WidgetType`, `dsl/interactive.ts`): `simulation`, `diagram` (flowchart/mindmap/hierarchy/system), `code` (python/javascript/typescript/java/cpp), `game` (quiz/puzzle/strategy/card/action), `visualization3d` (molecular/solar/anatomy/geometry/physics/custom), `procedural-skill` (repair/assembly/inspection/operation/custom; gated by `allowProceduralSkill`).\n4. **pbl** — Project-Based Learning module (`PBLProject`: milestones/microtasks/one Instructor role; optional `scenarioRoleplay` role-play variant). Action generation covers all four (+ `INTERACTIVE_WIDGET_ACTIONS` whitelist).\n\nFallbacks (`applyOutlineFallbacks`): missing widget config → slide; missing pblConfig/languageModel → slide; procedural-skill disabled → diagram widget.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Where assets (images/videos) get generated\n\nTwo distinct asset channels:\n\n**A. Source (material/PDF) images** — extracted in `material-analysis`, stored as course assets (`materialImages()` in `engine.ts` 474–500: each image → `storeGeneratedAsset` → `assetId`, producing `imageMapping: {[img_N]: assetId}`); slides reference `img_N` Resolve `src` → asset id (server) or data URL (browser) in `resolveImageIds` (mapping value written verbatim — RFC #1153). Vision images are pre-resolved server-side (`ownerVisionImages`, `resolveOwnedAsset`) before prompt assembly, with a 20-image cap.\n\n**B. AI-generated media** — requested by the outline itself:\n1. Outline may emit `mediaGenerations: [{type:'image'|'video', prompt, elementId:'gen_img_*', aspectRatio, style}]` (snippets `image-instructions.md` / `video-instructions.md` include the media-safety-guidelines block). IDs are made globally unique by `uniquifyMediaElementIds` (`outline-media.ts`).\n2. Server: `mediaItemsOf` (`run/plan.ts`) collects requests; a **media lane** (`run/media.ts` `runMediaLane`) runs alongside scene generation. Per item: resolve image/video slot → `services.generateImage` → `generateImageStep` (`steps/image.ts`) → `generateImage` (`lib/media/image-providers.ts`, providers: seedream, openai-image, qwen-image, nano-banana, minimax, grok, glm, comfyui, lemonade, openrouter; the **prompt sent is exactly `request.prompt`** plus aspectRatio/style — no extra safety wrapper server-side) → bytes stored via `storeGeneratedAsset` (asset pool, with quotas; video posters stored too) → checkpoint `media:<elementId>`.\n3. Placement: after scene generation, `placeHeldMedia`/`placeMedia`/`placeIntoCurrentCourse` (`engine.ts` 1120–1366) find scenes carrying the `gen_img_*` placeholder (`sceneCarriesMediaReference`) and rewrite the element `src` to the stored `assetId`; unreferenced results are dropped as `MEDIA_ELEMENT_REMOVED`. Meanwhile the slide generator never invents URLs — `resolveImageIds` keeps placeholders so the \"frontend renders skeleton\" until placement.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Concrete answers to the specific ask re: slide design linkage\n\n- **Colors**: the LLM chooses hex colors freely per element/shape/chart (`fill`, `defaultColor`, `themeColors` in charts); the only sanctioned palettes are the worked examples in the prompt (`#5b9bd5` blue, `#ed7d31` orange, etc.) and the fixed `defaultTheme` minted by `buildCompleteScene`. There is **no user-context-driven color directive**: nothing maps the topic (or \"visual style\" inferred at outline time) into a palette or theme.\n- **Layout**: fully hand-computed absolute geometry (left/top/width/height in 1000×562.5 canvas, 50px margins, lookup-table heights, centering/symmetry formulas, spacing standards) — validated only by the model itself via the pre-output checklist, plus DSL `normalizeElement` + aspect-ratio reconciliation code.\n- **Animation**: none — the slide prompt contains zero animation guidance; `Slide.animations`/`turningMode` are never generated. Motion lives only in interactive HTML widgets (canvas animations, reveal steps) and AI-generated videos.\n- **Style tokens per course**: none exist; per-scene variation comes only from `teacherContext` persona-tone (visual neutrality enforced), language directive, and the outline's title/description/keyPoints wording.\n</task_result>\n</task>",

Here is the full report.\n\n# OpenMAIC TTS provider architecture — research report\n\n## 1. Where TTS providers live; the shared interface\n\nThere is **one** central implementation module (not per-provider files), plus a client-safe metadata registry:\n\n| Role | File |\n|---|---|\n| Type definitions (interfaces) | `/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/lib/audio/types.ts` |\n| Provider metadata registry (client-safe) + model/voice lists | `lib/audio/constants.ts` (`TTS_PROVIDERS`, `ASR_PROVIDERS`, `DEFAULT_TTS_VOICES`, `DEFAULT_TTS_MODELS`) |\n| Implementation factory (`generateTTS` switch) | `lib/audio/tts-providers.ts` |\n| Server env-key resolution / disables | `lib/server/provider-config.ts` (`TTS_ENV_MAP`, keys like `TTS_MINIMAX_API_KEY`) |\n| Slot resolution server-side | `lib/server/model-config/media.ts`, `lib/server/model-config/resolve-slot.ts` |\n| ASR (separate, same pattern) | `lib/audio/asr-providers.ts` |\n\nAll providers are **plain async functions**, not classes — they share no base class; the shared \"interface\" is a function contract `async function generateXxxTTS(config, text): Promise<TTSGenerationResult>` plus the shared registry config `TTSProviderConfig`. Verbatim from `lib/audio/tts-providers.ts` (lines 142–145, 294–359):\n\n```ts\n/** Result of TTS generation */\nexport interface TTSGenerationResult {\n  audio: Uint8Array;\n  format: string;\n}\n\nexport async function generateTTS(\n  config: TTSModelConfig,\n  text: string,\n): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n  const provider = TTS_PROVIDERS[config.providerId as keyof typeof TTS_PROVIDERS];\n\n  // Validate API key if required (only for built-in providers with known config)\n  if (provider?.requiresApiKey && !config.apiKey) {\n    throw new Error(`API key required for TTS provider: ${config.providerId}`);\n  }\n\n  const signal = ttsRequestSignal(config.signal);\n  try {\n    switch (config.providerId) {\n      case 'openai-tts':\n        return await generateOpenAITTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'azure-tts':\n        return await generateAzureTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'glm-tts':\n        return await generateGLMTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'qwen-tts':\n        return await generateQwenTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'voxcpm-tts':\n        return await generateVoxCPMTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'minimax-tts':\n        return await generateMiniMaxTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'doubao-tts':\n        return await generateDoubaoTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'elevenlabs-tts':\n        return await generateElevenLabsTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'google-tts':\n        return await generateGoogleTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'lemonade-tts':\n        return await generateLemonadeTTS(config, text, signal);\n      case 'browser-native-tts':\n        throw new Error(\n          'Browser Native TTS must be handled client-side using Web Speech API. This provider cannot be used on the server.',\n        );\n      default:\n        if (isCustomTTSProvider(config.providerId)) {\n          return await generateOpenAITTS(config, text, signal);\n        }\n        throw new Error(`Unsupported TTS provider: ${config.providerId}`);\n    }\n  } catch (error) { /* timeout/cancel normalization omitted */ }\n}\n```\n\nNote: `generateTTS` wraps every fetch through `ttsFetch(...)` → `audioProviderFetch(url, init, audioEndpointPolicy(target))` (SSRF-pinned-DNS transport, `lib/server/audio-provider-fetch.ts`), with a combined cancel+timeout abort signal (`TTS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 30 s).\n\nThe per-call config interface, verbatim from `lib/audio/types.ts` (lines 159–191):\n\n```ts\nexport interface TTSModelConfig {\n  providerId: TTSProviderId;\n  modelId?: string;\n  apiKey?: string;\n  baseUrl?: string;\n  voice: string;\n  speed?: number;\n  format?: string;\n  providerOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  signal?: AbortSignal;\n  publicOnly?: boolean;\n  managed?: boolean;\n}\n```\n\nAnd the provider registry entry interface (`TTSProviderConfig`, types.ts lines 115–154) — this is where voices/models/speed live:\n\n```ts\nexport interface TTSProviderConfig {\n  id: TTSProviderId;\n  name: string;\n  requiresApiKey: boolean;\n  defaultBaseUrl?: string;\n  icon?: string;\n  excludeFromAgentVoiceCatalog?: boolean;\n  requiresRegisteredVoice?: boolean;\n  /** Available models. Empty array means provider has no model concept (e.g. Azure, Browser Native). */\n  models: Array<{ id: string; name: string }>;\n  defaultModelId: string;\n  voices: TTSVoiceInfo[];\n  supportedFormats: string[]; // ['mp3', 'wav', 'opus', etc.]\n  speedRange?: { min: number; max: number; default: number };\n  supportsSpeed?: boolean;\n}\n```\n\nRelevant today: the doc header of `lib/audio/types.ts` (lines 22–29) explicitly lists Fish Audio as a future provider — *\"Future Provider Support (extensible): … Fish Audio TTS (https://fish.audio/docs)\"*. All other hits for \"fish\" are unrelated (a Qwen voice named `Nofish`).\n\nProvider IDs are a string-union type (types.ts lines 83–96):\n\n```ts\nexport type BuiltInTTSProviderId =\n  | 'openai-tts' | 'azure-tts' | 'glm-tts' | 'qwen-tts' | 'voxcpm-tts'\n  | 'doubao-tts' | 'elevenlabs-tts' | 'minimax-tts' | 'google-tts'\n  | 'lemonade-tts' | 'browser-native-tts';\n\nexport type TTSProviderId = BuiltInTTSProviderId | `custom-tts-${string}`;\n```\n\n## 2. Registration: exact files + functions a new provider must touch\n\nPer the \"HOW TO ADD A NEW PROVIDER\" doc comments in both `lib/audio/types.ts` and `lib/audio/tts-providers.ts` (verbatim, 5 steps):\n\n1. **`lib/audio/types.ts`** — add `'fish-tts'` to `BuiltInTTSProviderId`.\n2. **`lib/audio/constants.ts`** — add an entry to `export const TTS_PROVIDERS: Record<BuiltInTTSProviderId, TTSProviderConfig>` (line 133) — this supplies name, requiresApiKey, defaultBaseUrl, icon, `models`, `defaultModelId`, `voices`, `supportedFormats`, `speedRange`. Also add entries to `DEFAULT_TTS_VOICES` (line 1543) and `DEFAULT_TTS_MODELS` (line 1557).\n3. **`lib/audio/tts-providers.ts`** — implement `generateFishAudioTTS(config, text, signal)` and add `case 'fish-tts': return await generateFishAudioTTS(config, text, signal);` inside `generateTTS`'s switch (line ~307).\n4. **`lib/i18n`** — add `providerFishTTS` to the TTS name-key map in `lib/audio/provider-display.ts` (`TTS_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS`, lines 25–37) plus locale strings in `lib/i18n/locales/*.json` (all locales carry these keys, e.g. en-US.json line 1432 `\"providerMiniMaxTTS\": \"MiniMax TTS\"`).\n5. **`lib/server/provider-config.ts`** — add `TTS_FISH: 'fish-tts'` to `TTS_ENV_MAP` (lines 99–110) so server env keys (`TTS_FISH_API_KEY`, `TTS_FISH_MODELS`, `TTS_FISH_BASE_URL`) resolve and the `<CAP>_<VENDOR>_ENABLED=false` force-off switch works (DISNABLE_ENV_MAPS line 182 pipes from the same map).\n6. **`components/settings/tts-settings.tsx`** — add the request-URL hint path to `ttsEndpointPath(providerId)` (lines 99–118), otherwise the endpoint hint shows nothing.\n7. **Presto automatic**: provider presets are *generated from the registries* — put the entry in `TTS_PROVIDERS` and a single-capability preset (`fish-tts`) appears for free in `lib/config/provider-presets.ts` → `singlePresets()`. Test `tests/config/provider-presets.test.ts` verifies *every* registry entry is served by a preset.\n\n## 3. How TTS is called: route → narration → provider\n\nAPI route: **`app/api/generate/tts/route.ts`** (`POST`). Verbatim flow (lines 57–131, abridged to the key lines):\n\n```ts\nexport async function POST(req: NextRequest) {\n  const trace: { providerId?: string; voice?: string } = {};\n  let audioId: string | undefined;\n  try {\n    const body = await req.json();\n    const { text, ttsModelId, ttsSpeed, ttsApiKey, ttsBaseUrl, ttsProviderOptions } = body as {\n      text: string;\n      audioId: string;\n      ttsProviderId: TTSProviderId;\n      ttsModelId?: string;\n      ttsVoice: string;\n      ttsSpeed?: number;\n      ttsApiKey?: string;\n      ttsBaseUrl?: string;\n      ttsProviderOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;\n    };\n    ...\n    // The tts slot decides; the provider, key and base URL a request names\n    // (deprecated) count only when it is unassigned.\n    // A settings preview names a saved provider instead (`previewProvider`).\n    let connection: MediaConnection;\n    try {\n      const preview = savedProviderRef(body.previewProvider, body.previewModel);\n      connection = preview\n        ? await savedMediaConnection(req, 'tts', preview)\n        : await resolveMediaSlot('tts', {\n            workspaceId: await requestWorkspaceId(req),\n            legacyRequest: async () => requestedProviderId ? ... : undefined,\n          });\n    } ...\n    const narration = await synthesizeNarration({ text, audioId, connection, requestedProviderId,\n      requestedVoice, requestedModelId: ttsModelId, speed: ttsSpeed,\n      providerOptions: ttsProviderOptions, trace }, { log });\n\n    // Convert to base64\n    const base64 = Buffer.from(narration.audio).toString('base64');\n\n    return apiSuccess({ audioId, base64, format: narration.format });\n  }\n```\n\n**Response shape to clients: JSON `{ success, base64: string, format: string }` — base64, not streaming, not binary.**\n\nSlot resolution lives in `lib/server/model-config/media.ts` → `resolveMediaSlot('tts', ...)` → `MediaConnection { providerId (registry id e.g. 'minimax-tts'), modelId?, apiKey?, baseUrl?, options?, managed, userEndpoint, origin }`.\n\nNarration step: **`lib/server/generation/steps/narration.ts`** (`synthesizeNarration`, lines 52–165). Key excerpt:\n\n```ts\n  const config = {\n    providerId: ttsProviderId as TTSProviderId,\n    modelId: resolvedModelId,\n    voice: ttsVoice,\n    speed: qwenCloneVoice ? 1 : requestedSpeed,\n    apiKey: apiKey ?? '',\n    baseUrl,\n    publicOnly,\n    managed,\n    signal: ctx.signal,\n    providerOptions: {\n      ...adapterOptions(connection, ttsProviderOptions),\n      ...(qwenCloneVoice ? { qwenVoiceClone: true } : {}),\n    },\n  };\n  authorizeMediaModel(connection, 'tts', config.modelId);\n  const { audio, format } = await generateTTS(config, text);\n  void recordGenerationUsage({ kind: 'tts', unit: 'character', providerId: ttsProviderId,\n    modelId: config.modelId, quantity: text.length });\n  return { audio, format, providerId: ttsProviderId, modelId: config.modelId };\n```\n\nSecond server path (classroom generation jobs): `lib/server/agent-runtime/scene-tts.ts` → `synthesizeSceneNarration()` calls `generateTTS` directly with `serverMediaConnection('tts', ownerId)` and writes bytes via `persistClassroomMediaBytes` to the classroom media store; mime helper there:\n\n```ts\nfunction audioMime(format: string) {\n  return format === 'wav' ? 'audio/wav' : format === 'ogg' ? 'audio/ogg' : 'audio/mpeg';\n}\n```\n\n## 4. One complete simple TTS provider — MiniMax (verbatim)\n\nConstants registry entry, `lib/audio/constants.ts` lines 724–802 (edited excerpt; `MINIMAX_TTS_MODELS` const is lines 73–80):\n\n```ts\nexport const MINIMAX_TTS_MODELS = [\n  { id: 'speech-2.8-hd', name: 'Speech 2.8 HD' },\n  { id: 'speech-2.8-turbo', name: 'Speech 2.8 Turbo' },\n  { id: 'speech-2.6-hd', name: 'Speech 2.6 HD' },\n  { id: 'speech-2.6-turbo', name: 'Speech 2.6 Turbo' },\n  { id: 'speech-02-hd', name: 'Speech 02 HD' },\n  { id: 'speech-02-turbo', name: 'Speech 02 Turbo' },\n] as const;\n\n'minimax-tts': {\n  id: 'minimax-tts',\n  name: 'MiniMax TTS',\n  requiresApiKey: true,\n  defaultBaseUrl: 'https://api.minimaxi.com',\n  icon: '/logos/minimax.svg',\n  models: MINIMAX_TTS_MODELS.map((m) => ({ id: m.id, name: m.name })),\n  defaultModelId: 'speech-2.8-hd',\n  voices: [\n    { id: 'female-yujie', name: '御姐音色', language: 'zh-CN', gender: 'female' },\n    { id: 'male-qn-jingying', name: '精英青年', language: 'zh-CN', gender: 'male' },\n    ... // more voices; English ones like { id: 'English_Trustworthy_Man', ... }\n  ],\n  supportedFormats: ['mp3', 'wav', 'flac', 'pcm'],\n  speedRange: { min: 0.5, max: 2.0, default: 1.0 },\n},\n```\n\nImplementation, `lib/audio/tts-providers.ts` lines 1125–1197 (rate-limit helpers omitted):\n\n```ts\nasync function generateMiniMaxTTS(\n  config: TTSModelConfig,\n  text: string,\n  signal: AbortSignal,\n): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n  const baseUrl = (config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['minimax-tts'].defaultBaseUrl || '').replace(\n    /\\/$/,\n    '',\n  );\n  const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/v1/t2a_v2`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: {\n      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`,\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',\n      ...appAttributionHeaders(baseUrl),\n    },\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      model: config.modelId || 'speech-2.8-hd',\n      text,\n      stream: false,\n      output_format: 'hex',\n      voice_setting: {\n        voice_id: config.voice,\n        speed: config.speed || 1.0,\n        vol: 1,\n        pitch: 0,\n      },\n      audio_setting: {\n        sample_rate: 32000,\n        bitrate: 128000,\n        format: config.format || 'mp3',\n        channel: 1,\n      },\n      language_boost: 'auto',\n    }),\n    signal,\n  });\n\n  if (!response.ok) { /* rate-limit & quota handling -> throwIfTtsRateLimited / ProviderQuotaExhaustedError */ }\n\n  const data = await response.json();\n  throwIfMiniMaxBaseRespFailed(data, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n  const hexAudio = data?.data?.audio;\n  if (!hexAudio || typeof hexAudio !== 'string') {\n    throw new Error(`MiniMax TTS error: No audio returned. Response: ${JSON.stringify(data)}`);\n  }\n\n  const cleanedHex = hexAudio.trim();\n  if (cleanedHex.length % 2 !== 0) {\n    throw new Error('MiniMax TTS error: invalid hex audio payload length');\n  }\n\n  const audio = new Uint8Array(\n    cleanedHex.match(/.{1,2}/g)?.map((byte: string) => parseInt(byte, 16)) || [],\n  );\n  return {\n    audio,\n    format: data?.extra_info?.audio_format || config.format || 'mp3',\n  };\n}\n```\n\nA more typical binary-returning example is `generateOpenAITTS` (lines 364–406) — POST `${baseUrl}/audio/speech`, request `response_format: 'mp3'`, then `return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'OpenAI')`. The shared `validateTTSAudioResponse` (lines 550–626) decodes `arrayBuffer`, rejects HTML/JSON/text/empty bodies with `TTSInvalidResponseError`, and maps `Content-Type` → format via `getAudioResponseFormat` (wav/mp3/flac/ogg/webm/aac/opus).\n\nNotable other implementations: Doubao (`generateDoubaoTTS`, concatenated JSON stream parsed with `splitConcatenatedJsonObjects`, base64 chunks merged), Google (`generateGoogleTTS`, L16 PCM base64 wrapped into WAV via `pcmS16leMonoToWav`), ElevenLabs (`voice` in the URL path), Azure (SSML POST), Qwen (JSON → audio URL → `downloadAudio`).\n\n## 5. Provider presets — the exact files\n\n- **Token plans (a key covering several modalities):** `/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/lib/config/token-plan-presets.ts` — `TOKEN_PLAN_PRESETS`. The **`minimax` preset with its TTS models is verbatim at lines 162–211**:\n  ```ts\n  {\n    id: 'minimax',\n    name: 'MiniMax',\n    websiteUrl: 'https://platform.minimaxi.com',\n    apiKeyPlaceholder: 'sk-...',\n    icon: '/logos/minimax.svg',\n    category: 'token_plan',\n    modalities: {\n      llm: { providerId: 'minimax', baseUrl: 'https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1', apiFormat: 'anthropic', defaultModels: [...'MiniMax-M2'] },\n      image: { providerId: 'minimax-image', baseUrl: 'https://api.minimaxi.com', defaultModels: ['image-01', 'image-01-live'] },\n      video: { providerId: 'minimax-video', baseUrl: 'https://api.minimaxi.com', defaultModels: [...] },\n      tts: {\n        providerId: 'minimax-tts',\n        baseUrl: 'https://api.minimaxi.com',\n        defaultModelId: 'speech-2.8-turbo',\n        defaultModels: ['speech-2.8-hd','speech-2.8-turbo','speech-2.6-hd','speech-2.6-turbo','speech-02-hd','speech-02-turbo'],\n      },\n      webSearch: { providerId: 'minimax', baseUrl: 'https://api.minimaxi.com' },\n    },\n  },\n  ```\n- **Single-capability presets are auto-derived** from each registry entry in `lib/config/provider-presets.ts` (`REGISTRIES` map line 83 links `tts: TTS_PROVIDERS`; `singlePresets()` lines 114–143; `PROVIDER_PRESETS = buildPresets()` line 185). There is **no hand-written \"minimax-tts single preset\"** — it is generated with `id: presetIdFor('tts','minimax-tts')` → `'minimax-tts'`.\n- **Preset id overrides / collisions:** `lib/config/preset-ids.ts` (`PRESET_ID_OVERRIDES` — e.g. webSearch `minimax → 'minimax-search'`).\n- Deployment-side config example: `openmaic.example.yml` — providers are `preset: minimax` / `apiKey: ${MINIMAX_API_KEY}` and slots like `# tts: minimax:speech-2.8-turbo`.\n- Env example: `.env.example` lines 190–191 `TTS_MINIMAX_API_KEY=`, `TTS_MINIMAX_MODELS=` (+ `TTS_MINIMAX_BASE_URL=`).\n\nSettings-read side: `lib/server/model-config/settings.ts` builds `ModelSettingsView` (`/api/model-config` route is `app/api/model-config/route.ts`), and `registryModels('tts', registryId)` in provider-presets.ts returns each registry entry's `models` to the UI.\n\n## 6. The \"provider models\" settings UI + voice selection\n\nSettings dialog root: **`components/settings/index.tsx`** — sections `token-plan` / `model-services` / `course-models`. The \"Model Services\" section is **`components/settings/model-services.tsx`** (`ModelServicesPanel`): tab list `providers|image|video|tts|asr|pdf|web-search` (`SERVICE_TABS`, tab `tts` ↔ capability `tts` in `TAB_CAPABILITY`), provider list on the left (`components/settings/provider-list.tsx`), and per-entry panels dispatched at lines 297–303:\n\n```tsx\n{tab === 'providers' && <ProviderConfigPanel {...panelProps} />}\n{tab === 'image'    && <ImageSettings {...panelProps} />}\n{tab === 'video'    && <VideoSettings {...panelProps} />}\n{tab === 'tts'      && <TTSSettings {...panelProps} />}\n{tab === 'asr'      && <ASRSettings {...panelProps} />}\n...\n```\n\n**TTS panel: `components/settings/tts-settings.tsx`** (`TTSSettings`, `ServicePanelProps { view, apply, entry }`). It shows: API key field (`ApiKeyField` from `components/settings/server-settings.tsx`, keys are write-only to the server), base URL + request-URL hint via `ttsEndpointPath`, the speed control (`TTSSpeedField`, `supportsSpeed: false` locks it), a server-driven \"Test TTS\" (`useTTSPreview` with `previewProvider: entry.id`), and an **\"Available Models\" read-only list** rendered from `getManuallySelectableTTSModels(providerId)` (a badge+dot list, no radios — the model is effectively decided by voice choice; for Qwen the text is `{t('settings.modelSelectedViaVoice')}`):\n\n```tsx\n{/* Available Models */}\n{manuallySelectableModels.length > 0 && !isVoxCPM && (\n  <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n    <Label className=\"text-sm text-muted-foreground\">{t('settings.availableModels')}</Label>\n    <div className=\"flex flex-wrap gap-2\">\n      {manuallySelectableModels.map((model) => (... {model.name} ...))}\n    </div>\n    <p className=\"text-[11px] text-muted-foreground/60\">\n      {t('settings.modelSelectedViaVoice')}\n    </p>\n  </div>\n)}\n{/* The voices a user makes: for the workspace's narration service. */}\n{isVoxCPM && use.inUse && <VoxCPMVoiceManager />}\n{providerId === 'qwen-tts' && use.inUse && <QwenVoiceCloneManager />}\n```\n\nService naming/icons per capability come from `components/settings/service-display.tsx` → `service-display.ts` `REGISTRY_INFO.tts = { ids: Object.keys(TTS_PROVIDERS), name: resolveTTSProviderName, icon: entry.icon, requiresApiKey }` — again, derived from the registry, so Fish Audio appears automatically once registered (plus its i18n key in `lib/audio/provider-display.ts`).\n\n**Where a voice is actually picked:** the classroom/agent \"Teacher voice pill\" — `components/agent/agent-bar.tsx` (`TeacherVoicePill` and per-agent pills; excerpt lines 528–563):\n\n```tsx\n{group.voices.map((voice) => {\n  const isActive = ttsProviderId === provider.providerId && ttsVoice === voice.id;\n  ...\n  <button type=\"button\" onClick={() => {\n      setTTSVoice(voice.id, provider.providerId);\n      setPopoverOpen(false);\n  }}>\n      {voice.id === VOXCPM_AUTO_VOICE_ID ? t('settings.voxcpmAutoVoice') : voice.name}\n  </button>\n  {canPreview && <button onClick={() => handlePreview(provider.providerId, voice.id, group.modelId)}>...}\n```\n\n- Persisted globally in `lib/store/settings.ts`: `ttsVoice`, `ttsVoiceProviderId`, `ttsSpeed` via `setTTSVoice(voice, providerId)` (line 257). Per-agent overrides: `setAgentVoiceOverride(agent.id, { providerId, modelId, voiceId })`.\n- Voice/model grouping source: `lib/audio/voice-resolver.ts` → `getEnabledProvidersWithVoices(ttsProvidersConfig, voiceProfiles)` builds `ProviderWithVoices { providerId, providerName, voices: [{id,name,language}], modelGroups: [{ modelId, modelName, voices[] }] }` — a provider with `models: []` yields one group of all voices; with models, voices are grouped and filtered by `compatibleModels` (`voiceServesModel`, constants.ts line 125).\n- Selection glue: `lib/audio/tts-selection.ts` (`ttsSelection(capabilities, preference)`; `slotTTSProviderConfig` from the `tts` slot's `EffectiveTarget` server view) and hook `lib/audio/use-tts-selection.ts` (`useTTSSelection()`); per-agent/per-provider option assembly is `lib/audio/agent-voice.ts` → `resolveAgentVoiceOptions(agent, { providerId, providerConfig, voiceId, language })` producing `ttsProviderOptions` sent to the route (e.g. VoxCPM `voicePrompt`, `registeredVoiceId`, `referenceAudioBase64`).\n\n**\"Voice ID by free-text entry\" — existing patterns to copy:**\n- Custom `custom-tts-*` providers carry arbitrary user voices: `TTSProvidersConfig[id].customVoices: Array<{ id, name }>` consumed by `getServerVoiceList` / `findVoiceDisplayName` / `getEnabledProvidersWithVoices` in `lib/audio/voice-resolver.ts`, and entries in `provider-registry`.\n- Server-managed dynamic voice list route exists: **`app/api/azure-voices/route.ts`** — POST `{ apiKey, baseUrl }` → upstream list → `apiSuccess({ voices })` (a precedent if Fish Audio should fetch its voice bank instead of a static list).\n- User-created voice managers: `components/settings/tts-voice-managers.tsx` (`VoxCPMVoiceManager`, `QwenVoiceCloneManager` shown only when the workspace's tts slot uses them, per `lib/model-settings/shape.ts` `USER_VOICE_SERVICES = ['voxcpm-tts', 'qwen-tts']` and `narrationVoicesManageable`).\n- Per-provider non-secret options channel: `providerOptions` in openmaic.yml (`providerOptionsSchema`, `lib/server/model-config/openmaic-yml.ts` lines 105–114) merged with per-request voice options by `adapterOptions()` (`lib/server/model-config/adapter-options.ts`; configured provider wins over request, deprecated path vice versa).\n\n## 7. Validation schemas (zod / JSON)\n\n- **openmaic.yml provider schema** — `lib/server/model-config/openmaic-yml.ts` (verbatim lines 118–135):\n  ```ts\n  export const providerSchema = z\n    .object({\n      preset: z.string().min(1),\n      apiKey: z.string().min(1).optional(),\n      baseUrl: z.url().optional(),\n      models: z.array(z.string().trim().min(1)).min(1).optional(),\n      proxy: z.url().optional(),\n      credentials: z.record(z.string().min(1), z.string().min(1)).optional(),\n      options: providerOptionsSchema.optional(),\n    })\n    .strict();\n  ```\n  plus `providerOptionsSchema` (lines 105–114: name regex, credential-sounding names refused, scalar values) and `fileSchema` (providers/slots/lock/allowUserKeys). Slot assignments: `assignmentSchema` → `null | \"providerId:modelId\" | { model, thinking?, fallback?, api?, contextWindow? }`.\n- **Workspace settings import** — `lib/server/model-config/settings.ts` `importedProviderSchema` (lines 840–847: `preset/apiKey/baseUrl/models`), used by `importModelSettings` (line 887) backed by `applyModelSettingsChange`.\n- **Route request body shape** of `/api/generate/tts` is checked by hand (`req.json()` destructure + `apiError('MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD', 400, ...)`), not zod.\n- Agent-facing voice binding validation uses `TTS_PROVIDERS` catalogs via `buildVoiceCatalog` (`lib/audio/voice-catalog.ts`) for `list_voices`/`set_roster` (`providerId::voiceId` bindings), honoring `excludeFromAgentVoiceCatalog` / `requiresRegisteredVoice`.\n\n## 8. Audio playback consumption (format/mime/streaming?)\n\n- **Transport**: `/api/generate/tts` returns **base64 in JSON** (`{ base64, format }`), NOT streaming/binary. Every provider call inside `generateTTS` completes its whole buffer before returning `Uint8Array` — there is no player-facing streaming (Doubao internally \"streams\" JSON chunks but they're concatenated server-side first).\n- **Client → blob**: `lib/audio/narration-tts.ts` `generateAndStoreTTS()` — `atob(data.base64)` → `Uint8Array` → `new Blob([bytes], { type: `audio/${data.format}` })` → stored in the asset pool/db via `commitToPool` (blob, mimeType, duration from `measureAudioDuration`, `lib/audio/audio-duration.ts` which sniffs magic bytes and parses WAV/MP3).\n- **Playback engine**: `lib/playback/engine.ts` uses `lib/utils/audio-player.ts` — `play(audioId)` → `resolveBytes(audioId)` → `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` → a single reused `HTMLAudioElement` (mobile autoplay policy), with legacy `audioUrl` fetch fallback.\n- **Previews** (`lib/audio/use-tts-preview.ts`, `agent-bar.tsx`): either `new Audio(`data:audio/${data.format};base64,${body.base64}`)` or Blob→ObjectURL.\n- **Server-generated classroom narration**: `persistClassroomMediaBytes` → served by `app/api/classroom-media/[classroomId]/[...path]/route.ts`; mime table in `lib/server/classroom-storage.ts` `CLASSROOM_MEDIA_MIME_TYPES` (`.mp3: audio/mpeg`, `.wav`, `.ogg`, `.aac`, `.flac`, `.m4a`, `.opus: audio/ogg`).\n- **Renderer**: `packages/@openmaic/renderer/src/elements/audio/BaseAudioElement.tsx` plays `<audio>` assets; `configs/mime.ts` `MIME_MAP` maps audio/video mime→extension. Video export relies on pre-measured durations (WAV/MP3 parsers only in `lib/audio/audio-duration.ts` — anything else degrades to \"no duration\").\n- Because of this, Fish Audio should return **mp3 (or wav)** — the browser-playable formats everything above assumes.\n\n## 9. Other call sites to keep in mind when adding Fish Audio\n\n- Server: `lib/server/provider-config.ts` (`resolveTTSApiKey/resolveTTSBaseUrl/resolveTTSModel/slotTTSModel`, `getServerTTSProviders` draining `enabledServerTTSProviderIds`), `lib/server/model-config/media.ts` (`FORCE_OFF_SECTION.tts`), `lib/server/model-config/legacy-config.ts` (imports legacy server TTS section), `lib/server/generation-capabilities.ts` (probe), `lib/server/generation/steps/agent-profiles.ts` (narrator pin uses global voice).\n- Client: `lib/audio/provider-enablement.ts` (`isTTSProviderEnabled`), `lib/audio/voice-resolver.ts` (picker lists + fallback), `lib/audio/voice-catalog.ts` (agent tools), `lib/hooks/use-discussion-tts.ts` (discussion lines → `data:audio/${format};base64,<…>`), `lib/hooks/use-browser-tts.ts` (browser only), `app/api/generate-classroom/*` capabilities route.\n- i18n: add `providerFishTTS` (etc.) to `lib/i18n/locales/*.json` for every locale file present (en-US, zh-CN, zh-TW, de-DE, vi-VN, ar-SA, ru-RU, pt-BR, es-MX, ko-KR …).\n- Icon: put `public/logos/fish-audio.svg` and reference `'icon: /logos/fish-audio.svg'`.\n\n**Contextual note (external knowledge, not from this repo):** fish.audio's REST TTS endpoint is `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and a JSON body `{ text, reference_id, format: 'mp3'|'wav'|'opus', mp3_bitrate, chunk_length, normalize, latency }` — `reference_id` is the voice ID (exactly matching the app's `config.voice` and the free-text-voice-ID requirement), and the response is binary audio (mp3 default), so `validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'Fish Audio', 'mp3')` is the natural fit.\n</task_result>\n</task>",

Extract from requirement text: topic, target audience, duration, style, etc.\n12: 2. Make reasonable default assumptions when information is insufficient\n13: 3. Generate structured outlines to prepare for subsequent teaching action generation\n14: \n15: ---\n16: \n17: ## Language Inference\n18: \n19: Infer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n20: \n21: 1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n22: 2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n23: \n24: ### Decision rules (apply in order)\n25: \n26: 1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n27: \n28: 2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n29: \n30: 3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n31:    - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n32:    - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n33:    - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n34: \n35: 4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n36: \n37: 5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n38: \n39: 6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n40: \n41: ### Terminology\n42: \n43: - **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n44: - **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n45: - **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n46: - **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n47: \n48: ### Course Title\n49: \n50: Produce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n51: \n52: - **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n53: - **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n54: - **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动入门\", \"Intro to Recursion\", \"光合作用原理\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n55: - **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n56: - If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n57: \n58: ---\n59: \n60: ## Design Principles\n61: \n62: ### MAIC Platform Technical Constraints\n63: \n64: - **Scene Types**: `slide` (presentation), `quiz` (assessment), `interactive` (interactive visualization), and `pbl` (project-based learning) are supported\n65: - **Slide Scene**: Static PPT pages supporting text, charts, formulas, and other visual components.\n66: - **Quiz Scene**: Supports single-choice, multiple-choice, and short-answer (text) questions\n67: - **Interactive Scene**: Self-contained interactive HTML page rendered in an iframe, ideal for simulations and visualizations\n68: - **PBL Scene**: Complete project-based learning module with roles, issues, and collaboration workflow. Ideal for complex projects, engineering practice, and research tasks\n69: - **Duration Control**: Each scene should be 1-3 minutes (PBL scenes are longer, typically 15-30 minutes)\n70: \n71: ### Instructional Design Principles\n72: \n73: - **Clear Purpose**: Each scene has a clear teaching function\n74: - **Logical Flow**: Scenes form a natural teaching progression\n75: - **Experience Design**: Consider learning experience and emotional response from the student's perspective\n76: \n77: ---\n78: \n79: ## Default Assumption Rules\n80: \n81: When user requirements don't specify, use these defaults:\n82: \n83: | Information         | Default Value          |\n84: | ------------------- | ---------------------- |\n85: | Course Duration     | 15-20 minutes          |\n86: | Target Audience     | General learners       |\n87: | Teaching Style      | Interactive (engaging) |\n88: | Visual Style        | Professional           |\n89: | Interactivity Level | Medium                 |\n90: \n91: ---\n92: \n93: ## Special Element Design Guidelines\n94: \n95: ### Chart Elements\n96: \n97: When content needs visualization, specify chart requirements in keyPoints:\n98: \n99: - **Chart Types**: bar, line, pie, radar\n100: - **Data Description**: Briefly describe data content and display purpose\n101: \n102: Example keyPoints:\n103: \n104: ```\n105: \"keyPoints\": [\n106:   \"Show sales growth trend over four years\",\n107:   \"[Chart] Line chart: X-axis years (2020-2023), Y-axis sales (1.2M-2.1M)\",\n108:   \"Analyze growth factors and key milestones\"\n109: ]\n110: ```\n111: \n112: ### Table Elements\n113: \n114: When comparing or listing information, specify in keyPoints:\n115: \n116: ```\n117: \"keyPoints\": [\n118:   \"Compare core metrics of three products\",\n119:   \"[Table] Product A/B/C comparison: price, performance, use cases\",\n120:   \"Help students understand product positioning\"\n121: ]\n122: ```\n123: \n124: {{#if imageEnabled}}\n125: {{snippet:image-instructions}}\n126: {{/if}}\n127: \n128: {{#if videoEnabled}}\n129: {{snippet:video-instructions}}\n130: {{/if}}\n131: \n132: {{#if mediaEnabled}}\n133: {{snippet:media-safety-guidelines}}\n134: {{/if}}\n135: \n136: ### Interactive Scene Guidelines\n137: \n138: Use `interactive` type when a concept benefits significantly from hands-on interaction and visualization. Good candidates include:\n139: \n140: - **Physics simulations**: Force composition, projectile motion, wave interference, circuits\n141: - **Math visualizations**: Function graphing, geometric transformations, probability distributions\n142: - **Data exploration**: Interactive charts, statistical sampling, regression fitting\n143: - **Chemistry**: Molecular structure, reaction balancing, pH titration\n144: - **Programming concepts**: Algorithm visualization, data structure operations\n145: \n146: **Constraints**:\n147: \n148: - Limit to **1-2 interactive scenes per course** (they are resource-intensive)\n149: - Interactive scenes **require** an `interactiveConfig` object\n150: - Do NOT use interactive for purely textual/conceptual content - use slides instead\n151: - The `interactiveConfig.designIdea` should describe the specific interactive elements and user interactions\n152: \n153: ### Widget Type Selection for Interactive Scenes\n154: \n155: When generating an interactive scene, you MUST select the appropriate widget type and provide widgetOutline:\n156: \n157: **Selection Logic:**\n158: \n159: | Concept Characteristics | Widget Type | widgetOutline Fields |\n160: |-------------------------|-------------|---------------------|\n161: | Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters | `simulation` | `concept`, `keyVariables` |\n162: | Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains | `diagram` | `diagramType` |\n163: | Programming concepts, algorithms | `code` | `language` |\n164: | Practice activities, gamified assessment | `game` | `gameType`, `challenge` |\n165: | Biological/geometric structures, 3D models | `visualization3d` | `visualizationType`, `objects` |\n166: \n167: **widgetOutline Format by Type:**\n168: \n169: ```json\n170: // simulation\n171: \"widgetOutline\": {\n172:   \"concept\": \"concept_name\",\n173:   \"keyVariables\": [\"variable1\", \"variable2\"]\n174: }\n175: \n176: // diagram\n177: \"widgetOutline\": {\n178:   \"diagramType\": \"flowchart\"\n179: }\n180: \n181: // code\n182: \"widgetOutline\": {\n183:   \"language\": \"python\"\n184: }\n185: \n186: // game\n187: \"widgetOutline\": {\n188:   \"gameType\": \"action\",\n189:   \"challenge\": \"description of what player controls\"\n190: }\n191: \n192: // visualization3d\n193: \"widgetOutline\": {\n194:   \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n195:   \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"mars\"]\n196: }\n197: ```\n198: \n199: **CRITICAL:** Every interactive scene MUST include both `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` fields. Interactive scenes without these are INVALID.\n200: \n201: ### PBL Scene Guidelines\n202: \n203: Use `pbl` type when the course involves complex, multi-step project work that benefits from structured collaboration. Good candidates include:\n204: \n205: - **Engineering projects**: Software development, hardware design, system architecture\n206: - **Research projects**: Scientific research, data analysis, literature review\n207: - **Design projects**: Product design, UX research, creative projects\n208: - **Business projects**: Business plans, market analysis, strategy development\n209: \n210: **Constraints**:\n211: \n212: - Limit to **at most 1 PBL scene per course** (they are comprehensive and long)\n213: - PBL scenes **require** a `pblConfig` object with: projectTopic, projectDescription, targetSkills, issueCount\n214: - PBL is for substantial project work - do NOT use for simple exercises or single-step tasks\n215: - The `pblConfig.targetSkills` should list 2-5 specific skills students will develop\n216: - The `pblConfig.issueCount` should typically be 2-5 issues\n217: \n218: **Role-play scenario PBL (optional PBL sub-type)**:\n219: \n220: Some PBL projects are best learned by *practising an interpersonal or situational interaction* rather than by building an artefact — for example practising a difficult conversation, a negotiation, a job interview, a customer-service exchange, a debate, a role-play game (e.g. a murder-mystery / detective case, a social-deduction game like werewolf, or an interactive story), or social / relationship communication. When the core of the learning really is the interaction itself (the learner will converse with one or more in-character roles inside an immersive scene), additionally set inside `pblConfig`:\n221: \n222: - `scenarioRoleplay: true` — marks this PBL as a role-play scenario.\n223: - `scenarioBrief` (optional string) — a short hint about the situation and who the character(s) are, to steer the later design step.\n224: \n225: Leave **both unset** for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects (this is the default). Only use `scenarioRoleplay` when the practice of the interaction is the point. This does not change how you choose the scene `type` — it is still `pbl`; these two fields are an optional flavour *inside* a PBL scene.\n226: \n227: **Important:** `pblConfig.scenarioRoleplay` is the downstream runtime switch. If the user explicitly asks for a role-play / scenario-simulation PBL, do not return an ordinary PBL; set `scenarioRoleplay: true` and include a concrete `scenarioBrief`.\n228: \n229: ---\n230: \n231: ## Output Format\n232: \n233: ### Top-level shape — NON-NEGOTIABLE\n234: \n235: Your entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these three top-level keys:\n236: \n237: ```json\n238: {\n239:   \"languageDirective\": \"<the directive you inferred in the Language Inference step>\",\n240:   \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n241:   \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects */ ]\n242: }\n243: ```\n244: \n245: Rules:\n246: \n247: - **Never** return a bare array. The top level is an object, not an array.\n248: - **Never** omit `languageDirective` or `courseTitle`. Both are required even if you think they are obvious.\n249: - **Never** wrap the response in any other structure, prose, or code fence.\n250: \n251: ### Minimal complete example\n252: \n253: ```json\n254: {\n255:   \"languageDirective\": \"Deliver the entire course in English. Use simple vocabulary suitable for a beginner.\",\n256:   \"courseTitle\": \"Intro to Projectile Motion\",\n257:   \"outlines\": [\n258:     {\n259:       \"id\": \"scene_1\",\n260:       \"type\": \"slide\",\n261:       \"title\": \"Introduction\",\n262:       \"description\": \"Welcome students and introduce the core concept.\",\n263:       \"keyPoints\": [\"Context\", \"Agenda\", \"Goals\"],\n264:       \"order\": 1\n265:     },\n266:     {\n267:       \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n268:       \"type\": \"interactive\",\n269:       \"title\": \"Interactive Exploration\",\n270:       \"description\": \"Students explore the concept via a hands-on simulation.\",\n271:       \"keyPoints\": [\"Observe variable 1\", \"Observe variable 2\"],\n272:       \"order\": 2,\n273:       \"widgetType\": \"simulation\",\n274:       \"widgetOutline\": {\n275:         \"concept\": \"Projectile Motion\",\n276:         \"keyVariables\": [\"angle\", \"velocity\"]\n277:       }\n278:     },\n279:     {\n280:       \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n281:       \"type\": \"quiz\",\n282:       \"title\": \"Knowledge Check\",\n283:       \"description\": \"Test student understanding of the key concepts.\",\n284:       \"keyPoints\": [\"Test point 1\", \"Test point 2\"],\n285:       \"order\": 3,\n286:       \"quizConfig\": {\n287:         \"questionCount\": 2,\n288:         \"difficulty\": \"medium\",\n289:         \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\"]\n290:       }\n291:     }\n292:   ]\n293: }\n294: ```\n295: \n296: ### Scene field descriptions\n297: \n298: | Field             | Type                     | Required | Description                                                                                      |\n299: | ----------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n300: | id                | string                   | ✅       | Unique identifier, format: `scene_1`, `scene_2`...                                               |\n301: | type              | string                   | ✅       | `\"slide\"`, `\"quiz\"`, `\"interactive\"`, or `\"pbl\"`                                                 |\n302: | title             | string                   | ✅       | Scene title, concise and clear                                                                   |\n303: | description       | string                   | ✅       | 1-2 sentences describing teaching purpose                                                        |\n304: | keyPoints         | string[]                 | ✅       | 3-5 core points                                                                                  |\n305: | teachingObjective | string                   | ❌       | Corresponding learning objective                                                                 |\n306: | estimatedDuration | number                   | ❌       | Estimated duration (seconds)                                                                     |\n307: | order             | number                   | ✅       | Sort order, starting from 1                                                                      |\n308: {{#if hasSourceImages}}\n309: | suggestedImageIds | string[]                 | ❌       | Suggested image IDs to use                                                                       |\n310: {{/if}}\n311: {{#if mediaEnabled}}\n312: | mediaGenerations  | MediaGenerationRequest[] | ❌       | AI-generated media requests when generated media would enhance a slide scene                     |\n313: {{/if}}\n314: | quizConfig        | object                   | ❌       | Required for quiz type, contains questionCount/difficulty/questionTypes                          |\n315: | interactiveConfig | object                   | ❌ (deprecated) | Legacy: use widgetType + widgetOutline instead                                                                                       |\n316: | widgetType        | string                   | ✅ (for interactive) | Widget type: \"simulation\", \"diagram\", \"code\", \"game\", \"visualization3d\"                                                 |\n317: | widgetOutline     | object                   | ✅ (for interactive) | Widget-specific configuration (see Widget Type Selection)                                                               |\n318: | pblConfig         | object                   | ❌       | Required for pbl type, contains projectTopic/projectDescription/targetSkills/issueCount/language |\n319: \n320: ### quizConfig Structure\n321: \n322: ```json\n323: {\n324:   \"questionCount\": 2,\n325:   \"difficulty\": \"easy\" | \"medium\" | \"hard\",\n326:   \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\", \"short_answer\"]\n327: }\n328: ```\n329: \n330: ### interactiveConfig Structure\n331: \n332: ```json\n333: {\n334:   \"conceptName\": \"Name of the concept to visualize\",\n335:   \"conceptOverview\": \"Brief description of what this interactive demonstrates\",\n336:   \"designIdea\": \"Detailed description of interactive elements and user interactions\",\n337:   \"subject\": \"Subject area (e.g., Physics, Mathematics)\"\n338: }\n339: ```\n340: \n341: ### pblConfig Structure\n342: \n343: ```json\n344: {\n345:   \"projectTopic\": \"Main topic of the project\",\n346:   \"projectDescription\": \"Brief description of what students will build/accomplish\",\n347:   \"targetSkills\": [\"Skill 1\", \"Skill 2\", \"Skill 3\"],\n348:   \"issueCount\": 3\n349: }\n350: ```\n351: \n352: For a **role-play scenario** PBL (see PBL Scene Guidelines), additionally include the two optional fields:\n353: \n354: ```json\n355: {\n356:   \"projectTopic\": \"Practise comforting a stressed friend\",\n357:   \"projectDescription\": \"Have a supportive conversation with a friend who is going through a hard week\",\n358:   \"targetSkills\": [\"Active listening\", \"Empathetic responding\", \"De-escalation\"],\n359:   \"issueCount\": 3,\n360:   \"scenarioRoleplay\": true,\n361:   \"scenarioBrief\": \"The character is a close friend overwhelmed by exams and a part-time job; the learner practises listening and offering support\"\n362: }\n363: ```\n364: \n365: Omit `scenarioRoleplay` and `scenarioBrief` entirely for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects.\n366: \n367: ---\n368: \n369: ## Important Reminders\n370: \n371: **Top-level response shape (these come first because they are most often violated):**\n372: \n373: 1. Return exactly one JSON **object** — never a bare array.\n374: 2. That object MUST have `languageDirective` (string), `courseTitle` (string, ≤30 chars), and `outlines` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n375: 3. Do not wrap the object in prose, markdown, or code fences.\n376: \n377: **Scene-level rules:**\n378: \n379: 4. `type` is one of `\"slide\"`, `\"quiz\"`, `\"interactive\"`, `\"pbl\"`.\n380: 5. `quiz` scenes must include `quizConfig`.\n381: 6. `interactive` scenes must include `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` (preferred). `interactiveConfig` is deprecated and only accepted for backwards compatibility.\n382: 7. `pbl` scenes must include `pblConfig` with `projectTopic`, `projectDescription`, `targetSkills`, `issueCount`.\n383: 8. Arrange scenes by inferred duration (typically 1-2 scenes per minute). Insert quizzes at appropriate points. Use interactive scenes sparingly (max 1-2 per course).\n384: 9. **Language**: Infer from the user's requirement text and context. Output all scene content in the inferred language.\n385: 10. Regardless of information completeness, always output conforming JSON - do not ask questions or request more information\n386: 11. **No teacher identity on slides**: Scene titles and keyPoints must be neutral and topic-focused. Never include the teacher's name or role (e.g., avoid \"Teacher Wang's Tips\", \"Teacher's Wishes\"). Use generic labels like \"Tips\", \"Summary\", \"Key Takeaways\" instead.\n\n(End of file - total 386 lines)\n</content>",

Interactive Scene Guidelines\n\nUse `interactive` type when a concept benefits significantly from hands-on interaction and visualization. Good candidates include:\n\n- **Physics simulations**: Force composition, projectile motion, wave interference, circuits\n- **Math visualizations**: Function graphing, geometric transformations, probability distributions\n- **Data exploration**: Interactive charts, statistical sampling, regression fitting\n- **Chemistry**: Molecular structure, reaction balancing, pH titration\n- **Programming concepts**: Algorithm visualization, data structure operations\n\n**Constraints**:\n\n- Limit to **1-2 interactive scenes per course** (they are resource-intensive)\n- Interactive scenes **require** an `interactiveConfig` object\n- Do NOT use interactive for purely textual/conceptual content - use slides instead\n- The `interactiveConfig.designIdea` should describe the specific interactive elements and user interactions\n\n### Widget Type Selection for Interactive Scenes\n\nWhen generating an interactive scene, you MUST select the appropriate widget type and provide widgetOutline:\n\n**Selection Logic:**\n\n| Concept Characteristics | Widget Type | widgetOutline Fields |\n|-------------------------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters | `simulation` | `concept`, `keyVariables` |\n| Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains | `diagram` | `diagramType` |\n| Programming concepts, algorithms | `code` | `language` |\n| Practice activities, gamified assessment | `game` | `gameType`, `challenge` |\n| Biological/geometric structures, 3D models | `visualization3d` | `visualizationType`, `objects` |\n\n**widgetOutline Format by Type:**\n\n```json\n// simulation\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"concept\": \"concept_name\",\n  \"keyVariables\": [\"variable1\", \"variable2\"]\n}\n\n// diagram\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"diagramType\": \"flowchart\"\n}\n\n// code\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"language\": \"python\"\n}\n\n// game\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"gameType\": \"action\",\n  \"challenge\": \"description of what player controls\"\n}\n\n// visualization3d\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n  \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"mars\"]\n}\n```\n\n**CRITICAL:** Every interactive scene MUST include both `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` fields. Interactive scenes without these are INVALID.\n\n### PBL Scene Guidelines\n\nUse `pbl` type when the course involves complex, multi-step project work that benefits from structured collaboration. Good candidates include:\n\n- **Engineering projects**: Software development, hardware design, system architecture\n- **Research projects**: Scientific research, data analysis, literature review\n- **Design projects**: Product design, UX research, creative projects\n- **Business projects**: Business plans, market analysis, strategy development\n\n**Constraints**:\n\n- Limit to **at most 1 PBL scene per course** (they are comprehensive and long)\n- PBL scenes **require** a `pblConfig` object with: projectTopic, projectDescription, targetSkills, issueCount\n- PBL is for substantial project work - do NOT use for simple exercises or single-step tasks\n- The `pblConfig.targetSkills` should list 2-5 specific skills students will develop\n- The `pblConfig.issueCount` should typically be 2-5 issues\n\n**Role-play scenario PBL (optional PBL sub-type)**:\n\nSome PBL projects are best learned by *practising an interpersonal or situational interaction* rather than by building an artefact — for example practising a difficult conversation, a negotiation, a job interview, a customer-service exchange, a debate, a role-play game (e.g. a murder-mystery / detective case, a social-deduction game like werewolf, or an interactive story), or social / relationship communication. When the core of the learning really is the interaction itself (the learner will converse with one or more in-character roles inside an immersive scene), additionally set inside `pblConfig`:\n\n- `scenarioRoleplay: true` — marks this PBL as a role-play scenario.\n- `scenarioBrief` (optional string) — a short hint about the situation and who the character(s) are, to steer the later design step.\n\nLeave **both unset** for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects (this is the default). Only use `scenarioRoleplay` when the practice of the interaction is the point. This does not change how you choose the scene `type` — it is still `pbl`; these two fields are an optional flavour *inside* a PBL scene.\n\n**Important:** `pblConfig.scenarioRoleplay` is the downstream runtime switch. If the user explicitly asks for a role-play / scenario-simulation PBL, do not return an ordinary PBL; set `scenarioRoleplay: true` and include a concrete `scenarioBrief`.\n\n---\n\n## Output Format\n\n### Top-level shape — NON-NEGOTIABLE\n\nYour entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these three top-level keys:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"languageDirective\": \"<the directive you inferred in the Language Inference step>\",\n  \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n  \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects */ ]\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- **Never** return a bare array. The top level is an object, not an array.\n- **Never** omit `languageDirective` or `courseTitle`. Both are required even if you think they are obvious.\n- **Never** wrap the response in any other structure, prose, or code fence.\n\n### Minimal complete example\n\n```json\n{\n  \"languageDirective\": \"Deliver the entire course in English. Use simple vocabulary suitable for a beginner.\",\n  \"courseTitle\": \"Intro to Projectile Motion\",\n  \"outlines\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_1\",\n      \"type\": \"slide\",\n      \"title\": \"Introduction\",\n      \"description\": \"Welcome students and introduce the core concept.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Context\", \"Agenda\", \"Goals\"],\n      \"order\": 1\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n      \"type\": \"interactive\",\n      \"title\": \"Interactive Exploration\",\n      \"description\": \"Students explore the concept via a hands-on simulation.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Observe variable 1\", \"Observe variable 2\"],\n      \"order\": 2,\n      \"widgetType\": \"simulation\",\n      \"widgetOutline\": {\n        \"concept\": \"Projectile Motion\",\n        \"keyVariables\": [\"angle\", \"velocity\"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n      \"type\": \"quiz\",\n      \"title\": \"Knowledge Check\",\n      \"description\": \"Test student understanding of the key concepts.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Test point 1\", \"Test point 2\"],\n      \"order\": 3,\n      \"quizConfig\": {\n        \"questionCount\": 2,\n        \"difficulty\": \"medium\",\n        \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\"]\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n### Scene field descriptions\n\n| Field             |       | string                   | ✅       | 1-2 sentences describing teaching purpose                                                        |\n| keyPoints         | string[]                 | ✅       | 3-5 core points                                                                                  |\n| teachingObjective | string                   | ❌       | Corresponding learning objective                                                                 |\n| estimatedDuration | number                   | ❌       | Estimated duration (seconds)                                                                     |\n| order             | number                   | ✅       | Sort order, starting from 1                                                                      |\n{{#if Users compare against Opus-5.5-class motion-graphic explainers.\n- **Interactive widgets get no design guidance either** — the simulation/game/3d prompts\n  specify behavior and safety, not visual quality.\n- **Lesson narration voices are limited to the built-in TTS presets**; Fish Audio\n  (fish.audio, controllable per-voice via a voice model ID) is listed as \"future provider\"\n  in `lib/audio/types.ts` but not implemented.\n\n## 2. binary audio response; errors 401/402/400/429 |\n\nNot used: dead/stub listings (motion-matching, remotion-video-graphics, interactive-tech-learning,\nkindergarten assistant, ai-academic-tutor mirror, learn-chat-deep-tutor retirement) and the three\nMCP-server listings (retrieval surfaces, no design content).\n\n## 4. Architecture decisions\n\n### D1 — Motion graphics land as a new widget type: `animation-explainer`\n\nThe interactive scene pipeline already: renders self-contained HTML in an iframe, validates\ninline JS via parse5+`node:vm`, publishes live state via `data-maic-observation`, lets the\nteacher drive it with `widget_setState / widget_reveal / widget_highlight / widget_annotation`\n(`interactive-actions` prompt). A motion graphic is *code-generated animation HTML* — exactly the\nsame contract. This avoids touching the PPTist renderer (which has no per-element animation\nsystem) and is model-cheap (pure code, zero AI media dependency).\n\nContract for the new widget:\n\n- Deterministic GSAP timeline (CDN import), no `Date.now()`/`Math.random`/network — replaying\n  the timeline is exact, so the teacher can re-run a beat during discussion.\n- Auto-starts on load with the **HOOK** phase; later phases are advanced by teacher narration\n  beats via `SET_WIDGET_STATE { phase: 'p1' | 'p2' … }` and a big Replay button restarts.\n  Ambient loop after the final phase keeps the scene alive (a looping, deterministic\n  sub-timeline on `window.__timelines`.\n- Phases: **HOOK → TEASE (why/what) → SPARK (key visual/insight) → TITLE (course title lockup + recap)**\n  — 20–45 s total, screen-readable titles, no audio in the widget.\n- Publishes `{ phase, step, startedAt }` via `data-maic-observation`; stable `#phase-dots`,\n  `#replay-btn`.\n\n### D2 — Per-course `designDirective` threaded through the whole pipeline\n\nStage-1 outline gains a required top-level output field:\n\n```json\n\"designDirective\": {\n  \"concept\": \"cinematic dark-mode tech explainer with electric accents\",\n  \"palette\": [\"#0b1020\", \"#22d3ee\", \"#f472b6\", \"#e2e8f0\"],\n  \"background\": \"dark\" | \"light\",\n  \"motionPersonality\": \"playful\" | \"premium\" | \"energetic\" | \"calm\" | \"storytelling\"\n}\n```\n\nInferred from the requirement + materials + (later steps) teacher persona, like\n`languageDirective`; flows from `engine` into every scene-content/action prompt as\n`{{designDirective}}`. This is the single root-cause fix for \"all lessons have the same colors.\"\n\n### D3 — Master skill = generation-package snippets (+ templates)\n\nNew snippets under `packages/@openmaic/generation/snippets/`:\n\n- `design-directive.md` — how every scene must read & apply the directive (60-30-10, contrast,\n  dark/light backgrounds, accent discipline).\n- `motion-script-contract.md` — the deterministic-timeline render contract (used by the\n  animation-explainer template; reusable).\n- `widget-visual-polish.md` — shared visual QA for all interactive widgets (surface, depth,\n  states, motion cues, iconography, mobile).\n- `slide-visual-design.md` — icon system (inline SVG paths, consistent stroke), infographic\n  patterns (hero stats, donut/progress, comparison cards, process flows, timeline), composition\n  (asymmetry, focal point, whitespace), anti-slop bans.\n- `kinetic-typography.md` — word-level staging vocabulary for the explainers.\n\nNew template: `templates/animation-explainer-content/{system,user}.md` — the distilled\nhyperframes/OpenDesign/LottieFiles doctrine into one self-contained scene-builder prompt.\nRegistered in `src/prompts/`.\n\n### D4 — Outline changes (`requirements-to-outlines`, app-side `interactive-outlines` parity)\n\n- **Scene 1 of every course is the course intro `animation-explainer`** (the \"trailer\"): must be\n  grounded in the topic, teach the *why* in one line, no fake data; if the user explicitly asked\n  for a plain/textual lesson, the explainer still plays — it is the hook that pulls them in.\n- widget selection table gains the `animation-explainer` row (`concept`, `keyBeats`, `mood`).\n- `designDirective` output section + validation in the outline step.\n- Interactive budget wording updated: the intro does not count against the 1-2 deep-interactive\n  budget (`animation-explainer` is passive-watch; `simulation/game/code/visualization3d/diagram`\n  remain capped).\n\n### D5 — Fish Audio TTS\n\nSeven documented touch points (per the HOW-TO-ADD comments): ids, registry config, implementation\nswitch, provider-display names + i18n, `TTS_ENV_MAP`, endpoint-path hint, preset auto-derivation\n(comes free from the registry — `tests/config/provider-presets.test.ts` enforces it).\n\nVoice strategy: fish voices are user-owned models, so the registry ships with a couple of\ndocumented sample voice IDs **plus a free-text voice ID field** in the TTS settings panel that\npersists through `setTTSVoice(<id>, 'fish-tts')` (the same store the voice pill writes). Helper\ncopy shows how to copy an ID from `fish.audio/m/<id>` / `?modelId=…` URLs.\n\n## 5. Scope guard\n\n- No renderer/engine behavioral rewrites beyond threading one extra context string.\n- `defaultTheme`/fonts left alone (user-editable today; changing it touches editor symmetry).\n- No new model providers beyond Fish TTS; no video-generation changes.\n- i18n: add new keys to every locale file present (en-US first, others mirrored in English so\n  nothing breaks; zh-CN translated).\n\n## 6. Validation plan\n\n1. `pnpm typecheck` (or package-scoped `tsc`) + lint.\n2. Existing vitest suites for `@openmaic/generation`, `@openmaic/dsl`, `tests/config/*`.\n3. Fish TTS contract test against a mock (fetch-level) if a key is absent.\n4. One smoke generation (≤2 scenes: intro animation + one slide) using the cheapest configured\n   model to keep tokens tiny; inspected by hand for palette adherence + animation presence.\n\n## 7. Rollback\n\nFull implementation is additive: new template/snippet files, one new union member wired through\nswitch statements, one new optional outline field, one new TTS provider entry. Reverting = revert\nthe commit; generated artifacts are unaffected (old scenes remain valid because\n`WidgetType` validation accepts legacy values from schemas that only widen).\n"
