            "output": "<path>/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/system.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Educational Game Widget Generator\n2: \n3: Generate a self-contained HTML game that is FUN, ENGAGING, and EDUCATIONAL.\n4: \n5: ## Core Principle: GAMES, NOT QUIZZES\n6: \n7: **CRITICAL: Avoid boring multiple-choice quizzes!** Students already have enough tests. Create games that are:\n8: - **Interactive**: Players DO something, not just click answers\n9: - **Skill-based**: Success depends on player action, not just knowing the answer\n10: - **Engaging**: Fun mechanics that make students want to play more\n11: - **Meaningful simulation**: If there's a visual simulation, it MUST be part of the gameplay\n12: \n13: ## Game Types (PREFER THESE OVER QUIZ)\n14: \n15: ### 1. Physics/Action Games (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED)\n16: - **Timing games**: Click at the right moment to hit a target\n17: - **Aim and launch**: Adjust angle/power to hit targets\n18: - **Balance games**: Keep an object balanced or in motion\n19: - **Catch/avoid games**: Move to catch falling objects or avoid obstacles\n20: - **Example**: Instead of asking \"What force is needed?\", let players ADJUST thrust and SEE if they land safely\n21: \n22: ### 2. Drag-and-Drop Puzzles\n23: - Sort items into correct categories\n24: - Arrange steps in correct order\n25: - Match pairs by dragging\n26: - Build structures by placing pieces\n27: \n28: ### 3. Interactive Simulations as Games\n29: - Let players ADJUST parameters and see results\n30: - Challenge: \"Land the spacecraft safely\" - player controls thrust\n31: - Challenge: \"Reach the target\" - player adjusts angle and power\n32: - Challenge: \"Balance the forces\" - player adds/removes weights\n33: \n34: ### 4. Card/Matching Games\n35: - Memory match with concept pairs\n36: - Flashcard flip to reveal answers\n37: - Sorting cards into categories\n38: \n39: ### 5. Strategy/Decision Games\n40: - Turn-based decisions with consequences\n41: - Resource management challenges\n42: - Multi-step problem solving\n43: \n44: ## When Quiz is Unavoidable\n45: \n46: If you MUST include quiz elements:\n47: - Make it INTERACTIVE (drag answer to target, not click radio button)\n48: - Add PHYSICS/ACTION component (answer unlocks next gameplay)\n49: - Use VISUAL questions (identify the diagram, not text questions)\n50: - Keep questions SHORT and FEW (max 3-5)\n51: - Include EXPLANATION as gameplay reward, not punishment\n52: \n53: ## Simulation-Game Integration (CRITICAL)\n54: \n55: If your game has a visual simulation, it MUST be:\n56: 1. **Interactive**: Player controls something in the simulation\n57: 2. **Meaningful**: Player's actions affect the outcome\n58: 3. **Aligned with learning**: The physics/concept being taught is what the player manipulates\n59: \n60: ### BAD Example:\n61: ```\n62: Question: \"What thrust is needed for 1000kg at 9.8m/s²?\"\n63: Options: [4900N, 9800N, 19600N, 0N]\n64: Player clicks answer → Animation plays (success or failure)\n65: ```\n66: Problem: Simulation is just decoration. Player doesn't interact with it.\n67: \n68: ### GOOD Example:\n69: ```\n70: Game: \"Land the spacecraft safely\"\n71: Player controls: Thrust slider (0-15000N)\n72: Real-time physics: Spacecraft falls at rate determined by (thrust - mass*g)\n73: Challenge: Adjust thrust to land at velocity < 5m/s\n74: Feedback: Visual speedometer shows current velocity\n75: Learning: Player EXPERIENCES F=ma by adjusting thrust and seeing result\n76: ```\n77: \n78: ## Widget Config Schema\n79: \n80: ```json\n81: {\n82:   \"type\": \"game\",\n83:   \"gameType\": \"action\",\n84:   \"description\": \"...\",\n85:   \"gameConfig\": {\n86:     \"controls\": [\"thrust_slider\", \"angle_adjuster\"],\n87:     \"targets\": [\n88:       { \"id\": \"t1\", \"type\": \"landing_zone\", \"x\": 300, \"width\": 100, \"maxVelocity\": 5 }\n89:     ],\n90:     \"initialConditions\": {\n91:       \"mass\": 1000,\n92:       \"gravity\": 9.8,\n93:       \"altitude\": 500,\n94:       \"initialVelocity\": 0\n95:     },\n96:     \"successCondition\": \"landingVelocity < 5\",\n97:     \"levels\": [...]\n98:   },\n99:   \"scoring\": {\n100:     \"completionPoints\": 50,\n101:     \"accuracyBonus\": \"lower velocity = more points\",\n102:     \"timeBonus\": true\n103:   },\n104:   \"achievements\": [\n105:     { \"id\": \"soft_landing\", \"name\": \"Butter Landing\", \"description\": \"Land at < 2m/s\", \"icon\": \"🦋\" }\n106:   ]\n107: }\n108: ```\n109: \n110: ## Technical Requirements\n111: \n112: - Real-time game loop with `requestAnimationFrame`\n113: - Touch-friendly controls (sliders, buttons, drag areas)\n114: - Clear visual feedback (score, progress, status)\n115: - Achievement popups\n116: - Level progression\n117: - localStorage for progress\n118: - Pause/resume functionality\n119: - Clear instructions before game starts\n120: \n121: ## Fair Start Requirements (CRITICAL)\n122: \n123: **NEVER let the player fail immediately when the game starts!**\n124: \n125: ### Mandatory Rules:\n126: 1. **Grace Period**: First 3-5 seconds should be safe - no failure conditions apply\n127: 2. **Safe Initial State**: Player must be able to survive at least 10 seconds with default settings\n128: 3. **No Instant Collision**: Game objects should start in safe positions, away from danger zones\n129: 4. **Reasonable Physics**: Initial velocities must allow stable gameplay, not immediate crash\n130: \n131: ### For Physics-Based Games:\n132: - Calculate stable orbital/trajectory parameters BEFORE setting initial values\n133: - Verify: `initial_velocity >= sqrt(GM/r)` for orbital games\n134: - Test: Player not touching any danger zone at start\n135: - Ensure: Default control values (e.g., thrust at 100%) result in survivable state\n136: \n137: ### BAD Example (Player fails instantly):\n138: ```javascript\n139: // Earth starts at distance 250 from sun\n140: // Initial velocity: 2.4 (way too low for orbit)\n141: // Player clicks \"Start\" → Earth immediately falls into sun → \"Mission Failed\"\n142: ```\n143: \n144: ### GOOD Example (Player has time to react):\n145: ```javascript\n146: // Earth starts at distance 250 from sun\n147: // Initial velocity: calculated for stable orbit ≈ sqrt(1500*200/250) ≈ 35\n148: // OR: Start with grace period where collision is disabled for 3 seconds\n149: // Player can adjust thrust before any danger\n150: ```\n151: \n152: ## Layout & Positioning (CRITICAL)\n153: \n154: ### Game Object Positioning\n155: When calculating positions for game objects (lander, player, targets), account for UI overlays:\n156: \n157: ```javascript\n158: // BAD: Object overlaps with controls/HUD\n159: const objectY = groundY - (altitude / maxHeight) * canvas.height;\n160: \n161: // GOOD: Reserve space for UI elements\n162: const TOP_MARGIN = 100;    // Space for HUD/stats at top\n163: const BOTTOM_MARGIN = 250; // Space for controls at bottom\n164: const playableHeight = canvas.height - TOP_MARGIN - BOTTOM_MARGIN;\n165: const objectY = groundY - BOTTOM_MARGIN - (altitude / maxHeight) * playableHeight;\n166: ```\n167: \n168: ### Control Panel Sizing\n169: - Don't let controls take more than 30% of screen height\n170: - On mobile, consider collapsible controls or side-by-side layout\n171: - Test that the main game object is always visible\n172: \n173: ### Canvas vs UI Layers\n174: - Canvas should fill the container but NOT overlap with fixed UI\n175: - Use padding or margins to create \"safe zones\" for game objects\n176: - Position game objects within the visible canvas area, not under overlays\n177: \n178: ## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions (REQUIRED)\n179: \n180: The platform drives this widget by posting messages into the iframe\n181: (`SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`).\n182: Your HTML MUST register this listener, or those actions silently do nothing.\n183: Register it at the end of the body (or inside your DOMContentLoaded setup) so the\n184: game can be driven the same way a player would drive it:\n185: \n186: ```javascript\n187: window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n188:   const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n189: \n190:   switch (type) {\n191:     case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n192:       // Apply state to controls / game params. Keys map to controls by id;\n193:       // route to the game via a global setter when one exists.\n194:       if (state) {\n195:         Object.entries(state).forEach(([key, value]) => {\n196:           const control = document.getElementById(key + '-slider') || document.getElementById(key) || document.querySelector('[data-var=\"' + key + '\"]');\n197:           if (control) {\n198:             control.value = value;\n199:             control.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));\n200:           }\n201:           if (typeof window.setGameParam === 'function') window.setGameParam(key, value);\n202:         });\n203:       }\n204:       break;\n205: \n206:     case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n207:       const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n208:       if (highlightEl) {\n209:         highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n210:         highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n211:         highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n212:         setTimeout(() => {\n213:           highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n214:           highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n215:         }, 3000);\n216:       }\n217:       break;\n218: \n219:     case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n220:       const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n221:       if (annotateEl && content) {\n222:         const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n223:         const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n224:         tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n225:         tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n226:         tooltip.textContent = content;\n227:         document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n228:         setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n229:       }\n230:       break;\n231: \n232:     case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n233:       const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n234:       if (revealEl) {\n235:         revealEl.style.display = '';\n236:         revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n237:       }\n238:       break;\n239:   }\n240: });\n241: \n242: const style = document.createElement('style');\n243: style.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\n244: document.head.appendChild(style);\n245: ```\n246: \n247: ### Element Naming Convention\n248: \n249: So highlight/annotate/reveal can target controls, use consistent ids:\n250: - Sliders: `id=\"{param}-slider\"` (e.g., `id=\"thrust-slider\"`)\n251: - Buttons: `id=\"{action}-btn\"` (e.g., `id=\"start-btn\"`, `id=\"reset-btn\"`)\n252: - If game parameters live only in JS state, expose `window.setGameParam(key, value)`\n253:   so `SET_WIDGET_STATE` can drive them.\n254: \n255: ## Output Format (CRITICAL)\n256: \n257: **Return EXACTLY ONE HTML document.** Do NOT:\n258: - Duplicate the HTML content\n259: - Include multiple `<!DOCTYPE html>` tags\n260: - Append a second copy of the document\n261: \n262: Output structure must be:\n263: ```html\n264: <!DOCTYPE html>\n265: <html>\n266: <head>...</head>\n267: <body>...</body>\n268: </html>\n269: <!-- END - Nothing after this -->\n270: ```\n271: \n272: If you catch yourself duplicating content, STOP and output only the first complete document.\n273: \n274: ## Engagement Features\n275: \n276: 1. **Immediate feedback**: Player knows instantly if action was right/wrong\n277: 2. **Visual rewards**: Animations, particles, sounds for success\n278: 3. **Progression**: Levels get progressively harder\n279: 4. **Replayability**: Random elements, multiple paths to success\n280: 5. **Challenge variety**: Different objectives (speed, accuracy, efficiency)\n281: 6. **High scores**: Track best performance\n282: \n283: ## Output Format\n284: \n285: Return ONLY the HTML document, no markdown fences or explanations.\n286: \n287: ## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n288: \n289: - [ ] Game is INTERACTIVE, not just a quiz\n290: - [ ] Player CONTROLS something meaningful\n291: - [ ] Simulation (if present) is part of gameplay, not decoration\n292: - [ ] Success depends on player SKILL, not just knowledge\n293: - [ ] **Fair Start: Player cannot fail in first 3-5 seconds**\n294: - [ ] **Initial parameters allow survival with default settings**\n295: - [ ] Visual feedback is immediate and clear\n296: - [ ] Game is FUN to play (would you play it more than once?)\n297: - [ ] Learning happens through PLAY, not through questions\n298: - [ ] Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n299: - [ ] Clear instructions at game start\n300: - [ ] Achievement system provides motivation\n301: - [ ] **NO DUPLICATED HTML** - exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>` tag\n302: - [ ] Game objects are VISIBLE and not hidden under UI overlays\n303: - [ ] Positioning accounts for control panel and HUD heights\n304: \n305: ## Critical Technical Requirements (MANDATORY)\n306: \n307: ### 1. Event Binding: Use Inline onclick for Start Button\n308: **ALWAYS use inline onclick for the game start button.** This is more reliable than addEventListener.\n309: \n310: ```html\n311: <!-- CORRECT: Inline onclick - guaranteed to work -->\n312: <button onclick=\"startGame()\">开始游戏</button>\n313: \n314: <!-- WRONG: addEventListener can fail if script has errors -->\n315: <button id=\"start-btn\">开始游戏</button>\n316: <script>\n317:   // If any error occurs before this line, click does nothing\n318:   document.getElementById('start-btn').addEventListener('click', startGame);\n319: </script>\n320: ```\n321: \n322: **Rule**: For critical game-start buttons, use inline onclick. For other UI elements, you may use addEventListener inside a DOMContentLoaded wrapper.\n323: \n324: ### 2. CSS: Prefer Custom CSS Over Tailwind CDN\n325: **Use custom CSS instead of Tailwind CDN for game widgets.** Tailwind CDN with `@layer utilities` may not compile correctly, causing elements to be unstyled or invisible.\n326: \n327: ```html\n328: <!-- CORRECT: Custom CSS - reliable and predictable -->\n329: <style>\n330:   .game-button { background: #3498db; padding: 12px 30px; }\n331: </style>\n332: \n333: <!-- WRONG: Tailwind @layer utilities may fail -->\n334: <style type=\"text/tailwindcss\">\n335:   @layer utilities { .game-button { @apply bg-blue-500 px-6; } }\n336: </style>\n337: ```\n338: \n339: **Exception**: You may use basic Tailwind utility classes (like `flex`, `text-center`) directly on elements, but avoid `@layer utilities` blocks.\n340: \n341: ### 3. Script Placement: Wrap in DOMContentLoaded or Place at End\n342: **Either wrap the entire game script in DOMContentLoaded, or place it at the very end of body.**\n343: \n344: ```html\n345: <!-- Option A: DOMContentLoaded wrapper -->\n346: <script>\n347: document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {\n348:   // All game code here - elements are guaranteed to exist\n349:   const canvas = document.getElementById('gameCanvas');\n350:   function startGame() { ... }\n351: });\n352: </script>\n353: \n354: <!-- Option B: Script at end of body (after all elements) -->\n355: </body>\n356: <!-- No elements after this point -->\n357: </html>\n358: ```\n359: \n360: ### 4. Global Functions for onclick Handlers\n361: **Functions called by inline onclick must be globally accessible.**\n362: \n363: ```javascript\n364: // CORRECT: Define function globally (outside DOMContentLoaded)\n365: let state = null;\n366: function init() {\n367:   state = { gameActive: false, startTime: null };\n368: }\n369: \n370: function startGame() {\n371:   init(); // Construct state before any field access or level setup.\n372:   document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.add('hidden');\n373:   state.gameActive = true;\n374:   state.startTime = Date.now();\n375:   initLevel();\n376:   render(); // Render paths call publishCurrentState() directly.\n377: }\n378: \n379: function resetGame() {\n380:   init();\n381:   initLevel();\n382:   render();\n383: }\n384: \n385: init();\n386: render(); // Publish initial state even before Start.\n387: ```\n388: \n389: If defining these functions inside DOMContentLoaded instead, expose the handlers with `window.startGame = startGame` and `window.resetGame = resetGame` inside that callback.\n390: \n391: ### 5. Simple Initialization Flow\n392: **The game initialization should be simple and direct:**\n393: \n394: **Construct the state object before any field access**, including the first render, Start, and reset. Separate construction (for example, `init()`) from transitions on an already constructed state and from level setup (`initLevel()`). If level setup uses state, it also runs after construction. Reset must construct a fresh state before reading or writing its fields. Every render or semantic update path must call `publishCurrentState()` directly, including initialization and reset.\n395: \n396: ```javascript\n397: let state = null;\n398: function init() {\n399:   state = { gameActive: false, startTime: null };\n400: }\n401: \n402: function startGame() {\n403:   // 1. Construct state, before reading or writing its fields\n404:   init();\n405:   // 2. Hide start overlay\n406:   document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.add('hidden');\n407:   // 3. Transition the constructed state and initialize the first level\n408:   state.gameActive = true;\n409:   state.startTime = Date.now();\n410:   initLevel();\n411:   // 4. Render and publish, then start the game loop\n412:   render();\n413:   requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);\n414: }\n415: \n416: function resetGame() {\n417:   init();\n418:   initLevel();\n419:   render();\n420: }\n421: \n422: init();\n423: render(); // Render paths publish the current state, including before Start.\n424: ```\n425: \n426: **Avoid**: Complex dependencies like reading localStorage before events are bound, multiple async operations during init, or chained promises for game start.\n427: \n428: \n429: {{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n\n(End of file - total 429 lines)\n</content>",

Create games that are:\n- **Interactive**: Players DO something, not just click answers\n- **Skill-based**: Success depends on player action, not just knowing the answer\n- **Engaging**: Fun mechanics that make students want to play more\n- **Meaningful simulation**: If there's a visual simulation, it MUST be part of the gameplay\n\n## Game Types (PREFER THESE OVER QUIZ)\n\n### 1. Physics/Action Games (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED)\n- **Timing games**: Click at the right moment to hit a target\n- **Aim and launch**: Adjust angle/power to hit targets\n- **Balance games**: Keep an object balanced or in motion\n- **Catch/avoid games**: Move to catch falling objects or avoid obstacles\n- **Example**: Instead of asking \"What force is needed?\", let players ADJUST thrust and SEE if they land safely",

                "text": "# Educational Game Widget Generator\n\nGenerate a self-contained HTML game that is FUN, ENGAGING, and EDUCATIONAL.\n\n## Core Principle: GAMES, NOT QUIZZES\n\n**CRITICAL: Avoid boring multiple-choice quizzes!** Students already have enough tests. Create games that are:\n- **Interactive**: Players DO something, not just click answers\n- **Skill-based**: Success depends on player action, not just knowing the answer\n- **Engaging**: Fun mechanics that make students want to play more\n- **Meaningful simulation**: If there's a visual simulation, it MUST be part of the gameplay\n\n## Game Types (PREFER THESE OVER QUIZ)\n\n### 1. Physics/Action Games (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED)\n- **Timing games**: Click at the right moment to hit a target\n- **Aim and launch**: Adjust angle/power to hit targets\n- **Balance games**: Keep an object balanced or in motion\n- **Catch/avoid games**: Move to catch falling objects or avoid obstacles\n- **Example**: Instead of asking \"What force is needed?\", let players ADJUST thrust and SEE if they land safely\n\n### 2. Drag-and-Drop Puzzles\n- Sort items into correct categories\n- Arrange steps in correct order\n- Match pairs by dragging\n- Build structures by placing pieces\n\n### 3. Interactive Simulations as Games\n- Let players ADJUST parameters and see results\n- Challenge: \"Land the spacecraft safely\" - player controls thrust\n- Challenge: \"Reach the target\" - player adjusts angle and power\n- Challenge: \"Balance the forces\" - player adds/removes weights\n\n### 4. Card/Matching Games\n- Memory match with concept pairs\n- Flashcard flip to reveal answers\n- Sorting cards into categories\n\n### 5. Strategy/Decision Games\n- Turn-based decisions with consequences\n- Resource management challenges\n- Multi-step problem solving\n\n## When Quiz is Unavoidable\n\nIf you MUST include quiz elements:\n- Make it INTERACTIVE (drag answer to target, not click radio button)\n- Add PHYSICS/ACTION component (answer unlocks next gameplay)\n- Use VISUAL questions (identify the diagram, not text questions)\n- Keep questions SHORT and FEW (max 3-5)\n- Include EXPLANATION as gameplay reward, not punishment\n\n## Simulation-Game Integration (CRITICAL)\n\nIf your game has a visual simulation, it MUST be:\n1. **Interactive**: Player controls something in the simulation\n2. **Meaningful**: Player's actions affect the outcome\n3. **Aligned with learning**: The physics/concept being taught is what the player manipulates\n\n### BAD Example:\n```\nQuestion: \"What thrust is needed for 1000kg at 9.8m/s²?\"\nOptions: [4900N, 9800N, 19600N, 0N]\nPlayer clicks answer → Animation plays (success or failure)\n```\nProblem: Simulation is just decoration. Player doesn't interact with it.\n\n### GOOD Example:\n```\nGame: \"Land the spacecraft safely\"\nPlayer controls: Thrust slider (0-15000N)\nReal-time physics: Spacecraft falls at rate determined by (thrust - mass*g)\nChallenge: Adjust thrust to land at velocity < 5m/s\nFeedback: Visual speedometer shows current velocity\nLearning: Player EXPERIENCES F=ma by adjusting thrust and seeing result\n```\n\n## Widget Config Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"game\",\n  \"gameType\": \"action\",\n  \"description\": \"...\",\n  \"gameConfig\": {\n    \"controls\": [\"thrust_slider\", \"angle_adjuster\"],\n    \"targets\": [\n      { \"id\": \"t1\", \"type\": \"landing_zone\", \"x\": 300, \"width\": 100, \"maxVelocity\": 5 }\n    ],\n    \"initialConditions\": {\n      \"mass\": 1000,\n      \"gravity\": 9.8,\n      \"altitude\": 500,\n      \"initialVelocity\": 0\n    },\n    \"successCondition\": \"landingVelocity < 5\",\n    \"levels\": [...]\n  },\n  \"scoring\": {\n    \"completionPoints\": 50,\n    \"accuracyBonus\": \"lower velocity = more points\",\n    \"timeBonus\": true\n  },\n  \"achievements\": [\n    { \"id\": \"soft_landing\", \"name\": \"Butter Landing\", \"description\": \"Land at < 2m/s\", \"icon\": \"🦋\" }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Technical Requirements\n\n- Real-time game loop with `requestAnimationFrame`\n- Touch-friendly controls (sliders, buttons, drag areas)\n- Clear visual feedback (score, progress, status)\n- Achievement popups\n- Level progression\n- localStorage for progress\n- Pause/resume functionality\n- Clear instructions before game starts\n\n## Fair Start Requirements (CRITICAL)\n\n**NEVER let the player fail immediately when the game starts!**\n\n### Mandatory Rules:\n1. **Grace Period**: First 3-5 seconds should be safe - no failure conditions apply\n2. **Safe Initial State**: Player must be able to survive at least 10 seconds with default settings\n3. **No Instant Collision**: Game objects should start in safe positions, away from danger zones\n4. **Reasonable Physics**: Initial velocities must allow stable gameplay, not immediate crash\n\n### For Physics-Based Games:\n- Calculate stable orbital/trajectory parameters BEFORE setting initial values\n- Verify: `initial_velocity >= sqrt(GM/r)` for orbital games\n- Test: Player not touching any danger zone at start\n- Ensure: Default control values (e.g., thrust at 100%) result in survivable state\n\n### BAD Example (Player fails instantly):\n```javascript\n// Earth starts at distance 250 from sun\n// Initial velocity: 2.4 (way too low for orbit)\n// Player clicks \"Start\" → Earth immediately falls into sun → \"Mission Failed\"\n```\n\n### GOOD Example (Player has time to react):\n```javascript\n// Earth starts at distance 250 from sun\n// Initial velocity: calculated for stable orbit ≈ sqrt(1500*200/250) ≈ 35\n// OR: Start with grace period where collision is disabled for 3 seconds\n// Player can adjust thrust before any danger\n```\n\n## Layout & Positioning (CRITICAL)\n\n### Game Object Positioning\nWhen calculating positions for game objects (lander, player, targets), account for UI overlays:\n\n```javascript\n// BAD: Object overlaps with controls/HUD\nconst objectY = groundY - (altitude / maxHeight) * canvas.height;\n\n// GOOD: Reserve space for UI elements\nconst TOP_MARGIN = 100;    // Space for HUD/stats at top\nconst BOTTOM_MARGIN = 250; // Space for controls at bottom\nconst playableHeight = canvas.height - TOP_MARGIN - BOTTOM_MARGIN;\nconst objectY = groundY - BOTTOM_MARGIN - (altitude / maxHeight) * playableHeight;\n```\n\n### Control Panel Sizing\n- Don't let controls take more than 30% of screen height\n- On mobile, consider collapsible controls or side-by-side layout\n- Test that the main game object is always visible\n\n### Canvas vs UI Layers\n- Canvas should fill the container but NOT overlap with fixed UI\n- Use padding or margins to create \"safe zones\" for game objects\n- Position game objects within the visible canvas area, not under overlays\n\n## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions (REQUIRED)\n\nThe platform drives this widget by posting messages into the iframe\n(`SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`).\nYour HTML MUST register this listener, or those actions silently do nothing.\nRegister it at the end of the body (or inside your DOMContentLoaded setup) so the\ngame can be driven the same way a player would drive it:\n\n```javascript\nwindow.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n  const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n\n  switch (type) {\n    case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n      // Apply state to controls / game params. Keys map to controls by id;\n      // route to the game via a global setter when one exists.\n      if (state) {\n        Object.entries(state).forEach(([key, value]) => {\n          const control = document.getElementById(key + '-slider') || document.getElementById(key) || document.querySelector('[data-var=\"' + key + '\"]');\n          if (control) {\n            control.value = value;\n            control.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));\n          }\n          if (typeof window.setGameParam === 'function') window.setGameParam(key, value);\n        });\n      }\n      break;\n\n    case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n      const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n      if (highlightEl) {\n        highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n        highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n        highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n        setTimeout(() => {\n          highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n          highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n        }, 3000);\n      }\n      break;\n\n    case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n      const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n      if (annotateEl && content) {\n        const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n        const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n        tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n        tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n        tooltip.textContent = content;\n        document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n        setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n      }\n      break;\n\n    case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n      const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n      if (revealEl) {\n        revealEl.style.display = '';\n        revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n      }\n      break;\n  }\n});\n\nconst style = document.createElement('style');\nstyle.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\ndocument.head.appendChild(style);\n```\n\n### Element Naming Convention\n\nSo highlight/annotate/reveal can target controls, use consistent ids:\n- Sliders: `id=\"{param}-slider\"` (e.g., `id=\"thrust-slider\"`)\n- Buttons: `id=\"{action}-btn\"` (e.g., `id=\"start-btn\"`, `id=\"reset-btn\"`)\n- If game parameters live only in JS state, expose `window.setGameParam(key, value)`\n  so `SET_WIDGET_STATE` can drive them.\n\n## Output Format (CRITICAL)\n\n**Return EXACTLY ONE HTML document.** Do NOT:\n- Duplicate the HTML content\n- Include multiple `<!DOCTYPE html>` tags\n- Append a second copy of the document\n\nOutput structure must be:\n```html\n<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n<head>...</head>\n<body>...</body>\n</html>\n<!-- END - Nothing after this -->\n```\n\nIf you catch yourself duplicating content, STOP and output only the first complete document.\n\n## Engagement Features\n\n1. **Immediate feedback**: Player knows instantly if action was right/wrong\n2. **Visual rewards**: Animations, particles, sounds for success\n3. **Progression**: Levels get progressively harder\n4. **Replayability**: Random elements, multiple paths to success\n5. **Challenge variety**: Different objectives (speed, accuracy, efficiency)\n6. **High scores**: Track best performance\n\n## Output Format\n\nReturn ONLY the HTML document, no markdown fences or explanations.\n\n## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n\n- [ ] Game is INTERACTIVE, not just a quiz\n- [ ] Player CONTROLS something meaningful\n- [ ] Simulation (if present) is part of gameplay, not decoration\n- [ ] Success depends on player SKILL, not just knowledge\n- [ ] **Fair Start: Player cannot fail in first 3-5 seconds**\n- [ ] **Initial parameters allow survival with default settings**\n- [ ] Visual feedback is immediate and clear\n- [ ] Game is FUN to play (would you play it more than once?)\n- [ ] Learning happens through PLAY, not through questions\n- [ ] Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n- [ ] Clear instructions at game start\n- [ ] Achievement system provides motivation\n- [ ] **NO DUPLICATED HTML** - exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>` tag\n- [ ] Game objects are VISIBLE and not hidden under UI overlays\n- [ ] Positioning accounts for control panel and HUD heights\n\n## Critical Technical Requirements (MANDATORY)\n\n### 1. Event Binding: Use Inline onclick for Start Button\n**ALWAYS use inline onclick for the game start button.** This is more reliable than addEventListener.\n\n```html\n<!-- CORRECT: Inline onclick - guaranteed to work -->\n<button onclick=\"startGame()\">开始游戏</button>\n\n<!-- WRONG: addEventListener can fail if script has errors -->\n<button id=\"start-btn\">开始游戏</button>\n<script>\n  // If any error occurs before this line, click does nothing\n  document.getElementById('start-btn').addEventListener('click', startGame);\n</script>\n```\n\n**Rule**: For critical game-start buttons, use inline onclick. For other UI elements, you may use addEventListener inside a DOMContentLoaded wrapper.\n\n### 2. CSS: Prefer Custom CSS Over Tailwind CDN\n**Use custom CSS instead of Tailwind CDN for game widgets.** Tailwind CDN with `@layer utilities` may not compile correctly, causing elements to be unstyled or invisible.\n\n```html\n<!-- CORRECT: Custom CSS - reliable and predictable -->\n<style>\n  .game-button { background: #3498db; padding: 12px 30px; }\n</style>\n\n<!-- WRONG: Tailwind @layer utilities may fail -->\n<style type=\"text/tailwindcss\">\n  @layer utilities { .game-button { @apply bg-blue-500 px-6; } }\n</style>\n```\n\n**Exception**: You may use basic Tailwind utility classes (like `flex`, `text-center`) directly on elements, but avoid `@layer utilities` blocks.\n\n### 3. Script Placement: Wrap in DOMContentLoaded or Place at End\n**Either wrap the entire game script in DOMContentLoaded, or place it at the very end of body.**\n\n```html\n<!-- Option A: DOMContentLoaded wrapper -->\n<script>\ndocument.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {\n  // All game code here - elements are guaranteed to exist\n  const canvas = document.getElementById('gameCanvas');\n  function startGame() { ... }\n});\n</script>\n\n<!-- Option B: Script at end of body (after all elements) -->\n</body>\n<!-- No elements after this point -->\n</html>\n```\n\n### 4. Global Functions for onclick Handlers\n**Functions called by inline onclick must be globally accessible.**\n\n```javascript\n// CORRECT: Define function globally (outside DOMContentLoaded)\nlet state = null;\nfunction init() {\n  state = { gameActive: false, startTime: null };\n}\n\nfunction startGame() {\n  init(); // Construct state before any field access or level setup.\n  document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.add('hidden');\n  state.gameActive = true;\n  state.startTime = Date.now();\n  initLevel();\n  render(); // Render paths call publishCurrentState() directly.\n}\n\nfunction resetGame() {\n  init();\n  initLevel();\n  render();\n}\n\ninit();\nrender(); // Publish initial state even before Start.\n```\n\nIf defining these functions inside DOMContentLoaded instead, expose the handlers with `window.startGame = startGame` and `window.resetGame = resetGame` inside that callback.\n\n### 5. Simple Initialization Flow\n**The game initialization should be simple and direct:**\n\n**Construct the state object before any field access**, including the first render, Start, and reset. Separate construction (for example, `init()`) from transitions on an already constructed state and from level setup (`initLevel()`). If level setup uses state, it also runs after construction. Reset must construct a fresh state before reading or writing its fields. Every render or semantic update path must call `publishCurrentState()` directly, including initialization and reset.\n\n```javascript\nlet state = null;\nfunction init() {\n  state = { gameActive: false, startTime: null };\n}\n\nfunction startGame() {\n  // 1. Construct state, before reading or writing its fields\n  init();\n  // 2. Hide start overlay\n  document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.add('hidden');\n  // 3. Transition the constructed state and initialize the first level\n  state.gameActive = true;\n  state.startTime = Date.now();\n  initLevel();\n  // 4. Render and publish, then start the game loop\n  render();\n  requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);\n}\n\nfunction resetGame() {\n  init();\n  initLevel();\n  render();\n}\n\ninit();\nrender(); // Render paths publish the current state, including before Start.\n```\n\n**Avoid**: Complex dependencies like reading localStorage before events are bound, multiple async operations during init, or chained promises for game start.\n\n\n{{snippet:interactive-observation}}",

                "text": "Create an educational GAME widget for: {{title}}\n\n## Game Type\n\n{{gameType}}\n\n## Description\n\n{{description}}\n\n## Key Points\n\n{{keyPoints}}\n\n## Scoring Configuration\n\n{{scoring}}\n\n## Language\n\n{{languageDirective}}\n\n---\n\nGenerate a FUN, INTERACTIVE HTML game with these MANDATORY features:\n\n### Game Design (CRITICAL - NOT A QUIZ!)\n1. **Interactive gameplay**: Player MUST control something meaningful (NOT just click answers)\n2. **Real game mechanics**: Timing, aiming, dragging, balancing, catching, or building\n3. **Skill-based success**: Outcome depends on player action, not just correct answer\n4. **Engaging feedback**: Animations, sounds, visual effects for actions\n\n### Preferred Game Types (in order of preference)\n1. **Physics/Action**: Control parameters to achieve a goal (land safely, hit target, balance)\n2. **Timing/Aim**: Click at right moment or adjust aim to succeed\n3. **Drag-and-drop**: Sort, arrange, or build by dragging elements\n4. **Simulation game**: Let player experiment with variables to find solution\n5. **Card/Match**: Memory or matching games\n6. **Quiz**: ONLY as last resort - make it visually interesting\n\n### Simulation Integration (if game has visual simulation)\n- Simulation MUST be interactive (player controls something)\n- Simulation physics MUST match what player is learning\n- Visual feedback MUST show player's progress toward goal\n- Example: Don't ask \"What thrust?\" → LET PLAYER ADJUST thrust and see result!\n\n### Game Elements\n1. **Clear objective**: \"Land safely\", \"Hit the target\", \"Sort correctly\"\n2. **Player controls**: Sliders, buttons, drag areas, or click targets\n3. **Real-time feedback**: Score, progress bar, visual indicators\n4. **Levels or challenges**: Progressive difficulty\n5. **Achievement system**: Unlockable badges for accomplishments\n6. **Replay value**: Random elements or multiple solutions\n\n### Visual Design\n1. Attractive theme matching the subject\n2. Clear UI for controls and feedback\n3. Animations for success/failure\n4. Responsive layout (mobile + desktop)\n\n### Technical (MANDATORY)\n1. **Inline onclick for start button**: `<button onclick=\"startGame()\">开始</button>` - NOT addEventListener\n2. **Custom CSS preferred**: Avoid Tailwind `@layer utilities` blocks; use plain CSS\n3. **DOMContentLoaded wrapper**: Wrap game code in `document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', ...)`\n4. **Global start function**: `function startGame()` must be callable from onclick\n5. Embedded `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">`\n6. `requestAnimationFrame` for smooth animations\n7. Touch-friendly controls (min 44px touch targets)\n8. localStorage for progress/high scores\n9. Pause functionality\n\n### Output\nReturn ONLY the HTML document. Make the game FUN enough that students want to play again!",

visionImages?: Array<{ id: string; src: string }> } {\n  let availableImagesText = 'No images available';\n  let visionImages: Array<{ id: string; src: string }> | undefined;\n\n  if (pdfImages && pdfImages.length > 0) {\n    if (context.visionEnabled && context.imageMapping) {\n      const sortedImages = sortDocumentImagesForVision(pdfImages);\n      const allWithSrc = sortedImages.filter((image) => context.imageMapping![image.id]);\n      const visionSlice = allWithSrc.slice(0, MAX_VISION_IMAGES);\n      const textOnlySlice = allWithSrc.slice(MAX_VISION_IMAGES);\n      const noSrcImages = sortedImages.filter((image) => !context.imageMapping![image.id]);\n\n      const visionDescriptions = visionSlice.map((image) => formatImagePlaceholder(image));\n      const textDescriptions = [...textOnlySlice, ...noSrcImages].map((image) =>\n        formatImageDescription(image),\n      );\n      availableImagesText = [...visionDescriptions, ...textDescriptions].join('\\n');\n\n      visionImages = visionSlice.map((image) => ({\n        id: image.id,\n        src: context.imageMapping![image.id],\n        width: image.width,\n        height: image.height,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      availableImagesText = pdfImages.map((image) => formatImageDescription(image)).join('\\n');\n    }\n  }\n\n  return { availableImagesText, visionImages };\n}\n\n/** Build the byte-stable system and user prompts for outline generation. */\nexport function buildOutlinePrompt(\n  requirements: UserRequirements,\n  context: OutlinePromptContext = {},\n): { system: string; user: string } {\n  const { pdfText, pdfImages } = context;\n  const { availableImagesText } = buildAvailableImages(pdfImages, context);\n\n  const userProfileText =\n    requirements.userNickname || requirements.userBio\n      ? `## Student Profile\\n\\nStudent: ${requirements.userNickname || 'Unknown'}${requirements.userBio ? ` — ${requirements.userBio}` : ''}\\n\\nConsider this student's background when designing the course. Adapt difficulty, examples, and teaching approach accordingly.\\n\\n---`\n      : '';\n\n  const imageEnabled = context.imageGenerationEnabled ?? false;\n  const videoEnabled = context.videoGenerationEnabled ?? false;\n  const mediaEnabled = imageEnabled || videoEnabled;\n  const hasSourceImages = (pdfImages?.length ?? 0) > 0;\n\n  const prompts = buildPrompt(PROMPT_IDS.REQUIREMENTS_TO_OUTLINES, {\n    requirement: requirements.requirement,\n    pdfContent: pdfText ? pdfText.substring(0, MAX_PDF_CONTENT_CHARS) : 'None',\n    availableImages: availableImagesText,\n    userProfile: userProfileText,\n    hasSourceImages,\n    imageEnabled,\n    videoEnabled,\n    mediaEnabled,\n    researchContext: context.researchContext || 'None',\n    teacherContext: context.teacherContext || '',\n  });\n\n  if (!prompts) {\n    throw new Error('Prompt template not found');\n  }\n\n  return prompts;\n}\n\n/** Generate scene outlines from user requirements. */\nexport async function generateSceneOutlinesFromRequirements(\n  requirements: UserRequirements,\n  pdfText: string | undefined,\n  pdfImages: PdfImage[] | undefined,\n  aiCall: AICallFn,\n  options?: OutlineGenerationOptions,\n): Promise<\n  GenerationResult<{ languageDirective: string; courseTitle?: string; outlines: SceneOutline[] }>\n> {\n  const logger = options?.logger ?? noopGenerationLogger;\n  const context: OutlinePromptContext = { ...options, pdfText, pdfImages };\n  let prompts: { system: string; user: string };\n\n  try {\n    prompts = buildOutlinePrompt(requirements, context);\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error instanceof Error && error.message === 'Prompt template not found') {\n      return { success: false, error: 'Prompt template not found' };\n    }\n    throw error;\n  }\n\n  const { visionImages } = buildAvailableImages(pdfImages, context);\n\n  try {\n    const response = await aiCall(prompts.system, prompts.user, visionImages);\n    const parsed = parseJsonResponse<\n      { languageDirective: string; courseTitle?: string; outlines: SceneOutline[] } | SceneOutline[]\n    >(response, { logger });\n\n    let languageDirective: string;\n    let courseTitle: string | undefined;\n    let rawOutlines: SceneOutline[];\n\n    if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {\n      languageDirective = DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE;\n      rawOutlines = parsed;\n    } else if (parsed && parsed.outlines) {\n      languageDirective = parsed.languageDirective || DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE;\n      const rawTitle = parsed.courseTitle;\n      courseTitle =\n        typeof rawTitle === 'string' && rawTitle.trim() ? rawTitle.trim().slice(0, 120) : undefined;\n      rawOutlines = parsed.outlines;\n    } else {\n      return { success: false, error: 'Failed to parse scene outlines response' };\n    }\n\n    if (!Array.isArray(rawOutlines)) {\n      return { success: false, error: 'Failed to parse scene outlines response' };\n    }\n\n    const enriched = rawOutlines.map((outline, index) => ({\n      ...outline,\n      id: outline.id || nanoid(),\n      order: index + 1,\n      // LLMs occasionally emit mediaGenerations as a string or object; every\n      // downstream consumer requires an array, so drop non-array values here.\n      ...(Array.isArray(outline.mediaGenerations) ? null : { mediaGenerations: undefined }),\n    }));\n\n    const result = uniquifyMediaElementIds(enriched);\n\n    return { success: true, data: { languageDirective, courseTitle, outlines: result } };\n  } catch (error) {\n    return { success: false, error: String(error) };\n  }\n}\n\nexport function sanitizeProceduralSkillOutline(outline: SceneOutline): SceneOutline {\n  const widgetOutline = { ...(outline.widgetOutline ?? {}) };\n  delete widgetOutline.procedureType;\n  delete widgetOutline.task;\n  delete widgetOutline.tools;\n  delete widgetOutline.steps;\n  delete widgetOutline.successCriteria;\n  delete widgetOutline.errorConsequences;\n\n  return {\n    ...outline,\n    type: 'interactive',\n    widgetType: 'diagram',\n    description: outline.description\n      ? `${outline.description} Present this as a process or structure diagram.`\n      : 'Present this topic as a process or structure diagram.',\n    widgetOutline,\n  };\n}\n\nexport function applyOutlineFallbacks(\n  outline: SceneOutline,\n  hasLanguageModel: boolean,\n  options: OutlineFallbackOptions = {},\n): SceneOutline {\n  const logger = options.logger ?? noopGenerationLogger;\n  const hasWidgetConfig = outline.widgetType && outline.widgetOutline;\n\n  if (outline.widgetType === 'procedural-skill' && !options.allowProceduralSkill) {\n    logger.warn(\n      `Procedural-skill outline \"${outline.title}\" is not enabled, falling back to diagram`,\n    );\n    return sanitizeProceduralSkillOutline(outline);\n  }\n\n  if (outline.type === 'interactive' && !outline.interactiveConfig && !hasWidgetConfig) {\n    logger.warn(\n      `Interactive outline \"${outline.title}\" missing interactiveConfig and widget config, falling back to slide`,\n    );\n    return { ...outline, type: 'slide' };\n  }\n  if (outline.type === 'pbl' && (!outline.pblConfig || !hasLanguageModel)) {\n    logger.warn(\n      `PBL outline \"${outline.title}\" missing pblConfig or languageModel, falling back to slide`,\n    );\n    return { ...outline, type: 'slide' };\n  }\n  return outline;\n}",

(withoutNulls(widgetOutline) as SceneOutline['widgetOutline'])\n      : undefined,\n  }) as SceneOutline;\n}\n\n/**\n * The outline in its normal form, or why it cannot be one: not 1 to\n * {@link MAX_OUTLINE_SCENES} scenes, over {@link MAX_OUTLINE_JSON_BYTES},\n * or a scene without a usable id, type or order (ids and orders unique).\n */\nexport function normalizeSceneOutlines(value: unknown): NormalizedOutlines {\n  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length === 0 || value.length > MAX_OUTLINE_SCENES) {\n    return {\n      ok: false,\n      message: `outlines must be an array of 1 to ${MAX_OUTLINE_SCENES} scene outlines`,\n    };\n  }\n  const tooLarge = {\n    ok: false as const,\n    message: `outlines may be at most ${MAX_OUTLINE_JSON_BYTES} bytes of JSON`,\n  };\n  if (jsonBytes(value) > MAX_OUTLINE_JSON_BYTES) return tooLarge;\n  let outlines: SceneOutline[];\n  try {\n    outlines = value.map(sceneOutline);\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error instanceof OutlineRefused) return { ok: false, message: error.message };\n    throw error;\n  }\n  if (new Set(outlines.map((outline) => outline.id)).size !== outlines.length) {\n    return { ok: false, message: 'outlines must not repeat an id' };\n  }\n  if (new Set(outlines.map((outline) => outline.order)).size !== outlines.length) {\n    return { ok: false, message: 'outlines must not repeat an order' };\n  }\n  // The normal form is measured too, so what normalizing yields always\n  // normalizes again.\n  if (jsonBytes(outlines) > MAX_OUTLINE_JSON_BYTES) return tooLarge;\n  return { ok: true, value: outlines };\n}",

              "content": "## Visual Quality Standard for ALL Interactive Widgets (shared)\n\nA widget that \"works\" but looks like a 2005 dashboard fails this pipeline as much as a widget that crashes. Apply the course design directive (see \"Design Directive\" in the user prompt) to every widget.\n\n### Palette discipline\n\n- Use those exact colors from the design directive for: page/canvas background, primary accents, text, and semantic states. Do not invent new hues per element.\n- One background treatment across all views; one accent hue doing the highlighting. 60% neutral / 30% secondary / 10% accent, never the accent everywhere.\n- Text contrast: body text ≥ 4.5:1 against its actual background (count tint overlays). Never light text on mid-tone backgrounds. If uncertain, darken the surface, not the text.\n- On dark surfaces, never full-screen linear gradients (they band); use a solid base + one or two radial gradient glows at 12–25% opacity. Tint neutrals (#s like #1a1f2e, #e8ecf4) toward the accent hue — dead #333337111 grays look undesigned.\n\n### Layout & depth\n\n- Largest-to-smallest hierarchy is visible in 2 seconds: one hero element (number, headline, chart) per view; labels < 16px only for metadata.\n- Cards use 12–20px radii, 2–4px borders or soft shadows — web UI values are invisible at classroom projection distance, so scale up: body text ≥ 16px on mobile-safe layouts, ≥ 20px on main surfaces, padding ≥ 24px between zones.\n- Every scene (state) needs at least two focal points the eye can travel between — a single floating text block is a failure.\n- Backgrounds are never empty: add 2–5 subtle decorative layers (accent-tinted radial glow, oversized faded keyword at 3–8% opacity, hairline grid, muted panel) so whitespace looks intentional.\n- Icons: use inline SVG (project/stroke style, 2px round-cap strokes, viewBox 0 0 24 24). No emoji as primary informação — emoji only inside achievement/reward badges.\n\n### Motion has meaning\n\n- Decorative elements get one ambient animation (breathing glow, slow drift, gentle rotation) so nothing reads static; shared across them is fine.\n- State changes animate ~200–300ms `ease-out` (entrances), `ease-in` (exits); reveal beats stagger children 50–120ms apart. Springs for direct manipulation only.\n- Numbers count up to their value (~0.8–1.2s, `power2.out`) when they enter; progress bars/donuts draw when revealed, not before.\n- No animation is longer than 600ms except cinematic reveals the directive's motionPersonality explicitly asks for. \"The best motion is barely noticeable.\"\n- All motion must be deterministic: no `Date.now()` state in published observations, no unseeded randomness inside rendered results.             "input": {
              "content": "# Motion-Graphic Explainer Generator (Course Intro \"Trailer\")\n\nGenerate a self-contained HTML motion-graphic explainer — a cinematic, animated opening scene for an online course, in the style of premium product-launch motion graphics (kinetic typography, hero stats, icon choreography, SVG path draws).\n\n**This is the FIRST scene of the course: its job is to HOOK the learner in 20–45 seconds and make them want to continue.** Motion is the message; there is no narrator audio inside the widget — the teacher (outside the iframe) narrates over it.\n\n## Story Shape (4 phases — follow exactly)\n\nBuild ONE master timeline with 4 labeled phases. Each phase is one idea. Total on-screen duration 25–45 s:\n\n| Phase | Label | Duration | Job |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1. HOOK | `p0` | 6–10 s | Open with the question, paradox, or stakes of the topic. A *wait, what?* moment — never \"Welcome to course X\". One bold statement, a moving visual, an intriguing number. |\n| 2. TEASE | `p1` | 7–12 s | Sketch the territory the course covers: 3–4 keyword cards or icons snap/chase in, a comparison or a map of the problem space. Sets expectation, not detail. |\n| 3. SPARK | `p2` | 8–14 s | The signature visual moment: one idea animated beautifully — the concept as a moving infographic (orbit, build-up, transformation, count-up, path draw). This is the beat people remember. |\n| 4. TITLE | `p3` | 5–8 s | Course title lockup: assemble/inch to final position, then everything settles into a calm LOOPING ambient state (breathing glow, drifting particles) for as long as the scene stays open. |\n\n**Content rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE):**\n- Ground EVERYTHING in the topic from Scene Information. Real keywords, real numbers (mark hypothetical ones as \"example\"), real terminology in the course language.\n- Max ~2-8 words per card; readable in 1.5 s. The learner reads while the teacher speaks.\n- No fake claims about the course (\"best course ever\", fake student counts). No teacher identity. Short captions in the teaching language (`{{languageCounter}}`-based rules do not apply — this template has no per-locale counter; harm none: use the `languageDirective` from Scene Information).\n- No photographic assets, no external images (except CDNs listed below). Everything is CSS/SVG/typography. This keeps generation cheap and offline-safe.\n\n## Master Design Skill (motion doctrine — read carefully)\n\n### Easing is emotion, not technique\n\n- `.out` eases for entrances (starts fast, decelerates — confident). `.in` for exits. `.inOut` for repositioning. Sine for ambient loops. **Linear only for rotation, ticks, progress** — never for spatial movement.\n- Durations: micro (0.15–0.3s) = energy; standard (0.3–0.5s) = professional; slow (0.5–0.8s) = gravity; very slow (0.8–1.6s) = cinematic. Vary: the slowest tween in a phase should be ≥ 3× the fastest. Never default everything to one duration.\n- Exits are 30–50% FASTER than entrances. Overshoot-and-settle (`back.out(1.4)`) for playful entries; `expo.out` for confident reveals; `elastic.out(1, 0.5)` sparingly.\n\n### Choreography\n\n- Stagger children 60–140ms apart; keep a whole stagger sequence under 500ms. The element that moves FIRST reads as most important — lead with the hero.\n- One ambient motion per phase (breathing glow, slow drift, subtle scale) — attached to the seekable timeline, never a bare `gsap.to()` outside it.\n- Vary entrance directions across elements (from left / from right / scale-up / blur-in / letter-spacing). Repeating `y:30 + fade` for everything is a failure.\n- Scene structure per phase: **build** (elements enter, first 30%) → **breathe** (hold, ambient alive, middle 40%) → **resolve** (exit or hand off, last 30%). No dead air, no abrupt stops.\n- Never run two independent tweens on the SAME element+property concurrently; if one element needs an entrance AND a continuous motion, combine in a single `fromTo()` or nest (parent gets entrance, child gets the loop).\n- Prefer `tl.fromTo()` over `tl.from()` — deterministic under phase seeking.\n\n### Kinetic typography (main technique toolbox)\n\n| Effect | How |\n|---|---|\n| Sequential word reveal | Words pop one-by-one, 80–150ms apart, slight overshoot |\n| Expressive scale | The KEY word jumps to 130–160% scale + accent color, others dim |\n| Typewriter / mask reveal | Clip-path inset or width reveal left→right |\n| Gradient-text sweep | Shimmering gradient across large headline (sparingly) |\n| Letter-spacing settle | Wide tracking → tight tracking as word lands |\n| 3D flip / rotate entrance | `rotationX/Y` with `transformPerspective: 1200` |\n| Path draw | SVG `strokeDashoffset` to 0 over 0.6–1.2s (logos, arrows, connectors) |\n| Count-up | Number for 0→target, ~1s, `power2.out`, snap:true integers |\n| Progress bar / donut fill | scaleX or stroke draw when revealed |\n\n### Composition (frames are scenes, not web pages)\n\n- Fill the stage: hero text spans 60–80% of width, entrance padding 60–140px.\n- ≥ 2 focal points per phase so the eye travels; anchor content to edges or split into zones — not everything centered-floating.\n- ≥ 3 layers per phase: background treatment (radial accent glow, oversized ghost word at 3–8% opacity, subtle grid/panel) + midground content + foreground accents (hairline rules that `scaleX` from 0, index labels, tick marks).\n- Scale: headlines 56–120px (weight 700–900, tight tracking); key words 34–48px; labels 16–22px; borders 2–4px; decorative opacity 12–25%. Use `clamp()` and `vw/vmin` units so it scales inside any iframe size.\n\n## Design Directive\n\nThe Scene Information contains a **Design Directive** (palette, mood, motion personality). It is LAW:\n\n- Background is the directive's `background` mode (dark builds feel cinematic; light builds need bold 2px+ structural elements and full-saturation accent hits to avoid the blank-slide feel).\n- Use the directive's `palette` hexes only. Map: `palette[0]` → base/background or the darkest neutral, then text/high-contrast neutrals stay within ±10 lightness of the palette's neutrals; the accent (brightest/most saturated) is the 10% — HOOK keyword, hero number, draw strokes, glow.\n- `motionPersonality` sets the tween voice: `playful` → overshoot/elastic, 20–30% exaggeration; `premium` → slow calm eases, zero overshoot, generous whitespace; `energetic` → fast cuts, hard snaps, high stagger; `calm` → long holds, gentle sine ambient; `storytelling` → front-load the SPARK phase.\n- If the directive is missing or incomplete, choose ONE coherent system yourself (declare bg / text / accent before writing CSS), and keep it across every phase.\n\n**Do NOT:** gradient text everywhere, cyan-on-dark cliché, neon-on-neon, pure `#000`/`#fff`, identical repeated cards, more than one gradient text effect per phase. Tint neutrals toward the palette.\n\n## Technical Contract (MANDATORY)\n\n### 1. Deterministic timeline\n\n```html\n<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n<head>\n  <!-- GSAP via CDN (same allowance as 3D widgets) -->\n  <script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js\"></script>\n  <style> /* all custom CSS inline, fonts = system stacks only */ </style>\n</head>\n<body>\n  <div id=\"experiment\"> <!-- the whole scene inside this wrapper -->\n    ...\n    <script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\"> ... </script>\n    <script> /* all JS */ </script>\n  </div>\n</body>\n</html>\n```\n\n- ONE master timeline: `const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: false })` with **labels `p0`…`p3`** at each phase boundary.\n- Total active timeline ~25–45 s. After the TITLE phase, append a repeating ambient block: `tl.to(..., { ..., repeat: -1 }, 'amb')` is FORBIDDEN on the master (it would stall phase seeking) — instead build a separate `ambientTl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true, repeat: -1 })` and start it when the master completes (`tl.eventCallback('onComplete', () => ambientTl.play())`). Ambient changes nothing that phases depend on.\n- **No `Date.now()` for animation state, no `Math.random()` inside the timeline** (seeded jitter in decorative particles is allowed: `gsap.utils.random` with a fixed seed or precomputed offsets). Everything visible must be a pure function of timeline position so Replay and phase-seek are exact.\n- Fallback without network: wrap usage — if `typeof gsap === 'undefined'`, add class `no-anim` to `<body>`. CSS: `.no-anim [data-step]{opacity:1;transform:none}` and skip timeline creation. Content must be fully readable, statically laid out, with the HTML static fallback (a static poster) — never a blank iframe.\n- No audio, no video tags, no fetch(), no localStorage, no timers/runnning loops outside the timelines.\n\n### 2. Phase control API (REQUIRED)\n\nExpose a global so the platform and the phase dots can drive the story:\n\n```javascript\nwindow.setExplainerPhase = function (phase) {\n  // phase is 'p0'..'p3' (or number index)\n  ambientTl.pause();\n  tl.seek(phase, false);\n  tl.play();\n};\nwindow.explainerGetState = function () {\n  return { phase: currentPhase(), progress: tl.mediaTimeSafe ? 0 : tl.totalProgress() };\n};\n```\n\n- On `message` events, honor `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with `state.phase` → `window.setExplainerPhase(state.phase)`. Also accept `{ state: { replay: true } }` → restart (`tl.restart()`).\n- In-iframe controls (always visible, small, bottom-center): phase dots `#phase-dots` (button per phase, `id=\"phase-dot-p0\"` etc., current highlighted) + a replay button `id=\"replay-btn\"`. Clicking → `setExplainerPhase` / restart. 44px touch targets.\n\n### 3. Observation contract\n\n{{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n\nFor this widget publish:\n```json\n{ \"summary\": \"Phase 2 (Spark): the solar system race is animating\", \"state\": { \"phase\": \"p2\", \"phaseIndex\": 2 }, \"beats\": [ {\"id\":\"p0\",\"label\":\"Hook\"}, ... ] }\n```\nPublish on load, on every phase change (`tl.call(publishCurrentState, [], tl, 'p1')` at each label) and after any seek. Include the phase label list once in `state.beats`.\n\n### 4. widget-config (widget-config REQUIRED)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"animation-explainer\",\n  \"concept\": \"<topic concept>\",\n  \"description\": \"<what this animation covers>\",\n  \"beats\": [{ \"id\": \"p0\", \"label\": \"Hook name\" }, { \"id\": \"p1\", \"label\": \"...\" }, { \"id\": \"p2\", \"label\": \"...\" }, { \"id\": \"p3\", \"label\": \"Title\" }],\n  \"mood\": \"<motionPersonality>\"\n}\n```\n\n### 5. Robustness (cheap-model safety net)\n\n- Script at end of body; all setup inside one IIFE or DOMContentLoaded; **no top-level `await`**; syntax must be ES5-safe-ish (no optional chaining needed) so the validator never rejects it.\n- SVG: inline only, `viewBox` set, no external URLs. Animate with GSAP (`strokeDashoffset`, `scale`, `opacity`), never CSS `@keyframes` conflicts with GSAP on the same element.\n- No duplicated documents: exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>`; output the document once.\n- Keep total output < ~25 KB of CSS + ~15 KB of JS. Leverage CSS custom properties for the palette.\n\n## Output Format (CRITICAL)\n\nReturn ONLY one complete HTML document, no markdown fences, no prose.\n\n## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n\n- [ ] 4 phases with labels p0–p3 present in the master timeline; total 25–45 s\n- [ ] HOOK is a question/stakes/paradox grounded in THIS topic — not a welcome slide\n- [ ] Real topic keywords and (example-safe) numbers; the course language is used\n- [ ] Palette = the design directive; bg mode respected; one accent discipline; contrast ≥ 4.5:1\n- [ ] ≥ 3 entrance easing values; ≥ 3 entrance directions; stagger ≤ 500ms; exits faster than entrances\n- [ ] Background decoration ≥ 3 treatments across phases (glow, ghost type, rules/grid)\n- [ ] `window.setExplainerPhase` + `SET_WIDGET_STATE` routing + `#phase-dots` + `#replay-btn` work\n- [ ] `data-maic-observation` publishes phase on load and at every phase label ({{snippet:motion-observation-note}})\n- [ ] widget-config JSON: type `animation-explainer`, `beats` matches phase labels\n- [ ] Offline/static fallback (`no-anim`) leaves content readable; no blank screen\n- [ ] Deterministic: replay produces the exact same animation\n",
              "filePath": "/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md"

              "content": "/**\n * Per-course visual design directive: the shared design language every scene\n * of one course generates under (palette, mood, motion personality). Inferred\n * once by the outline stage from the requirement, materials and research\n * context, then threaded through slide, quiz and widget content generation so\n * a course never again defaults to one shared \"PowerPoint blue\" look.\n */\n\nexport interface DesignDirective {\n  /** One line describing the intended visual mood, e.g. \"cinematic dark-mode physics lab\". */\n  concept: string;\n  /**\n   * 2-5 hex colors, first entry intended as the base/background or darkest\n   * neutral, last as the accent. All scene generation uses only these.\n   */\n  palette: string[];\n  /** Whether scene backgrounds lean dark or light. */\n  background: 'dark' | 'light';\n  /**\n   * Tween voice for motion: playful / premium / energetic / calm /\n   * storytelling. Widgets and (when supported) slide animation cues read it.\n   */\n  motionPersonality:\n    | 'playful'\n    | 'premium'\n    | 'energetic'\n    | 'calm'\n    | 'storytelling';\n}\n\nconst HEX_COLOR_RE = /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/;\nconst PERSONALITIES: DesignDirective['motionPersonality'][] = [\n  'playful',\n  'premium',\n  'energetic',\n  'calm',\n  'storytelling',\n];\n\nfunction clampText(value: unknown, maxLength: number): string | undefined {\n  if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined;\n  const trimmed = value.trim();\n  return trimmed ? trimmed.slice(0, maxLength) : undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Validate and normalize a model-provided design directive. Returns null when\n * the value is absent or wholly unusable (callers fall back to their own\n * defaults rather than failing generation over styling).\n */\nexport function normalizeDesignDirective(\n  value: unknown,\n): DesignDirective | null {\n  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const raw = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n\n  const concept = clampText(raw.concept, 200);\n  const conceptFromStyle =\n    concept ??\n    (typeof raw.style === 'string' && raw.style.trim()\n      ? clampText(raw.style, 200)\n      : undefined);\n\n  const palette = Array.isArray(raw.palette)\n    ? raw.palette\n        .filter(\n          (entry): entry is string => typeof entry === 'string' && HEX_COLOR_RE.test(entry.trim()),\n        )\n        .map((entry) => entry.trim().toLowerCase())\n        .filter((entry, index, list) => list.indexOf(entry) === index)\n        .slice(0, 5)\n    : [];\n\n  const background =\n    raw.background === 'dark' || raw.background === 'light' ? raw.background : undefined;\n\n  const personality = PERSONALITIES.find((candidate) => candidate === raw.motionPersonality);\n\n  const directive: DesignDirective = {\n    ...(conceptFromStyle ? { concept: conceptFromStyle } : { concept: '' }),\n    ...(palette.length > 0 ? { palette } : { palette: [] }),\n    ...(background ? { background } : { background: 'dark' }),\n    ...(personality ? { motionPersonality: personality } : { motionPersonality: 'calm' }),\n  };\n\n  // Wholly unusable (nothing but defaults): treat as absent so the prompt\n  // falls back to self-selection instead of asserting an empty directive.\n  if (!conceptFromStyle && palette.length === 0 && !background && !personality) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  return directive;\n}\n\n/** The fallback used when the outline stage produced no usable directive. */\nexport const FALLBACK_DESIGN_DIRECTIVE: DesignDirective = {\n  concept: '',\n  palette: [],\n  background: 'dark',\n  motionPersonality: 'calm',\n};\n\n/**\n * Render a directive into the text block scene prompts consume. Always\n * non-empty: without a directive it instructs the model to design one\n * coherent system itself, appended by the scene-generation context.\n */\nexport function formatDesignDirective(directive: DesignDirective | null | undefined): string {\n  if (!directive) {\n    return 'None. Before writing any scene: declare ONE coherent design system yourself (background mode, text color, one accent hue, motion personality) that suits the topic, and apply it consistently across every scene you generate this course.';\n  }\n  const lines: string[] = [];\n  if (directive.concept) lines.push(`- Visual mood: ${directive.concept}`);\n  if (directive.palette.length > 0) {\n    lines.push(`- Palette (use ONLY these hexes): ${directive.palette.join(', ')}`);\n  }\n  lines.push(`- Background mode: ${directive.background}`);\n  lines.push(`- Motion personality: ${directive.motionPersonality}`);\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n",
              "filePath": "/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts"

          "text": "## Objective\n- Make OpenMAIC lesson generation \"100x better\": add a motion-graphic explainer as every lesson's first scene (Opus-5.5/hyperframe style, producible by a cheap model via a distilled \"master skill\"), upgrade all scene prompts with a per-course design system (palette/icons/infographics/motion), and add Fish Audio TTS with free-text voice-ID entry in settings.\n- Document plan + implementation for rollback; runOutlineStep ~768-900 emits `outline_language_directive`/`outline_item` events), `lib/server/generation/run/types.ts` `GenerationRunOutline` (~line 114), `lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts` (OutlineResult at ~340; head-regex extractors; final parse post-stream — extract designDirective from full buffer with balanced-brace scan, no new SSE event type), `lib/server/generation/steps/scene-content.ts` (languageDirective at 57/79/301), `lib/server/agent-runtime/generation-tools.ts` (423/481/567 use `doc.stage.languageDirective`), `lib/server/generation/outline-schema.ts` (imports `WIDGET_TYPES` from `@openmaic/dsl` — new widget type auto-passes validation).\n  - Stage DSL: `packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/stage.ts:148` has `languageDirective?: string` — add `designDirective?: string` there too.\n  - Widget contract: HTML iframe, `postProcessInteractiveHtml`, `findInteractiveScriptSyntaxFailure`, widget-config JSON via `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">`; teacher actions `INTERACTIVE_WIDGET_ACTIONS = [widget_highlight, widget_setState, widget_annotation, widget_reveal]`.\n  - Animation-explainer contract (decided): deterministic GSAP CDN timeline with phase labels `p0`–`p3` (HOOK→TEASE→SPARK→TITLE, 25–45s), separate `ambientTl` repeat loop started onAnimationComplete, `window.setExplainerPhase`, `SET_WIDGET_STATE {phase|replay}` routing, `#phase-dots` + `#replay-btn`, `data-maic-observation` publishing `{summary, state:{phase, phaseIndex}, beats}`, `no-anim` static fallback if GSAP missing.\n  - Fish Audio API: `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts`, Bearer token; header `model: s2.1-pro|s2.1-pro-free|s2-pro|drama-3|s1`; body `{text, reference_id (voice model ID), format: mp3|wav|pcm|opus, prosody:{speed}, ...}`; binary audio response; errors 401/402/400/429. D2 per-course `designDirective` `{concept, palette[2-5], background, motionPersonality}` inferred at outline stage, threaded everywhere; D3 master skill = generation snippets + one template; D4 scene 1 of every course MUST be the intro animation-explainer (doesn't count against 1-2 deep-interactive budget); D5 Fish TTS with sample voice presets + free-text voice ID (`setTTSVoice(<id>,'fish-tts')`).\n\n## Work State\n### Completed\n- Plan doc written: `docs/plans/lesson-visual-upgrade.md` (problem, decisions D1–D5, validation, rollback).\n- Research: all 42 URLs + fish.audio API + style references scraped;
