The server\n # warns at startup when stored keys were sealed under a different secret.\n # Instances that share a database also share one persistent data directory\n # (data/, /app/data in the image): uploaded materials are stored there.\n # OPENMAIC_SECRET_KEY=\n \n # --- LLM Providers -----------------------------------------------------------\n # Server-managed credentials authorize only the explicit *_MODELS list and deployment\n # default/fallback or slot model references for that capability. Catalogue models are\n # not implicitly authorized. Set *_MODELS for each provider, then restart the server.\n # Users bringing their own credentials and keyless local providers are unaffected.\n # A provider without a key is unrestricted: do not use one for a gateway that adds its\n # own upstream credential; give the gateway a key and a *_MODELS list instead.\n # Format: {PROVIDER}_API_KEY, {PROVIDER}_BASE_URL (optional), {PROVIDER}_MODELS (required for server-managed model selection, comma-separated)\n # Legacy: without openmaic.yml these configure providers directly. With\n # openmaic.yml they no longer configure providers on their own: reference them\n # from the file as ${VAR} (for example apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}). The TTS,\n # ASR, image, video, PDF and web search variables below work the same way.\n \n OPENAI_API_KEY=\n OPENAI_BASE_URL=\n OPENAI_MODELS=\n # For relays whose non-streaming Chat Completions response is incompatible.\n # Forces custom OpenAI base URLs to use Chat Completions and buffers SSE responses.\n # Has no effect on the official OpenAI base URL. Disabled by default.\n # OPENAI_COMPAT_USE_STREAMING_CHAT=true\n \n # Azure uses deployment names as model IDs.\n AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=\n AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-RESOURCE.openai.azure.com/openai\n AZURE_OPENAI_MODELS=\n \n ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY=\n ATLASCLOUD_BASE_URL=https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1\n # Example: qwen/qwen3.5-flash,deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro\n ATLASCLOUD_MODELS=\n \n ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=\n ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=\n ANTHROPIC_MODELS=\n \n GOOGLE_API_KEY=\n GOOGLE_BASE_URL=\n GOOGLE_MODELS=\n \n DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=\n DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL=\n # Example: deepseek-v4-pro,deepseek-v4-flash,deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp\n DEEPSEEK_MODELS=\n \n QWEN_API_KEY=\n QWEN_BASE_URL=\n QWEN_MODELS=\n \n KIMI_API_KEY=\n KIMI_BASE_URL=\n KIMI_MODELS=\n \n MINIMAX_API_KEY=\n # MiniMax Anthropic-compatible endpoint for the built-in Anthropic SDK integration\n MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1\n # Example: MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed,MiniMax-M2.7,MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed,MiniMax-M2.5\n MINIMAX_MODELS=\n \n GLM_API_KEY=\n GLM_BASE_URL=\n GLM_MODELS=\n \n SILICONFLOW_API_KEY=\n SILICONFLOW_BASE_URL=\n SILICONFLOW_MODELS=\n \n DOUBAO_API_KEY=\n DOUBAO_BASE_URL=\n DOUBAO_MODELS=\n \n OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\n OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\n # Example: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro,deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash\n OPENROUTER_MODELS=\n \n GROK_API_KEY=\n GROK_BASE_URL=\n # Example: grok-4.6,grok-4.5\n GROK_MODELS=\n \n TENCENT_API_KEY=\n # Tencent TokenHub OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Hy3 is a model ID, not an env prefix.\n # TENCENT_HUNYUAN_* is also accepted as an alias.\n TENCENT_BASE_URL=https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1\n # Example: hy3-preview,hunyuan-2.0-thinking-20251109,hunyuan-2.0-instruct-20251111\n TENCENT_MODELS=\n \n XIAOMI_API_KEY=\n # MIMO_* is also accepted as an alias. Use tp-... keys only with Token Plan URLs.\n XIAOMI_BASE_URL=https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1\n # Token Plan regional examples:\n # XIAOMI_BASE_URL=https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1\n # XIAOMI_BASE_URL=https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1\n # XIAOMI_BASE_URL=https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1\n # Example: mimo-v2.6-pro,mimo-v2.6-flash,mimo-v2.5-pro,mimo-v2-pro,mimo-v2.5,mimo-v2-omni,mimo-v2-flash\n XIAOMI_MODELS=\n \n TOKENDANCE_API_KEY=\n # OpenAI-compatible gateway. The same key also works for the image, video, TTS\n # and web-search routes on this host (see the README quick example).\n TOKENDANCE_BASE_URL=https://tokendance.space/gateway/v1\n # Example: deepseek-v4.1-flash,deepseek-v4-pro,glm-5.3,kimi-k3,qwen3.8-max\n TOKENDANCE_MODELS=\n \n OPENCODE_API_KEY=\n # OpenCode Console (https://opencode.ai/docs/zen) OpenAI-compatible gateway.\n # Free models are officially callable only from within the OpenCode client; a\n # Console key serves the paid catalog (and may serve free models for some\n # accounts).\n OPENCODE_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1\n # Example: deepseek-v4.1-flash-free,glm-5.3-flash-free,deepseek-v4.1-flash\n OPENCODE_MODELS=\n \n # --- Ollama (Local Models) ---------------------------------------------------\n # No API key needed. Configure BASE_URL here (server-side) so it bypasses SSRF\n # protection automatically. Client-supplied localhost URLs are blocked in production.\n # OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1\n # OLLAMA_MODELS=llama3.3,llama3.2,qwen2.5,mistral,gemma3\n \n # Lemonade local server (OpenAI-compatible, no API key required)\n # LEMONADE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:13305/v1\n # LEMONADE_MODELS=Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF,Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Hybrid,Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct\n \n # Amazon Bedrock LLMs (no OpenAI-style API key required)\n # Set BEDROCK_REGION to enable Bedrock server-side provider config.\n # AWS credentials are resolved from the standard AWS environment / credential chain.\n # BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1\n # BEDROCK_MODELS=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5,us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8\n # Optional bearer-token authentication or custom Bedrock-compatible endpoint.\n # AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=\n # BEDROCK_API_KEY=\n # BEDROCK_BASE_URL=\n # DEFAULT_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5\n \n # --- TTS (Text-to-Speech) ----------------------------------------------------\n \n TTS_OPENAI_API_KEY=\n TTS_OPENAI_MODELS=\n TTS_OPENAI_BASE_URL=\n \n TTS_AZURE_API_KEY=\n TTS_AZURE_MODELS=\n TTS_AZURE_BASE_URL=\n \n TTS_GLM_API_KEY=\n TTS_GLM_MODELS=\n TTS_GLM_BASE_URL=\n \n TTS_QWEN_API_KEY=\n TTS_QWEN_MODELS=\n TTS_QWEN_BASE_URL=\n # List the voice-clone target in TTS_QWEN_MODELS when using cloned voices.\n # Qwen voice cloning reuses TTS_QWEN_API_KEY. Override the target model if needed.\n # TTS_QWEN_VOICE_CLONE_MODEL=qwen3-tts-vc-2026-01-22\n \n TTS_DOUBAO_API_KEY=\n TTS_DOUBAO_MODELS=\n TTS_DOUBAO_BASE_URL=\n \n TTS_MINIMAX_API_KEY=\n TTS_MINIMAX_MODELS=\n # MiniMax TTS endpoint (speech-2.8 / 2.6 / 02 / 01 series)\n TTS_MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimaxi.com\n TTS_ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=\n TTS_ELEVENLABS_MODELS=\n TTS_ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL=\n \n+# Fish Audio TTS (https://fish.audio). The backend model is the `model` header\n+# (s2.1-pro, s2.1-pro-free, s2-pro, drama-3 or s1); the voice is a voice-model\n+# ID picked in the UI (or pasted from a https://fish.audio/m/<id> page).\n+TTS_FISH_API_KEY=\n+TTS_FISH_MODELS=\n+TTS_FISH_BASE_URL=\n+\n # Google Gemini TTS (Interactions API). Reuse an AI Studio / Gemini API key.\n TTS_GOOGLE_API_KEY=\n TTS_GOOGLE_MODELS=\n TTS_GOOGLE_BASE_URL=\n \n # VoxCPM2 TTS (local, OpenAI-compatible; API key is optional)\n # TTS_VOXCPM_API_KEY=\n # TTS_VOXCPM_MODELS=\n # TTS_VOXCPM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1\n \n # Lemonade TTS (local, no API key required)\n # TTS_LEMONADE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:13305/v1\n \n # Operators can force-disable any built-in TTS provider. Examples:\n # TTS_OPENAI_ENABLED=false\n # TTS_BROWSER_NATIVE_ENABLED=false\n \n # --- ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) --------------------------------------\n \n ASR_OPENAI_API_KEY=\n ASR_OPENAI_MODELS=\n ASR_OPENAI_BASE_URL=\n \n ASR_QWEN_API_KEY=\n ASR_QWEN_MODELS=\n ASR_QWEN_BASE_URL=\n \n ASR_AZURE_API_KEY=\n ASR_AZURE_MODELS=\n ASR_AZURE_BASE_URL=https://{region}.api.cognitive.microsoft.com\n \n # FunASR (local, WAV input only, no API key required)\n # ASR_FUNASR_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1\n \n # Lemonade ASR (local, WAV input only, no API key required)\n # ASR_LEMONADE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:13305/v1\n \n # Operators can force-disable any built-in ASR provider. Examples:\n # ASR_OPENAI_ENABLED=false\n # ASR_BROWSER_NATIVE_ENABLED=false\n \n # Optional local audio/video material extraction uses the first enabled server\n # ASR provider above. It also requires the system `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`\n # executables on PATH; no bundled binary or npm dependency is installed.\n # Without both executables, OpenMAIC skips the local extractor and uses a\n # configured AliDocMind cloud extractor when available. With neither path\n # enabled, media materials fail cleanly with setup guidance.\n \n # --- PDF Processing -----------------------------------------------------------\n \n PDF_UNPDF_API_KEY=\n PDF_UNPDF_BASE_URL=\n \n PDF_MINERU_API_KEY=\n PDF_MINERU_BASE_URL=\n # Optional. Defaults to \"pipeline\"; use \"hybrid-auto-engine\" only when your MinerU\n # service has the required GPU/device configuration.\n PDF_MINERU_BACKEND=\n \n PDF_MINERU_CLOUD_API_KEY=\n PDF_MINERU_CLOUD_BASE_URL=https://mineru.net/api/v4\n # Self-hosted MinerU never falls back to MinerU Cloud implicitly: a request that\n # selects self-hosted MinerU without a configured base URL fails loudly. Set this\n # to \"true\" to explicitly opt in to MinerU Cloud as a fallback (documents then\n # leave your infrastructure). Default: off.\n ALLOW_MINERU_CLOUD_FALLBACK=\n \n # AliDocMind uses an Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pair instead of a single API key.\n ALIDOCMIND_ACCESS_KEY_ID=\n ALIDOCMIND_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET=\n ALIDOCMIND_BASE_URL=\n \n # --- Image Generation ---------------------------------------------------------\n \n IMAGE_OPENAI_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_OPENAI_MODELS=\n IMAGE_OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1\n \n IMAGE_SEEDREAM_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_SEEDREAM_MODELS=\n IMAGE_SEEDREAM_BASE_URL=\n \n IMAGE_QWEN_IMAGE_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_QWEN_IMAGE_MODELS=\n IMAGE_QWEN_IMAGE_BASE_URL=\n \n IMAGE_NANO_BANANA_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_NANO_BANANA_MODELS=\n IMAGE_NANO_BANANA_BASE_URL=\n \n IMAGE_MINIMAX_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_MINIMAX_MODELS=\n # Example models: image-01, image-01-live\n IMAGE_MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimaxi.com\n \n IMAGE_GROK_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_GROK_MODELS=\n IMAGE_GROK_BASE_URL=\n \n IMAGE_GLM_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_GLM_MODELS=\n # Example models: cogview-3-flash, cogview-4\n IMAGE_GLM_BASE_URL=https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4\n \n # OpenRouter image generation. Optional; read at runtime. One key reaches every\n # image model OpenRouter hosts (FLUX, Seedream, GPT Image, Gemini, Qwen Image,\n # Recraft, Krea, ...). The model list in Settings is fetched live from\n # GET /images/models. List the authorized ids in IMAGE_OPENROUTER_MODELS. Base URL defaults to\n # https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 when left blank.\n IMAGE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\n IMAGE_OPENROUTER_MODELS=\n IMAGE_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=\n \n # Lemonade image generation (local, no API key required)\n # IMAGE_LEMONADE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:13305/v1\n \n # Operators can force-disable any built-in image provider, including the\n # client-only ComfyUI provider (it has no credential env). Examples:\n # IMAGE_OPENAI_ENABLED=false\n # IMAGE_COMFYUI_ENABLED=false\n \n # --- Video Generation ---------------------------------------------------------\n \n VIDEO_SEEDANCE_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_SEEDANCE_MODELS=\n VIDEO_SEEDANCE_BASE_URL=\n \n VIDEO_KLING_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_KLING_MODELS=\n VIDEO_KLING_BASE_URL=\n \n VIDEO_VEO_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_VEO_MODELS=\n VIDEO_VEO_BASE_URL=\n \n VIDEO_SORA_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_SORA_BASE_URL=\n \n VIDEO_MINIMAX_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_MINIMAX_MODELS=\n # Example models: MiniMax-Hailuo-2.3, MiniMax-Hailuo-2.3-Fast, MiniMax-Hailuo-02\n VIDEO_MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimaxi.com\n \n VIDEO_GROK_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_GROK_MODELS=\n VIDEO_GROK_BASE_URL=\n \n VIDEO_HAPPYHORSE_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_HAPPYHORSE_MODELS=\n VIDEO_HAPPYHORSE_BASE_URL=https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com\n \n # OpenRouter video generation. Optional; read at runtime. One key reaches every\n # video model OpenRouter hosts (Veo, Kling, Runway, Seedance, Hailuo, Wan,\n # Sora, Grok Imagine, ...). The model list in Settings is fetched live from\n # GET /videos/models. List the authorized ids in VIDEO_OPENROUTER_MODELS. Base URL defaults to\n # https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 when left blank.\n VIDEO_OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\n VIDEO_OPENROUTER_MODELS=\n VIDEO_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=\n \n # Operators can force-disable any built-in video provider. Examples:\n # VIDEO_GROK_ENABLED=false\n # VIDEO_KLING_ENABLED=false\n \n # --- Web Search ---------------------------------------------------------------\n # Note: Grok (xAI) web search is available via chat completions + search tools,\n # not as a standalone search API. Use Grok LLM provider with search_parameters\n # in chat requests. See: https://docs.x.ai/docs/guides/tools/search-tools\n \n TAVILY_API_KEY=\n TAVILY_BASE_URL=\n EXA_API_KEY=\n EXA_BASE_URL=https://api.exa.ai\n BOCHA_API_KEY=\n BOCHA_BASE_URL=https://api.bocha.cn\n BRAVE_API_KEY=\n BRAVE_BASE_URL=\n BAIDU_API_KEY=\n BAIDU_BASE_URL=https://qianfan.baidubce.com\n # Self-hosted SearXNG instance (no API key required)\n SEARXNG_BASE_URL=\n # Dedicated MiniMax web-search vars avoid conflicting with the LLM MINIMAX_* endpoint.\n WEB_SEARCH_MINIMAX_API_KEY=\n WEB_SEARCH_MINIMAX_BASE_URL=https://api.minimaxi.com\n # Dedicated Doubao web-search vars avoid conflicting with the Doubao LLM provider.\n WEB_SEARCH_DOUBAO_API_KEY=\n WEB_SEARCH_DOUBAO_BASE_URL=https://open.feedcoopapi.com\n # Claude (Anthropic) native web search. Dedicated vars avoid conflicting with\n # ANTHROPIC_* LLM provider vars. Set WEB_SEARCH_CLAUDE_MODELS to authorize the\n # search models server-side (first entry is the default), e.g. claude-sonnet-5.\n WEB_SEARCH_CLAUDE_API_KEY=\n WEB_SEARCH_CLAUDE_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com/v1\n WEB_SEARCH_CLAUDE_MODELS=\n \n # Operators can force-disable any built-in web search provider. Examples:\n # TAVILY_ENABLED=false\n # EXA_ENABLED=false\n # WEB_SEARCH_DOUBAO_ENABLED=false\n # SEARXNG_ENABLED=false\n \n # Server-only, default-OFF selector for the Native Child execution harness.\n # OPENMAIC_ENABLE_PI_NATIVE_CHILD_RUNTIME=true\n # Server-only, default-OFF Native Spotlight capability; does not select the runtime.\n # OPENMAIC_ENABLE_PI_NATIVE_CHILD_SPOTLIGHT=true\n \n # --- Feature Flags -----------------------------------------------------------\n \n # Boolean feature flags accept \"true\" or \"1\". NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are compiled\n # into the browser bundle at build time, so changing them requires a rebuild.\n \n # Enable the Pro workbench entry (the workbench also requires the agent\n # runtime to be configured server-side; see the Agent Runtime section).\n # Implies the MAIC Editor gate below — Pro mode always ships with the editor.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_PRO_WORKBENCH_ENABLED=true\n \n # Master gate for the MAIC Editor Pro-mode entry point. Implied by\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_PRO_WORKBENCH_ENABLED; set it alone to enable the classroom\n # editor on a deployment without the workbench.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIC_EDITOR_ENABLED=true\n \n # Select @openmaic/editor inside Pro mode. This does not enable Pro mode by itself.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIC_EDITOR_RENDERER_ENABLED=true\n \n # Use @openmaic/renderer for the classroom playback canvas.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIC_PLAYBACK_RENDERER_ENABLED=true\n \n # Pi-based classroom chat is enabled by default. Set this build-time flag to\n # false or 0 and rebuild to roll back to the legacy classroom chat runtime.\n # Pi requires model/provider tool (function) calling support.\n # Docker Compose's env_file loads .env.local at runtime, not into build args.\n # To rebuild with legacy chat: NEXT_PUBLIC_PI_CHAT_ENABLED=false docker compose up -d --build openmaic\n # Runtime-only changes leave the built client/server choice unchanged.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_PI_CHAT_ENABLED=false\n \n # Enable the unified PPT/Interactive courseware-reference entry in Pi playback.\n # Pi chat and editor element references remain independent from this default-off build-time gate.\n # Changing a NEXT_PUBLIC_* value requires rebuilding the application.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_COURSEWARE_REFERENCE_ENABLED=true\n \n # Enable the server-side vocational task-engine generation path.\n # OPENMAIC_ENABLE_VOCATIONAL=true\n \n # Show the experimental vocational task-engine control in the client.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_VOCATIONAL_TEST_UI=true\n \n # Show the video export and PPTX import entry points.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_VIDEO_EXPORT=true\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_PPTX_IMPORT=true\n \n # Informational destination shown on exported Quiz/PBL cover cards. Unset or\n # blank defaults to open.maic.chat; set to \"off\" to omit it.\n # NEXT_PUBLIC_VIDEO_EXPORT_CTA_DESTINATION=open.maic.chat\n \n # --- Agent Runtime (experimental) ---------------------------------------------\n \n # Server-only gate for durable background agent sessions: the /api/agent\n # session and owner-event control-plane routes plus the in-process session\n # runner. Default OFF — while disabled, every /api/agent/sessions* and\n # /api/agent/owner-events route answers 404. Truthy values are \"true\" or \"1\";\n # anything else (including unset) is treated as disabled.\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_ENABLED=true\n \n # The runtime uses the PostgreSQL connection (DATABASE_URL) from the\n # \"Persistence\" section below, which every deployment configures.\n \n # The agent runs on the `agent` slot of the model configuration (openmaic.yml,\n # or the model settings): a model that supports tool calling. Optional fields\n # on the slot: api (\"openai-completions\", the default, or \"openai-responses\"),\n # contextWindow (pins the window compaction assumes below the catalogue value),\n # and thinking, which must never set effort (the tool-using driver cannot\n # combine reasoning_effort with function tools on this transport). A\n # deployment configured only through DEFAULT_MODEL has the agent turned off.\n \n # Runner tuning. Defaults are shown; only relevant once the runtime is enabled.\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS=1000\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_HEARTBEAT_MS=2000\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_LEASE_TTL_MS=10000\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_MAX_CONCURRENT=2\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5\n \n # Global per-tool-call execution bound for every agent run (ms). A tool call\n # that neither resolves nor rejects within the budget is aborted and settles as\n # an error tool-result the agent can retry or proceed from; the session does\n # not die. Default 600000 (10 minutes). Tools with known longer budgets (media\n # synthesis, material extraction) carry their own explicit bounds in code.\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS=600000\n \n # Conversation compaction is reserved and OFF by default. The reusable\n # compaction runtime is not implemented yet — it lands in a later slice of\n # work — and until then the runner runs without context transformation, so\n # these knobs are inert placeholders.\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_COMPACTION_ENABLED=true\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_COMPACTION_RESERVE_TOKENS=0\n # OPENMAIC_AGENT_COMPACTION_KEEP_RECENT_TOKENS=0\n \n # Session prompts and follow-up messages are capped server-side at a fixed\n # 100,000 characters; this limit is a constant and is not configurable.\n \n # --- Generation runs ----------------------------------------------------------\n \n # Course generation runs on the server: a run is a PostgreSQL record that a\n # worker in every server process executes, step by step, and another process\n # takes over from its last checkpoint if one dies. The worker always runs (it\n # does not depend on OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_ENABLED) and needs a process that\n # outlives requests, so serverless hosts are not supported. It shares the lease\n # timing of the agent runtime (OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS,\n # _HEARTBEAT_MS, _LEASE_TTL_MS and _MAX_ATTEMPTS above). Defaults are shown;\n # values must be positive integers.\n #\n # Runs one owner may have in progress at once (a run waiting for its outline to\n # be confirmed, or paused at a failed step, does not count). Over the limit,\n # starting, confirming or retrying a run answers 429 ACTIVE_RUN_LIMIT.\n # OPENMAIC_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS_PER_OWNER=2\n # Runs one owner may have waiting for outline confirmation at once.\n # OPENMAIC_MAX_WAITING_RUNS_PER_OWNER=10\n # Runs one server process executes at once.\n # OPENMAIC_GENERATION_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT=4\n # Uploaded materials one server process extracts at once in the background\n # (each is parsed or transcribed right after its upload, before generation).\n # OPENMAIC_MATERIAL_EXTRACTION_CONCURRENCY=2\n # One owner's extractions running at once across every server process, so one\n # owner's uploads cannot hold every worker while others wait.\n # OPENMAIC_MATERIAL_EXTRACTION_PER_OWNER=2\n # The largest stored extraction result (text and images) of one material, in\n # MB; a larger one fails with EXTRACTION_RESULT_TOO_LARGE. Results count\n # against the owner's material byte quota.\n # OPENMAIC_MATERIAL_EXTRACTION_MAX_RESULT_MB=100\n # Hours an uploaded material that no generation run or agent session uses is\n # kept after it was last read (an open composer reads its materials back) before\n # it is deleted.\n # OPENMAIC_UNUSED_MATERIAL_TTL_HOURS=24\n # Run event streams (one run's events, or the owner's run changes) one owner may\n # hold open on one process.\n # OPENMAIC_GENERATION_RUN_STREAMS_PER_OWNER=16\n # Hours a finished run keeps its full event log before it is compacted to its\n # final snapshot.\n # OPENMAIC_GENERATION_RUN_RETENTION_HOURS=24\n \n # --- Proxy (optional) --------------------------------------------------------\n \n # HTTP_PROXY=\n # HTTPS_PROXY=\n # Comma-separated hosts that bypass the proxy. Supports domain suffixes and *.\n # NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,.internal.example.com\n \n # --- Misc ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n \n # Default model (deprecated: prefer openmaic.yml). Without openmaic.yml it\n # becomes the default of every chat slot (the `llm` root), below the models a\n # workspace picks in the settings; the agent stays off. There is no hardcoded\n # vendor fallback: a call with no model configured fails.\n # Example: openai:gpt-5.5, minimax:MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed,\n # bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5\n DEFAULT_MODEL=\n \n # Per-stage models are slots in openmaic.yml (course.outline,\n # course.content.slide, classroom, agent, ...). MODEL_ROUTES is no longer read:\n # a server that still sets it without openmaic.yml refuses to start. The agent\n # runtime's former \"maic-agent-driver\" route is now the `agent` slot (with its\n # `api` and `contextWindow`).\n \n # Retry model (deprecated: prefer a slot's `fallback` in openmaic.yml). When a\n # generation call fails with a retryable failure (SDK-classified transient\n # error, timeout, network error, quota 429, capacity 503) or returns empty\n # output, the shared callLLM layer retries ONCE on the slot's fallback model.\n # Content-safety rejections and other 4xx failures never fall back. Without\n # openmaic.yml, MODEL_FALLBACK becomes the fallback of DEFAULT_MODEL.\n # MODEL_FALLBACK=\n \n # LOG_LEVEL=info\n # LOG_FORMAT=pretty\n # LLM_THINKING_DISABLED=false\n \n # Opt-in parallel scene-content generation (#572). 0/unset = serial (default).\n # A value > 1 fetches scene content concurrently (capped at 10); actions + TTS\n # stay serial. Leave off if your API key has a low per-key concurrency quota.\n # PARALLEL_SCENE_CONCURRENCY=3\n \n # --- Local/Self-hosted Deployment ---------------------------------------------\n # Set to \"true\" to allow private/local network URLs. That covers private\n # (RFC1918), loopback, link-local and CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10, used by Tailscale\n # and similar overlay networks) targets. Required for self-hosted models like\n # Ollama. Do NOT enable on public deployments.\n # The known cloud instance-metadata and credential endpoints (169.254.169.254,\n # 169.254.170.2, 169.254.170.23, 100.100.100.200, 168.63.129.16, 192.0.0.192,\n # fd00:ec2::254, fd00:ec2::23, metadata.google.internal) are blocked with or\n # without this flag, as are IANA reserved, multicast and broadcast ranges. That\n # is a fixed address list, not a general link-local block, and under the flag a\n # hostname whose DNS lookup fails, times out or returns no answer is still\n # allowed through.\n # ALLOW_LOCAL_NETWORKS=true\n \n # Build-time, space-separated CSP frame-ancestor sources in addition to 'self'.\n # Configure only origins you trust to embed OpenMAIC, then rebuild the app. The\n # Docker and Compose builds also accept this value as a build argument.\n # ALLOWED_FRAME_ANCESTORS=https://partner.example.com\n \n # Optional MP4 render service (issue #866). When set, the in-app \"Export Video\"\n # menu offers one-click MP4 rendering; when unset, it degrades to downloading a\n # project ZIP for local CLI rendering. Point this at the isolated render-service\n # container (see render-service/ and the \"video-export\" docker-compose profile).\n # This is operator-supplied trusted config: the app forwards uploads to it\n # without the SSRF guard, so a private/compose-network target works WITHOUT\n # setting ALLOW_LOCAL_NETWORKS.\n # RENDER_SERVICE_URL=http://render-service:9000\n \n # Optional runtime setting for render-service-only preview concurrency, independent\n # of video exports. Defaults to 1; maximum 2 for standard, 1 for low-memory.\n # Values above the resource profile's limit fail startup.\n # Each executing preview launches its own browser alongside the export, so\n # provision additional memory before raising this value. Passed through by Compose.\n # RENDER_PREVIEW_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1\n \n # Render-service-only opt-in for bounded local chunk execution. These variables\n # are read at runtime by the isolated render-service container; the public HTTP\n # API is unchanged. Defaults keep the existing in-process renderer.\n # RENDER_CHUNK_EXECUTION=false\n # RENDER_CHUNK_COUNT=1\n # RENDER_CHUNK_WORKERS=1\n # RENDER_MAX_PARALLEL_CHUNKS=1\n # RENDER_CHUNK_SIZE_FRAMES=0\n # RENDER_TARGET_CHUNK_FRAMES=0\n \n # Honor x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip when deriving client identity for both\n # render-service admission and access-code verification throttling.\n # Enable only behind a trusted reverse proxy that overwrites these headers.\n # TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true\n \n # --- Persistence (PostgreSQL, required) ---------------------------------------\n \n # Courses, chat history, learner progress and generated media are stored in\n # PostgreSQL through the embedded /api/persistence endpoint. The server refuses\n # to start without DATABASE_URL. Requests are attributed to the owner the owner\n # identity seam resolves (by default the anonymous owner cookie); there is no\n # separate persistence credential.\n #\n # Local development: `pnpm db:up` starts a separate development PostgreSQL\n # (its own Compose project, container and volume, see docker-compose.db.yml)\n # on 127.0.0.1 (port OPENMAIC_DB_PORT, default 5432); then uncomment this line.\n # `pnpm db:down` stops it again (the data volume is kept).\n # DATABASE_URL=postgres://openmaic:openmaic-dev@127.0.0.1:5432/openmaic\n #\n # Under docker-compose.yml, the default points at the bundled PostgreSQL (from\n # PERSISTENCE_POSTGRES_PASSWORD, which must then be letters and digits); a value\n # set here overrides it. Other deployments (the Docker image on its own, or\n # `pnpm start`) point this at a PostgreSQL database they run themselves.\n \n # Logical bytes of live assets each owner may hold (default 10 GiB; 0 opts\n # out). Per owner, not per deployment: with anonymous-cookie owners a cleared\n # cookie is a new owner with a fresh quota.\n # ASSET_QUOTA_BYTES=\n \n # The anonymous owner cookie and the ACCESS_CODE cookie carry the `Secure` flag\n # in production builds. Over plain HTTP other than localhost no browser stores\n # them, so every request is a new owner and the access code is asked again.\n # Safari refuses to store `Secure` cookies served over plain http://localhost\n # (unlike Chromium/Firefox, it does not special-case localhost), so every\n # request mints a fresh anonymous owner and owner-scoped document writes fail\n # with 403. Deployments that serve plain HTTP (no TLS) opt out with the exact\n # value 0 — any other spelling (false, no) leaves `Secure` on:\n # COOKIE_SECURE=0\n # Only do this on a trusted network or locally: without `Secure` the cookie\n # travels in the clear and can be replayed by anyone on-path.\n \n # Single-tenant deployments: resolve every request to this fixed owner id\n # instead of a per-browser anonymous cookie. One team behind one ACCESS_CODE\n # then shares one course library — a second browser no longer sees an empty\n # list, and `publish` becomes usable (it refuses anonymous owners, since\n # publishing a cookie partition is not something the product allows).\n # Unset, every browser keeps its own partition and this block changes nothing.\n #\n # This answers WHO owns a course; DATABASE_URL above answers WHERE one lives.\n # Without this setting (or OWNER_SINGLE_USER), a second browser is a different\n # anonymous owner and sees an empty list.\n #\n # ACCESS_CODE is required: without one the middleware lets every request\n # through, so a single shared owner would expose one readable, editable and\n # publishable course library to anyone who can reach the deployment. Setting\n # this without an access code fails startup. Everyone holding the access code\n # then sees, edits and can publish the same courses, with no per-person\n # attribution — which is what SECURITY.md already says ACCESS_CODE is, and not\n # user authentication. 1-128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-]; the reserved `anon:`\n # prefix is rejected, and a malformed value fails startup rather than being\n # ignored.\n # PERSISTENCE_SHARED_OWNER_ID=\n \n # Personal installations: resolve every request to one fixed owner for a\n # single person, who may publish. On by default under Docker Compose (see\n # docker-compose.defaults.env); unset elsewhere. \"true\"/\"1\" or \"false\"/\"0\";\n # anything else fails startup. Excludes PERSISTENCE_SHARED_OWNER_ID above:\n # setting both fails startup.\n # OWNER_SINGLE_USER=true\n #\n # The owner id (default \"local\"), same format as PERSISTENCE_SHARED_OWNER_ID.\n # Setting it while OWNER_SINGLE_USER is off fails startup.\n # OWNER_SINGLE_USER_ID=local\n #\n # Exposure: every request becomes the owner of the whole library. The mode runs\n # with or without ACCESS_CODE; without one, anyone who can reach the server\n # shares, edits and can delete the single library, so the server logs a\n # prominent startup warning. Keep it on 127.0.0.1 or a private network\n # (docker-compose.yml publishes on 127.0.0.1 by default; OPENMAIC_PUBLISH_ADDRESS\n # changes that), or set ACCESS_CODE below.\n #\n # A browser that used the deployment anonymously before keeps its anonymous\n # cookie; single-user mode can claim that earlier work into the single owner\n # with POST /api/identity/claim. OWNER_CLAIM_TRIGGER=auto below would claim on\n # every visiting browser's first request, irreversibly merging the libraries of\n # everyone who used the deployment anonymously; set it only knowingly.\n # The owner id is permanent: changing OWNER_SINGLE_USER_ID (or switching from\n # PERSISTENCE_SHARED_OWNER_ID) strands the previous owner's library.\n \n # Real accounts (your own sessions, API keys, or an identity gateway such as\n # oauth2-proxy or Cloudflare Access) are not configured here: a host registers\n # owner auth methods in instrumentation.ts. See \"Owner identity\" in README.md,\n # which includes a recipe for verifying a gateway-signed JWT. When a host\n # registers methods and still wants the shared owner above, it includes\n # sharedTeamAuthMethod() last; setting PERSISTENCE_SHARED_OWNER_ID beside a\n # registration that leaves it out fails startup.\n \n # Store asset bytes in S3 instead of PostgreSQL. Region, endpoint, and credentials\n # are resolved through the standard AWS SDK environment / credential chain.\n # ASSET_S3_BUCKET=\n \n # Use endpoint/bucket/key addressing for S3-compatible stores such as MinIO and\n # Ceph. These stores commonly require path-style requests when configured\n # through AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3. Accepts \"true\" or \"1\"; leave unset for Amazon S3.\n # AWS_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=1\n \n # Opt into indirect asset byte egress: answer asset byte GETs with a short-lived\n # signed S3 URL (a 302, or a JSON descriptor for the packaged client) instead of\n # the bytes. Unset or \"direct\" keeps direct egress (the safe default). Requires\n # the object store's CORS to admit this app's origin and expose Content-Type, and\n # the signing identity to hold s3:ListBucket on the bucket so a missing key\n # answers 404 NoSuchKey rather than 403.\n # ASSET_BYTE_EGRESS=redirect\n \n # Claiming anonymous work on sign-in (see README \"Claiming anonymous work\").\n # explicit (default): the app calls POST /api/identity/claim; auto: the first\n # request that carries both an account and an anonymous owner claims it.\n # OWNER_CLAIM_TRIGGER=explicit\n \n # The page response of a browser's first load mints the anonymous owner cookie\n # (default on), so the page's first API requests do not each mint an owner.\n # Set it to false only when registered owner auth methods set\n # anonymousFallback: false (startup warns when they do and this is on); hosts\n # that keep anonymous visitors need it, and skip it per request in\n # middleware.ts for requests their methods authenticate.\n # \"true\", \"1\", \"false\" or \"0\"; anything else fails startup.\n # OWNER_ANONYMOUS_PREMINT=true\n \n # How long an owner-scoped write (default 30000) and a claim (default 5000) wait\n # for the owner's identity lock before answering 503 OWNER_BUSY with\n # Retry-After. Positive integers in milliseconds, checked at startup.\n # OWNER_WRITE_LOCK_WAIT_MS=30000\n # OWNER_CLAIM_LOCK_WAIT_MS=5000\n \n # The asset collector is enabled by default.\n # ASSET_COLLECTION_ENABLED=true\n # ASSET_COLLECTION_INTERVAL_MS=900000\n # ASSET_COLLECTION_GRACE_MS=3600000\n \n # Directory of the file-backed classroom store of earlier versions. Defaults to\n # <cwd>/data/classrooms. Classrooms generated through /api/generate-classroom\n # are now saved in PostgreSQL (courses) and the asset pool (media, narration);\n # at startup the server imports the <id>.json classrooms it finds here, once,\n # retrying in the background until it completes, and logs a summary. They go to\n # the shared team owner or the single user when one is configured; otherwise to\n # a dedicated owner no visitor resolves to, so each classroom keeps opening\n # read-only from its old link and appears in no visitor's library (export it as\n # a ZIP and import it to own a copy). An id another course already holds is\n # skipped. Keep this directory in place: the import leaves the files where they\n # are, imported classrooms may still reference files in it, and agent-run\n # courses serve narration and material media from it. The old\n # <cwd>/data/classroom-jobs directory is no longer read.\n # OPENMAIC_CLASSROOMS_DIR=/var/lib/openmaic/classrooms\n \n # How long an allocated asset stays pending -- stored, but not yet named by any\n # document -- before the collector expires it. A value that is not a positive\n # integer stops the server from starting.\n # ASSET_PENDING_TTL_MS=86400000\n \n # --- Access Control -----------------------------------------------------------\n # Set a password to restrict site access. When set, users must enter this code\n # before using the app. Leave empty or remove to disable access control\n # (fail-open: middleware lets every request through with no credential).\n # Read at runtime. When unset, the server logs a one-time startup warning (in\n # single-user mode, the single-user warning, which names ACCESS_CODE, instead);\n # GET /api/health reports accessCodeConfigured: false. Set this before exposing\n # the server to a network. The warning does not prevent local zero-config use.\n # Use a long random value (at least 16 characters from a random generator):\n # this code is the only secret guarding the deployment. The code is remembered\n # in a signed token stored in an HTTP-only cookie for 7 days; the lifetime is\n # enforced server-side, so visitors re-verify after it expires.\n # ACCESS_CODE=your-secret-code\n #\n # Verification is rate limited only when TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true (see above):\n # behind a trusted reverse proxy that overwrites x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip,\n # each client is limited to 10 attempts per 60 seconds, and a trusted client's\n # successful verification clears its own counter. onClick={inc}\n         disabled={value >= max}\n         aria-label=\"Increase\"\n         className=\"flex size-7 items-center justify-center text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-muted               "patch": "Index: lib/audio/constants.ts\n===================================================================\n--- lib/audio/constants.ts\t\n+++ lib/audio/constants.ts\t\n@@ -1,1663 +1,1712 @@\n /**\n  * Audio Provider Constants\n  *\n  * Registry of all TTS and ASR providers with their metadata.\n  * Separated from tts-providers.ts and asr-providers.ts to avoid importing\n  * Node.js libraries (like sharp, buffer) in client components.\n  *\n  * This file is client-safe and can be imported in both client and server components.\n  *\n  * To add a new provider:\n  * 1. Add the provider ID to TTSProviderId or ASRProviderId in types.ts\n  * 2. Add provider configuration to TTS_PROVIDERS or ASR_PROVIDERS below\n  * 3. Implement provider logic in tts-providers.ts or asr-providers.ts\n  * 4. Add i18n translations in lib/i18n.ts\n  *\n  * Provider configuration should include:\n  * - id: Unique identifier matching the type definition\n  * - name: Display name for the provider\n  * - requiresApiKey: Whether the provider needs an API key\n  * - The server\n  * maps the VC sentinel to its operator-resolved model and applies model pins.\n  */\n export function resolveTTSModelForVoice(\n   providerId: TTSProviderId,\n   voiceId: string,\n   requestedModelId?: string,\n ): string | undefined {\n   if (providerId !== 'qwen-tts') return requestedModelId;\n   if (isQwenCloneVoice(voiceId)) return QWEN_TTS_VOICE_CLONE_MODEL;\n   return requestedModelId && !isQwenVoiceCloneModel(requestedModelId)\n     ? requestedModelId\n     : TTS_PROVIDERS['qwen-tts'].defaultModelId;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Whether a model can speak a voice: a catalogue voice that lists compatible\n  * models (OpenAI's Marin and Cedar need gpt-4o-mini-tts) only on those; any\n  * other voice (no such list, a clone, a user voice) on any model. 'voxcpm-tts': VOXCPM_VLLM_MODEL_ID,\n   'doubao-tts': '',\n   'elevenlabs-tts': 'eleven_multilingual_v2',\n   'minimax-tts': 'speech-2.8-hd',\n   'google-tts': 'gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview',\n   'lemonade-tts': 'kokoro-v1',\n+  'fish-tts': 's2.1-pro',\n   'browser-native-tts': '',\n };\n \n /**\n  * Get all available TTS providers (built-in + custom)\n  */\n export function getAllTTSProviders(\n   customProviders?: Record<string, TTSProviderConfig>,\n ): TTSProviderConfig[] {\n   const builtIn = Object.values(TTS_PROVIDERS);\n   const custom = customProviders ? Object.values(customProviders) : [];\n   return [...builtIn, ...custom];\n }\n \n /**\n  * Narrow an arbitrary string (e.g. from a persisted document or an imported\n  * manifest, where the contract keeps providerId an open string) to a known\n  * TTS provider id: a registered built-in provider or the user-defined\n  * custom-provider namespace.               "patch": "Index: lib/audio/provider-display.ts\n===================================================================\n--- lib/audio/provider-display.ts\t\n+++ lib/audio/provider-display.ts\t\n@@ -1,61 +1,62 @@\n /**\n  * Localized display names for the built-in audio providers.\n  *\n  * The `name` field in `ASR_PROVIDERS` / `TTS_PROVIDERS` is a registry label, not\n  * a UI string: several are written in Chinese (`浏览器原生 ASR (Web Speech API)`,\n  * `Qwen ASR (阿里云百炼)`). Rendering it directly leaks Chinese into every other\n  * locale, so any surface that shows a provider to the user must resolve the\n  * name through i18n instead.\n  *\n  * Kept here rather than in a component so the settings dialog and the\n  * generation toolbar cannot drift apart on what a provider is called.\n  */\n \n import type { ASRProviderId, TTSProviderId } from './types';\n \n const ASR_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS: Record<string, string> = {\n   'openai-whisper': 'settings.providerOpenAIWhisper',\n   'browser-native': 'settings.providerBrowserNative',\n   'qwen-asr': 'settings.providerQwenASR',\n   'azure-asr': 'settings.providerAzureASR',\n   'funasr-asr': 'settings.providerFunASRASR',\n   'lemonade-asr': 'settings.providerLemonadeASR',\n };\n \n const TTS_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS: Record<string, string> = {\n   'openai-tts': 'settings.providerOpenAITTS',\n   'azure-tts': 'settings.providerAzureTTS',\n   'glm-tts': 'settings.providerGLMTTS',\n   'qwen-tts': 'settings.providerQwenTTS',\n   'voxcpm-tts': 'settings.providerVoxCPMTTS',\n   'doubao-tts': 'settings.providerDoubaoTTS',\n   'elevenlabs-tts': 'settings.providerElevenLabsTTS',\n   'minimax-tts': 'settings.providerMiniMaxTTS',\n   'google-tts': 'settings.providerGoogleTTS',\n   'lemonade-tts': 'settings.providerLemonadeTTS',\n+  'fish-tts': 'settings.providerFishAudioTTS',\n   'browser-native-tts': 'settings.providerBrowserNativeTTS',\n };\n \n /**\n  * Translate a built-in ASR provider's name. Unknown ids (custom providers,\n  * which carry their own user-supplied name) fall back to `fallback`, then to\n  * the id, so a caller never renders an empty label.\n  */\n export function resolveASRProviderName(\n   providerId: ASRProviderId | string,\n   t: (key: string) => string,\n   fallback?: string,\n ): string {\n   const key = ASR_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS[providerId];\n   return key ? t(key) : fallback || providerId;\n }\n \n /** TTS counterpart of {@link resolveASRProviderName}. */\n export function resolveTTSProviderName(\n   providerId: TTSProviderId | string,\n   t: (key: string) => string,\n   fallback?: string,\n ): string {\n   const key = TTS_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS[providerId];\n   return key ? t(key) : fallback || providerId;\n }\n",
              "additions": 1,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },

              "patch": "Index: lib/audio/tts-providers.ts\n===================================================================\n--- lib/audio/tts-providers.ts\t\n+++ lib/audio/tts-providers.ts\t\n@@ -1,1472 +1,1526 @@\n /**\n  * TTS (Text-to-Speech) Provider Implementation\n  *\n  * Factory pattern for routing TTS requests to appropriate provider implementations.\n  * Follows the same architecture as lib/ai/providers.ts for consistency.\n  *\n  * Currently Supported Providers:\n  * - OpenAI TTS: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/text-to-speech\n  * - Azure TTS: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/text-to-speech\n  * - GLM TTS: https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/models/sound-and-video/glm-tts\n  * - Qwen TTS: https://bailian.console.aliyun.com/\n  * - MiniMax TTS: https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/speech-t2a-http\n  * - Doubao TTS: https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6561/1257543\n  * - ElevenLabs TTS: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert\n+ * - Fish Audio TTS: https://docs.fish.audio/text-to-speech/api\n  * - Google Gemini TTS: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation\n  * - Browser Native: Web Speech API (client-side only)\n  *\n  * HOW TO ADD A NEW PROVIDER:\n  *\n  * 1. Add provider ID to TTSProviderId in lib/audio/types.ts\n  *    Example: | 'elevenlabs-tts'\n  *\n  * 2. Add provider configuration to lib/audio/constants.ts\n  *    Example:\n  *    'elevenlabs-tts': {\n  *      id: 'elevenlabs-tts',\n  *      name: 'ElevenLabs',\n  *      requiresApiKey: true,\n  *      defaultBaseUrl: 'https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1',\n  *      icon: '/logos/elevenlabs.svg',\n  *      voices: [...],\n  *      supportedFormats: ['mp3', 'pcm'],\n  *      speedRange: { min: 0.5, max: 2.0, default: 1.0 }\n  *    }\n  *\n  * 3. Implement provider function in this file\n  *    Pattern: async function generateXxxTTS(config, text): Promise<TTSGenerationResult>\n  *    - Validate config and build API request\n  *    - Handle API authentication (apiKey, headers)\n  *    - Convert provider-specific parameters (voice, speed, format)\n  *    - Return { audio: Uint8Array, format: string }\n  *\n  *    Example:\n  *    async function generateElevenLabsTTS(\n  *      config: TTSModelConfig,\n  *      text: string\n  *    ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n  *      const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['elevenlabs-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n  *\n  *      const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/text-to-speech/${config.voice}`, {\n  *        method: 'POST',\n  *        headers: {\n  *          'xi-api-key': config.apiKey!,\n  *          'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n  *        },\n  *        body: JSON.stringify({\n  *          text,\n  *          model_id: 'eleven_multilingual_v2',\n  *          voice_settings: {\n  *            stability: 0.5,\n  *            similarity_boost: 0.75,\n  *          }\n  *        }),\n  *      });\n  *\n  *      if (!response.ok) {\n  *        throw new Error(`ElevenLabs TTS API error: ${response.statusText}`);\n  *      }\n  *\n  *      const arrayBuffer = await response.arrayBuffer();\n  *      return {\n  *        audio: new Uint8Array(arrayBuffer),\n  *        format: 'mp3',\n  *      };\n  *    }\n  *\n  * 4. Add case to generateTTS() switch statement\n  *    case 'elevenlabs-tts':\n  *      return await generateElevenLabsTTS(config, text);\n  *\n  * 5. Add i18n translations in lib/i18n.ts\n  *    providerElevenLabsTTS: { zh: 'ElevenLabs TTS', en: 'ElevenLabs TTS' }\n  *\n  * Error Handling Patterns:\n  * - Always validate API key if requiresApiKey is true\n  * - Throw descriptive errors for API failures\n  * - Include response.statusText or error messages from API\n  * - For client-only providers (browser-native), throw error directing to client-side usage\n  *\n  * API Call Patterns:\n  * - Direct API: Use fetch with appropriate headers and body format (recommended for better encoding support)\n  * - SSML: For Azure-like providers requiring SSML markup\n  * - URL-based: For providers returning audio URL (download in second step)\n  */\n \n import type { TTSModelConfig } from './types';\n import { isCustomTTSProvider } from './types';\n import {\n   isQwenCloneVoice,\n   resolveTTSModelForVoice,\n   TTS_PROVIDERS,\n   DEFAULT_TTS_VOICES,\n } from './constants';\n import { downloadAudio, QwenVoiceCloneError, synthesizeQwenVoiceClone } from './qwen-voice-clone';\n import { evictQwenVoiceRegistrationMemo } from './qwen-voice-clone-registration';\n import { splitConcatenatedJsonObjects } from './json-stream';\n import {\n   VOXCPM_VLLM_MODEL_ID,\n   VOXCPM_AUTO_VOICE_ID,\n   normalizeVoxCPMBackend,\n   type VoxCPMProviderOptions,\n } from './voxcpm';\n import { createLogger } from '@/lib/logger';\n import {\n   audioEndpointPolicy,\n   audioProviderFetch,\n   type AudioEndpointTarget,\n } from '@/lib/server/audio-provider-fetch';\n import { ProviderQuotaExhaustedError } from '@/lib/server/provider-quota';\n import { appAttributionHeaders } from '@/lib/config/app-attribution';\n import { pcmS16leMonoToWav } from './pcm-wav';\n \n const log = createLogger('TTSProviders');\n \n /**\n  * Every server-side provider request goes through the strict redirect +\n  * pinned-DNS helper under the address policy the route resolved: strict public\n  * for a client BYOK URL, local networks allowed for a server-configured\n  * provider, the operator policy for an unmanaged provider's default endpoint.\n  */\n function ttsFetch(\n   target: AudioEndpointTarget | undefined,\n   url: string,\n   init: RequestInit,\n ): Promise<Response> {\n   return audioProviderFetch(url, init, audioEndpointPolicy(target));\n }\n \n /**\n  * Result of TTS generation\n  */\n export interface TTSGenerationResult {\n   audio: Uint8Array;\n   format: string;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Thrown when a TTS provider returns a rate-limit / concurrency-quota error.\n  * Allows downstream consumers to distinguish rate-limit errors from other TTS failures.\n  *\n  * TODO: The API route currently catches all errors uniformly as GENERATION_FAILED.\n  * This class enables future retry/backoff logic without changing the throw sites.\n  */\n export class TTSRateLimitError extends Error {\n   /** Milliseconds from a `Retry-After` header, when the provider sent one. */\n   readonly retryAfterMs?: number;\n \n   constructor(\n     public readonly provider: string,\n     message: string,\n     retryAfterMs?: number,\n     options?: ErrorOptions,\n   ) {\n     super(message, options);\n     this.name = 'TTSRateLimitError';\n     if (retryAfterMs !== undefined && Number.isFinite(retryAfterMs) && retryAfterMs > 0) {\n       this.retryAfterMs = retryAfterMs;\n     }\n   }\n }\n \n /** Neutral identity for ordinary Qwen TTS failures (never VC-branded). */\n export class QwenTTSError extends Error {\n   readonly code = 'QWEN_TTS_ERROR';\n   readonly httpStatus: number;\n \n   constructor(message: string, httpStatus = 502) {\n     super(message);\n     this.name = 'QwenTTSError';\n     this.httpStatus = httpStatus;\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * Thrown when a TTS provider responds with HTTP 200 but returns a non-audio body\n  * (such as HTML error page, web front-end response, or JSON without an audioUrl).\n  * Prevents non-audio bytes from being stored, referenced, or billed.\n  */\n export class TTSInvalidResponseError extends Error {\n   readonly code = 'TTS_INVALID_RESPONSE';\n   readonly httpStatus: number;\n \n   constructor(\n     public readonly provider: string,\n     message: string,\n     httpStatus = 502,\n   ) {\n     super(message);\n     this.name = 'TTSInvalidResponseError';\n     this.httpStatus = httpStatus;\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * Per-request bound for one TTS provider call, ported from the reference\n  * runtime's TTS bounds (30s request timeouts on the managed TTS clients).\n  * Overridable via `TTS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (ms) for deployments with slower\n  * upstreams; a hung provider fails the call with this error instead of\n  * wedging the session.\n  */\n const DEFAULT_TTS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;\n \n function ttsRequestTimeoutMs(): number {\n   const raw = process.env.TTS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS?.trim();\n   const parsed = raw ? Number(raw) : NaN;\n   return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : DEFAULT_TTS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Thrown when a single TTS provider request exceeds {@link ttsRequestTimeoutMs}.\n  * Distinct from `AbortSignal`-driven cancellation (session cancel): a timeout\n  * is a provider failure the caller may retry.\n  */\n export class TTSRequestTimeoutError extends Error {\n   constructor(\n     public readonly provider: string,\n     message: string,\n   ) {\n     super(message);\n     this.name = 'TTSRequestTimeoutError';\n   }\n }\n \n /** Combine the caller's cancel signal with the per-request timeout. */\n function ttsRequestSignal(callerSignal?: AbortSignal): AbortSignal {\n   const timeout = AbortSignal.timeout(ttsRequestTimeoutMs());\n   return callerSignal ? AbortSignal.any([callerSignal, timeout]) : timeout;\n }\n \n /** True when `signal` aborted because the per-request timeout fired. */\n function isTimeoutSignal(signal: AbortSignal): boolean {\n   return (\n     signal.aborted && signal.reason instanceof DOMException && signal.reason.name === 'TimeoutError'\n   );\n }\n \n /**\n  * `Retry-After` as milliseconds. Accepts delta-seconds or an HTTP-date.\n  * Undefined when the header is missing or not a delay.\n  */\n function parseRetryAfterMs(\n   header: string | null | undefined,\n   now = Date.now(),\n ): number | undefined {\n   if (!header) return undefined;\n   const trimmed = header.trim();\n   if (!trimmed) return undefined;\n   if (/^\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?$/.test(trimmed)) return Math.max(0, Number(trimmed) * 1000);\n   const dateMs = Date.parse(trimmed);\n   if (Number.isNaN(dateMs)) return undefined;\n   return Math.max(0, dateMs - now);\n }\n \n /**\n  * Map an upstream HTTP 429 to a typed {@link TTSRateLimitError} so the API route\n  * can surface it as 429 instead of a generic 500. Call right after an\n  * `!response.ok` check, before building the provider-specific error message.\n  * Pass the `Retry-After` header when the response has one.\n  */\n export function throwIfTtsRateLimited(\n   provider: string,\n   status: number,\n   retryAfterHeader?: string | null,\n   options?: ErrorOptions,\n ): void {\n   if (status === 429) {\n     throw new TTSRateLimitError(\n       provider,\n       `${provider} TTS rate limit exceeded (HTTP 429)`,\n       parseRetryAfterMs(retryAfterHeader),\n       options,\n     );\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * Generate speech using specified TTS provider\n  *\n  * Every provider request is created with a signal that combines the caller's\n  * cancel signal (`config.signal`) with the per-request timeout, so a session\n  * cancel aborts the in-flight fetch within seconds and a hung provider fails\n  * with {@link TTSRequestTimeoutError} instead of hanging forever.\n  */\n export async function generateTTS(\n   config: TTSModelConfig,\n   text: string,\n ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n   const provider = TTS_PROVIDERS[config.providerId as keyof typeof TTS_PROVIDERS];\n \n   // Validate API key if required (only for built-in providers with known config)\n   if (provider?.requiresApiKey && !config.apiKey) {\n     throw new Error(`API key required for TTS provider: ${config.providerId}`);\n   }\n \n   const signal = ttsRequestSignal(config.signal);\n   try {\n     switch (config.providerId) {\n       case 'openai-tts':\n         return await generateOpenAITTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'azure-tts':\n         return await generateAzureTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'glm-tts':\n         return await generateGLMTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'qwen-tts':\n         return await generateQwenTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'voxcpm-tts':\n         return await generateVoxCPMTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'minimax-tts':\n         return await generateMiniMaxTTS(config, text, signal);\n       case 'doubao-tts':\n         return await generateDoubaoTTS(config, text, signal);\n       case 'elevenlabs-tts':\n         return await generateElevenLabsTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'google-tts':\n         return await generateGoogleTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n+      case 'fish-tts':\n+        return await generateFishAudioTTS(config, text, signal);\n+\n       case 'lemonade-tts':\n         return await generateLemonadeTTS(config, text, signal);\n \n       case 'browser-native-tts':\n         throw new Error(\n           'Browser Native TTS must be handled client-side using Web Speech API. This provider cannot be used on the server.',\n         );\n \n       default:\n         if (isCustomTTSProvider(config.providerId)) {\n           return await generateOpenAITTS(config, text, signal);\n         }\n         throw new Error(`Unsupported TTS provider: ${config.providerId}`);\n     }\n   } catch (error) {\n     // A caller cancel must propagate as-is so the enclosing run treats it as an\n     // interruption, not a provider failure.\n     if (config.signal?.aborted) throw error;\n     if (isTimeoutSignal(signal)) {\n       throw new TTSRequestTimeoutError(\n         config.providerId,\n         `TTS request timed out after ${ttsRequestTimeoutMs()}ms (provider ${config.providerId}) — the provider did not respond. Retry the tool call.`,\n       );\n     }\n     throw error;\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * OpenAI TTS implementation (direct API call with explicit UTF-8 encoding)\n  */\n async function generateOpenAITTS(\n   config: TTSModelConfig,\n   text: string,\n   signal: AbortSignal,\n ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n   const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['openai-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n \n   // Use gpt-4o-mini-tts for best quality and intelligent realtime applications\n   const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/audio/speech`, {\n     method: 'POST',\n     headers: {\n       Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`,\n       'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',\n     },\n     body: JSON.stringify({\n       model: config.modelId || 'gpt-4o-mini-tts',\n       input: text,\n       voice: config.voice,\n       speed: config.speed || 1.0,\n       // Ask for a container the browser can decode. OpenAI defaults to mp3, but\n       // this same function serves every custom OpenAI-compatible provider and\n       // their defaults differ — OpenRouter's /audio/speech defaults to raw\n       // `pcm`, which arrives headerless, gets labelled mp3 below, and fails in\n       // the client with \"no supported source was found\". Naming the format\n       // removes the guess. Providers that ignore the field are unaffected.\n       response_format: 'mp3',\n     }),\n     signal,\n   });\n \n   if (!response.ok) {\n     const error = await response.json().catch(() => ({ error: response.statusText }));\n     // Retain the response without changing the HTTP status used by route retries.\n     const options = { cause: { data: error } };\n     throwIfTtsRateLimited('OpenAI', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'), options);\n     throw new Error(\n       `OpenAI TTS API error: ${error.error?.message || response.statusText}`,\n       options,\n     );\n   }\n \n   return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'OpenAI');\n }\n \n /**\n  * Lemonade TTS implementation (OpenAI-compatible new Error(message);\n }\n \n /**\n  * MiniMax TTS implementation (synchronous HTTP API)\n  */\n async function generateMiniMaxTTS(\n   config: TTSModelConfig,\n   text: string,\n   signal: AbortSignal,\n ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n   const baseUrl = (config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['minimax-tts'].defaultBaseUrl || '').replace(\n     /\\/$/,\n     '',\n   );\n   const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/v1/t2a_v2`, {\n     method: 'POST',\n     headers: {\n       Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`,\n       'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',\n       ...appAttributionHeaders(baseUrl),\n     },\n     body: JSON.stringify({\n       model: config.modelId || 'speech-2.8-hd',\n       text,\n       stream: false,\n       output_format: 'hex',\n       voice_setting: {\n         voice_id: config.voice,\n         speed: config.speed || 1.0,\n         vol: 1,\n         pitch: 0,\n       },\n       audio_setting: {\n         sample_rate: 32000,\n         bitrate: 128000,\n         format: config.format || 'mp3',\n         channel: 1,\n       },\n       language_boost: 'auto',\n     }),\n     signal,\n   });\n \n   if (!response.ok) {\n     const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n     const message = `MiniMax TTS API error: ${errorText}`;\n     // A quota code in the body says what the HTTP status does not; an HTTP 429\n     // keeps its rate-limit type and carries the quota error as its cause.\n     const quota = minimaxQuotaError(minimaxBodyStatusCode(errorText), message);\n     throwIfTtsRateLimited(\n       'MiniMax',\n       response.status,\n       response.headers?.get('retry-after'),\n       quota ? { cause: quota } : undefined,\n     );\n     throw quota ?? new Error(message);\n   }\n \n   const data = await response.json();\n   throwIfMiniMaxBaseRespFailed(data, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n   const hexAudio = data?.data?.audio;\n   if (!hexAudio || typeof hexAudio !== 'string') {\n     throw new Error(`MiniMax TTS error: No audio returned. Response: ${JSON.stringify(data)}`);\n   }\n \n   const cleanedHex = hexAudio.trim();\n   if (cleanedHex.length % 2 !== 0) {\n     throw new Error('MiniMax TTS error: invalid hex audio payload length');\n   }\n \n   const audio = new Uint8Array(\n     cleanedHex.match(/.{1,2}/g)?.map((byte: string) => parseInt(byte, 16)) || [],\n   );\n   return {\n     audio,\n     format: data?.extra_info?.audio_format || config.format || 'mp3',\n   };\n }\n \n /**\n  * Google Gemini TTS via the Interactions API.\n  * Response audio is raw 24 kHz mono s16le PCM; wrap as WAV for classroom playback.\n  */\n async function generateGoogleTTS(\n   config: TTSModelConfig,\n   text: string,\n   signal: AbortSignal,\n ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n   const baseUrl = (config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['google-tts'].defaultBaseUrl || '').replace(\n     /\\/$/,\n     '',\n   );\n   const modelId = config.modelId || TTS_PROVIDERS['google-tts'].defaultModelId;\n   const voice = config.voice || DEFAULT_TTS_VOICES['google-tts'] || 'Kore';\n \n   const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/interactions`, {\n     method: 'POST',\n     headers: {\n       'x-goog-api-key': config.apiKey!,\n       'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',\n       ...appAttributionHeaders(baseUrl),\n     },\n     body: JSON.stringify({\n       model: modelId,\n       input: text,\n       response_format: { type: 'audio' },\n       generation_config: {\n         speech_config: [{ voice }],\n       },\n     }),\n     signal,\n   });\n \n   if (!response.ok) {\n     throwIfTtsRateLimited('Google', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n     const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n     throw new Error(`Google Gemini TTS API error: ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n   }\n \n   const payload = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as Record<string, unknown> | null;\n   const audio = extractGoogleInteractionsAudio(payload);\n   if (!audio) {\n     throw new Error('Google Gemini TTS API error: response missing audio data');\n   }\n \n   const pcm = new Uint8Array(Buffer.from(audio.data, 'base64'));\n   if (pcm.byteLength === 0) {\n     throw new Error('Google Gemini TTS API error: empty audio payload');\n   }\n \n   return {\n     audio: pcmS16leMonoToWav(pcm, audio.sampleRate),\n     format: 'wav',\n   };\n }\n \n /**\n  * Interactions REST responses put audio on `steps[].content[]`, not on the\n  * SDK convenience field `output_audio`. See speech-generation single-speaker docs.\n  */\n function extractGoogleInteractionsAudio(\n   payload: Record<string, unknown> | null,\n ): { data: string; sampleRate: number } | null {\n   if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.steps)) return null;\n \n   for (const step of payload.steps) {\n     if (!step || typeof step !== 'object') continue;\n     const content = (step as { content?: unknown }).content;\n     if (!Array.isArray(content)) continue;\n     for (const part of content) {\n       if (!part || typeof part !== 'object') continue;\n       const block = part as { type?: unknown; data?: unknown; mime_type?: unknown };\n       if (block.type !== 'audio' || typeof block.data !== 'string' || block.data.length === 0) {\n         continue;\n       }\n       return { data: block.data, sampleRate: sampleRateFromL16Mime(block.mime_type) };\n     }\n   }\n \n   return null;\n }\n \n /** `audio/l16;rate=24000` → 24000. Missing or unparseable rate stays at 24 kHz. */\n function sampleRateFromL16Mime(mime: unknown): number {\n   if (typeof mime !== 'string') return 24_000;\n   const match = /(?:^|[;\\s])rate=(\\d+)/i.exec(mime);\n   const rate = match ? Number(match[1]) : NaN;\n   return Number.isFinite(rate) && rate > 0 ? rate : 24_000;\n }\n \n /**\n  * ElevenLabs TTS implementation (direct API call with voice-specific endpoint)\n  */\n async function generateElevenLabsTTS(\n   config: TTSModelConfig,\n   text: string,\n   signal: AbortSignal,\n ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n   const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['elevenlabs-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n   const requestedFormat = config.format || 'mp3';\n   const clampedSpeed = Math.min(1.2, Math.max(0.7, config.speed || 1.0));\n   const outputFormatMap: Record<string, string> = {\n     mp3: 'mp3_44100_128',\n     opus: 'opus_48000_96',\n     pcm: 'pcm_44100',\n     wav: 'wav_44100',\n     ulaw: 'ulaw_8000',\n     alaw: 'alaw_8000',\n   };\n   const outputFormat = outputFormatMap[requestedFormat] || outputFormatMap.mp3;\n \n   const response = await ttsFetch(\n     config,\n     `${baseUrl}/text-to-speech/${encodeURIComponent(config.voice)}?output_format=${outputFormat}`,\n     {\n       method: 'POST',\n       headers: {\n         'xi-api-key': config.apiKey!,\n         'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',\n       },\n       body: JSON.stringify({\n         text,\n         model_id: config.modelId || 'eleven_multilingual_v2',\n         voice_settings: {\n           stability: 0.5,\n           similarity_boost: 0.75,\n           speed: clampedSpeed,\n         },\n       }),\n       signal,\n     },\n   );\n \n   if (!response.ok) {\n     throwIfTtsRateLimited('ElevenLabs', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n     const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n     throw new Error(`ElevenLabs TTS API error: ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n   }\n \n   return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'ElevenLabs', requestedFormat);\n }\n \n // Re-export from constants for convenience\n export { getAllTTSProviders, getTTSProvider, getTTSVoices } from './constants';\n \n /**\n+ * Fish Audio TTS implementation (https://docs.fish.audio/text-to-speech/api).\n+ *\n+ * - `POST {baseUrl}/tts` (default baseUrl `https://api.fish.audio/v1`), Bearer\n+ *   auth, and the model is carried in a `model` HEADER (s2.1-pro default;\n+ *   s2.1-pro-free, s2-pro, drama-3, s1 are the other routes).\n+ * - `reference_id` is the voice-model ID from a fish.audio voice page URL.\n+ *   The `default` registry voice is the sentinel for the service default\n+ *   voice (verified: the official quickstart omits `reference_id` entirely).\n+ * - Binary audio response (mp3/wav/opus/pcm).\n+ */\n+async function generateFishAudioTTS(\n+  config: TTSModelConfig,\n+  text: string,\n+  signal: AbortSignal,\n+): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n+  const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['fish-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n+  const requestedFormat = config.format || 'mp3';\n+  const format = ['mp3', 'wav', 'opus', 'pcm'].includes(requestedFormat) ? requestedFormat : 'mp3';\n+\n+  const body: Record<string, unknown> = { text, format };\n+  if (config.voice && config.voice !== 'default') {\n+    body.reference_id = config.voice;\n+  }\n+  const speed = config.speed && config.speed > 0 ? Math.min(2.0, Math.max(0.5, config.speed)) : 1.0;\n+  if (speed !== 1.0) {\n+    body.prosody = { speed };\n+  }\n+\n+  const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/tts`, {\n+    method: 'POST',\n+    headers: {\n+      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey!}`,\n+      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n+      // Fish routes the backend model through a plain `model` header, not the body.\n+      model: config.modelId || TTS_PROVIDERS['fish-tts'].defaultModelId,\n+    },\n+    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n+    signal,\n+  });\n+\n+  if (!response.ok) {\n+    throwIfTtsRateLimited('Fish Audio', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n+    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n+    throw new Error(`Fish Audio TTS API error (${response.status}): ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n+  }\n+\n+  return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'Fish Audio', requestedFormat);\n+}\n+\n+/**\n  * Doubao TTS 2.0 implementation (Volcengine Seed-TTS 2.0).\n  *\n  * Two auth modes, distinguished by the API key shape — Volcengine exposes\n  * Seed-TTS as two separate products that do NOT share credentials or endpoints\n  * (verified: a plan key 401s on the normal endpoint, and the plan endpoint\n  * rejects Bearer auth):\n  *  - Standalone speech console: `appId:accessKey` → normal endpoint\n  *    (.../api/v3/tts/unidirectional) with `X-Api-App-Id` + `X-Api-Access-Key`.\n  *  - Ark Agent Plan: a single `ark-...` plan key → plan endpoint\n  *    (.../api/plan/tts/unidirectional, carried in config.baseUrl) with\n  *    `X-Api-Key`. Lit up via the Token Plan one-click setup.\n  * The endpoint and auth header are bound together, so we pick both from the key\n  * shape — never a normal endpoint with X-Api-Key, or vice versa.\n  */\n async function generateDoubaoTTS(\n   config: TTSModelConfig,\n   text: string,\n   signal: AbortSignal,\n ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n   const rawKey = config.apiKey || '';\n   if (!rawKey) {\n     throw new Error(\n       'Doubao TTS requires an API key: an Agent Plan key, or \"appId:accessKey\" from the Volcengine speech console.',\n     );\n   }\n   const colonIdx = rawKey.indexOf(':');\n   // A colon means the classic appId:accessKey pair; otherwise treat the whole\n   // value as an Agent Plan single key (X-Api-Key auth on the /plan endpoint).\n   const isPlanKey = colonIdx < 0;\n   const appId = isPlanKey ? '' : rawKey.slice(0, colonIdx);\n   const accessKey = isPlanKey ? '' : rawKey.slice(colonIdx + 1);\n   // A colon with an empty half is a malformed pair — fail clearly rather than\n   // sending an empty appId/accessKey header that the API rejects opaquely.\n   if (!isPlanKey && (!appId || !accessKey)) {\n     throw new Error(\n       'Doubao TTS appId:accessKey is malformed — both halves are required (or use an Agent Plan key).',\n     );\n   }\n \n   const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['doubao-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n   const speechRate = Math.round(((config.speed || 1.0) - 1.0) * 100);\n \n   const authHeaders: Record<string, string> = isPlanKey\n     ? { 'X-Api-Key': rawKey }\n     : { 'X-Api-App-Id': appId, 'X-Api-Access-Key': accessKey };\n \n   const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/unidirectional`, {\n     method: 'POST',\n     headers: {\n       'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n       ...authHeaders,\n       'X-Api-Resource-Id': 'seed-tts-2.0',\n     },\n     body: JSON.stringify({\n       user: { uid: 'openmaic' },\n       req_params: {\n         text,\n         speaker: config.voice,\n         audio_params: {\n           format: 'mp3',\n           sample_rate: 24000,\n           speech_rate: speechRate,\n         },\n       },\n     }),\n     signal,\n   });\n \n   if (!response.ok) {\n     throwIfTtsRateLimited('Doubao', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n     const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n     throw new Error(`Doubao TTS API error (${response.status}): ${errorText}`);\n   }\n \n   const responseText = await response.text();\n   const audioChunks: Uint8Array[] = [];\n \n   // Doubao streams a run of concatenated JSON objects with no delimiter. Split\n   // them string-aware (see splitConcatenatedJsonObjects) — a naive `{`/`}` depth\n   // counter miscounts braces that appear inside a string value (e.g. an error\n   // `message` containing `}`), which corrupts the object boundaries.\n   for (const objectText of splitConcatenatedJsonObjects(responseText)) {\n     let chunk: { code: number; message?: string; data?: string };\n     try {\n       chunk = JSON.parse(objectText);\n     } catch {\n       continue;\n     }\n \n     if (chunk.code === 0 && chunk.data) {\n       audioChunks.push(new Uint8Array(Buffer.from(chunk.data, 'base64')));\n     } else if (chunk.code === 20000000) {\n       break;\n     } else if (chunk.code && chunk.code !== 0) {\n       if (chunk.code === 45000000 || chunk.code === 45000292) {\n         throw new TTSRateLimitError('doubao-tts', chunk.message || 'concurrency quota exceeded');\n       }\n       throw new Error(`Doubao TTS error: ${chunk.message || 'unknown'} (code: ${chunk.code})`);\n     }\n   }\n \n   if (audioChunks.length === 0) {\n     throw new Error('Doubao TTS: no audio data received');\n   }\n \n   const totalLength = audioChunks.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.length, 0);\n   const combined = new Uint8Array(totalLength);\n   let offset = 0;\n   for (const chunk of audioChunks) {\n     combined.set(chunk, offset);\n     offset += chunk.length;\n   }\n \n   return { audio: combined, format: 'mp3' };\n }\n \n /**\n  * Escape XML special characters for SSML\n  */\n function escapeXml(text: string): string {\n   return text\n     .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')\n     .replace(/</g, '&lt;')\n     .replace(/>/g, '&gt;')\n     .replace(/\"/g, '&quot;')\n     .replace(/'/g, '&apos;');\n }\n",

OpenAI TTS (https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/text-to-speech)\n  * - Azure TTS (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/text-to-speech)\n  * - GLM TTS (https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/models/sound-and-video/glm-tts)\n  * - In i18n.ts:\n  *    providerElevenLabsTTS: 'ElevenLabs TTS' / 'ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech'\n  */\n \n // ============================================================================\n // TTS (Text-to-Speech) Types\n // ============================================================================\n \n /**\n  * TTS Provider IDs\n  *\n  * Add new TTS providers here as union members.\n  * Keep in sync with TTS_PROVIDERS registry in constants.ts\n  */\n export type BuiltInTTSProviderId =\n   | 'openai-tts'\n   | 'azure-tts'\n   | 'glm-tts'\n   | 'qwen-tts'\n   | 'voxcpm-tts'\n   | 'doubao-tts'\n   | 'elevenlabs-tts'\n   | 'minimax-tts'\n   | 'google-tts'\n   | 'lemonade-tts'\n+  | 'fish-tts'\n   | 'browser-native-tts';\n \n export type TTSProviderId = BuiltInTTSProviderId | `custom-tts-${string}`;\n \n /**\n  * Voice information for TTS\n  */\n export interface TTSVoiceInfo {\n   id: string;\n   name: string;\n   language: string;\n   localeName?: string; // Language name in its native script (e.g., \"中文（简体，中国）\", \"日本語\")\n   gender?: 'male' | 'female' | 'neutral';\n   description?: string;\n   /** Model IDs this voice is compatible with. Undefined = all models. */\n   compatibleModels?: string[];\n }\n \n /**\n  * TTS Provider Configuration\n  */\n export interface TTSProviderConfig {\n   id: TTSProviderId;\n   name: string;\n   requiresApiKey: boolean;\n   defaultBaseUrl?: string;\n   icon?: string;\n   /**\n    * Declared exclusion from the agent-facing voice catalog. A provider flagged\n    * here (e.g. a paid showcase whose presets must never be offered to the\n    * agent) is dropped from `list_voices` / `set_roster` binding validation\n    * even when it is served and keyed — an explicit mechanism, not \"no env so\n    * absent\". Session-registered clones of the provider remain bindable when a\n    * registration adapter is configured (see the agent catalog assembly).\n    */\n   excludeFromAgentVoiceCatalog?: boolean;\n   /**\n    * True when the provider has NO deployment default voice: its only\n    * synthesizable voices are the ones registered at runtime. Such a provider's\n    * registered voices stay in the catalog regardless of clone-synthesis\n    * capability, because they are the only voices that provider can produce.\n    */\n   requiresRegisteredVoice?: boolean;\n   /** Available models. Empty array means provider has no model concept (e.g. Azure, Browser Native). */\n   models: Array<{ id: string; name: string }>;\n   /** Default model ID used when user hasn't selected one. Empty string if no models. */\n   defaultModelId: string;\n   voices: TTSVoiceInfo[];\n   supportedFormats: string[]; // ['mp3', 'wav', 'opus', etc.]\n   speedRange?: {\n     min: number;\n     max: number;\n     default: number;\n   };\n   /**\n    * `false` when the provider ignores the requested speed, which locks the speed\n    * control in settings. Omitted means speed is supported; a missing\n    * `speedRange` does not imply the opposite.\n    */\n   supportsSpeed?: boolean;\n }\n \n /**\n  * TTS Model Configuration for API calls\n  */\n export interface TTSModelConfig {\n   providerId: TTSProviderId;\n   modelId?: string;\n   apiKey?: string;\n   baseUrl?: string;\n   voice: string;\n   speed?: number;\n   format?: string;\n   providerOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;\n   /**\n    * Cancel the provider request(s) when this signal aborts. The agent runtime\n    * threads the session cancel signal here so an in-flight synthesis fetch is\n    * aborted within seconds of a cancel, instead of wedging the session until a\n    * restart repairs it.\n    */\n   signal?: AbortSignal;\n   /**\n    * Server-side outbound address policy for this provider call. `true` marks a\n    * client-supplied BYOK `baseUrl`: the request is pinned to the strict public\n    * policy, so metadata, private, loopback and CGNAT targets are refused even\n    * when the operator enabled local networks. When unset (a server-managed or\n    * built-in default target) the adapter falls back to the process-wide\n    * `ALLOW_LOCAL_NETWORKS` behavior.\n    */\n   publicOnly?: boolean;\n   /**\n    * `true` when the provider is server-configured: its endpoint is operator\n    * configuration and may be on a local network without ALLOW_LOCAL_NETWORKS\n    * (cloud metadata stays refused). Set by the server, never from request\n    * input; an unmanaged provider's catalog default leaves it unset.\n    */\n   managed?: boolean;\n }\n \n // ============================================================================\n // ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) Types\n // ============================================================================\n \n /**\n  * ASR Provider IDs\n  *\n  * Add new ASR providers here as union members.\n  * Keep in sync with ASR_PROVIDERS registry in constants.ts\n  */\n export type BuiltInASRProviderId =\n   | 'openai-whisper'\n   | 'browser-native'\n   | 'qwen-asr'\n   | 'funasr-asr'\n   | 'lemonade-asr'\n   | 'azure-asr';\n \n export type ASRProviderId = BuiltInASRProviderId | `custom-asr-${string}`;\n \n /**\n  * ASR Provider Configuration\n  */\n export interface ASRProviderConfig {\n   id: ASRProviderId;\n   name: string;\n   requiresApiKey: boolean;\n   defaultBaseUrl?: string;\n   icon?: string;\n   models: Array<{ id: string; name: string }>;\n   defaultModelId: string;\n   supportedLanguages: string[];\n   supportedFormats: string[];\n }\n \n /**\n  * ASR Model Configuration for API calls\n  */\n export interface ASRModelConfig {\n   providerId: ASRProviderId;\n   modelId?: string;\n   apiKey?: string;\n   baseUrl?: string;\n   language?: string;\n   /**\n    * Server-side outbound address policy (see {@link TTSModelConfig.publicOnly}).\n    * A client-supplied BYOK `baseUrl` sets this so the strict public policy wins.\n    */\n   publicOnly?: boolean;\n   /** Server-configured provider (see {@link TTSModelConfig.managed}). */\n   managed?: boolean;\n }\n \n /** Returns true if the provider ID is a user-defined custom TTS provider. */\n export function isCustomTTSProvider(id: string): boolean {\n   return typeof id === 'string' && id.startsWith('custom-tts-');\n }\n \n /** Returns true if the provider ID is a user-defined custom ASR provider. */\n export function isCustomASRProvider(id: string): boolean {\n   return typeof id === 'string' && id.startsWith('custom-asr-');\n }\n",
