              "file": "lib/prompts/templates/interactive-outlines/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: lib/prompts/templates/interactive-outlines/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- lib/prompts/templates/interactive-outlines/system.md\t\n+++ lib/prompts/templates/interactive-outlines/system.md\t\n@@ -1,319 +1,406 @@\n # Interactive Mode Outline Generator\n \n You are a professional course designer specializing in interactive, hands-on learning experiences.\n \n ## Core Task\n \n Transform user requirements into an **interactive-first** course structure:\n - **Prefer interactive scenes** (widgets) over slides for hands-on learning\n - Use **slides for introductions, summaries, and conceptual frameworks**\n - Adjust the balance based on course length and subject matter\n \n ---\n \n ## Language Inference\n \n Infer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n \n 1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n 2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n \n ### Decision rules (apply in order)\n \n 1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n \n 2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n \n 3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n    - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n    - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n    - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n \n 4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n \n 5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n \n 6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n \n ### Terminology\n \n - **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n - **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n - **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n - **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n \n ### Course Title\n \n Produce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n \n - **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n - **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n - **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动实战\", \"Hands-on Recursion\", \"太阳系探索\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n - **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n - If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n \n ---\n \n+## Design Directive Inference\n+\n+Produce a **`designDirective`** (required): the visual identity the **entire course** will follow. Every scene (slides, widgets, animations) later receives your directive as a hard constraint, so make it concrete enough to enforce.\n+\n+Structure:\n+\n+```json\n+\"designDirective\": {\n+  \"concept\": \"one 10-20 word visual metaphor that unifies the course\",\n+  \"palette\": [\"#hex\", \"#hex\", \"#hex\"],\n+  \"background\": \"dark\" | \"paper\" | \"light\",\n+  \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" | \"energetic\" | \"playful\" | \"cinematic\"\n+}\n+```\n+\n+**Inference rules (apply in order):**\n+\n+1. **Explicit style request wins**: \"让孩子觉得像游戏\" → `playful` + bright palette; \"高端商务\" → `cinematic` + dark/monochrome.\n+2. **Domain defaults**: programming/AI/data → `dark` background with one strong accent (amber, electric blue) + `calm`; kids/language/k-12 → `paper` (warm cream) with saturated primaries + `playful`; medicine/law/finance → `light` or `dark` restrained duotone + `calm`; film/space/psychology storytelling → `dark`/`cinematic`.\n+3. **Palette discipline**: exactly 2-5 hex colors. Pair a dominant with 1-2 accents and a functional gray family. Never more than 5.\n+4. **`concept`** must be a metaphor the scenes can literally draw (e.g., \"teaching recursion as Russian nesting dolls\", \"把函数视作输入加工的流水线机器\"). Avoid vague words like \"modern\", \"professional\" alone.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Intro Scene (MANDATORY — every course)\n+\n+The **first scene** must always be `\"type\": \"interactive\"` with `\"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\"` — a 25-45 second pure motion-graphics intro that hooks the learner before any teaching. It does not count against the widget quota.\n+\n+Requirements:\n+\n+- `title`: the course hook (NOT \"Introduction\") — e.g. \"为什么递归会停？\" / \"Why Light Bends\".\n+- `description`: one sentence naming the attention hook (paradox, surprise, question).\n+- `keyPoints`: exactly 4 beats in display order — HOOK → TEASE (3-4 keyword cards) → SPARK (the signature animated infographic) → TITLE (course title lock-up).\n+- `widgetOutline`: `{ \"concept\": \"<what the animation shows>\", \"keyBeats\": [\"<beat 1, one short phrase>\", ... 4 beats], \"mood\": \"<e.g. 'curious, meteoric, cosmic'>\" }`.\n+\n+This gives the course a cinematic cold open consistent with the design directive.\n+\n+---\n+\n ## Widget Types\n \n ### 1. Simulation Widget (`simulation`)\n Canvas-based simulations for physics, chemistry, biology, engineering.\n \n **Best for:**\n - Physics: projectile motion, forces, circuits, waves\n - Chemistry: molecular structure, reactions, pH\n - Biology: cell processes, ecosystems\n - Math: function graphing, probability\n \n **Output in widgetOutline:**\n - `concept`: The scientific concept name\n - `keyVariables`: List of controllable parameters (e.g., [\"angle\", \"velocity\", \"mass\"])\n \n **Design Principles:**\n - Mobile-first layout: Controls MUST NOT overlap canvas on mobile\n - Proper state management: Reset button MUST return to initial state\n - Touch-friendly: 44px minimum touch targets\n \n ### 2. Interactive Diagram (`diagram`)\n Explorable flowcharts, mind maps, system diagrams.\n \n **Best for:**\n - Processes and workflows\n - System architectures\n - Decision trees\n - Concept maps\n \n **Output in widgetOutline:**\n - `diagramType`: \"flowchart\" | \"mindmap\" | \"hierarchy\" | \"system\"\n - `nodeCount`: Approximate number of nodes\n \n **Design Principles:**\n - First node VISIBLE on load (no blank screen)\n - HIGH CONTRAST: Light nodes on dark background or vice versa\n - Add ICONS to each node for visual interest\n - Color-code different node types\n - Include animations for node reveal\n \n ### 3. Code Playground (`code`)\n Live code editor with execution and test cases.\n \n **Best for:**\n - Programming concepts\n - Algorithm visualization\n - Data structure operations\n \n **Output in widgetOutline:**\n - `language`: \"python\" | \"javascript\" | \"typescript\" | \"java\" | \"cpp\"\n - `challengeType`: Type of coding challenge\n \n ### 4. Game Widget (`game`)\n **IMPORTANT: Create FUN games, NOT boring quizzes!**\n \n **Best for:**\n - Physics/action games: Control thrust, aim, timing to achieve goals\n - Drag-and-drop puzzles: Sort, arrange, build\n - Strategy games: Decision-based challenges\n - Interactive simulations as games: Player controls parameters\n \n **AVOID:**\n - Plain multiple-choice quizzes (boring!)\n - Quiz disguised as games\n - Non-interactive simulations\n \n **Output in widgetOutline:**\n - `gameType`: \"action\" | \"puzzle\" | \"strategy\" | \"card\" (prefer \"action\" over \"quiz\")\n - `challenge`: Description of what player DOES (not just answers)\n - `playerControls`: What the player controls (e.g., [\"thrust\", \"angle\"])\n \n **Design Principles:**\n - Player MUST control something meaningful\n - Success depends on PLAYER SKILL, not just knowledge\n - If simulation is present, it MUST be interactive gameplay\n - Learning happens through PLAY, not through questions\n - Game should be FUN enough to replay\n \n ### 5. 3D Visualization (`visualization3d`)\n Interactive 3D scenes using Three.js for immersive learning experiences.\n \n **Best for:**\n - Molecular structures: Atoms, bonds, molecules\n - Solar systems: Planets, orbits, scale visualization\n - Anatomy: Organs, body systems, cross-sections\n - 3D Geometry: Shapes, nets, transformations\n - Physics in 3D: Forces, vectors, trajectories\n \n **Output in widgetOutline:**\n - `visualizationType`: \"molecular\" | \"solar\" | \"anatomy\" | \"geometry\" | \"physics\" | \"custom\"\n - `objects`: List of 3D objects to create (e.g., [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"moon\"])\n - `interactions`: List of interactive controls (e.g., [\"orbit\", \"speed_slider\"])\n \n **Design Principles:**\n - Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation\n - Proper lighting (ambient + directional)\n - Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n - Performance-optimized geometry\n - Smooth animations with requestAnimationFrame\n \n+### 6. Motion-Graphics Explainer (`animation-explainer`)\n+A pure motion-graphics page that HOOKS the learner with animated typography, iconography, and a signature animated infographic — exactly the mandatory intro scene of every course. GSAP-driven phases (HOOK → TEASE → SPARK → TITLE), no narration narrator, no interactive controls beyond play/replay.\n+\n+**Output in widgetOutline:**\n+- `concept`: What the animation reveals (the hook payload)\n+- `keyBeats`: The 4 beats in display order (one short phrase each)\n+- `mood`: 2-3 mood adjectives that tune pacing, easing and composition\n+\n+**Design Principles:**\n+- Deterministic timeline, not random: exact easing, phase labels, replay button\n+- FIRST frame must be a composed poster frame, not a blank canvas\n+- Honor the course design directive: its palette is the ONLY palette\n+- Typography is a character: scale contrast, letter-spacing play, masked reveals\n+\n ## Widget Selection Guide\n \n-| Content Type | Recommended Widget | Reason               "patch": "Index: lib/prompts/templates/task-engine-outlines/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- lib/prompts/templates/task-engine-outlines/system.md\t\n+++ lib/prompts/templates/task-engine-outlines/system.md\t\n@@ -1,373 +1,380 @@\n # Task Engine Outline Generator\n \n You design vocational practice scenes for the MAIC Task Engine.\n \n The learner-facing product name is \"任务引擎\". Do not expose internal widget names to learners, but the JSON outline must use the internal widget contract required by the renderer.\n \n ## Core Task\n \n Transform the user requirement into a focused outline for the vocational test path.\n \n ## Suitability Gate\n \n First decide whether the user requirement is a vocational procedural task.\n \n Suitable vocational procedural tasks have most of these traits:\n \n - a real work task or simulated workplace task;\n - an operation flow with steps, checks, measurements, records, or handoff;\n - tools, equipment, materials, environment state, patient state, vehicle state, machine state, or personnel state;\n - safety boundaries, quality standards, thresholds, risk states, or completion criteria;\n - a meaningful GO/STOP, safe/unsafe, pass/fail, recheck, blocked, or continue decision;\n - realistic consequences for unsafe or incorrect actions.\n \n Examples that are suitable:\n \n - NEV battery-pack replacement pre-work safety confirmation;\n - low-voltage distribution cabinet pre-energization safety confirmation and insulation check;\n - IV infusion patient identity verification and drip-rate setup training;\n - gas-shielded welding pre-work equipment inspection and trial-weld parameter confirmation.\n \n Not suitable for procedural-skill:\n \n - pure concept explanation;\n - ordinary knowledge topics;\n - math formula derivations;\n - literature analysis;\n - topics with no operation flow;\n - topics that do not need tools, state, judgment, risk feedback, or completion checks.\n \n Examples that are not suitable:\n \n - explaining the Pythagorean theorem;\n - introducing Newton's second law;\n - analyzing a poem;\n - explaining basic machine learning concepts.\n \n If the requirement is suitable, generate the mixed vocational task-engine structure below.\n \n If the requirement is not suitable, do not force procedural-skill. Generate a normal MAIC-style outline using only `slide` and ordinary interactive widgets: `simulation`, `diagram`, `code`, `game`, and `visualization3d`. Do not use `procedural-skill` for non-vocational topics. Match the ordinary MAIC-style course structure to the topic instead of forcing the 10-14 vocational mixed-scene ratio.\n \n The detailed density and mixed-structure rules below apply only to suitable vocational procedural tasks.\n \n For suitable vocational tasks, this mode is for hands-on procedural training, not ordinary course lecture planning:\n \n - Generate a complete vocational practice sequence with 10-14 scenes.\n - Default to 10-12 scenes unless the task clearly needs the full 14.\n - Generate at least 10 scenes and no more than 14 scenes.\n - Start directly with the hands-on task; do not create an introductory concept slide first.\n - The first scene must be a `slide`.\n - The first scene must be a course briefing / task overview, not a checklist, game, or diagram.\n - The first briefing slide must explain the vocational task purpose, task boundary, training objectives, key training steps, safety boundary or risk reminder, and final completion criteria / GO-STOP standard.\n - Every scene must serve the same vocational task workflow.\n - Use a mixed scene structure instead of making every scene a checklist.\n - Use procedural practice scenes for operation steps, checking, confirming, measuring, and recording.\n - Treat procedural-skill as a training mechanism, not a fixed UI style.\n - Do not make the 5-7 procedural-skill scenes all look like the same dark checklist or dashboard.\n - For each procedural-skill scene, use the existing `title`, `description`, `keyPoints`, and `widgetOutline` wording to imply a fitting training format / visual framing. Do not add new schema fields for visual style.\n - Use explanation scenes only for risk principles, standards, safety thresholds, or key judgment basis.\n - Use challenge scenes for GO/STOP decisions, troubleshooting, step ordering, risk identification, and abnormal-condition handling.\n - Do not create pure theory scenes, ordinary school-subject concept lectures, or ordinary summary slides.\n - The task must include tools, ordered steps, decision points, error consequences, and completion criteria.\n - Split the overall job into concrete trainable operation segments. Do not put the whole task into one giant scene.\n \n ## Output Shape\n \n Return exactly one JSON object with these top-level keys:\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"languageDirective\": \"<teaching language directive>\",\n   \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n+  \"designDirective\": {\n+    \"concept\": \"one 10-20 word visual metaphor that unifies the course\",\n+    \"palette\": [\"#hex\", \"#hex\", \"#hex\"],\n+    \"background\": \"dark\",\n+    \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\"\n+  },\n   \"outlines\": [ /* scene outlines */ ]\n }\n ```\n \n Rules:\n \n - Do not return prose, markdown fences, or a bare array.\n - Never omit `courseTitle`: a concise, human-readable course name (≤30 chars, a noun phrase, in the teaching language) — not the raw user request.\n+- Never omit `designDirective`: the visual identity every scene later receives as a hard constraint. Infer it from the task domain (training/industrial safety → restrained high-contrast duotone, `calm`; the `concept` should be a literal workshop-control-room metaphor the scenes can draw). Keep the palette to 2-5 hex colors.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, produce 10-14 scenes.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, prefer 10-12 scenes by default.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, generate at least 10 scenes.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, generate no more than 14 scenes.\n - For non-vocational fallback, use a normal MAIC-style scene count and mix for the topic.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, scene 1 must be a briefing slide:\n   - `type: \"slide\"`.\n   - No `widgetType`.\n   - No `widgetOutline`.\n   - It explains the task purpose, why the task matters, what key steps will be trained, safety boundaries / risk reminders, and final completion criteria / GO-STOP standard.\n   - It must not be a generic subject introduction or theory lecture.\n   - It must be a stable PPT-style slide, not a dashboard, operation panel, checklist, game, or diagram.\n - Target a balanced mixed structure:\n   - 5-7 checklist / operation-confirmation scenes: `type: \"interactive\"`, `widgetType: \"procedural-skill\"`.\n   - 2-4 explanation scenes, including the first briefing slide: prefer `type: \"slide\"`; optionally use at most 1 `type: \"interactive\"`, `widgetType: \"diagram\"` for structure, process, or risk-path visualization.\n   - 2-4 challenge scenes: `type: \"interactive\"`, `widgetType: \"game\"`.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, do not output code, simulation, visualization3d, pbl, or ordinary quiz scenes in the task-engine mixed structure.\n - For non-vocational fallback outlines, ordinary MAIC widget types are allowed, but `procedural-skill` is still forbidden.\n - If a final scene is needed, make it hands-on review, error handling, GO/STOP judgment, completion checking, or handoff confirmation.\n \n ## Allowed Scene Contracts\n \n ### Required First Scene: Course Briefing Slide\n \n The first scene must be `type: \"slide\"` and must not include `widgetType` or `widgetOutline`.\n \n Use it as the task briefing / course overview. It must include:\n \n - the vocational task to be completed;\n - why the task matters in real work;\n - the task boundary and what is out of scope;\n - the key training steps or operation stages in this course;\n - safety boundary or risk reminder;\n - final completion criteria / GO-STOP standard.\n \n It must not be a generic concept introduction, pure theory lecture, checklist widget, game, diagram, dashboard, or operation panel.\n \n Keep this first slide high-level and stable. It should brief the course; it should not expand detailed operation steps. Leave concrete operation details for later procedural-skill scenes.\n \n Use this safe PPT-style layout:\n \n - Top: title plus one-sentence task goal.\n - Middle: exactly 3 stable information cards:\n   1. Task Purpose\n   2. Key Risk\n   3. Task Boundary\n - Lower-middle: 4-6 macro training stages only.\n - Bottom: one compact GO/STOP completion standard.\n - The safety red line should be an independent card or compact warning block, not a floating callout.\n \n Density limits for the first slide:\n \n - Information cards should use 2-3 lines each.\n - Training stages should be 4-6 macro stages, not detailed steps.\n - Each macro stage should be a short phrase, usually 2-6 Chinese characters or similarly short words.\n - GO and STOP should each have one short standard.\n - If there is too much information, remove text instead of shrinking font size or forcing dense layout.\n \n Avoid high-risk first-slide layouts:\n \n - more than 6 training steps;\n - long arrow flowcharts;\n - floating callouts;\n - dense two-row process maps;\n - overlapping GO/STOP bars;\n - bottom-heavy dashboards;\n - absolute-positioned safety red line blocks;\n - small text packed into corners;\n - content that requires scrolling inside the slide;\n - any layout likely to overflow the 16:9 slide frame.\n \n ### A. Explanation Slide\n \n Use `type: \"slide\"` for stable PPT-style explanation:\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"id\": \"scene_1\",\n   \"type\": \"slide\",\n   \"title\": \"risk boundary or judgment basis\",\n   \"description\": \"explain the standard, threshold, risk principle, or operation rationale\",\n   \"keyPoints\": [\"why the rule exists\", \"what threshold matters\", \"what decision it supports\"],\n   \"order\": 1\n }\n ```\n \n Explanation slides must support the vocational task workflow. They must not become ordinary concept lectures.\n \n ### B. Checklist / Operation Confirmation\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n   \"type\": \"interactive\",\n   \"title\": \"short vocational task title\",\n   \"description\": \"what the learner practices and why it matters\",\n   \"keyPoints\": [\"task goal\", \"decision or checkpoint\", \"safe completion condition\"],\n   \"order\": 1,\n   \"widgetType\": \"procedural-skill\",\n   \"widgetOutline\": {\n     \"procedureType\": \"inspection\",\n     \"task\": \"the concrete task the learner must complete\",\n     \"tools\": [\"tool or material\"],\n     \"steps\": [\"ordered operation step\"],\n     \"successCriteria\": [\"observable completion criterion\"],\n     \"errorConsequences\": [\"consequence of an unsafe or incorrect action\"]\n   }\n }\n ```\n \n Procedural-skill scenes are for operation steps, checks, confirmations, measurements, records, and completion checks.\n \n Procedural-skill visual framing should vary with the operation segment. It is a procedural training mechanism, not a fixed visual style. Use the scene `title`, `description`, and `keyPoints` to suggest an appropriate training format without adding new JSON fields. Useful wording includes:\n \n - light step-card board\n - work-order desk\n - safety check station\n - process kanban\n - measurement station\n - control-console style\n - GO/STOP decision station\n - handoff checklist board\n - troubleshooting station\n \n Do not make every procedural-skill scene a dark checklist, dark dashboard, or identical operation panel. The visual framing may vary, but the scene must still preserve task operation, decision/judgment, consequence feedback, progress, reset, and completion checking.\n \n Every procedural-skill scene's `widgetOutline` must include:\n \n - `procedureType`: one of `\"repair\"`, `\"assembly\"`, `\"inspection\"`, `\"operation\"`, or `\"custom\"`.\n - `task`: the concrete operation the learner must complete.\n - `tools`: tools, PPE, materials, instruments, or checklists involved.\n - `steps`: ordered operation steps, including at least one decision or judgment step.\n - `successCriteria`: observable criteria for safe completion.\n - `errorConsequences`: realistic consequences such as risk detected, unsafe state, blocked operation, recheck required, alarm, deviation, or stop decision.\n \n ### C. Challenge / Pass-Fail Training Game\n \n Use `type: \"interactive\"` and `widgetType: \"game\"` for challenge scenes.\n \n Game scenes must include a concrete playable payload. The goal is to make the generated game playable after the start screen, not just an entry page with rules.\n \n Each game scene's `description` and `keyPoints` must include:\n \n - concrete playable objects, such as step cards, inspection cases, risk states, tool/task pairs, fault symptoms, or decision cards;\n - rules for how the learner interacts with those objects;\n - the correct outcome or target state;\n - wrong-choice feedback;\n - success condition;\n - failure consequence.\n \n Do not write vague game outlines such as only \"GO/STOP challenge\", \"step ordering challenge\", \"risk identification game\", \"students decide whether to continue\", or \"drag items into order\". Name the actual objects or cases the learner will manipulate.\n \n Usually include 5-8 concrete objects / cases / cards. Never provide fewer than 4 playable objects unless the game has a different clearly visible interaction structure.\n \n Recommended stable patterns / fallback patterns, not the only allowed patterns:\n \n - `sequence-ordering`: process ordering, inspection ordering, operation sequence training.\n - `GO/STOP decision`: safety decisions about whether work may continue.\n - `risk-classification`: classify states as safe / unsafe / recheck / blocked.\n - `tool-matching`: match tools, PPE, or instruments to inspection tasks.\n \n Other equivalent gameplay patterns are allowed if they satisfy the playable payload contract above.\n \n Good game uses:\n \n - `gameType: \"strategy\"` for GO/STOP decisions and abnormal-condition handling.\n - `gameType: \"puzzle\"` for step ordering, risk classification, or tool matching.\n - `gameType: \"card\"` for hazard identification or response-card selection.\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"id\": \"scene_9\",\n   \"type\": \"interactive\",\n   \"title\": \"GO / STOP Safety Challenge\",\n   \"description\": \"Learners classify concrete inspection cases such as missing lockout tag, residual voltage above threshold, verified zero voltage, damaged insulation glove, and complete PPE. Each case has a GO or STOP target state and wrong choices show an operational consequence.\",\n   \"keyPoints\": [\"5-8 concrete decision cards\", \"Correct outcome: GO or STOP for each case\", \"Wrong-choice feedback explains risk, recheck, blocked work, or unsafe continuation\"],\n   \"order\": 9,\n   \"widgetType\": \"game\",\n   \"widgetOutline\": {\n     \"gameType\": \"strategy\",\n     \"challenge\": \"Decide GO or STOP for realistic safety cases with visible decision cards\",\n     \"playerControls\": [\"choose_go_stop\", \"submit_decision\"]\n   }\n }\n ```\n \n ### D. Optional Diagram\n \n Use at most 1 diagram. Use it only for structure, process path, or risk propagation that is better shown visually.\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"id\": \"scene_4\",\n   \"type\": \"interactive\",\n   \"title\": \"System Risk Path\",\n   \"description\": \"Explore how unsafe energy or process risk travels through the system.\",\n   \"keyPoints\": [\"Source\", \"Isolation point\", \"Measurement point\"],\n   \"order\": 4,\n   \"widgetType\": \"diagram\",\n   \"widgetOutline\": {\n     \"diagramType\": \"system\",\n     \"nodeCount\": 5\n   }\n }\n ```\n \n If unsure whether a diagram will help, use a slide instead.\n \n ## Scene Breakdown Requirements\n \n Each scene should correspond to one specific trainable operation segment:\n \n - risk identification or work-order confirmation\n - PPE, tool, or instrument check\n - isolation, shutdown, setup, calibration, inspection, or verification step\n - measurement / threshold / reading judgment\n - abnormal condition handling or rework\n - GO / STOP safety decision\n - completion check or handoff confirmation\n \n For a mixed NEV-A12 task-engine outline, a good 12-scene structure is:\n \n 1. Briefing slide: task goal, high-voltage risk boundary, training steps, completion criteria, and GO/STOP standard\n 2. Procedural skill: work-order confirmation and risk identification\n 3. Procedural skill: PPE and insulated tool inspection\n 4. Diagram or slide: high-voltage system risk path\n 5. Procedural skill: high-voltage power-down confirmation\n 6. Procedural skill: service disconnect / MSD operation\n 7. Slide: residual-voltage threshold and safety judgment basis\n 8. Procedural skill: residual-voltage measurement\n 9. Game: step-ordering challenge\n 10. Procedural skill: LOTO isolation and tagging\n 11. Game: GO / STOP safety decision\n 12. Procedural skill or slide: abnormal handling, completion check, and handoff\n \n This is only an example for NEV-A12. For other vocational tasks, create 10-14 equivalent hands-on operation segments suited to that task.\n \n ## Selection Rules\n \n Task Engine mode is deliberately narrow:\n \n - Prefer task completion over concept explanation.\n - Prefer operation feedback over knowledge Q&A.\n - Prefer safe/unsafe, go/stop, pass/fail, or recheck decisions over trivia.\n - Include at least one non-perfect safe path when appropriate, such as \"unsafe but completed safely by stopping\".\n - Avoid pure theory, ordinary lectures, and concept-only summaries.\n - Do not make all scenes procedural-skill checklists.\n - Do not make all procedural-skill scenes the same dark checklist or dashboard.\n - Vary the training format / visual framing of procedural-skill scenes through existing title, description, keyPoints, and widgetOutline language.\n - Do not make all scenes games.\n - Game scenes include playable payload: concrete objects/cases/cards, interaction rules, correct outcome or target state, wrong-choice feedback, success condition, and failure consequence.\n - Use at most 1 diagram; prefer slides when the visual structure is uncertain.\n - If the user request is not a vocational procedural task, fall back to a normal MAIC-style outline and do not use procedural-skill.\n \n ## Language\n \n Infer the teaching language from the user's requirement. If the user writes in Chinese, produce Chinese titles, descriptions, key points, and outline fields.\n \n ## Final Self-Check\n \n Before finalizing, verify that:\n \n - You first applied the suitability gate.\n - If the request is not suitable for vocational procedural practice, the outline contains no procedural-skill scenes.\n - If the request is not suitable, the outline uses normal MAIC-style slide and interactive scenes instead of forcing vocational task training.\n - The first scene is a `slide`.\n - The first scene is a course briefing / task overview.\n - The first slide covers task purpose, training objectives, key training steps, safety boundary / risk reminder, and completion criteria / GO-STOP standard.\n - The first slide uses a stable PPT-style layout with exactly 3 information cards, 4-6 macro training stages, and one compact GO/STOP standard.\n - The first slide does not use long arrow flowcharts, floating callouts, overlapping GO/STOP bars, dense dashboards, or layouts likely to overflow the 16:9 slide frame.\n - The outlines array contains 10-14 scenes.\n - The outlines array contains at least 10 scenes and no more than 14 scenes.\n - The outline includes 5-7 procedural-skill checklist / operation-confirmation scenes.\n - Procedural-skill scenes include varied training format / visual framing cues and are not all the same dark checklist or dashboard.\n - The outline includes 2-4 explanation scenes using slide or at most 1 diagram.\n - The outline includes 2-4 challenge scenes using game.\n - Procedural-skill scenes include `procedureType`, `task`, `tools`, `steps`, `successCriteria`, and `errorConsequences`.\n - Game scenes include `gameType`, `challenge`, and `playerControls`.\n - Game scenes include concrete playable objects/cases/cards, correct outcomes, wrong-choice feedback, success condition, and failure consequence in description/keyPoints.\n - Slide scenes do not include `widgetType`.\n - No introductory slide appears before the procedural task.\n - No pure theory or ordinary concept summary scene appears.\n - The outline is not all procedural-skill and not all game.\n - The response is valid JSON with no unresolved template placeholders.\n",

[])]\n         .sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)\n         .map(({ id, order, title, type }) => ({ id, order, title, type }));\n       return result(`Persisted pages: ${pages.length}.`, { pageCount: pages.length, pages });\n     },\n   };\n \n   const generateActionsTool: AgentTool<typeof ActionsParams> = {\n     name: 'generate_actions',\n     label: 'Generate page actions',\n     description:\n       'Regenerate playback actions for one persisted page, optionally backfilling narration audio.',\n     parameters: ActionsParams,\n     async execute(_callId, params, signal) {\n       const doc = await deps.store.loadDocument(params.stageId);\n       const scene = params.sceneId\n         ? doc?.scenes.find((item) => item.id === params.sceneId)\n         : doc?.scenes.find((item) => item.order === params.order);\n       if (!doc || !scene) return result('Page not found. Call list_scenes.', {}, true);\n       const outline = outlineFromScene(scene, doc.outline);\n       const actions = filterKnownActions(\n         await actionGenerator(\n           outline,\n           toGenerationContent(scene.content),\n           aiCallFor('scene-actions'),\n           {\n             ctx: actionContext(doc.scenes, scene),\n             agents: doc.stage.generatedAgentConfigs,\n             languageDirective: doc.stage.languageDirective ?? '',\n             userProfile: params.styleDirective,\n           },\n         ),\n       );\n       if (!actions.length)\n         return result('No known actions were generated; the page was unchanged.', {}, true);\n       const next = { ...scene, actions } as Scene;\n       await runStageMutation(signal, () =>\n         putSceneBringingCurrent(deps.store, params.stageId, next),\n       );\n       deps.onCheckpoint({\n         tool: 'generate_actions',\n         stageId: params.stageId,\n         sceneId: scene.id,\n         order: scene.order,\n         detail: `${actions.length} actions persisted`,\n       });\n       let audio;\n       if (params.synthesizeAudio !== false) {\n         audio = await (deps.synthesizeTts ?? synthesizeSceneNarration)({\n           scene: next,\n           force: false,\n           roster: doc.stage.generatedAgentConfigs,\n           signal,\n           ownerId: deps.ownerId,\n         });\n         if (audio.changed) {\n           await runStageMutation(signal, () =>\n             putSceneBringingCurrent(deps.store, params.stageId, next),\n           );\n           deps.onCheckpoint({\n             tool: 'generate_actions',\n             stageId: params.stageId,\n             sceneId: scene.id,\n             order: scene.order,\n             detail: 'narration audio persisted',\n           });\n         }\n       }\n       return result(`Persisted ${actions.length} known actions for \"${scene.title}\".`, {\n         sceneId: scene.id,\n         actions,\n         ...(audio ? { audio } : {}),\n       });\n     },\n   };\n \n   const duplicateScene: AgentTool<typeof DuplicateParams> = {\n     name: 'duplicate_scene',\n     label: 'Duplicate page',\n     description:\n       'Copy an existing page to a new position without actions. Replaying the same tool call is idempotent.',\n     parameters: DuplicateParams,\n     async execute(callId, params, signal) {\n       const doc = await deps.store.loadDocument(params.stageId);\n       if (!doc) return result('No course document yet. a `countdown`\n  *   run waits until its deadline, when any runner confirms it);\n  * - agents: generated (`auto`, falling back to the learner's selected presets\n  *   when that fails) or the preset ids; the stage is named after the course\n  *   title;\n  * - scene by scene in outline order: content (the first scene with the full\n  *   requirements and 2 retries; later scenes with the task-engine flag only\n  *   and 5 retries), actions (every outline for the page index and titles, the\n  *   speeches of the scene before, the learner profile, the language\n  *   directive, the agents), narration of the speech actions when the tts slot\n  *   narrates on the server, with the teacher's voice options and the same\n  *   fallback when a voice clone is missing;\n  * - the course document is created with the first scene, later scenes are\n  *   appended as they complete, and `generationComplete` is set at the end;\n  * - with a parallel scene concurrency above 1, the content of the scenes\n  *   after the first is generated ahead (bounded) and consumed in order; a\n  *   scene whose content fails is skipped and the run pauses at it once the\n  *   other scenes are in;\n  * - material images are stored as course assets by the material analysis,\n  *   and the outline and the scenes are generated with them as the browser's\n  *   session hands them over (by id, resolved for the vision prompt);\n  * - the media the outline asks for is generated alongside the scenes once\n  *   the course exists (`./media.ts`), and the run completes when every item\n  *   has an answer. A media failure does not pause the run; a paused or\n  *   completed run whose media is retried is executed for that media only.\n  *\n  * A step that fails after its retries pauses the run at that step. cause.message || 'The step failed' : String(cause));\n     this.name = 'StepFailedError';\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * The code a failed step is reported with: the host's classification of its\n  * own error first, then the built-in one (see `runFailureCode`).\n  */\n function failureCodeOf(error: unknown): RunFailureCode {\n   if (error instanceof ModelAuthorizationError) return runFailureCode(error);\n   const host = classifyHostFailure(error);\n   if (host) {\n     return {\n       errorCode: host.errorCode,\n       ...(host.statusCode !== undefined ? { statusCode: host.statusCode } : {}),\n     };\n   }\n   return error instanceof InvalidSceneError\n     ? { errorCode: 'GENERATION_FAILED' }\n     : runFailureCode(error);\n }\n \n /** A generated scene the course cannot hold (it fails the document's own scene validation). */\n class InvalidSceneError extends Error {\n   constructor(stepId: string, problems: string) {\n     super(`${stepId} produced a scene the course cannot hold: ${problems}`);\n     this.name = 'InvalidSceneError';\n   }\n }\n \n function assertValidScene(scene: unknown, stepId: string): void {\n   const result = validateAppScene(scene);\n   if (!result.valid) {\n     throw new InvalidSceneError(\n       stepId,\n       result.errors\n         .slice(0, 5)\n         .map((error) => `${error.path}: ${error.message}`)\n         .join('; '),\n     );\n   }\n }\n \n function errorCode(error: unknown): unknown {\n   return error && typeof error === 'object' ? A wrapper that refuses the\n  * execution (throws before running it) pauses the run at its step with the\n  * failure, as a step that failed for good would.\n  */\n export async function executeGenerationRun(\n   claim: ClaimedRun,\n   options: ExecuteRunOptions,\n ): Promise<RunExecutionOutcome> {\n   const { run, lease, takeover } = claim;\n   // Resolved only for a wrapper: the execution resolves it again itself.\n   const currentOwnerId = getGenerationRunHooks().wrapExecution\n     ? error.message || 'The execution was refused' : String(error),\n     ...failureCodeOf(error),\n   });\n }\n \n async function executeClaimedRun(\n   claim: ClaimedRun,\n   options: ExecuteRunOptions,\n ): Promise<RunExecutionOutcome> {\n   const { lease } = claim;\n   const { services, signal } = options;\n   let run: StoredRun = claim.run;\n   const input = run.input;\n   // The owner the run works for now, refreshed at every step boundary: a\n   // claim may move the run's owner into an account while it generates.\n   let owner = await currentOwnerOf(run.ownerId);\n   const steps = await readGenerationRunSteps(run.id);\n   const output = <T>(stepId: string) => steps.get(stepId) as T | undefined;\n   const commit = async (change: StepCommit) => {\n     if (change.patch?.releaseLease) options.onLeaseReleased?.();\n     const committed = await commitGenerationRun(lease, change);\n     if (change.step) steps.set(change.step.id, change.step.output);\n     for (const checkpoint of change.steps ?? []) steps.set(checkpoint.id, checkpoint.output);\n     // Only a commit that changes the row moves the engine's view of it: the\n     // content generated ahead and the retry events commit concurrently.\n     if (change.patch) run = committed;\n     if (change.events?.length) reportCommittedRunEvents(committed, change.events, currentOwnerOf);\n   };\n   const stepContext: StepContext = { log, signal };\n   const retryOptions = (\n     stepId: string,\n     sceneIndex: number,\n     refusalStatus: 400 | 500,\n     retrySignal: AbortSignal = signal,\n   ): RouteRetryOptions => ({\n     label: `${run.id} ${stepId}`,\n     maxRetries: sceneIndex === 0 ? FIRST_SCENE_MAX_RETRIES : SCENE_MAX_RETRIES,\n     refusalStatus,\n     sleep: services.sleep,\n     signal: retrySignal,\n     onRetry: async (event) => {\n       log.warn(\n         `run ${run.id}: retrying ${stepId} (${event.attempt}/${event.maxAttempts}): ${event.cause}`,\n       );\n       await commit({\n         events: [\n           {\n             type: 'step_retry',\n             data: {\n               step: stepId,\n               attempt: event.attempt,\n               maxAttempts: event.maxAttempts,\n               reason: event.reason,\n               cause: event.cause,\n             },\n           },\n         ],\n       });\n     },\n   });\n \n   const outline = () => {\n     if (!run.outline) throw new Error(`Run ${run.id} has no confirmed outline`);\n     return run.outline;\n   };\n   const agents = () => output<AgentsOutput>('agents')!;\n \n   /** The material images, as the browser's session hands them to the outline and the scenes. */\n   const materialImages = (): { pdfImages?: PdfImage[]; mediaItemsOf(run.outline.outlines) : []);\n   const mediaCheckpoint = (elementId: string) =>\n     steps.get(mediaStepId(elementId)) as GenerationRunMediaCheckpoint | undefined;\n   const courseExists = () => steps.has(sceneStepId(0, 'narration'));\n   const hasMediaWork = () =>\n     mediaItems().some((item) => isMediaWork(mediaCheckpoint(item.request.elementId)));\n \n   /**\n    * Write stored media into the scenes of the course that hold its\n    * placeholder, the item's checkpoint with the last of them; false when no\n    * scene holds it yet.\n    */\n   const placeMedia = (\n     elementId: string,\n     checkpoint: Extract<GenerationRunMediaCheckpoint, { status: 'done' }>,\n     events: NewGenerationRunEvent[],\n   ): Promise<boolean> =>\n     exclusive(async () => {\n       const carrying: Array<{ index: number; scene: Scene }> = [];\n       outline().outlines.forEach((_, index) => {\n         const narrated = output<NarrationOutput>(sceneStepId(index, 'narration'));\n         if (narrated && sceneCarriesMediaReference(narrated.scene, elementId)) {\n           carrying.push({ index, scene: narrated.scene });\n         }\n       });\n       if (carrying.length === 0) return false;\n       for (const [position, { index, scene }] of carrying.entries()) {\n         const next = structuredClone(scene);\n         placeInScene(next, elementId, checkpoint);\n         const last = position === carrying.length - 1;\n         const change: StepCommit = {\n           // The narration checkpoint is the scene as the course holds it.\n           steps: [\n             {\n               id: sceneStepId(index, 'narration'),\n               output: { scene: next } satisfies NarrationOutput,\n             },\n             ...(last ? [])\n           steps.set(checkpointed.id, checkpointed.output);\n       }\n       return true;\n     });\n \n   /**\n    * Place a Retry's media into a course that has completed, which its author\n    * may be editing meanwhile. When the author removed the element\n    * (or its scene), the result is dropped and its bytes released: the item\n    * fails as {@link MEDIA_ELEMENT_REMOVED}, final, so the element is not\n    * resurrected and no Retry pays for media nothing shows.\n    */\n   const placeIntoCurrentCourse = (\n     elementId: string,\n     checkpoint: Extract<GenerationRunMediaCheckpoint, { status: 'done' }>,\n     events: NewGenerationRunEvent[],\n   ): Promise<boolean> =>\n     exclusive(async () => {\n       owner = await currentOwnerOf(run.ownerId);\n       const stageId = agents().stage.id;\n       const course = await loadRunCourse({ ownerId: owner, lease, stageId });\n       const candidates = course.scenes.filter((scene) =>\n         sceneCarriesMediaReference(scene as Scene, elementId),\n       );\n       // Placed before an interruption: a scene already names these bytes.\n       let placed = course.scenes.some((scene) =>\n         sceneCarriesMediaReference(scene as Scene, checkpoint.assetId),\n       );\n       const finish = async (tx: Queryable) => {\n         await commitGenerationRunIn(tx, lease, {\n           step: { id: mediaStepId(elementId), output: checkpoint },\n           events,\n         });\n       };\n       for (const [position, candidate] of candidates.entries()) {\n         const last = position === candidates.length - 1;\n         await mutateRunScene({\n           ownerId: owner,\n           lease,\n           stageId,\n           sceneId: candidate.id,\n           mutate: (scene) => {\n             if (!scene) return null;\n             const next = structuredClone(scene) as Scene;\n             return placeInScene(next, elementId, checkpoint) ? [checkpoint.posterAssetId] : [])],\n         stepContext,\n       );\n       const dropped: GenerationRunMediaCheckpoint = {\n         mediaType: checkpoint.mediaType,\n         status: 'failed',\n         message: `The ${checkpoint.mediaType} was generated after its element was removed from the course`,\n         errorCode: MEDIA_ELEMENT_REMOVED,\n       };\n       await commit({\n         step: { id: mediaStepId(elementId), output: dropped },\n         events: [mediaEvent(elementId, dropped)],\n       });\n       return true;\n     });\n \n   /** Where stored media goes: the generated scenes, or a completed course as it is now. */\n   const placeInto = () => (run.state === 'completed' ? placeIntoCurrentCourse : placeMedia);\n \n   /**\n    * Place stored bytes, counting the placements that fail: the bytes stay\n    * stored (and are placed again later) until {@link MAX_PLACEMENT_ATTEMPTS}\n    * failed in a row; then the item fails with a Retry and its bytes are\n    * released, as every failed item's are (a Retry generates anew), so the run\n    * stops being claimed for it.\n    */\n   const placer =\n     () =>\n     async (\n       elementId: string,\n       checkpoint: Extract<GenerationRunMediaCheckpoint, { status: 'done' }>,\n       events: NewGenerationRunEvent[],\n     ): Promise<boolean> => {\n       try {\n         return await placeInto()(elementId, checkpoint, events);\n       } catch (error) {\n         if (endsLane(error, signal)) throw error;\n         const current = mediaCheckpoint(elementId);\n         if (current?.status !== 'stored') throw error;\n         const failures = (current.placementFailures ?? The browser, the headless API and scripts\n  * start a run, follow its ordered event log and send it commands; none of them\n  * drives the steps.\n  */\n import type { AgentInfo } from '@openmaic/generation';\n \n import type { AgentConfig } from '@/lib/orchestration/registry/types';\n import type { SceneOutline } from '@/lib/types/generation';\n import type { GeneratedAgentConfig } from '@/lib/types/stage';\n \n /**\n  * `preparing` (material analysis, research) → `outlining` →\n  * `awaiting_outline_confirmation` → `generating` → `completed`. customAgents?: GenerationRunCustomAgent[];\n }\n \n /** The failure a paused run stopped at. */\n export interface GenerationRunFailure {\n   /** The step that failed; null when the run stopped before checkpoint (`media:<elementId>`)\n  * records it.\n  *\n  * - `queued`: to be generated; `generating`: a worker is generating it (a\n  *   takeover generates it again);\n  * - `submitted`: a video posterAssetId?: string;\n       /** Placements of these bytes that failed in a row (see `MAX_PLACEMENT_ATTEMPTS`). */\n       placementFailures?: number;\n     }\n   | { status: 'done'; assetId: /** `{ state, step }`: the run changed state. */\n   'state',\n   /** `{ step }`: a step started. */\n   'step_started',\n   /** `{ step, attempt, maxAttempts, reason }`: a step is being retried. */\n               "patch": "Index: lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts\n===================================================================\n--- lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts\t\n+++ lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts\t\n@@ -1,875 +1,876 @@\n /**\n  * Outline: plan a course's scenes from the requirements, the material and\n  * the research, streaming each scene outline as the model writes it. The\n  * logic of 1.1.x's POST /api/generate/scene-outlines-stream; a run streams\n  * the step's events to the browser.\n  *\n  * Interactive mode and the server-enabled task engine mode keep their own\n  * prompt templates; standard generation is byte-identical to the generation\n  * package's outline prompt. The stream is retried on the same model, then\n  * once on the stage's fallback model, and every retry is reported as an event.\n  */\n import { attachedModelFallback } from '@/lib/ai/model-fallbacks';\n import { streamLLM } from '@/lib/ai/llm';\n import {\n   resolveFallbackModel,\n   shouldFallbackFor,\n   logFallbackFired,\n } from '@/lib/server/llm-fallback';\n import { buildPrompt, PROMPT_IDS } from '@/lib/prompts';\n import {\n   formatImageDescription,\n   formatImagePlaceholder,\n   buildVisionUserContent,\n   buildOutlinePrompt,\n   uniquifyMediaElementIds,\n   formatTeacherPersonaForPrompt,\n } from '@openmaic/generation';\n import type { AgentInfo } from '@openmaic/generation';\n import { DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE } from '@openmaic/generation';\n import {\n   formatDesignDirective,\n   normalizeDesignDirective,\n   type DesignDirective,\n } from '@openmaic/generation';\n import { MAX_PDF_CONTENT_CHARS, MAX_VISION_IMAGES } from '@/lib/constants/generation';\n import { MAX_OUTLINE_SCENES } from '@/lib/server/generation/outline-schema';\n import { nanoid } from 'nanoid';\n import type {\n   UserRequirements,\n   PdfImage,\n   SceneOutline,\n   ImageMapping,\n } from '@/lib/types/generation';\n import { resolveServerGenerationCapabilities } from '@/lib/server/generation-capabilities';\n import {\n   isNonRetryableHostFailure,\n   isProviderQuotaRefusal,\n } from '@/lib/server/generation-run-hooks/runtime';\n import { sortDocumentImagesForVision } from '@/lib/document/bundle';\n import { resolveVocationalActive } from '@/lib/config/feature-flags';\n \n import {\n   StepAbortedError,\n   StepRefusal,\n   type OwnerStepContext,\n   type StepContext,\n   type StepLanguageModel,\n   type WorkspaceStepContext,\n } from './context';\n \n const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 2;\n // Hard ceiling on the accumulated stream buffer. Legitimate outline JSON is\n // small (tens of KB); anything past this is a runaway/degenerate generation\n // and must not be allowed to grow the heap unbounded.\n const MAX_OUTLINE_STREAM_BYTES = 512 * 1024;\n \n /**\n  * Extract the languageDirective from the streamed wrapper JSON.\n  * Matches `\"languageDirective\":\"<value>\"` in partial JSON like:\n  *   {\"languageDirective\":\"Teach in English...\",\"outlines\":[...\n  */\n function extractLanguageDirective(buffer: string): string | null {\n   // The directive is the first key of the wrapper object, so it can only ever\n   // appear in the head of the buffer. Bound the scan to keep this O(1) per\n   // streamed chunk — it is called on the full, growing buffer on every chunk,\n   // which is otherwise O(n²) over the stream.\n   const head = buffer.length > 8192 ? buffer.slice(0, 8192) : buffer;\n   const match = head.match(/\"languageDirective\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/);\n   if (!match) return null;\n   try {\n     return JSON.parse(`\"${match[1]}\"`);\n   } catch {\n     return match[1];\n   }\n }\n \n /**\n  * Extract the courseTitle from the streamed wrapper JSON.\n  * Same head-bound scan as `extractLanguageDirective` — the title is a\n  * top-level key near the start of the wrapper object, so it only appears in\n  * the buffer head. Returns the decoded title, or null if not yet streamed.\n  */\n const COURSE_TITLE_RE = /\"courseTitle\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/;\n \n // Normalize a captured title identically to the non-streaming parser\n // (@openmaic/generation outline parser): ignore whitespace-only titles and cap\n // length defensively so a hallucinating model cannot push a blank or unbounded\n // value into the stage name. Returning null lets callers fall back / keep scanning.\n function normalizeStreamedTitle(raw: string): string | null {\n   let title: string;\n   try {\n     title = JSON.parse(`\"${raw}\"`);\n   } catch {\n     title = raw;\n   }\n   const normalized = title.trim();\n   return normalized ? normalized.slice(0, 120) : null;\n }\n \n function extractCourseTitle(buffer: string): string | null {\n   const head = buffer.length > 8192 ? buffer.slice(0, 8192) : buffer;\n   const match = head.match(COURSE_TITLE_RE);\n   return match ? normalizeStreamedTitle(match[1]) : null;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Extract the designDirective from the streamed wrapper JSON. Unlike the two\n  * string directives above, the directive is an object, so it is recovered by\n  * a balanced-brace scan (string-aware) starting at its key. The scan re-runs\n  * per chunk until found; it is bounded to the 16 KB head, where the wrapper\n  * directives live — normal shape is `\"designDirective\":{...},\"outlines\":[`.\n  */\n const DESIGN_DIRECTIVE_KEY_RE = /\"designDirective\"\\s*:\\s*\\{/;\n \n function extractDesignDirective(buffer: string): DesignDirective | null {\n   const head = buffer.length > 16384 ? buffer.slice(0, 16384) : buffer;\n   const match = head.match(DESIGN_DIRECTIVE_KEY_RE);\n-  if (!match) return null;\n+  if (!match || match.index === undefined) return null;\n+  const start = match.index + match[0].length - 1;\n   let depth = 0;\n   let inString = false;\n   let escaped = false;\n-  for (let i = match.index + match[0].length - 1; i < head.length; i++) {\n+  for (let i = start; i < head.length; i++) {\n     const char = head[i];\n     if (escaped) {\n       escaped = false;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (char === '\\\\' && inString) {\n       escaped = true;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (char === '\"') inString = !inString;\n     if (inString) continue;\n     if (char === '{') depth++;\n     else if (char === '}') {\n       depth--;\n       if (depth === 0) {\n         try {\n-          const raw: unknown = JSON.parse(head.substring(match.index + match[0].length - 1, i + 1));\n+          const raw: unknown = JSON.parse(head.substring(start, i + 1));\n           return normalizeDesignDirective(raw);\n         } catch {\n           return null;\n         }\n       }\n     }\n   }\n   return null; // Object not complete in the head yet — scan again next chunk.\n }\n \n /**\n  * Full-buffer fallback, run once after the stream completes: recovers a title\n  * the model emitted after the `outlines` array or beyond the 8KB head window —\n  * cases the head-bound `extractCourseTitle` scan would miss. Only invoked when\n  * the streaming scan produced nothing, so the extra full-buffer regex is paid once.\n  */\n function extractCourseTitleFromComplete(buffer: string): string | null {\n   const match = buffer.match(COURSE_TITLE_RE);\n   return match ? normalizeStreamedTitle(match[1]) : null;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Incremental JSON array parser.\n  * Extracts complete top-level objects from a partially-streamed JSON array,\n  * resuming from `scanFrom` (an index into `buffer`) so the growing buffer is\n  * scanned only ONCE across the whole stream — O(n) total instead of O(n²).\n  * Supports both a flat array `[{...},{...}]` and a wrapper object\n  * `{\"languageDirective\":\"...\",\"outlines\":[{...},{...}]}`, with or without a\n  * markdown ```json fence (the array is located by content, not by stripping).\n  * Returns newly found objects plus the index to resume scanning from next time.\n  */\n function extractNewOutlines(\n   buffer: string,\n   scanFrom: number,\n ): { outlines: SceneOutline[]; scanFrom: number } {\n   const results: SceneOutline[] = [];\n \n   let i: number;\n   if (scanFrom > 0) {\n     // Resume just past the last fully-parsed object (between array elements,\n     // so not inside a string and at brace depth 0).\n     i = scanFrom;\n   } else {\n     // Locate the outlines array opening once.\n     const outlinesKeyIdx = buffer.indexOf('\"outlines\"');\n     const arrayStart =\n       outlinesKeyIdx >= 0 ? buffer.indexOf('[', outlinesKeyIdx) : buffer.indexOf('[');\n     if (arrayStart === -1) return { outlines: results, scanFrom: 0 };\n     i = arrayStart + 1;\n   }\n \n   let depth = 0;\n   let objectStart = -1;\n   let inString = false;\n   let escaped = false;\n   let consumed = i; // index just past the last fully-parsed object\n \n   for (; i < buffer.length; i++) {\n     const char = buffer[i];\n \n     if (escaped) {\n       escaped = false;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (char === '\\\\' && inString) {\n       escaped = true;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (char === '\"') {\n       inString = !inString;\n       continue;\n     }\n     if (inString) continue;\n \n     if (char === '{') {\n       if (depth === 0) objectStart = i;\n       depth++;\n     } else if (char === '}') {\n       depth--;\n       if (depth === 0 && objectStart >= 0) {\n         try {\n           results.push(JSON.parse(buffer.substring(objectStart, i + 1)));\n         } catch {\n           // Incomplete or invalid JSON — skip\n         }\n         objectStart = -1;\n         consumed = i + 1;\n       }\n     }\n   }\n \n   return { outlines: results, scanFrom: consumed };\n }\n \n function normalizeTaskEngineProceduralOutline(\n   outline: SceneOutline,\n   requirement: string,\n ): SceneOutline {\n   const widgetOutline = outline.widgetOutline ?? {};\n \n   return {\n     ...outline,\n     type: 'interactive',\n     widgetType: 'procedural-skill',\n     widgetOutline: {\n       ...widgetOutline,\n       procedureType: widgetOutline.procedureType ?? 'inspection',\n       task: widgetOutline.task || requirement,\n       tools:\n         widgetOutline.tools && widgetOutline.tools.length > 0\n           ? widgetOutline.tools\n           : ['required PPE', 'task checklist'],\n       steps:\n         widgetOutline.steps && widgetOutline.steps.length > 0\n           ? widgetOutline.steps\n           : ['Confirm task conditions', 'Select required tools', 'Complete safety check'],\n       successCriteria:\n         widgetOutline.successCriteria && widgetOutline.successCriteria.length > 0\n           ? widgetOutline.successCriteria\n           : ['Required checks completed', 'Unsafe conditions are not ignored'],\n       errorConsequences:\n         widgetOutline.errorConsequences && widgetOutline.errorConsequences.length > 0\n           ? widgetOutline.errorConsequences\n           : ['Unsafe or incorrect actions require stopping and rechecking'],\n     },\n   };\n }\n \n function normalizeTaskEngineSlideOutline(outline: SceneOutline): SceneOutline {\n   const normalized: SceneOutline = {\n     ...outline,\n     type: 'slide',\n   };\n   delete normalized.widgetType;\n   delete normalized.widgetOutline;\n   delete normalized.interactiveConfig;\n   return normalized;\n }\n \n const ORDINARY_WIDGET_TYPES = new Set(['simulation', 'diagram', 'code', 'game', 'visualization3d']);\n \n function normalizeTaskEngineOutline(outline: SceneOutline, requirement: string): SceneOutline {\n   if (outline.type === 'slide') {\n     return normalizeTaskEngineSlideOutline(outline);\n   }\n \n   if (outline.type === 'interactive' && outline.widgetType === 'procedural-skill') {\n     return normalizeTaskEngineProceduralOutline(outline, requirement);\n   }\n \n   if (\n     outline.type === 'interactive' &&\n     outline.widgetType &&\n     ORDINARY_WIDGET_TYPES.has(outline.widgetType)\n   ) {\n     return outline;\n   }\n \n   return normalizeTaskEngineSlideOutline(outline);\n }\n \n function sanitizeNonTaskEngineOutline(outline: SceneOutline): SceneOutline {\n   if (outline.widgetType !== 'procedural-skill') {\n     return outline;\n   }\n \n   const widgetOutline = { ...(outline.widgetOutline ?? {}) };\n   delete widgetOutline.procedureType;\n   delete widgetOutline.task;\n   delete widgetOutline.tools;\n   delete widgetOutline.steps;\n   delete widgetOutline.successCriteria;\n   delete widgetOutline.errorConsequences;\n \n   // procedural-skill is gated behind taskEngineMode to protect ordinary MAIC generation.\n   return {\n     ...outline,\n     type: 'interactive',\n     widgetType: 'diagram',\n     description: outline.description\n       ? model: languageModel,\n         abortSignal: ctx.signal,\n         system: systemPrompt,\n         prompt: userPrompt,\n         maxOutputTokens: modelInfo?.outputWindow,\n         maxRetries: 0,\n effectiveOutline.suggestedImageIds.length > 0\n   ) {\n     const suggestedIds = new Set(effectiveOutline.suggestedImageIds);\n     assignedImages = sortDocumentImagesForVision(\n       pdfImages.filter((img) => suggestedIds.has(img.id)),\n     );\n   }\n \n   // ── N3: resolve-then-slice the vision candidates BEFORE prompt assembly ──\n   // The prompt text and the multimodal attachments must be built from the\n   // SAME resolved set: an image the server cannot resolve (a reclaimed\n   // asset, a store failure) is dropped from BOTH — its `[see attached]`\n   // text mention and its attachment — instead of leaving a dangling promise\n   // in the prompt. The candidates are computed in the generator's OWN order\n   // (the shared `partitionImagesForVision` helper, so the step and the\n   // generator cannot drift) and resolved IN ORDER with refill until the cap\n   // is met or the candidates are exhausted: a drop admits the next image\n   // WITH its resolution, so the generator's re-slice (same helper, same\n   // cap) can never admit an image this step has not resolved (review P2).\n   // Every id the resolution drops is STRIPPED from the `imageMapping` (and\n   // `assignedImages`) passed onward, so a model-hallucinated reference to a\n   // dropped id takes the existing clean \"no mapping → remove element\" path\n   // in `resolveImageIds` instead of writing a dangling allocated id into\n   // `src` (review P3). The resolved slice is passed to the generator so\n   // `aiCall` does not re-resolve (its resolution is a defensive no-op).\n   let visionImageMapping: ImageMapping | undefined = imageMapping;\n   let resolvedVisionImages: VisionPromptImage[] | undefined;\n   if (assignedImages && assignedImages.length > 0 && hasVision && imageMapping) {\n     const { withSrc } = partitionImagesForVision(assignedImages, imageMapping, MAX_VISION_IMAGES);\n     // Bound the resolve-with-refill loop (review P2, round 3): the store may\n     // be down, and each probe is an unbounded server-side round trip, so an\n     // all-fail phase must not churn every candidate (and emit a warn per\n     // candidate) until the route's 300 s platform cap. Two stops, both\n     // degrading to \"whatever resolved so far\" — never failing the step:\n     // (a) an aggregate budget for the WHOLE phase (the shared 15 s ingest\n     // constant, raced against each probe so even ONE hanging probe cannot\n     // outlive it) and (b) a consecutive-failure fuse (3 unresolvable/errored\n     // candidates in a row → stop). When a stop fires, every candidate that\n     // did not resolve — unresolvable OR unprobed — is STRIPPED from the\n     // mapping, so the generator can never hand an unresolved allocated id to\n     // the defensive aiCall resolution (which would re-open the unbounded\n     // probe the stop just closed); ONE summary warn names the stop.\n     let phaseTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n     const phaseBudget = new Promise<'__vision-resolution-budget-expired__'>((resolve) => {\n       phaseTimer = setTimeout(\n         () => resolve('__vision-resolution-budget-expired__'),\n         VISION_RESOLUTION_BUDGET_MS,\n       );\n     });\n     const resolvedById = new Map<string, VisionPromptImage>();\n     let consecutiveUnresolvable = 0;\n     let stopReason: 'fuse' | 'budget' | null = null;\n     for (const candidate of withSrc) {\n       if (resolvedById.size >= MAX_VISION_IMAGES) break;\n       if (consecutiveUnresolvable >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_UNRESOLVABLE_VISION_IMAGES) {\n         stopReason = 'fuse';\n         break;\n       }\n       let attempted: VisionPromptImage[] | '__vision-resolution-budget-expired__';\n       try {\n         attempted = await Promise.race([\n           ctx.resolveVisionImages([\n             {\n               id: candidate.id,\n               src: imageMapping[candidate.id],\n               ...(candidate.width !== undefined ? { width: candidate.width } : {}),\n               ...(candidate.height !== undefined ? { height: candidate.height } : {}),\n             },\n           ]),\n           phaseBudget,\n         ]);\n       } catch (error) {\n         // A throwing probe counts as an unresolvable candidate (an errored\n         // store must degrade, never fail the step).\n         log.error(\n           `Vision image resolution probe for \"${candidate.id}\" failed; treating it as unresolvable:`,\n           error,\n         );\n         attempted = [];\n       }\n       if (attempted === '__vision-resolution-budget-expired__') {\n         stopReason = 'budget';\n         break;\n       }\n       if (attempted.length === 1) {\n         resolvedById.set(attempted[0]!.id, attempted[0]!);\n         consecutiveUnresolvable = 0;\n       } else {\n         consecutiveUnresolvable += 1;\n       }\n     }\n     if (phaseTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(phaseTimer);\n     resolvedVisionImages = [...resolvedById.values()];\n     // Every candidate that did not resolve — an unresolvable probe, OR an\n     // unprobed one when the fuse/budget stopped the phase — is stripped from\n     // the mapping and the assigned set, so the generator's re-slice (same\n     // helper, same cap) can never admit an image this step has not resolved\n     // (possibly all of them = text-only generation).\n     const droppedIds = new Set(\n       withSrc\n         .filter((candidate) => !resolvedById.has(candidate.id))\n         .map((candidate) => candidate.id),\n     );\n     if (droppedIds.size > 0) {\n       assignedImages = assignedImages.filter((img) => !droppedIds.has(img.id));\n       visionImageMapping = Object.fromEntries(\n         Object.entries(imageMapping).filter(([id]) => !droppedIds.has(id)),\n       );\n     }\n     if (stopReason !== null) {\n       log.warn(\n         `Stopped probing vision image candidates early: the ${\n           stopReason === 'fuse'\n             ? `consecutive-failure fuse (${MAX_CONSECUTIVE_UNRESOLVABLE_VISION_IMAGES} unresolvable in a row)`\n             : `${VISION_RESOLUTION_BUDGET_MS}ms aggregate resolution budget`\n         } fired; proceeding to generation with ${resolvedById.size} resolved image(s) and the rest dropped to text-only (degrade, not fail).`,\n       );\n     }\n   }\n \n   // ── Media generation is handled client-side in parallel (media-orchestrator.ts) ──\n   // The content generator receives placeholder IDs (gen_img_1, gen_vid_1) as-is.\n   // resolveImageIds() in generation-pipeline.ts will keep these placeholders in elements.\n   const generatedMediaMapping: ImageMapping = {};\n \n   // ── Generate content ──\n   log.info(\n     `Generating content: \"${effectiveOutline.title}\" (${effectiveOutline.type}) [model=${modelString}]`,\n   );\n \n   const content = await generateContent(effectiveOutline, aiCall, {\n     assignedImages,\n     imageMapping: visionImageMapping,\n     visionEnabled: hasVision,\n     generatedMediaMapping,\n     resolvedVisionImages,\n     agents,\n     languageDirective,\n+    designDirective,\n     targetLanguage: input.targetLanguage || undefined,\n     userRequirements: requirements,\n     allowProceduralSkill: vocationalActive,\n     ...(effectiveOutline.type === 'pbl'\n       ? {\n           pblLoopFallback: (plannerInput) =>\n             generatePBLV2Project(\n               plannerInput,\n               languageModel,\n               callLLM,\n               { logger: log },\n               thinkingConfig,\n             ),\n         }\n       : {}),\n   });\n \n   if (!content) {\n     log.error(`Failed to generate content for: \"${effectiveOutline.title}\"`);\n \n     throw new StepRefusal<SceneContentRefusal>(\n       'generation-failed',\n       `Failed to generate content: ${effectiveOutline.title}`,\n     );\n   }\n \n   log.info(`Content generated successfully: \"${effectiveOutline.title}\"`);\n   return { content, effectiveOutline };\n }\n",

...IMAGE_ENV_MAP,\n     // comfyui-image lives in the client-side catalog only (no credential env),\n     // but operators may still want to force it off fleet-wide.\n     IMAGE_COMFYUI: 'comfyui-image',\n   },\n   video: { ...VIDEO_ENV_MAP },\n   webSearch: { ...WEB_SEARCH_ENV_MAP },\n };\n \n /** YAML section key per capability (web-search is hyphenated in YAML). */\n const YAML_SECTION_KEY: Record<CapabilitySection, keyof YamlData> = {\n   tts: 'tts',\n   asr: 'asr',\n   image: 'image',\n   video: 'video',\n   webSearch: 'web-search',\n };\n \n // Partial<ServerProviderEntry>>;\n }>;\n \n function loadYamlFile(filename: string): YamlData {\n   try {\n     const filePath = path.join(process.cwd(), filename);\n     if (!fs.existsSync(filePath))  return parsed as YamlData;\n   } catch (e) {\n     log.warn(`[ServerProviderConfig] Failed to load ${filename}:`, e);\n     return {};\n   }\n }\n \n // parsed : undefined;\n }\n \n function loadEnvSection(\n   envMap: Record<string, string>,\n   yamlSection: Record<string, Partial<ServerProviderEntry>> | undefined,\n   {\n     requiresBaseUrl = false,\n     keylessProviders = new Set<string>(),\n     baseUrlOptionalProviders = new Set<string>(),\n   }: {\n     requiresBaseUrl?: boolean;\n     keylessProviders?: Set<string>;\n     baseUrlOptionalProviders?: Set<string>;\n   } = {},\n ): Record<string, ServerProviderEntry> {\n   const result: Record<string, ServerProviderEntry> = {};\n   const requiresBaseUrlForProvider = (providerId: string) =>\n     requiresBaseUrl && !baseUrlOptionalProviders.has(providerId);\n \n   // First, add everything from YAML as defaults\n   if (yamlSection) {\n     for (const [id, entry] of Object.entries(yamlSection)) {\n       if (\n         requiresBaseUrlForProvider(id)\n           ? !!entry?.baseUrl\n           : entry?.apiKey || (entry?.baseUrl && keylessProviders.has(id))\n       ) {\n         result[id] = {\n           apiKey: entry.apiKey || '',\n           baseUrl: entry.baseUrl,\n           models: normalizeModelList(entry.models),\n           proxy: entry.proxy,\n         };\n       }\n     }\n   }\n \n   // Then, apply env vars (env takes priority over YAML)\n   for (const [prefix, providerId] of Object.entries(envMap)) {\n     const envApiKey = process.env[`${prefix}_API_KEY`] || undefined;\n     const envBaseUrl = process.env[`${prefix}_BASE_URL`] || undefined;\n     const envModelsStr = process.env[`${prefix}_MODELS`];\n     const envModels = envModelsStr\n       ? envModelsStr\n           .split(',')\n           .map((m) => m.trim())\n           .filter(Boolean)\n       : undefined;\n \n     if (result[providerId]) {\n       // YAML entry exists — env vars override individual fields\n       if (envApiKey) result[providerId].apiKey = envApiKey;\n       if (envBaseUrl) result[providerId].baseUrl = envBaseUrl;\n       if (envModels) result[providerId].models = envModels;\n       continue;\n     }\n \n     // Activate on API key, or base URL alone for keyless providers (e.g. Ollama)\n     if (\n       requiresBaseUrlForProvider(providerId)\n         ? !envBaseUrl\n         : !(envApiKey || (envBaseUrl && keylessProviders.has(providerId)))\n     )\n       continue;\n     result[providerId] = {\n       apiKey: envApiKey || '',\n       baseUrl: envBaseUrl,\n       models: envModels,\n     };\n   }\n \n   return result;\n }\n \n /** Parse a boolean-ish env value. Falsey words ⇒ false; anything else ⇒ true. */\n function parseBooleanEnv(raw: string): boolean {\n   return !/^(false|0|no|off)$/i.test(raw.trim());\n }\n \n /**\n  * Collect provider IDs the operator force-disabled per capability section, from\n  * YAML (`<section>.<id>.enabled: false`) and env (`<CAP>_<PREFIX>_ENABLED`).\n  * An explicit env `true` overrides a YAML disable (env precedence, matching the\n  * rest of this module). The `_ENABLED` vars can only\n  * disable; they never create or force-enable a provider entry.\n  */\n function collectDisabledProviders(yamlData: YamlData): Record<CapabilitySection, Set<string>> {\n   const disabled: Record<CapabilitySection, Set<string>> = {\n     tts: new Set<string>(),\n     asr: new Set<string>(),\n     image: new Set<string>(),\n     video: new Set<string>(),\n     webSearch: new Set<string>(),\n   };\n   for (const section of Object.keys(DISABLE_ENV_MAPS) as CapabilitySection[]) {\n     const yamlSection = yamlData[YAML_SECTION_KEY[section]];\n     if (yamlSection) {\n       for (const [id, entry] of Object.entries(yamlSection)) {\n         if (entry?.enabled === false) disabled[section].add(id);\n       }\n     }\n     for (const [prefix, providerId] of Object.entries(DISABLE_ENV_MAPS[section])) {\n       const raw = process.env[`${prefix}_ENABLED`];\n       // Treat unset / empty (e.g. a blank CI-templated value) as \"no opinion\" so\n       // it never silently overrides an explicit YAML disable.\n       if (raw === undefined || raw.trim() === '') continue;\n       if (parseBooleanEnv(raw)) disabled[section].delete(providerId);\n       else disabled[section].add(providerId);\n     }\n   }\n   return disabled;\n }\n \n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n // Module-level cache (process singleton)\n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n \n const DEFAULT_FILENAME = 'server-providers.yml';\n const OPENAI_IMAGE_PROVIDER_ID = 'openai-image';\n const ALIDOCMIND_PROVIDER_ID = 'alidocmind';\n const BEDROCK_PROVIDER_ID = 'bedrock';\n \n /** Cache keyed by YAML filename (empty string = default file). */\n const _configs: Map<string, ServerConfig> = new Map();\n \n /**\n  * AliDocMind is server-configured when AK/SK are provided via env\n  * (ALIDOCMIND_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET) or YAML. The generic\n     // loader may have created a bare entry from a YAML `baseUrl` alone — drop\n     // it so the provider stays UNMANAGED (clients supply their own creds)\n     // rather than \"managed\" with no usable credentials, which would both lock\n     // the provider out and silently discard client-entered AK/SK.\n     delete pdfConfig[ALIDOCMIND_PROVIDER_ID];\n     return pdfConfig;\n   }\n \n   // Merge the AK/SK into any entry the generic env/YAML loader already created.\n   // That loader copies only apiKey/baseUrl/models/proxy — never AK/SK — and a\n   // YAML entry with a `baseUrl` makes it create the entry, so returning early\n   // here would leave a \"managed\" provider with no usable credentials.\n   const existing = pdfConfig[ALIDOCMIND_PROVIDER_ID];\n   pdfConfig[ALIDOCMIND_PROVIDER_ID] = {\n     apiKey: existing?.apiKey ?? '',\n     accessKeyId,\n     accessKeySecret,\n     baseUrl:\n       existing?.baseUrl || yamlEntry?.baseUrl || process.env.ALIDOCMIND_BASE_URL || undefined,\n     models: existing?.models,\n     proxy: existing?.proxy,\n   };\n   return pdfConfig;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Server-owned AliDocMind AK/SK, if this deployment manages the provider.\n  * Returns undefined when AliDocMind is not server-configured (client must\n  * supply its own credentials).\n  */\n export function resolveManagedAliDocMindCredentials():\n   | { accessKeyId: string; accessKeySecret: string; baseUrl?: string }\n   | undefined {\n   const entry = getConfig().pdf[ALIDOCMIND_PROVIDER_ID];\n   if (entry?.accessKeyId && entry?.accessKeySecret) {\n     return {\n       accessKeyId: entry.accessKeyId,\n       accessKeySecret: entry.accessKeySecret,\n       baseUrl: entry.baseUrl,\n     };\n   }\n   return undefined;\n }\n \n /** Provider-neutral extraction input populated from server-managed media credentials. */\n export function resolveServerMediaExtractorConfig(): {\n   providerId: string;\n   accessKeyId?: string;\n   accessKeySecret?: string;\n   baseUrl?: string;\n   allowEnvFallback: boolean;\n } {\n   const credentials = resolveManagedAliDocMindCredentials();\n   return {\n     providerId: '',\n     accessKeyId: credentials?.accessKeyId,\n     accessKeySecret: credentials?.accessKeySecret,\n     baseUrl: credentials?.baseUrl,\n     allowEnvFallback: true,\n   };\n }\n \n function applyOpenAIImageFallback(\n   imageConfig: Record<string, ServerProviderEntry>,\n   yamlImageSection: Record<string, Partial<ServerProviderEntry>> | undefined,\n ): Record<string, ServerProviderEntry> {\n   if (imageConfig[OPENAI_IMAGE_PROVIDER_ID]) return imageConfig;\n \n   const apiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;\n   if (!apiKey) return imageConfig;\n \n   const yamlOpenAIImage = yamlImageSection?.[OPENAI_IMAGE_PROVIDER_ID];\n   imageConfig[OPENAI_IMAGE_PROVIDER_ID] = {\n     apiKey,\n     baseUrl:\n       yamlOpenAIImage?.baseUrl || process.env.IMAGE_OPENAI_BASE_URL || process.env.OPENAI_BASE_URL,\n     models:\n       splitModels(process.env.IMAGE_OPENAI_MODELS) ?? normalizeModelList(yamlOpenAIImage?.models),\n     proxy: yamlOpenAIImage?.proxy,\n   };\n   return imageConfig;\n }\n \n function splitModels(models: string | undefined): string[] | undefined {\n   const parsed = models\n     ?.split(',')\n     .map((model) => model.trim())\n     .filter(Boolean);\n   return parsed && parsed.length > 0 ? parsed : asr: loadEnvSection(ASR_ENV_MAP, yamlData.asr, {\n       keylessProviders: new Set(['funasr-asr', 'lemonade-asr']),\n     }),\n     pdf: applyAliDocMindFallback(\n       loadEnvSection(PDF_ENV_MAP, disabled: collectDisabledProviders(yamlData),\n   };\n }\n \n function logConfig(config: ServerConfig, label: string): void {\n   const counts = [\n     Object.keys(config.providers).length,\n     Object.keys(config.tts).length,\n     Object.keys(config.asr).length,\n     Object.keys(config.pdf).length,\n     Object.keys(config.image).length,\n     Object.keys(config.video).length,\n ASR, ${counts[3]} PDF, ${counts[4]} Image, ${counts[5]} Video, ${counts[6]} WebSearch providers`,\n     );\n   }\n }\n \n function getConfig(): ServerConfig {\n   const cached = _configs.get('');\n   if (cached) return cached;\n \n   const yamlData = loadYamlFile(DEFAULT_FILENAME);\n   const config = buildConfig(yamlData);\n   // Environment variables are always read; the file only when it has config);\n   return config;\n }\n \n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n // Managed-provider resolution\n //\n // A provider is \"server-managed\" iff the
