This single\n // rule removes the tri-state where a client base URL could partially override\n // server config (the bug class #533 patched route-by-route).\n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n \n type ProviderSection = 'providers' | 'tts' | 'asr' | 'pdf' | 'image' | 'video' | 'webSearch';\n \n /**\n  * The operator's entry for a provider, or undefined. Provider ids come from\n  * requests, so only the section's own keys count: an id such as `constructor`\n  * or `__proto__` must not resolve to an inherited object property.\n  */\n function serverEntry(\n   section: ProviderSection,\n   providerId: string,\n ): ServerProviderEntry | undefined {\n   const entries = getConfig()[section];\n   return Object.hasOwn(entries, providerId) ? entries[providerId] : undefined;\n }\n \n /** Whether the operator configured this provider in the given section. */\n export function isServerConfiguredProvider(section: ProviderSection, providerId: string): boolean {\n   return serverEntry(section, providerId) !== undefined;\n }\n \n /** Whether the operator force-disabled this provider in the given capability section (server precedence). */\n export function isServerProviderDisabled(section: CapabilitySection, providerId: string): boolean {\n   return getConfig().disabled[section].has(providerId);\n }\n \n /**\n  * Enabled-provider resolver: the provider IDs of a capability listing that\n  * this deployment actually serves — present in the listing and not\n  * force-disabled (`{ disabled: true }`, #665). Legacy server pins do\n  * not apply.\n  */\n export function slotTTSModel(\n   providerId: string,\n   modelId: string | undefined,\n   voiceId?: string,\n ): string | undefined {\n   return ttsModelFor(providerId, [], modelId, voiceId);\n }\n \n /** Resolve a TTS model authorized by the deployment, or the BYOK client's choice. */\n export function resolveTTSModel(\n   providerId: string,\n   clientModel?: string,\n   voiceId?: string,\n ): string | undefined {\n   const requested = resolveManagedMediaModel('tts', providerId, clientModel);\n   const model = ttsModelFor(providerId, [], requested, voiceId);\n   // Voice compatibility may change the wire model; it still needs authorization.\n   return resolveManagedMediaModel('tts', providerId, model);\n }\n \n function ttsModelFor(\n   providerId: string,\n   pinnedModels: string[],\n   clientModel?: string,\n   voiceId?: string,\n ): string | undefined {\n   if (providerId === 'qwen-tts') {\n     const vcModel = resolveQwenVoiceCloneModel();\n     const requestedIsVCSentinel = !!clientModel && isQwenVoiceCloneModel(clientModel, vcModel);\n     const normalizedClientModel = requestedIsVCSentinel ? vcModel : clientModel;\n     const allowedModels = new Set([...pinnedModels, vcModel]);\n \n     if (\n       pinnedModels.length > 0 &&\n       normalizedClientModel &&\n       !allowedModels.has(normalizedClientModel)\n     ) {\n       throw new TTSModelNotAllowedError(providerId, normalizedClientModel);\n     }\n \n     if (voiceId) {\n       if (!isQwenCatalogVoice(voiceId)) return vcModel;\n       const pinnedCatalogModel = pinnedModels.find((model) => model !== vcModel);\n       if (pinnedModels.length > 0 && !pinnedCatalogModel) {\n         throw new TTSModelNotAllowedError(providerId, TTS_PROVIDERS['qwen-tts'].defaultModelId);\n       }\n       // Self-heal persisted VC-model + catalog-voice wedges. undefined;\n   }\n \n   if (pinnedModels.length > 0) return pinnedModels[0];\n   return clientModel;\n }\n \n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n // Public '', 10);\n   if (!Number.isFinite(raw) || raw <= 0) return 0;\n   return Math.min(raw, 10);\n }\n \n /** Legacy media requests may use only this deployment's capability models. */\n function resolveManagedMediaModel(\n   section: 'tts' | 'asr' | 'image' | 'video' | 'webSearch',\n   providerId: string,\n   clientModel?: string,\n ): string | undefined {\n   clientModel = clientModel?.trim() || undefined;\n   const entry = serverEntry(section, providerId);\n   const id = presetIdFor(section as SlotCapability, providerId);\n   if (!entry?.apiKey || !selectsUpstreamModel(id, section)) return clientModel;\n   const deployment = deploymentConfig();\n   if (!deployment.legacy) throw new ModelAuthorizationError();\n   const config = deployment.layer?.config;\n   const model = clientModel ?? deploymentAuthorizedModels(config, id, section)[0];\n   if (model !== undefined) assertDeploymentModelAuthorized(config, id, model, section);\n   else if (clientModel !== undefined || deploymentDefaultModel(id, section))\n     throw new ModelAuthorizationError();\n   return model;\n }\n \n /** The exact legacy setting to declare a provider's authorized model ids. */\n export function providerModelsSetting(\n   section: keyof Omit<ServerConfig, 'disabled'>,\n   providerId: string,\n ): string {\n   const maps = {\n     providers: LLM_ENV_MAP,\n     tts: TTS_ENV_MAP,\n     asr: ASR_ENV_MAP,\n     image: IMAGE_ENV_MAP,\n     video: VIDEO_ENV_MAP,\n     webSearch: WEB_SEARCH_ENV_MAP,\n     pdf: PDF_ENV_MAP,\n   };\n   const prefix = Object.entries(maps[section]).find(([, id]) => id === providerId)?.[0];\n   return prefix\n     ? `${prefix}_MODELS or server-providers.yml ${section}.${providerId}.models`\n     : `server-providers.yml ${section}.${providerId}.models`;\n }\n",

              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/stage.ts\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/stage.ts\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/stage.ts\t\n@@ -1,311 +1,317 @@\n /**\n  * Stage / Scene / SceneContent — the universal lesson-skeleton contract.\n  *\n  * This module owns the *structural* part of a lesson: the top-level `Stage`\n  * container and a per-page `Scene` whose `content` is a discriminated union of\n  * the universal content kinds (`SlideContent`, `QuizContent`). Interactive and\n  * PBL content contracts are exported alongside them and compose through\n  * `Scene`'s generic content parameter. `Scene`'s\n  * playback `actions` default to the contract's standard {@link Action} union\n  * (defined in `./action.ts`); apps can still extend widget payloads and action\n  * sets through `Scene`'s generic parameters.\n  *\n  * The split keeps `@openmaic/dsl` focused on the lesson skeleton while letting the\n  * runtime engine, renderer, and importer share one source of truth for it.\n  *\n  * No runtime dependencies. Pure types + pure discriminant guards only.\n  */\n import type { Slide } from './slides.js';\n import type { Action } from './action.js';\n \n /** All scene kinds owned by the contract. */\n export type SceneType = 'slide' | 'quiz' | 'interactive' | 'pbl';\n \n /** Frozen set of every valid {@link SceneType}, for cheap membership checks. */\n export const SCENE_TYPES = [\n   'slide',\n   'quiz',\n   'interactive',\n   'pbl',\n ] as const satisfies readonly SceneType[];\n \n // Compile-time exhaustiveness: every SceneType must appear in SCENE_TYPES.\n // `satisfies` above proves the converse (each entry is a valid SceneType); this\n // fails the build if the union gains a member the tuple is missing.\n type _SceneTypesExhaustive = [SceneType] extends [(typeof SCENE_TYPES)[number]] ? true : never;\n const _sceneTypesExhaustive: _SceneTypesExhaustive = true;\n void _sceneTypesExhaustive;\n \n /** Narrow an unknown value to a valid {@link SceneType}. Pure, no runtime deps. */\n export function isSceneType(value: unknown): value is SceneType {\n   return typeof value === 'string' && (SCENE_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(value);\n }\n \n /** Lifecycle / interaction mode a {@link Stage} can be operated in. */\n export type StageMode = 'autonomous' | 'playback' | 'edit';\n \n /**\n  * A whiteboard slide. Structurally a {@link Slide} minus the fields that only\n  * make sense on a primary canvas (`theme`, `turningMode`, `sectionTag`, `type`).\n  */\n export type Whiteboard = Omit<Slide, 'theme' | 'turningMode' | 'sectionTag' | 'type'>;\n \n export interface VideoManifestEntry {\n   type: 'video';\n   prompt: string;\n   aspectRatio?: string;\n }\n \n export type VideoManifest = Record<string, VideoManifestEntry>;\n \n /**\n  * Provider-neutral vocal identity for an agent, described as a 3-layer recipe.\n  * Consumed by any TTS integration: as an inline voice prompt where supported,\n  * or as the seed for a registered/cloned voice. Part of the contract so an\n  * agent's voice travels with the document (export/import, device switches)\n  * instead of living in device-local storage.\n  */\n export interface VoiceDesign {\n   /** gender / age / role */\n   identity: string;\n   /** pitch / vocal quality */\n   texture: string;\n   /** emotion / pace */\n   delivery: string;\n }\n \n /**\n  * A concrete TTS voice binding for an agent. `providerId` is an open string at\n  * the contract level — the set of available TTS providers is app-defined, and\n  * readers must treat an unknown provider as \"no bound voice\". Deliberately\n  * minimal: fields are added here only once a producer actually emits them.\n  */\n export interface AgentVoiceConfig {\n   providerId: string;\n   /** Model the voice was selected or enrolled for, when model-bound. */\n   modelId?: string;\n   voiceId: string;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Generated agent configuration. Embedded in the persisted stage document\n  * (`stage.generatedAgentConfigs`) so clients can hydrate the agent registry\n  * without relying on IndexedDB pre-population. Present for generated-roster\n  * classrooms; preset classrooms carry `agentIds` instead.\n  *\n  * The voice fields are optional and additive: documents written before they\n  * existed simply lack them, and readers treat an absent voice as \"no bound\n  * voice\" (the TTS path falls back at call time). Adding them did not change\n  * the meaning of any existing field, so within this codebase — whose\n  * structural validators tolerate unknown fields — the addition is\n  * non-breaking and does not bump `DSL_VERSION` (see `version.ts`).\n  *\n  * It is NOT transparent to schema-validating consumers, however: the\n  * generated `stage.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties: false` on every\n  * definition, so a cross-language consumer validating against a pinned copy\n  * of an older published schema artifact rejects any document that carries\n  * these fields. Under strict schema validation, additive fields ARE a\n  * breaking change — such consumers must upgrade their schema artifact in\n  * lockstep with the documents they accept. (A `DSL_VERSION` bump would not\n  * help them: an old schema rejects the new documents either way.)\n  */\n export interface GeneratedAgentConfig {\n   id: string;\n   name: string;\n   role: string;\n   persona: string;\n   avatar: string;\n   color: string;\n   priority: number;\n   /** Bound TTS voice, when the generation pipeline selected one. */\n   voiceConfig?: AgentVoiceConfig;\n   /** 3-layer vocal descriptor for automatic voice synthesis/registration. */\n   voiceDesign?: VoiceDesign;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Multi-agent discussion configuration for a single scene.\n  */\n export interface MultiAgentConfig {\n   /** Enable multi-agent for this scene. */\n   enabled: boolean;\n   /** Which agents to include (from the registry). */\n   agentIds: string[];\n   /** Optional custom director instructions. */\n   directorPrompt?: string;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Stage - Represents the entire classroom/course.\n  */\n export interface Stage {\n   id: string;\n   name: string;\n   description?: string;\n   createdAt: number;\n   updatedAt: number;\n   // Stage metadata\n   languageDirective?: string;\n+  /**\n+   * The formatted per-course design directive (concept, palette, background\n+   * mode, motion personality) every scene's generation received. Absent on\n+   * legacy classrooms.\n+   */\n+  designDirective?: string;\n   style?: string;\n   // Whiteboard data\n   whiteboard?: Whiteboard[];\n   // Generated video requests keyed by the mediaRef used by PPTVideoElement.\n   // Runtime media state lives in the media task store / persisted media files.\n   videoManifest?: VideoManifest;\n   // Agent IDs selected when this classroom was created\n   agentIds?: string[];\n   /**\n    * Server-generated agent configurations. See {@link GeneratedAgentConfig}.\n    */\n   generatedAgentConfigs?: GeneratedAgentConfig[];\n   /**\n    * True when this classroom was generated with Interactive Mode enabled\n    * (the INTERACTIVE_OUTLINES prompt branch).\n    * Absent on legacy classrooms, imports, and regular-mode generations.\n    */\n   interactiveMode?: boolean;\n   /**\n    * True when this classroom was generated with the vocational Task Engine\n    * path enabled. This is distinct from `interactiveMode`: task-engine\n    * classrooms are interactive, but not every interactive classroom is\n    * vocational.\n    */\n   taskEngineMode?: boolean;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Slide content - PPTist Canvas data.\n  *\n  * `schemaVersion` tags the on-disk shape of this content so future schema\n  * changes can ship behind a migration step (see the app's `migrateSlideContent`).\n  * Optional for backward compatibility — legacy / pre-versioning data lacks the\n  * field and the app normalizes it.\n  */\n export interface SlideContent {\n   type: 'slide';\n   schemaVersion?: number;\n   // PPTist slide data structure\n   canvas: Slide;\n }\n \n export interface QuizOption {\n   label: string; // Display text\n   value: string; // Selection key: \"A\", \"B\", \"C\", \"D\"\n }\n \n export interface QuizQuestion {\n   id: string;\n   type: 'single' | 'multiple' | 'short_answer';\n   question: string;\n   options?: QuizOption[];\n   answer?: string[]; // Correct answer values: [\"A\"], [\"A\",\"C\"], or undefined for text\n   analysis?: string; // Explanation shown after grading\n   commentPrompt?: string; // Grading guidance for text questions\n   hasAnswer?: boolean; // Whether auto-grading is possible\n   points?: number; // Points per question (default 1)\n }\n \n /**\n  * Quiz content - React component props/data.\n  */\n export interface QuizContent {\n   type: 'quiz';\n   questions: QuizQuestion[];\n }\n \n /**\n  * The universal scene-content subset used by {@link Scene}'s compatibility\n  * default. Interactive and PBL content are also contract-owned and are composed\n  * into concrete scene unions through the generic content parameter.\n  */\n export type SceneContent = SlideContent | QuizContent;\n \n /**\n  * The content-kind-independent fields of a {@link Scene}. Everything except the\n  * `type` discriminant and the `content` payload, which {@link Scene} binds\n  * together per kind.\n  */\n export interface SceneCore<TAction = Action> {\n   id: string;\n   stageId: string; // ID of the parent stage (for data integrity checks)\n   title: string;\n   order: number; // Display order\n \n   // Actions to execute during playback (app-injected)\n   actions?: TAction[];\n \n   // Whiteboards to explain deeply\n   whiteboards?: Slide[];\n \n   // Multi-agent discussion configuration\n   multiAgent?: MultiAgentConfig;\n \n   // Metadata\n   createdAt?: number;\n   updatedAt?: number;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Scene - Represents a single page/scene in the course.\n  *\n  * The scene-level `type` discriminant is **bound to its `content`**: a\n  * slide-typed scene must carry `SlideContent`, a quiz-typed scene `QuizContent`,\n  * and so on. This is a real invariant — consumers branch on `scene.type` and\n  * then read `scene.content` as the matching shape — so the contract enforces it\n  * at the type level rather than leaving the two free to disagree.\n  *\n  * Implemented as a distributive conditional over `TContent`: the binding holds\n  * per member of the content union, so the default `Scene<Action, SlideContent |\n  * QuizContent>` is `({ type: 'slide'; content: SlideContent } | { type: 'quiz';\n  * content: QuizContent }) & SceneCore`; consumers compose the exported\n  * interactive and PBL types into `TContent`, and every member ties its own\n  * `type` to its shape.\n  *\n  * ```ts\n  * // app side — widen content; widen actions only if the app adds its own\n  * type AppScene = Scene<Action, AppSceneContent>;\n  * ```\n  *\n  * Skeleton-only consumers that reject actions entirely can still opt out with\n  * `Scene<never, …>`.\n  *\n  * @template TAction  - The playback action type (defaults to the standard {@link Action} union).\n  * @template TContent - The scene-content union; any object union tagged with a\n  *                      `type: {@link SceneType}` discriminant (defaults to the\n  *                      slide/quiz compatibility subset). Each member binds its\n  *                      own `type`.\n  */\n export type Scene<\n   TAction = Action,\n   TContent extends { type: SceneType } = SlideContent | QuizContent,\n > = TContent extends unknown\n   ? SceneCore<TAction> & { type: TContent['type']; content: TContent }\n   : never;\n \n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n // Pure discriminant guards\n // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n \n /**\n  * Narrow a candidate to {@link SlideContent}. Accepts any value tagged with a\n  * `type: SceneType` discriminant, including a consumer-specialized interactive\n  * content union.\n  * Pure, no runtime deps.\n  */\n export function isSlideContent<T extends { type: SceneType }>(\n   content: T,\n ): content is T & SlideContent {\n   return content.type === 'slide';\n }\n \n /**\n  * Narrow a candidate to {@link QuizContent}. Accepts any value tagged with a\n  * `type: SceneType` discriminant, including a consumer-specialized interactive\n  * content union.\n  * Pure, no runtime deps.\n  */\n export function isQuizContent<T extends { type: SceneType }>(\n   content: T,\n ): content is T & QuizContent {\n   return content.type === 'quiz';\n }\n",

              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts\t\n@@ -1,121 +1,145 @@\n /**\n  * Per-course visual design directive: the shared design language every scene\n  * of one course generates under (palette, mood, motion personality). Inferred\n  * once by the outline stage from the requirement, materials and research\n  * context, then threaded through slide, quiz and widget content generation so\n  * a course never again defaults to one shared \"PowerPoint blue\" look.\n  */\n \n export interface DesignDirective {\n   /** One line describing the intended visual mood, e.g. \"cinematic dark-mode physics lab\". */\n   concept: string;\n   /**\n    * 2-5 hex colors, first entry intended as the base/background or darkest\n    * neutral, last as the accent. All scene generation uses only these.\n    */\n   palette: string[];\n-  /** Whether scene backgrounds lean dark or light. */\n-  background: 'dark' | 'light';\n   /**\n-   * Tween voice for motion: playful / premium / energetic / calm /\n-   * storytelling. Widgets and (when supported) slide animation cues read it.\n+   * Background lean: `dark` (near-black canvas, tech/AI/storytelling),\n+   * `paper` (warm cream, kids/language/k-12), or `light` (plain white,\n+   * medicine/law/finance).\n    */\n-  motionPersonality:\n-    | 'playful'\n-    | 'premium'\n-    | 'energetic'\n-    | 'calm'\n-    | 'storytelling';\n+  background: 'dark' | 'paper' | 'light';\n+  /**\n+   * Tween voice for motion: playful / energetic / calm / cinematic. Widgets\n+   * and (when supported) slide animation cues read it.\n+   */\n+  motionPersonality: 'playful' | 'energetic' | 'calm' | 'cinematic';\n }\n \n const HEX_COLOR_RE = /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/;\n const PERSONALITIES: DesignDirective['motionPersonality'][] = [\n   'playful',\n-  'premium',\n   'energetic',\n   'calm',\n-  'storytelling',\n+  'cinematic',\n ];\n+const PERSONALITY_ALIASES: Record<string, DesignDirective['motionPersonality']> = {\n+  premium: 'calm',\n+  storytelling: 'calm',\n+  bouncy: 'playful',\n+  dramatic: 'cinematic',\n+};\n+const BACKGROUND_ALIASES: Record<string, DesignDirective['background']> = {\n+  black: 'dark',\n+  night: 'dark',\n+  cream: 'paper',\n+  warm: 'paper',\n+  white: 'light',\n+  bright: 'light',\n+};\n \n function clampText(value: unknown, maxLength: number): string | undefined {\n   if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined;\n   const trimmed = value.trim();\n   return trimmed ? trimmed.slice(0, maxLength) : undefined;\n }\n \n /**\n  * Validate and normalize a model-provided design directive. Returns null when\n  * the value is absent or wholly unusable (callers fall back to their own\n  * defaults rather than failing generation over styling).\n  */\n export function normalizeDesignDirective(\n   value: unknown,\n ): DesignDirective | null {\n   if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {\n     return null;\n   }\n   const raw = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n \n   const concept = clampText(raw.concept, 200);\n   const conceptFromStyle =\n     concept ??\n     (typeof raw.style === 'string' && raw.style.trim()\n       ? clampText(raw.style, 200)\n       : undefined);\n \n   const palette = Array.isArray(raw.palette)\n     ? raw.palette\n         .filter(\n           (entry): entry is string => typeof entry === 'string' && HEX_COLOR_RE.test(entry.trim()),\n         )\n         .map((entry) => entry.trim().toLowerCase())\n         .filter((entry, index, list) => list.indexOf(entry) === index)\n         .slice(0, 5)\n     : [];\n \n-  const background =\n-    raw.background === 'dark' || raw.background === 'light' ? raw.background : undefined;\n+  const rawBackground =\n+    typeof raw.background === 'string' ? raw.background.trim().toLowerCase() : '';\n+  const background: DesignDirective['background'] | undefined =\n+    rawBackground === 'dark' || rawBackground === 'paper' || rawBackground === 'light'\n+      ? rawBackground\n+      : BACKGROUND_ALIASES[rawBackground];\n \n   const personality = PERSONALITIES.find((candidate) => candidate === raw.motionPersonality);\n+  const personalityAlias =\n+    PERSONALITY_ALIASES[\n+      typeof raw.motionPersonality === 'string' ? raw.motionPersonality.trim().toLowerCase() : ''\n+    ];\n \n   const directive: DesignDirective = {\n     ...(conceptFromStyle ? { concept: conceptFromStyle } : { concept: '' }),\n     ...(palette.length > 0 ? { palette } : { palette: [] }),\n     ...(background ? { background } : { background: 'dark' }),\n-    ...(personality ? { motionPersonality: personality } : { motionPersonality: 'calm' }),\n+    ...(personality || personalityAlias\n+      ? { motionPersonality: (personality ?? personalityAlias)! }\n+      : { motionPersonality: 'calm' }),\n   };\n \n   // Wholly unusable (nothing but defaults): treat as absent so the prompt\n   // falls back to self-selection instead of asserting an empty directive.\n-  if (!conceptFromStyle && palette.length === 0 && !background && !personality) {\n+  if (!conceptFromStyle && palette.length === 0 && !background && !personality && !personalityAlias) {\n     return null;\n   }\n   return directive;\n }\n \n /** The fallback used when the outline stage produced no usable directive. */\n export const FALLBACK_DESIGN_DIRECTIVE: DesignDirective = {\n   concept: '',\n   palette: [],\n   background: 'dark',\n   motionPersonality: 'calm',\n };\n-\n /**\n  * Render a directive into the text block scene prompts consume. Always\n  * non-empty: without a directive it instructs the model to design one\n  * coherent system itself, appended by the scene-generation context.\n  */\n export function formatDesignDirective(directive: DesignDirective | null | undefined): string {\n   if (!directive) {\n     return 'None. Before writing any scene: declare ONE coherent design system yourself (background mode, text color, one accent hue, motion personality) that suits the topic, and apply it consistently across every scene you generate this course.';\n   }\n   const lines: string[] = [];\n-  if (directive.concept) lines.push(`- Visual mood: ${directive.concept}`);\n+  if (directive.concept) lines.push(`- Visual concept: ${directive.concept}`);\n   if (directive.palette.length > 0) {\n     lines.push(`- Palette (use ONLY these hexes): ${directive.palette.join(', ')}`);\n   }\n+  if (lines.length === 0) {\n+    lines.push('- No extras requested — keep the course coherent with a single system.');\n+  }\n   lines.push(`- Background mode: ${directive.background}`);\n   lines.push(`- Motion personality: ${directive.motionPersonality}`);\n   return lines.join('\\n');\n }\n",

              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/code-content/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/code-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/code-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/code-content/system.md\t\n@@ -1,234 +1,236 @@\n # Code Playground Widget Generator\n \n Generate a self-contained HTML code editor with execution and test validation.\n \n ## Supported Languages\n \n - Python (via Pyodide CDN)\n - JavaScript (native browser execution)\n - TypeScript (via Babel CDN transpilation)\n \n ## Widget Config Schema\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"type\": \"code\",\n   \"language\": \"python\",\n   \"description\": \"...\",\n   \"starterCode\": \"def solution(x):\\n    # Your code here\\n    pass\",\n   \"testCases\": [\n     { \"id\": \"t1\", \"input\": \"5\", \"expected\": \"25\", \"description\": \"Square the input\" }\n   ],\n   \"hints\": [\"Think about multiplication\", \"What is x * x?\"],\n   \"solution\": \"def solution(x):\\n    return x * x\"\n }\n ```\n \n ## Python Execution Requirements (CRITICAL)\n \n When generating Python widgets using Pyodide, follow these **mandatory patterns**:\n \n ### 1. Proper Stdout Capture Setup\n \n **ALWAYS use this exact pattern for stdout capture:**\n ```javascript\n // CORRECT - imports both sys AND io\n await pyodide.runPythonAsync(`\n     import sys\n     import io\n     sys.stdout = io.StringIO()\n `);\n ```\n \n **NEVER do this (causes NameError):**\n ```javascript\n // WRONG - missing import io\n pyodide.runPython('import sys; sys.stdout = io.StringIO()');\n ```\n \n ### 2. Use Async Execution\n \n - Always use `pyodide.runPythonAsync()` instead of `pyodide.runPython()`\n - Async execution is more reliable and handles module loading correctly\n - All Pyodide operations should be wrapped in async functions\n \n ### 3. Load Required Packages Before Execution\n \n If user code needs packages like numpy, load them during initialization:\n ```javascript\n await pyodide.loadPackage(['numpy']);\n ```\n \n `micropip` is included with Pyodide but is not loaded by default. If generated\n code installs PyPI packages with `micropip`, load it before importing it:\n \n ```javascript\n await pyodide.loadPackage('micropip');\n await pyodide.runPythonAsync(`\n     import micropip\n     await micropip.install('package-name')\n `);\n ```\n \n Never run `import micropip` before `loadPackage('micropip')` resolves, because\n that aborts widget initialization with `ModuleNotFoundError`.\n \n ### 4. Wait for Pyodide Initialization\n \n - Disable the run button until Pyodide is fully loaded\n - Show loading status to users\n - Check `pyodide !== null` before running code\n \n ### 5. Retrieve Output Correctly\n \n ```javascript\n const output = pyodide.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');\n ```\n \n ## Complete Python Widget Runtime Pattern\n \n ```javascript\n let pyodide = null;\n \n async function initPyodide() {\n     pyodide = await loadPyodide();\n     // Load any packages user code might need\n     await pyodide.loadPackage(['numpy']);\n     document.getElementById('run-btn').disabled = false;\n     document.getElementById('status').textContent = 'Python ready';\n }\n initPyodide();\n \n async function runCode() {\n     if (!pyodide) {\n         alert('Python environment not ready');\n         return;\n     }\n     const code = editor.getValue();\n     try {\n         // MUST import sys AND io before using StringIO\n         await pyodide.runPythonAsync(`\n             import sys\n             import io\n             sys.stdout = io.StringIO()\n         `);\n         await pyodide.runPythonAsync(code);\n         const output = pyodide.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');\n         document.getElementById('output').textContent = output;\n     } catch (e) {\n         document.getElementById('output').textContent = `Error: ${e.message}`;\n     }\n }\n ```\n \n ## Technical Requirements\n \n - Use CodeMirror or Monaco via CDN for editing\n - Syntax highlighting for the language\n - Run button with output display\n - Test case validation with pass/fail indicators\n - Hint button that reveals hints progressively\n - Mobile-responsive layout\n \n ## Layout Guidelines\n \n - Code editor should be visible and not overlap with output panel\n - On mobile, stack editor above output (not side-by-side)\n - Ensure editor has minimum height of 200px on mobile\n - Test cases should be collapsible on small screens\n \n ## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions (REQUIRED)\n \n The platform drives this widget by posting messages into the iframe\n (`SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`).\n Your HTML MUST register this listener, or those actions silently do nothing.\n For a code playground, `SET_WIDGET_STATE` typically loads code into the editor and\n optionally runs it:\n \n ```javascript\n window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n   const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n \n   switch (type) {\n     case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n       // e.g. { code: \"...\", run: true } — set editor contents, optionally run.\n       if (state && typeof state.code === 'string') {\n         // Guard the identifier itself: `editor?.setValue` still throws\n         // ReferenceError when no `editor` variable is declared (e.g. a\n         // textarea-only widget). `typeof editor` is safe for that case.\n         if (typeof editor !== 'undefined' && typeof editor.setValue === 'function') editor.setValue(state.code);\n         else { const ta = document.getElementById('code-input'); if (ta) ta.value = state.code; }\n       }\n       if (state && state.run && typeof runCode === 'function') runCode();\n       break;\n \n     case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n       const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (highlightEl) {\n         highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n         highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n         highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n         setTimeout(() => {\n           highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n           highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n         }, 3000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n       const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (annotateEl && content) {\n         const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n         const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n         tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n         tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n         tooltip.textContent = content;\n         document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n         setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n       // Reveal a hidden element (e.g. the solution or a hint panel)\n       const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (revealEl) {\n         revealEl.style.display = '';\n         revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n       }\n       break;\n   }\n });\n \n const style = document.createElement('style');\n style.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\n document.head.appendChild(style);\n ```\n \n ### Element Naming Convention\n \n So highlight/annotate/reveal can target UI, use consistent ids:\n - Run button: `id=\"run-btn\"`, output panel: `id=\"output\"`, editor host: `id=\"code-input\"`.\n - Solution/hint panels: `id=\"solution\"`, `id=\"hint-{n}\"`.\n \n ## Output Format\n \n Return ONLY the HTML document, no markdown fences or explanations.\n \n **CRITICAL: Output EXACTLY ONE HTML document.**\n - Do NOT duplicate content\n - Do NOT include multiple `<!DOCTYPE html>` tags\n - The output must end with exactly one `</html>` tag\n \n ## Quality Checklist\n \n - [ ] Code editor is visible and usable on mobile\n - [ ] Run button works correctly\n - [ ] Output panel doesn't overlap editor\n - [ ] Test cases show pass/fail clearly\n - [ ] Hints reveal progressively\n - [ ] **NO DUPLICATED HTML** - exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>` tag\n - [ ] **Python stdout uses correct import pattern** - imports BOTH `sys` AND `io`\n - [ ] **Pyodide uses async execution** - `runPythonAsync()` not `runPython()`\n \n \n+{{snippet:widget-visual-polish}}\n+\n {{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n",
              "additions": 2,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },

Code editor with syntax highlighting\n 2. Run button with output display\n 3. Test case validation\n 4. Progressive hint system\n 5. Embedded widget configuration JSON\n",

            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/system.md\t\n@@ -1,161 +1,163 @@\n # Interactive Diagram Generator\n \n Generate a self-contained HTML diagram with connected nodes.\n \n ## Data Schema\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"nodes\": [\n     { \"id\": \"n1\", \"label\": \"Label\", \"icon\": \"🎯\", \"details\": \"Description\" }\n   ],\n   \"edges\": [\n     { \"from\": \"n1\", \"to\": \"n2\", \"label\": \"next\" }\n   ],\n   \"revealOrder\": [\"n1\", \"n2\"]\n }\n ```\n \n ## Core Requirements\n \n 1. **SVG-based** with embedded JSON config\n 2. **First node visible** on load\n 3. **High contrast**: White nodes on dark background, light edge labels\n 4. **Edges connect to node edges** (account for node dimensions and arrow offset)\n 5. **Mobile**: Sidebar/panel collapsible, doesn't block diagram\n 6. **No jitter**: Never apply a CSS `transform` to an element that already carries an SVG `transform` attribute\n 7. **All nodes connected**: No orphan nodes\n \n ## Node Structure\n \n Positioning and animation MUST live on separate elements.\n \n ```html\n <!-- Outer <g>: position only. Never target this element with a CSS transform. -->\n <g id=\"node-n1\" class=\"node\" transform=\"translate(320, 180)\">\n   <!-- Inner <g>: every hover/active animation goes here. -->\n   <g class=\"node-body\">\n     <rect x=\"-90\" y=\"-35\" width=\"180\" height=\"70\" rx=\"12\"></rect>\n     <text text-anchor=\"middle\" dy=\"6\">Label</text>\n   </g>\n </g>\n ```\n \n ```css\n /* Correct: animates the inner group, so the node keeps its position. */\n .node:hover .node-body { transform: translateY(-4px); }\n .node:active .node-body { transform: scale(0.98); }\n \n /* WRONG: wipes out translate(320, 180) and snaps the node to the origin. */\n .node:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); }\n ```\n \n The `<rect>` is centred on the group origin, so each node's `translate()` is its\n centre — which is what the edge maths below expects for `from.x`/`from.y`.\n \n ## Edge Connection Code\n \n ```javascript\n const NODE_WIDTH = 180, NODE_HEIGHT = 70, ARROW_OFFSET = 10;\n \n function getEdgePoints(from, to) {\n     const dx = to.x - from.x, dy = to.y - from.y;\n     let sx, sy, ex, ey;\n \n     if (Math.abs(dy) > Math.abs(dx)) { // Vertical\n         sx = from.x;\n         sy = dy > 0 ? from.y + NODE_HEIGHT/2 : from.y - NODE_HEIGHT/2;\n         ex = to.x;\n         ey = dy > 0 ? to.y - NODE_HEIGHT/2 - ARROW_OFFSET : to.y + NODE_HEIGHT/2 + ARROW_OFFSET;\n     } else { // Horizontal\n         sx = dx > 0 ? from.x + NODE_WIDTH/2 : from.x - NODE_WIDTH/2;\n         sy = from.y;\n         ex = dx > 0 ? to.x - NODE_WIDTH/2 - ARROW_OFFSET : to.x + NODE_WIDTH/2 + ARROW_OFFSET;\n         ey = to.y;\n     }\n     return `M ${sx} ${sy} L ${ex} ${ey}`;\n }\n ```\n \n ## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions (REQUIRED)\n \n The platform drives this widget by posting messages into the iframe\n (`SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`).\n Your HTML MUST register this listener, or those actions silently do nothing:\n \n ```javascript\n // Add this script at the end of your HTML\n window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n   const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n \n   switch (type) {\n     case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n       // Apply state keyed by node id. Use the same convention as REVEAL_ELEMENT:\n       // each diagram node is `id=\"node-{id}\"` (matching the JSON node ids).\n       if (state) {\n         Object.entries(state).forEach(([key, value]) => {\n           const node = document.getElementById('node-' + key) || document.querySelector('[data-node=\"' + key + '\"]');\n           if (node) {\n             node.style.opacity = value ? '1' : '0.35';\n             node.classList.toggle('active', !!value);\n           }\n         });\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n       // Highlight the target element with a pulsing border\n       const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (highlightEl) {\n         highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n         highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n         highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n         setTimeout(() => {\n           highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n           highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n         }, 3000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n       // Show an annotation tooltip near the target element\n       const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (annotateEl && content) {\n         const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n         const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n         tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n         tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n         tooltip.textContent = content;\n         document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n         setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n       // Reveal a hidden node/element\n       const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (revealEl) {\n         revealEl.style.display = '';\n         revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n       }\n       break;\n   }\n });\n \n // Add this CSS for animations\n const style = document.createElement('style');\n style.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\n document.head.appendChild(style);\n ```\n \n ### Element Naming Convention\n \n So highlight/annotate/reveal can target nodes, give each node a stable id:\n - Node groups: `id=\"node-{id}\"` (e.g., `id=\"node-n1\"`), matching the JSON `id`.\n - Edge labels: `id=\"edge-{from}-{to}\"` if they need to be targeted.\n \n ## Output\n \n Return exactly ONE complete HTML document. No markdown fences, no duplication.\n \n+{{snippet:widget-visual-polish}}\n+\n {{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n",
              "additions": 2,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/user.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/user.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/user.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/diagram-content/user.md\t\n@@ -1,45 +1,50 @@\n Create an interactive diagram for: {{title}}\n \n ## Diagram Type\n {{diagramType}}\n \n ## Description\n {{description}}\n \n ## Key Points\n {{keyPoints}}\n \n {{#if hasNodeCount}}\n ## Node Count Constraint\n \n - Maximum node count: {{nodeCount}}\n - When no prescribed node list is provided, the `widget-config.nodes` array MUST NOT contain more nodes than this limit.\n - When prescribed nodes are provided, that list is authoritative.\n {{/if}}\n \n {{#if hasPrescribedNodes}}\n ## Prescribed Nodes\n \n {{prescribedNodes}}\n \n - Use every prescribed node exactly once.\n - Preserve each node's `id`, `label`, `icon`, and `details` when present.\n - Do not add, remove, or replace prescribed nodes.\n - Derive hierarchy edges from `parentId` when it is present.\n {{/if}}\n \n ## Language\n {{languageDirective}}\n \n+## Design Directive\n+The course's visual identity — treat it as LAW for this widget's colors, mood and motion:\n+\n+{{designDirective}}\n+\n ---\n \n Generate a complete HTML diagram with:\n \n 1. **SVG nodes** with icons, labels, and click-to-show details\n 2. **Edges with arrows** connecting nodes (calculate endpoints from node dimensions)\n 3. **Step-by-step reveal** (下一步/上一步)\n 4. **High contrast**: White nodes on dark background, light edge labels\n 5. **Mobile-friendly**: Collapsible sidebar, doesn't block diagram\n 6. **First node visible** on load\n \n Embed config in `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">`.\n",
              "additions": 5,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/system.md\t\n@@ -1,429 +1,431 @@\n # Educational Game Widget Generator\n \n Generate a self-contained HTML game that is FUN, ENGAGING, and EDUCATIONAL.\n \n ## Core Principle: GAMES, NOT QUIZZES\n \n **CRITICAL: Avoid boring multiple-choice quizzes!** Students already have enough tests. Create games that are:\n - **Interactive**: Players DO something, not just click answers\n - **Skill-based**: Success depends on player action, not just knowing the answer\n - **Engaging**: Fun mechanics that make students want to play more\n - **Meaningful simulation**: If there's a visual simulation, it MUST be part of the gameplay\n \n ## Game Types (PREFER THESE OVER QUIZ)\n \n ### 1. Physics/Action Games (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED)\n - **Timing games**: Click at the right moment to hit a target\n - **Aim and launch**: Adjust angle/power to hit targets\n - **Balance games**: Keep an object balanced or in motion\n - **Catch/avoid games**: Move to catch falling objects or avoid obstacles\n - **Example**: Instead of asking \"What force is needed?\", let players ADJUST thrust and SEE if they land safely\n \n ### 2. Drag-and-Drop Puzzles\n - Sort items into correct categories\n - Arrange steps in correct order\n - Match pairs by dragging\n - Build structures by placing pieces\n \n ### 3. Interactive Simulations as Games\n - Let players ADJUST parameters and see results\n - Challenge: \"Land the spacecraft safely\" - player controls thrust\n - Challenge: \"Reach the target\" - player adjusts angle and power\n - Challenge: \"Balance the forces\" - player adds/removes weights\n \n ### 4. Card/Matching Games\n - Memory match with concept pairs\n - Flashcard flip to reveal answers\n - Sorting cards into categories\n \n ### 5. Strategy/Decision Games\n - Turn-based decisions with consequences\n - Resource management challenges\n - Multi-step problem solving\n \n ## When Quiz is Unavoidable\n \n If you MUST include quiz elements:\n - Make it INTERACTIVE (drag answer to target, not click radio button)\n - Add PHYSICS/ACTION component (answer unlocks next gameplay)\n - Use VISUAL questions (identify the diagram, not text questions)\n - Keep questions SHORT and FEW (max 3-5)\n - Include EXPLANATION as gameplay reward, not punishment\n \n ## Simulation-Game Integration (CRITICAL)\n \n If your game has a visual simulation, it MUST be:\n 1. **Interactive**: Player controls something in the simulation\n 2. **Meaningful**: Player's actions affect the outcome\n 3. **Aligned with learning**: The physics/concept being taught is what the player manipulates\n \n ### BAD Example:\n ```\n Question: \"What thrust is needed for 1000kg at 9.8m/s²?\"\n Options: [4900N, 9800N, 19600N, 0N]\n Player clicks answer → Animation plays (success or failure)\n ```\n Problem: Simulation is just decoration. Player doesn't interact with it.\n \n ### GOOD Example:\n ```\n Game: \"Land the spacecraft safely\"\n Player controls: Thrust slider (0-15000N)\n Real-time physics: Spacecraft falls at rate determined by (thrust - mass*g)\n Challenge: Adjust thrust to land at velocity < 5m/s\n Feedback: Visual speedometer shows current velocity\n Learning: Player EXPERIENCES F=ma by adjusting thrust and seeing result\n ```\n \n ## Widget Config Schema\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"type\": \"game\",\n   \"gameType\": \"action\",\n   \"description\": \"...\",\n   \"gameConfig\": {\n     \"controls\": [\"thrust_slider\", \"angle_adjuster\"],\n     \"targets\": [\n       { \"id\": \"t1\", \"type\": \"landing_zone\", \"x\": 300, \"width\": 100, \"maxVelocity\": 5 }\n     ],\n     \"initialConditions\": {\n       \"mass\": 1000,\n       \"gravity\": 9.8,\n       \"altitude\": 500,\n       \"initialVelocity\": 0\n     },\n     \"successCondition\": \"landingVelocity < 5\",\n     \"levels\": [...]\n   },\n   \"scoring\": {\n     \"completionPoints\": 50,\n     \"accuracyBonus\": \"lower velocity = more points\",\n     \"timeBonus\": true\n   },\n   \"achievements\": [\n     { \"id\": \"soft_landing\", \"name\": \"Butter Landing\", \"description\": \"Land at < 2m/s\", \"icon\": \"🦋\" }\n   ]\n }\n ```\n \n ## Technical Requirements\n \n - Real-time game loop with `requestAnimationFrame`\n - Touch-friendly controls (sliders, buttons, drag areas)\n - Clear visual feedback (score, progress, status)\n - Achievement popups\n - Level progression\n - localStorage for progress\n - Pause/resume functionality\n - Clear instructions before game starts\n \n ## Fair Start Requirements (CRITICAL)\n \n **NEVER let the player fail immediately when the game starts!**\n \n ### Mandatory Rules:\n 1. **Grace Period**: First 3-5 seconds should be safe - no failure conditions apply\n 2. **Safe Initial State**: Player must be able to survive at least 10 seconds with default settings\n 3. **No Instant Collision**: Game objects should start in safe positions, away from danger zones\n 4. **Reasonable Physics**: Initial velocities must allow stable gameplay, not immediate crash\n \n ### For Physics-Based Games:\n - Calculate stable orbital/trajectory parameters BEFORE setting initial values\n - Verify: `initial_velocity >= sqrt(GM/r)` for orbital games\n - Test: Player not touching any danger zone at start\n - Ensure: Default control values (e.g., thrust at 100%) result in survivable state\n \n ### BAD Example (Player fails instantly):\n ```javascript\n // Earth starts at distance 250 from sun\n // Initial velocity: 2.4 (way too low for orbit)\n // Player clicks \"Start\" → Earth immediately falls into sun → \"Mission Failed\"\n ```\n \n ### GOOD Example (Player has time to react):\n ```javascript\n // Earth starts at distance 250 from sun\n // Initial velocity: calculated for stable orbit ≈ sqrt(1500*200/250) ≈ 35\n // OR: Start with grace period where collision is disabled for 3 seconds\n // Player can adjust thrust before any danger\n ```\n \n ## Layout & Positioning (CRITICAL)\n \n ### Game Object Positioning\n When calculating positions for game objects (lander, player, targets), account for UI overlays:\n \n ```javascript\n // BAD: Object overlaps with controls/HUD\n const objectY = groundY - (altitude / maxHeight) * canvas.height;\n \n // GOOD: Reserve space for UI elements\n const TOP_MARGIN = 100;    // Space for HUD/stats at top\n const BOTTOM_MARGIN = 250; // Space for controls at bottom\n const playableHeight = canvas.height - TOP_MARGIN - BOTTOM_MARGIN;\n const objectY = groundY - BOTTOM_MARGIN - (altitude / maxHeight) * playableHeight;\n ```\n \n ### Control Panel Sizing\n - Don't let controls take more than 30% of screen height\n - On mobile, consider collapsible controls or side-by-side layout\n - Test that the main game object is always visible\n \n ### Canvas vs UI Layers\n - Canvas should fill the container but NOT overlap with fixed UI\n - Use padding or margins to create \"safe zones\" for game objects\n - Position game objects within the visible canvas area, not under overlays\n \n ## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions (REQUIRED)\n \n The platform drives this widget by posting messages into the iframe\n (`SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`).\n Your HTML MUST register this listener, or those actions silently do nothing.\n Register it at the end of the body (or inside your DOMContentLoaded setup) so the\n game can be driven the same way a player would drive it:\n \n ```javascript\n window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n   const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n \n   switch (type) {\n     case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n       // Apply state to controls / game params. Keys map to controls by id;\n       // route to the game via a global setter when one exists.\n       if (state) {\n         Object.entries(state).forEach(([key, value]) => {\n           const control = document.getElementById(key + '-slider') || document.getElementById(key) || document.querySelector('[data-var=\"' + key + '\"]');\n           if (control) {\n             control.value = value;\n             control.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));\n           }\n           if (typeof window.setGameParam === 'function') window.setGameParam(key, value);\n         });\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n       const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (highlightEl) {\n         highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n         highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n         highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n         setTimeout(() => {\n           highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n           highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n         }, 3000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n       const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (annotateEl && content) {\n         const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n         const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n         tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n         tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n         tooltip.textContent = content;\n         document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n         setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n       const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (revealEl) {\n         revealEl.style.display = '';\n         revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n       }\n       break;\n   }\n });\n \n const style = document.createElement('style');\n style.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\n document.head.appendChild(style);\n ```\n \n ### Element Naming Convention\n \n So highlight/annotate/reveal can target controls, use consistent ids:\n - Sliders: `id=\"{param}-slider\"` (e.g., `id=\"thrust-slider\"`)\n - Buttons: `id=\"{action}-btn\"` (e.g., `id=\"start-btn\"`, `id=\"reset-btn\"`)\n - If game parameters live only in JS state, expose `window.setGameParam(key, value)`\n   so `SET_WIDGET_STATE` can drive them.\n \n ## Output Format (CRITICAL)\n \n **Return EXACTLY ONE HTML document.** Do NOT:\n - Duplicate the HTML content\n - Include multiple `<!DOCTYPE html>` tags\n - Append a second copy of the document\n \n Output structure must be:\n ```html\n <!DOCTYPE html>\n <html>\n <head>...</head>\n <body>...</body>\n </html>\n <!-- END - Nothing after this -->\n ```\n \n If you catch yourself duplicating content, STOP and output only the first complete document.\n \n ## Engagement Features\n \n 1. **Immediate feedback**: Player knows instantly if action was right/wrong\n 2. **Visual rewards**: Animations, particles, sounds for success\n 3. **Progression**: Levels get progressively harder\n 4. **Replayability**: Random elements, multiple paths to success\n 5. **Challenge variety**: Different objectives (speed, accuracy, efficiency)\n 6. **High scores**: Track best performance\n \n ## Output Format\n \n Return ONLY the HTML document, no markdown fences or explanations.\n \n ## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n \n - [ ] Game is INTERACTIVE, not just a quiz\n - [ ] Player CONTROLS something meaningful\n - [ ] Simulation (if present) is part of gameplay, not decoration\n - [ ] Success depends on player SKILL, not just knowledge\n - [ ] **Fair Start: Player cannot fail in first 3-5 seconds**\n - [ ] **Initial parameters allow survival with default settings**\n - [ ] Visual feedback is immediate and clear\n - [ ] Game is FUN to play (would you play it more than once?)\n - [ ] Learning happens through PLAY, not through questions\n - [ ] Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n - [ ] Clear instructions at game start\n - [ ] Achievement system provides motivation\n - [ ] **NO DUPLICATED HTML** - exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>` tag\n - [ ] Game objects are VISIBLE and not hidden under UI overlays\n - [ ] Positioning accounts for control panel and HUD heights\n \n ## Critical Technical Requirements (MANDATORY)\n \n ### 1. Event Binding: Use Inline onclick for Start Button\n **ALWAYS use inline onclick for the game start button.** This is more reliable than addEventListener.\n \n ```html\n <!-- CORRECT: Inline onclick - guaranteed to work -->\n <button onclick=\"startGame()\">开始游戏</button>\n \n <!-- WRONG: addEventListener can fail if script has errors -->\n <button id=\"start-btn\">开始游戏</button>\n <script>\n   // If any error occurs before this line, click does nothing\n   document.getElementById('start-btn').addEventListener('click', startGame);\n </script>\n ```\n \n **Rule**: For critical game-start buttons, use inline onclick. For other UI elements, you may use addEventListener inside a DOMContentLoaded wrapper.\n \n ### 2. CSS: Prefer Custom CSS Over Tailwind CDN\n **Use custom CSS instead of Tailwind CDN for game widgets.** Tailwind CDN with `@layer utilities` may not compile correctly, causing elements to be unstyled or invisible.\n \n ```html\n <!-- CORRECT: Custom CSS - reliable and predictable -->\n <style>\n   .game-button { background: #3498db; padding: 12px 30px; }\n </style>\n \n <!-- WRONG: Tailwind @layer utilities may fail -->\n <style type=\"text/tailwindcss\">\n   @layer utilities { .game-button { @apply bg-blue-500 px-6; } }\n </style>\n ```\n \n **Exception**: You may use basic Tailwind utility classes (like `flex`, `text-center`) directly on elements, but avoid `@layer utilities` blocks.\n \n ### 3. Script Placement: Wrap in DOMContentLoaded or Place at End\n **Either wrap the entire game script in DOMContentLoaded, or place it at the very end of body.**\n \n ```html\n <!-- Option A: DOMContentLoaded wrapper -->\n <script>\n document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {\n   // All game code here - elements are guaranteed to exist\n   const canvas = document.getElementById('gameCanvas');\n   function startGame() { ... }\n });\n </script>\n \n <!-- Option B: Script at end of body (after all elements) -->\n </body>\n <!-- No elements after this point -->\n </html>\n ```\n \n ### 4. Global Functions for onclick Handlers\n **Functions called by inline onclick must be globally accessible.**\n \n ```javascript\n // CORRECT: Define function globally (outside DOMContentLoaded)\n let state = null;\n function init() {\n   state = { gameActive: false, startTime: null };\n }\n \n function startGame() {\n   init(); // Construct state before any field access or level setup.\n   document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.add('hidden');\n   state.gameActive = true;\n   state.startTime = Date.now();\n   initLevel();\n   render(); // Render paths call publishCurrentState() directly.\n }\n \n function resetGame() {\n   init();\n   initLevel();\n   render();\n }\n \n init();\n render(); // Publish initial state even before Start.\n ```\n \n If defining these functions inside DOMContentLoaded instead, expose the handlers with `window.startGame = startGame` and `window.resetGame = resetGame` inside that callback.\n \n ### 5. Simple Initialization Flow\n **The game initialization should be simple and direct:**\n \n **Construct the state object before any field access**, including the first render, Start, and reset. Separate construction (for example, `init()`) from transitions on an already constructed state and from level setup (`initLevel()`). If level setup uses state, it also runs after construction. Reset must construct a fresh state before reading or writing its fields. Every render or semantic update path must call `publishCurrentState()` directly, including initialization and reset.\n \n ```javascript\n let state = null;\n function init() {\n   state = { gameActive: false, startTime: null };\n }\n \n function startGame() {\n   // 1. Construct state, before reading or writing its fields\n   init();\n   // 2. Hide start overlay\n   document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.add('hidden');\n   // 3. Transition the constructed state and initialize the first level\n   state.gameActive = true;\n   state.startTime = Date.now();\n   initLevel();\n   // 4. Render and publish, then start the game loop\n   render();\n   requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);\n }\n \n function resetGame() {\n   init();\n   initLevel();\n   render();\n }\n \n init();\n render(); // Render paths publish the current state, including before Start.\n ```\n \n **Avoid**: Complex dependencies like reading localStorage before events are bound, multiple async operations during init, or chained promises for game start.\n \n \n+{{snippet:widget-visual-polish}}\n+\n {{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n",
              "additions": 2,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/user.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/user.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/user.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/game-content/user.md\t\n@@ -1,73 +1,78 @@\n Create an educational GAME widget for: {{title}}\n \n ## Game Type\n \n {{gameType}}\n \n ## Description\n \n {{description}}\n \n ## Key Points\n \n {{keyPoints}}\n \n ## Scoring Configuration\n \n {{scoring}}\n \n ## Language\n \n {{languageDirective}}\n \n+## Design Directive\n+The course's visual identity — treat it as LAW for this widget's colors, mood and motion:\n+\n+{{designDirective}}\n+\n ---\n \n Generate a FUN, INTERACTIVE HTML game with these MANDATORY features:\n \n ### Game Design (CRITICAL - NOT A QUIZ!)\n 1. **Interactive gameplay**: Player MUST control something meaningful (NOT just click answers)\n 2. **Real game mechanics**: Timing, aiming, dragging, balancing, catching, or building\n 3. **Skill-based success**: Outcome depends on player action, not just correct answer\n 4. **Engaging feedback**: Animations, sounds, visual effects for actions\n \n ### Preferred Game Types (in order of preference)\n 1. **Physics/Action**: Control parameters to achieve a goal (land safely, hit target, balance)\n 2. **Timing/Aim**: Click at right moment or adjust aim to succeed\n 3. **Drag-and-drop**: Sort, arrange, or build by dragging elements\n 4. **Simulation game**: Let player experiment with variables to find solution\n 5. **Card/Match**: Memory or matching games\n 6. **Quiz**: ONLY as last resort - make it visually interesting\n \n ### Simulation Integration (if game has visual simulation)\n - Simulation MUST be interactive (player controls something)\n - Simulation physics MUST match what player is learning\n - Visual feedback MUST show player's progress toward goal\n - Example: Don't ask \"What thrust?\" → LET PLAYER ADJUST thrust and see result!\n \n ### Game Elements\n 1. **Clear objective**: \"Land safely\", \"Hit the target\", \"Sort correctly\"\n 2. **Player controls**: Sliders, buttons, drag areas, or click targets\n 3. **Real-time feedback**: Score, progress bar, visual indicators\n 4. **Levels or challenges**: Progressive difficulty\n 5. **Achievement system**: Unlockable badges for accomplishments\n 6. **Replay value**: Random elements or multiple solutions\n \n ### Visual Design\n 1. Attractive theme matching the subject\n 2. Clear UI for controls and feedback\n 3. Animations for success/failure\n 4. Responsive layout (mobile + desktop)\n \n ### Technical (MANDATORY)\n 1. **Inline onclick for start button**: `<button onclick=\"startGame()\">开始</button>` - NOT addEventListener\n 2. **Custom CSS preferred**: Avoid Tailwind `@layer utilities` blocks; use plain CSS\n 3. **DOMContentLoaded wrapper**: Wrap game code in `document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', ...)`\n 4. **Global start function**: `function startGame()` must be callable from onclick\n 5. Embedded `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">`\n 6. `requestAnimationFrame` for smooth animations\n 7. Touch-friendly controls (min 44px touch targets)\n 8. localStorage for progress/high scores\n 9. Pause functionality\n \n ### Output\n Return ONLY the HTML document. Make the game FUN enough that students want to play again!\n",
              "additions": 5,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },
