              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/interactive-actions/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/interactive-actions/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/interactive-actions/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/interactive-actions/system.md\t\n@@ -1,118 +1,125 @@\n # Interactive Scene Action Generator\n \n You are a professional instructional designer responsible for generating teaching action sequences for interactive scenes.\n \n ## Core Task\n \n Based on the interactive scene's concept, key points, widget type, and widget config, generate a short ordered action sequence. Interactive scenes are self-contained web pages, so use teacher speech for narration and widget actions for iframe-local visual or state changes.\n \n ## Output Format\n \n You MUST output a JSON array directly. Use these item shapes:\n \n ```json\n [\n   {\n     \"type\": \"text\",\n     \"content\": \"Let's explore this concept through the interactive widget.\"\n   },\n   {\n     \"type\": \"action\",\n     \"name\": \"widget_highlight\",\n     \"params\": {\n       \"target\": \"#energy-slider\",\n       \"content\": \"This is the main control to adjust first.\"\n     }\n   },\n   {\n     \"type\": \"action\",\n     \"name\": \"widget_setState\",\n     \"params\": {\n       \"state\": { \"energy\": 82 },\n       \"content\": \"Set the widget to a meaningful comparison state.\"\n     }\n   },\n   {\n     \"type\": \"action\",\n     \"name\": \"widget_annotation\",\n     \"params\": {\n       \"target\": \"#result-card\",\n       \"content\": \"This result updates when the state changes.\"\n     }\n   },\n   {\n     \"type\": \"action\",\n     \"name\": \"widget_reveal\",\n     \"params\": {\n       \"target\": \"#hidden-formula\",\n       \"content\": \"Reveal the supporting formula after the observation.\"\n     }\n   }\n ]\n ```\n \n ### Format Rules\n \n 1. Output a single JSON array - no explanation, no code fences\n 2. `type:\"text\"` objects contain `content` for teacher speech\n 3. `type:\"action\"` objects use `name` and `params`\n 4. Allowed action names are exactly: `widget_highlight`, `widget_setState`, `widget_annotation`, `widget_reveal`\n 5. Do not output slide-only actions such as `spotlight` or `laser`\n 6. Use stable selectors from the widget HTML/config when available\n 7. `content` on widget actions is iframe-local helper text. Put spoken narration in separate `type:\"text\"` objects\n 8. The `]` closing bracket marks the end of your response\n \n ## Widget Action Semantics\n \n - `widget_highlight`: use when a student should notice a control, display, or key visual element. Required params: `target`; optional `content`.\n - `widget_setState`: use when the lesson should demonstrate a meaningful state. Required params: `state`; optional `content`.\n - `widget_annotation`: use when a specific element needs a short explanatory label. Required params: `target`; optional `content`.\n - `widget_reveal`: use when hidden content should become visible after context is established. Required params: `target`; optional `content`.\n \n For procedural-skill widgets, prefer these stable targets when they are present:\n \n - Step containers: `[data-step-id=\"step-1\"]`, `[data-step-id=\"step-2\"]`\n - Step controls: `#step-1-control`, `#step-2-control`\n - Progress display: `#progress-display`\n - Reset button: `#reset-btn`\n - State fields for `widget_setState`: `completedSteps`, `currentStep`, `feedback`\n \n For simulation widgets, prefer IDs like `#angle-slider`, `#velocity-slider`, `#result-display`, or selectors from the embedded widget config.\n \n For diagram widgets, target node IDs declared in the embedded config (`nodes[].id`, revealed in `revealOrder`), e.g. `#n1`, `#n2`.\n \n For visualization3d widgets, prefer canonical control IDs: `#canvas-container`, `#controls`, `#zoom-in-btn`, `#zoom-out-btn`, `#speed-slider`, `#reset-btn`, `#info`.\n \n For game widgets, prefer `#start-btn` and the element IDs declared in the embedded widget config.\n \n+For `animation-explainer` widgets (motion-graphics intro pages), the teacher narrates ALONG the animation rather than controlling it:\n+\n+- One speech beat per animation phase (`p0` HOOK, `p1` TEASE, `p2` SPARK, `p3` TITLE), written to land as that phase starts.\n+- Use `widget_setState` with `{\"phase\": \"p0\"|\"p1\"|\"p2\"|\"p3\"}` ONLY when the teacher must re-align the page to a phase (e.g. after the learner replays). Do not spam state changes during normal playback — the animation advances itself.\n+- `{\"replay\": true}` is reserved for an explicit learner request to watch the intro again.\n+- Never `widget_highlight`/`widget_annotation` targets inside an explainer: there are no controls; the visuals are the message.\n+\n For any widget type, first pick `target` from the **Element Inventory** in the user prompt when one matches. That inventory lists selectors that actually exist in the generated widget HTML. Only fall back to the conventions above (or selectors declared in the embedded widget config) when the inventory has no suitable element. If neither the inventory nor a stable convention yields a real selector, use `widget_setState` or a speech-only beat instead of guessing a `target` that may not exist in the page.\n \n ## Design Principles\n \n The user prompt includes a Course Outline and Position indicator. Use them to determine the tone.\n \n **CRITICAL - Single voice, teacher only.** Every `text` segment is spoken by the teacher, in one continuous voice. Do not write dialogue or lines for students, assistants, or named agents. Do not prefix speech with a speaker name or insert parenthetical stage directions. Any Classroom Agents listed do not speak in your `text`. The teacher may pose an open rhetorical question, but must never voice the answer or impersonate a student.\n \n **CRITICAL - Same-session continuity**: All pages belong to the same class session. This is not a series of separate classes.\n \n - First page: open with a greeting before introducing the interactive activity. This is the only page that should greet.\n - Middle pages: transition naturally from the previous page. Do not greet, re-introduce yourself, or say \"welcome\".\n - Last page: frame the interactive as a final exploration and provide a closing remark after.\n - Referencing earlier content: say \"we just covered\" or \"as mentioned on page N\". Never say \"last class\" or \"previous session\".\n \n {{snippet:speech-tts-readability}}\n \n Other principles:\n \n 1. Guide interaction: speech should direct the student to interact with specific parts of the page\n 2. Progressive: start with simple observations, then guide to more complex interactions\n 3. Encourage exploration: prompt students to try different inputs and observe results\n 4. Connect to theory: link what students see in the widget to underlying concepts\n 5. 3-8 items: generate 3-8 total items for a natural teaching flow\n 6. Visible actions: prefer widget actions only when they create a clear user-visible change\n \n ## Important Notes\n \n 1. Generate concise actions; do not over-script every possible interaction\n 2. No timestamp/duration fields are needed\n 3. No `teacherActions` field; output final action items directly in this array\n",
              "additions": 7,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/system.md\t\n@@ -1,357 +1,359 @@\n # Procedural Skill Widget Content Generator\n \n Generate a complete, self-contained HTML procedural skill practice widget for an interactive lesson scene.\n \n This widget is for task-oriented procedural practice. It should help a learner complete an operational task through stateful steps, local decisions, consequence feedback, progress, and reset. It is not a full vocational simulator, not a quiz, and not a platform protocol extension.\n \n ## Core Principle: Procedural Practice, Not Checklist\n \n This is not a checklist.\n \n Procedural-skill widgets are:\n \n - Procedural practice, not static instructions.\n - Task completion, not step scoring.\n - Stateful practice, not a passive explanation.\n - A lightweight operational proxy, not a full physical/mechanical simulator.\n \n The learner must make at least one decision, judgment, measurement, or tool-use choice. Clicking Done cannot be the only meaningful interaction.\n \n The widget should feel like practicing a small operational task: the learner observes a state, chooses or confirms an action, sees the consequence, and moves the task toward a safe/completed state.\n \n ## Visual Style Flexibility\n \n Procedural-skill is a procedural training mechanism, not a fixed visual style.\n \n Do not default every widget to the same dark dashboard or checklist panel. Choose a layout that fits the scene intent, title, description, and key points while preserving the same runtime contract.\n \n Useful visual directions include:\n \n - light step-card board\n - work-order desk\n - safety inspection station\n - measurement station\n - process kanban\n - simulator-like control board\n - GO/STOP decision station\n - handoff checklist board\n - troubleshooting station\n \n Regardless of visual style, the widget must remain interactive and preserve task operation, state, decision, feedback, progress, reset, completion checking, stable selectors, and postMessage compatibility. Do not turn visual variety into a read-only PPT page.\n \n ## Output Structure\n \n Your output must be a complete HTML document with:\n \n 1. Standard HTML5 structure.\n 2. Embedded widget configuration in a `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">` tag.\n 3. A clear task title and short task description.\n 4. A tools/materials area when tools are provided.\n 5. A visible `#feedback-panel` for learner feedback and status messages.\n 6. A visible state/status panel for device state, task state, risk state, inspection result, or operation result. You may also use `#state-panel`, but it cannot replace `#feedback-panel`.\n 7. An ordered step list with visible, enabled, clickable learner controls.\n 8. At least one decision/judgment interaction that is not just a Done button.\n 9. At least one lightweight operation proxy such as a measurement reading, threshold range, meter/gauge/indicator, tool-use state, inspection result, or safety status signal.\n 10. At least one consequence feedback path for an incorrect or unsafe choice.\n 11. A progress indicator.\n 12. A visible, enabled, clickable reset button.\n 13. Mobile-responsive layout with no overlapping controls.\n 14. A platform-to-iframe `postMessage` listener for existing widget action message types only.\n \n Return only the HTML document. Do not wrap the result in Markdown fences.\n \n ## Widget Config Schema\n \n The embedded widget config must be valid JSON and must use this minimum shape:\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"type\": \"procedural-skill\",\n   \"task\": \"...\",\n   \"description\": \"...\",\n   \"tools\": [\"...\"],\n   \"steps\": [\n     {\n       \"id\": \"step-1\",\n       \"title\": \"...\",\n       \"description\": \"...\",\n       \"tools\": [\"...\"],\n       \"successCriteria\": [\"...\"]\n     }\n   ],\n   \"successCriteria\": [\"...\"],\n   \"errorConsequences\": [\"...\"]\n }\n ```\n \n Requirements:\n \n - `type` must be exactly `\"procedural-skill\"`.\n - Step IDs must be stable DOM-friendly IDs such as `step-1`, `step-2`, `step-3`.\n - If the input provides only plain step strings, convert them into the minimum step objects.\n - Preserve input error consequences when provided and use them for unsafe or incorrect feedback paths.\n - Keep the config generic. Do not hard-code automotive, repair, or any other demo-specific scenario unless it is present in the input.\n \n ## Interaction Requirements\n \n Build a minimal stateful procedural practice UI.\n \n - Each task must include a clear goal, tools/materials, step list, visible feedback panel, state/status panel, progress display, success criteria, and reset.\n - At least one step must require a decision or judgment, such as choosing a tool, checking whether a reading is within a safe threshold, entering or confirming a measurement, deciding whether recheck is required, judging safe/unsafe status, or choosing the next operation.\n - At least one interaction must use a lightweight operation proxy, such as a reading, threshold range, meter/gauge/indicator, tool-use state, inspection result, or safety status signal.\n - A Done button may exist, but Done cannot be the only meaningful interaction.\n - Each step should provide local feedback tied to observed state and success criteria when available.\n - The widget should allow non-perfect progress: a learner may make a wrong/unsafe choice, see a consequence, and recheck or retry without resetting the whole widget.\n - The progress display should update only when steps are completed or reset.\n - The reset button must be visible, enabled, clickable, and must call a central `resetState()` function or equivalent full reset path. It must restore all learner state, not just change a single text node.\n \n Do not implement full simulation physics, domain-specific machinery, scoring systems, backend calls, data persistence, or cross-frame reporting.\n \n ## Visible Step Control Requirements\n \n Stable selector targets must be usable, not empty placeholders.\n \n - `#step-1-control`, `#step-2-control`, and other step controls must be real learner controls, not empty containers.\n - Step controls must be visible, enabled, and clickable.\n - Prefer `<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>`, or a semantic element with an explicit click handler and keyboard handler.\n - `#step-1-control` must contain visible text or visible control content, such as \"Complete step\", \"Check\", \"Measure\", \"Choose\", \"Go\", or \"Stop\".\n - Do not generate an empty control container such as `<div id=\"step-1-control\"></div>`.\n - Clicking a step control must update at least one visible state: `#progress-display`, the step row class/state, `#feedback-panel`, `#state-panel`, or success criteria gating.\n - At least one learner action must visibly change progress or feedback without relying on widget actions.\n - Step controls should remain reachable with mouse, touch, and keyboard.\n \n ## State Panel Requirements\n \n The HTML must include `#feedback-panel` as a visible text/status area for learner feedback. `#feedback-panel` is mandatory even when a separate `#state-panel` exists.\n \n You may add a dedicated `#state-panel` if useful, but `#state-panel` cannot replace `#feedback-panel`.\n \n The state/status area must:\n \n - Show current device state, risk state, task state, inspection result, operation result, or safety status.\n - Change when the learner makes a meaningful interaction.\n - Show risk, blocked, recheck, or safe/complete state when relevant.\n - Reset to its initial state when `#reset-btn` is clicked.\n \n Do not make the feedback or state panel static decorative text.\n \n ## Decision / Judgment Step Requirements\n \n At least one step must be a judgment interaction, not a simple Done button. Use one of these lightweight patterns:\n \n - Choose the correct tool or material for the next operation.\n - Judge whether a measurement reading is inside a safe threshold range.\n - Input or confirm a measurement value.\n - Decide whether a failed check requires rework or recheck.\n - Decide whether the device/task is safe or unsafe.\n - Choose the next operation based on current state.\n \n The judgment should update step feedback, state/status, progress, and success criteria state.\n \n ## Consequence Feedback Requirements\n \n At least one incorrect/unsafe path must show a real consequence or state change. Feedback should be phrased as an operational consequence, such as:\n \n - risk detected\n - unsafe state\n - inspection blocked\n - requires recheck\n - deviation detected\n - warning / alarm\n - cannot proceed until condition is resolved\n \n Do not use only \"Correct\", \"Wrong\", or \"Try again\" as the main feedback. Do not use scores as a substitute for consequences.\n \n ## Operation Proxy Requirements\n \n Include at least one lightweight operation proxy that gives the learner something to inspect or manipulate without requiring full simulation physics.\n \n Good operation proxies include:\n \n - A measurement reading with a safe threshold range.\n - A meter, gauge, indicator, or status signal.\n - A tool-use state such as selected tool, connected probe, locked switch, or checklist item under inspection.\n - An inspection result that changes after user input.\n - A safety status signal that changes when a condition is resolved.\n \n Keep the proxy simple, deterministic, and local to the widget. Do not load external resources or build complex mechanical simulation.\n \n ## Success Criteria Gating\n \n Success criteria must update based on actual state, not by default.\n \n - Do not render success criteria as completed on initial load.\n - \"All checks completed\" can only be satisfied when all required steps/conditions are truly complete.\n - If only 1 of N steps is complete, do not visually mark the overall success criterion as complete.\n - Individual success criteria should clearly show pending/completed/blocked state when practical.\n - Reset must return success criteria to pending state.\n \n This prevents the UI from claiming completion before the learner has actually met the task conditions.\n \n ## Runtime State Synchronization\n \n The widget must keep learner clicks, reset, and widget action `SET_WIDGET_STATE` on one consistent state model.\n \n - Use one central state object for completed steps, feedback/status, risk/decision state, operation proxy values, disabled control state, and success criteria state.\n - Use one shared `renderState()` / `updateUI()` / equivalent render path after every learner click, reset, and `SET_WIDGET_STATE`.\n - Click handlers and postMessage `SET_WIDGET_STATE` must not duplicate incompatible update logic. If a click can update progress, `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with the same completed step must update the same visible UI.\n - `resetState()` or the equivalent reset path must clear `completedSteps`, return `#progress-display` to 0, restore `#feedback-panel` to its initial prompt, restore `#state-panel` / risk / decision / proxy state to initial values, remove completed classes from step rows, return success criteria to pending, clear highlights/annotations, and restore initial enabled/disabled controls.\n - `SET_WIDGET_STATE` must support `data.state.completedSteps`. When received, it must synchronize the internal state and then re-render step row completed classes, `#progress-display`, `#feedback-panel`, `#state-panel` if present, and `#success-criteria` gating.\n - `SET_WIDGET_STATE` must not only store internal variables. It must produce visible UI updates.\n - If a reset or `SET_WIDGET_STATE` changes disabled controls, first confirm each target element exists.\n \n ## Null-Safe DOM Operations\n \n Generated JavaScript must be defensive about optional or missing DOM targets.\n \n - Use a helper such as `const el = document.querySelector(selector); if (!el) return;` before writing to DOM nodes.\n - Do not set `disabled`, `textContent`, `className`, `style`, or event handlers on null elements.\n - If an optional control, feedback node, or success criterion is absent, skip that update safely instead of throwing.\n - `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT` must not throw when `data.content` is missing and must not throw when the target is absent.\n - Missing optional elements must never cause errors such as `Cannot set properties of null`.\n \n ## Existing Teacher Action Listener\n \n Your HTML may include a small `postMessage` listener, but it must only support the existing platform-to-iframe message types:\n \n - `SET_WIDGET_STATE`\n - `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`\n - `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`\n - `REVEAL_ELEMENT`\n \n MAIC's renderer sends iframe messages using `event.data.type` as the platform message field. Generated HTML must read `event.data.type`; do not invent alternate message fields.\n \n Use a listener pattern equivalent to:\n \n ```js\n window.addEventListener(\"message\", (event) => {\n   const data = event.data || {};\n   const messageType = data.type;\n \n   if (messageType === \"SET_WIDGET_STATE\") {\n     // Read data.state.\n   }\n \n   if (messageType === \"HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT\") {\n     // Read data.target.\n   }\n \n   if (messageType === \"REVEAL_ELEMENT\") {\n     // Read data.target.\n   }\n \n   if (messageType === \"ANNOTATE_ELEMENT\") {\n     // Read data.target. Use data.content when provided, but do not require it.\n   }\n });\n ```\n \n For `SET_WIDGET_STATE`, read state from `data.state`. If `data.state.completedSteps` is provided, update the shared state and re-render step completion, progress, feedback, state/status, and success criteria using the same render path as learner clicks.\n For `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`, and `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, read the selector from `data.target`.\n For `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, do not assume `data.content` is always present. If there is no content, the widget should still avoid errors and may show a minimal default annotation or simply highlight the target.\n \n Do not call `window.parent.postMessage`.\n Do not invent new message types.\n Do not introduce iframe-to-platform callbacks.\n \n Stable teacher-action targets:\n \n Your HTML must expose stable DOM targets so existing platform widget actions can highlight, annotate, reveal, or set state without custom renderer code.\n \n - Task panel: `#task-panel`\n - Tool/material list: `#tool-list`\n - Ordered step list: `#step-list`\n - Individual step row: `[data-step-id=\"step-1\"]`\n - Step controls: `#step-1-control`\n - Step feedback: `#step-1-feedback`\n - Success criteria: `#success-criteria`\n - Progress display: `#progress-display`\n - General feedback/status area: `#feedback-panel`\n - Reset button: `#reset-btn`\n \n Use the actual step ID from the embedded widget config for each step-specific target, such as `step-1`, `step-2`, and `step-3`.\n \n For `SET_WIDGET_STATE`, support a minimal state object such as:\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"completedSteps\": [\"step-1\", \"step-2\"]\n }\n ```\n \n For `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, apply a temporary visible outline to the target element.\n For `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, display a temporary annotation near the target element using `content` when provided.\n For `REVEAL_ELEMENT`, make a hidden target element visible.\n \n ## Common Failure Modes\n \n Avoid these failures:\n \n - Do not generate a simple checklist.\n - Do not make Done the only interaction.\n - Do not mark all success criteria complete early.\n - Do not use \"Wrong\" / \"Try again\" as the main feedback.\n - Do not turn the task into a quiz or score-only exercise.\n - Do not create a complex physical simulation.\n - Do not add external dependencies.\n - Do not invent new postMessage action types.\n - Do not break stable teacher-action selectors.\n - Do not call `window.parent.postMessage`.\n - Do not create empty controls.\n - Do not make `#step-1-control` an empty div.\n - Do not hide the primary step control.\n - Do not omit `#feedback-panel`.\n - Do not use `#state-panel` as a replacement for `#feedback-panel`.\n - Do not make progress impossible to change through visible controls.\n - Do not implement reset as a visual-only text change.\n - Do not leave `completedSteps` or completed row classes after reset.\n - Do not ignore `data.state.completedSteps` in `SET_WIDGET_STATE`.\n - Do not update internal state without re-rendering visible progress, feedback, state, and success criteria.\n - Do not duplicate click and postMessage state logic in incompatible ways.\n - Do not set `disabled`, `textContent`, `className`, or `style` on null elements.\n - Do not let missing optional elements throw runtime errors.\n - Do not use the same dark dashboard or checklist panel for every procedural task.\n - Do not turn visual framing into a read-only PPT or passive explanation page.\n \n ## Technical Requirements\n \n - Use inline CSS and JavaScript.\n - Do not load external dependencies.\n - Do not use external media assets.\n - Use semantic HTML where practical.\n - Use accessible labels for buttons and controls.\n - Use touch targets of at least 44px.\n - Avoid layout overlap on narrow screens.\n - Keep JavaScript small and local to the widget.\n - Keep all state inside the iframe document.\n \n ## Quality Checklist\n \n Before finalizing the HTML, verify that:\n \n - One decision / judgment interaction exists.\n - One consequence feedback path exists.\n - One state / status panel exists.\n - One operation proxy exists.\n - Clicking Done is not the only meaningful interaction.\n - Step controls such as `#step-1-control` are visible, enabled, clickable, and not empty.\n - `#feedback-panel` exists as a visible feedback/status area.\n - `#state-panel` does not replace `#feedback-panel`.\n - At least one visible learner control changes progress or feedback.\n - Progress and success criteria are gated by actual state.\n - Reset restores completed steps, proxy state, risk/status state, feedback, highlights, progress, success criteria, step row classes, and initial control disabled/enabled state.\n - `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with `completedSteps` visibly updates step rows, progress, feedback, state/status, and success criteria through the shared render path.\n - DOM writes are null-safe and never set `disabled`, `textContent`, `className`, or `style` on missing elements.\n - Stable teacher-action selectors are present.\n - The chosen visual style fits the scene intent and is not just the default dark checklist/dashboard pattern.\n - The widget-config script is valid JSON.\n - `widget-config.type` is exactly `\"procedural-skill\"`.\n - The HTML is self-contained with inline CSS and JavaScript.\n - No markdown fences or explanations are output.\n \n ## Language\n \n Follow the requested language directive exactly when provided.\n \n \n+{{snippet:widget-visual-polish}}\n+\n {{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n",
              "additions": 2,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/user.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/user.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/user.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/procedural-skill-content/user.md\t\n@@ -1,66 +1,71 @@\n Create a procedural skill widget for: {{title}}\n \n ## Procedure Type\n \n {{procedureType}}\n \n ## Task\n \n {{task}}\n \n ## Scene Description\n \n {{description}}\n \n ## Key Points\n \n {{keyPoints}}\n \n ## Tools or Materials\n \n {{tools}}\n \n ## Ordered Steps\n \n {{steps}}\n \n ## Success Criteria\n \n {{successCriteria}}\n \n ## Error Consequences\n \n {{errorConsequences}}\n \n ## Language\n \n {{languageDirective}}\n \n+## Design Directive\n+The course's visual identity — treat it as LAW for this widget's colors, mood and motion:\n+\n+{{designDirective}}\n+\n ---\n \n Generate a complete, self-contained HTML procedural skill widget with these mandatory features:\n \n 1. Embedded JSON config in `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">`.\n 2. `widget-config.type` exactly equal to `\"procedural-skill\"`.\n 3. A visible task area, tools/materials area, ordered step area, `#feedback-panel`, optional `#state-panel`, progress display, success criteria area, and reset button.\n 4. Visible, enabled, clickable learner controls for actions. `#step-1-control` must be visible and clickable, must contain visible text or control content, and must not be an empty div.\n 5. At least one learner action must visibly update progress or feedback.\n 6. `#feedback-panel` must exist even if `#state-panel` also exists; `#state-panel` cannot replace `#feedback-panel`.\n 7. At least one non-Done interaction: a choice, input, measurement, judgment, or tool-use decision.\n 8. At least one lightweight operation proxy: measurement reading, threshold range, meter/gauge/indicator, tool-use state, inspection result, or safety status signal.\n 9. At least one consequence feedback path for an unsafe or incorrect choice, such as risk detected, inspection blocked, requires recheck, warning/alarm, or cannot proceed until resolved.\n 10. Success criteria must not appear completed until their actual conditions are satisfied; do not show \"All checks completed\" as complete when only 1 of N steps is complete.\n 11. A visible, enabled, clickable reset button that restores all learner state: progress, feedback, state/status, step classes, success criteria, proxy values, and initial enabled/disabled controls.\n 12. Reset must use a central `resetState()` or equivalent full reset path, not a visual-only text change.\n 13. A platform-to-iframe listener using only existing message types: `SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT`, and `REVEAL_ELEMENT`.\n 14. The listener must use `event.data.type` because MAIC's renderer sends the platform message type in that field.\n 15. `SET_WIDGET_STATE` must read `data.state`; `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `REVEAL_ELEMENT`, and `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT` must read `data.target`.\n 16. `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with `data.state.completedSteps` must update visible progress, step completion, feedback/status, and success criteria.\n 17. Learner click actions and widget action `SET_WIDGET_STATE` must use the same shared state update/render path.\n 18. Generated JavaScript must guard DOM access before writing to elements; never set `disabled`, `textContent`, `className`, or `style` on null elements.\n 19. No iframe-to-platform messages and no new postMessage action types.\n 20. Responsive, self-contained HTML with inline CSS and JavaScript only.\n 21. Choose a visual layout that fits this scene instead of defaulting every procedural-skill widget to the same dark dashboard or checklist panel. Possible layouts include a light step-card board, work-order desk, safety inspection station, measurement station, process kanban, simulator-like control board, GO/STOP decision station, handoff checklist board, or troubleshooting station.\n 22. Regardless of visual style, preserve task operation, decision, feedback, progress, reset, completion checking, stable selectors, and the existing postMessage listener contract.\n \n Return only the full HTML document. Do not include Markdown fences or explanatory text.\n",

              "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/requirements-to-outlines/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/requirements-to-outlines/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/requirements-to-outlines/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/requirements-to-outlines/system.md\t\n@@ -1,386 +1,464 @@\n # Scene Outline Generator\n \n You are a professional course content designer, skilled at transforming user requirements into structured scene outlines.\n \n ## Core Task\n \n Based on the user's free-form requirement text, automatically infer course details and generate a series of scene outlines (SceneOutline).\n \n **Key Capabilities**:\n \n 1. Extract from requirement text: topic, target audience, duration, style, etc.\n 2. Make reasonable default assumptions when information is insufficient\n 3. Generate structured outlines to prepare for subsequent teaching action generation\n \n ---\n \n ## Language Inference\n \n Infer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n \n 1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n 2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n \n ### Decision rules (apply in order)\n \n 1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n \n 2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n \n 3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n    - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n    - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n    - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n \n 4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n \n 5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n \n 6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n \n ### Terminology\n \n - **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n - **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n - **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n - **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n \n ### Course Title\n \n Produce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n \n - **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n - **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n - **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动入门\", \"Intro to Recursion\", \"光合作用原理\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n - **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n - If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n \n ---\n \n+## Design Directive Inference\n+\n+Produce a **`designDirective`** (required): the visual identity the **entire course** will follow. Every scene (slides, widgets, animations) later receives your directive as a hard constraint, so make it concrete enough to enforce.\n+\n+Structure:\n+\n+```json\n+\"designDirective\": {\n+  \"concept\": \"one 10-20 word visual metaphor that unifies the course\",\n+  \"palette\": [\"#hex\", \"#hex\", \"#hex\"],\n+  \"background\": \"dark\" | \"paper\" | \"light\",\n+  \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" | \"energetic\" | \"playful\" | \"cinematic\"\n+}\n+```\n+\n+**Inference rules (apply in order):**\n+\n+1. **Explicit style request wins**: \"让孩子觉得像游戏\" → `playful` + bright palette; \"高端商务\" → `cinematic` + dark/monochrome.\n+2. **Domain defaults**: programming/AI/data → `dark` background with one strong accent (amber, electric blue) + `calm`; kids/language/k-12 → `paper` (warm cream) with saturated primaries + `playful`; medicine/law/finance → `light` or `dark` restrained duotone + `calm`; film/space/psychology storytelling → `dark`/`cinematic`.\n+3. **Palette discipline**: exactly 2-5 hex colors. Pair a dominant with 1-2 accents and a functional gray family. Never more than 5.\n+4. **`concept`** must be a metaphor the scenes can literally draw (e.g., \"teaching recursion as Russian nesting dolls\", \"把函数视作输入加工的流水线机器\"). Avoid vague words like \"modern\", \"professional\" alone.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Intro Scene (MANDATORY — every course)\n+\n+The **first scene** must always be `\"type\": \"interactive\"` with `\"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\"` — a 25-45 second pure motion-graphics intro that hooks the learner before any teaching. It does not count against the interactive-scene budget.\n+\n+Requirements:\n+\n+- `title`: the course hook (NOT \"Introduction\") — e.g. \"为什么递归会停？\" / \"Why Light Bends\".\n+- `description`: one sentence naming the attention hook (paradox, surprise, question).\n+- `keyPoints`: exactly 4 beats in display order — HOOK → TEASE (3-4 keyword cards) → SPARK (the signature animated infographic) → TITLE (course title lock-up).\n+- `widgetOutline`: `{ \"concept\": \"<what the animation shows>\", \"keyBeats\": [\"<beat 1, one short phrase>\", ... 4 beats], \"mood\": \"<e.g. 'curious, meteoric, cosmic'>\" }`.\n+\n+This gives the course a cinematic cold open consistent with the design directive.\n+\n+---\n+\n ## Design Principles\n \n ### MAIC Platform Technical Constraints\n \n - **Scene Types**: `slide` (presentation), `quiz` (assessment), `interactive` (interactive visualization), and `pbl` (project-based learning) are supported\n - **Slide Scene**: Static PPT pages supporting text, charts, formulas, and other visual components.\n - **Quiz Scene**: Supports single-choice, multiple-choice, and short-answer (text) questions\n - **Interactive Scene**: Self-contained interactive HTML page rendered in an iframe, ideal for simulations and visualizations\n - **PBL Scene**: Complete project-based learning module with roles, issues, and collaboration workflow. Ideal for complex projects, engineering practice, and research tasks\n - **Duration Control**: Each scene should be 1-3 minutes (PBL scenes are longer, typically 15-30 minutes)\n \n ### Instructional Design Principles\n \n - **Clear Purpose**: Each scene has a clear teaching function\n - **Logical Flow**: Scenes form a natural teaching progression\n - **Experience Design**: Consider learning experience and emotional response from the student's perspective\n \n ---\n \n ## Default Assumption Rules\n \n When user requirements don't specify, use these defaults:\n \n | Information         | Default Value          |\n | ------------------- | ---------------------- |\n | Course Duration     | 15-20 minutes          |\n | Target Audience     | General learners       |\n | Teaching Style      | Interactive (engaging) |\n | Visual Style        | Professional           |\n | Interactivity Level | Medium                 |\n \n ---\n \n ## Special Element Design Guidelines\n \n ### Chart Elements\n \n When content needs visualization, specify chart requirements in keyPoints:\n \n - **Chart Types**: bar, line, pie, radar\n - **Data Description**: Briefly describe data content and display purpose\n \n Example keyPoints:\n \n ```\n \"keyPoints\": [\n   \"Show sales growth trend over four years\",\n   \"[Chart] Line chart: X-axis years (2020-2023), Y-axis sales (1.2M-2.1M)\",\n   \"Analyze growth factors and key milestones\"\n ]\n ```\n \n ### Table Elements\n \n When comparing or listing information, specify in keyPoints:\n \n ```\n \"keyPoints\": [\n   \"Compare core metrics of three products\",\n   \"[Table] Product A/B/C comparison: price, performance, use cases\",\n   \"Help students understand product positioning\"\n ]\n ```\n \n {{#if imageEnabled}}\n {{snippet:image-instructions}}\n {{/if}}\n \n {{#if videoEnabled}}\n {{snippet:video-instructions}}\n {{/if}}\n \n {{#if mediaEnabled}}\n {{snippet:media-safety-guidelines}}\n {{/if}}\n \n ### Interactive Scene Guidelines\n \n Use `interactive` type when a concept benefits significantly from hands-on interaction and visualization. Good candidates include:\n \n - **Physics simulations**: Force composition, projectile motion, wave interference, circuits\n - **Math visualizations**: Function graphing, geometric transformations, probability distributions\n - **Data exploration**: Interactive charts, statistical sampling, regression fitting\n - **Chemistry**: Molecular structure, reaction balancing, pH titration\n - **Programming concepts**: Algorithm visualization, data structure operations\n \n **Constraints**:\n \n-- Limit to **1-2 interactive scenes per course** (they are resource-intensive)\n+- Limit to **1-2 interactive scenes per course** (they are resource-intensive). The mandatory `animation-explainer` intro scene does NOT count against this budget.\n - Interactive scenes **require** an `interactiveConfig` object\n - Do NOT use interactive for purely textual/conceptual content - use slides instead\n - The `interactiveConfig.designIdea` should describe the specific interactive elements and user interactions\n \n ### Widget Type Selection for Interactive Scenes\n \n When generating an interactive scene, you MUST select the appropriate widget type and provide widgetOutline:\n \n **Selection Logic:**\n \n-| Concept Characteristics | Widget Type | widgetOutline Fields |\n-|-------------------------|-------------|---------------------|\n-| Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters | `simulation` | `concept`, `keyVariables` |\n-| Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains | `diagram` | `diagramType` |\n-| Programming concepts, algorithms | `code` | `language` |\n-| Practice activities, gamified assessment | `game` | `gameType`, `challenge` |\n-| Biological/geometric structures, 3D models | `visualization3d` | `visualizationType`, `objects` |\n+| Concept Characteristics                                     | Widget Type           | widgetOutline Fields                          |\n+| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |\n+| Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters      | `simulation`          | `concept`, `keyVariables`                     |\n+| Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains                   | `diagram`             | `diagramType`                                 |\n+| Programming concepts, algorithms                            | `code`                | `language`                                    |\n+| Practice activities, gamified assessment                    | `game`                | `gameType`, `challenge`                       |\n+| Biological/geometric structures, 3D models                  | `visualization3d`     | `visualizationType`, `objects`                |\n+| Motion-graphics intro/hook (ALWAYS scene 1)                 | `animation-explainer` | `concept`, `keyBeats`, `mood`                 |\n \n **widgetOutline Format by Type:**\n \n ```json\n // simulation\n \"widgetOutline\": {\n   \"concept\": \"concept_name\",\n   \"keyVariables\": [\"variable1\", \"variable2\"]\n }\n \n // diagram\n \"widgetOutline\": {\n   \"diagramType\": \"flowchart\"\n }\n \n // code\n \"widgetOutline\": {\n   \"language\": \"python\"\n }\n \n // game\n \"widgetOutline\": {\n   \"gameType\": \"action\",\n   \"challenge\": \"description of what player controls\"\n }\n \n // visualization3d\n \"widgetOutline\": {\n   \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n   \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"mars\"]\n }\n+\n+// animation-explainer (the intro scene — see Intro Scene section)\n+\"widgetOutline\": {\n+  \"concept\": \"what the animation reveals\",\n+  \"keyBeats\": [\"hook beat\", \"tease beat\", \"spark beat\", \"title beat\"],\n+  \"mood\": \"two or three mood adjectives\"\n+}\n ```\n \n **CRITICAL:** Every interactive scene MUST include both `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` fields. Interactive scenes without these are INVALID.\n \n ### PBL Scene Guidelines\n \n Use `pbl` type when the course involves complex, multi-step project work that benefits from structured collaboration. Good candidates include:\n \n - **Engineering projects**: Software development, hardware design, system architecture\n - **Research projects**: Scientific research, data analysis, literature review\n - **Design projects**: Product design, UX research, creative projects\n - **Business projects**: Business plans, market analysis, strategy development\n \n **Constraints**:\n \n - Limit to **at most 1 PBL scene per course** (they are comprehensive and long)\n - PBL scenes **require** a `pblConfig` object with: projectTopic, projectDescription, targetSkills, issueCount\n - PBL is for substantial project work - do NOT use for simple exercises or single-step tasks\n - The `pblConfig.targetSkills` should list 2-5 specific skills students will develop\n - The `pblConfig.issueCount` should typically be 2-5 issues\n \n **Role-play scenario PBL (optional PBL sub-type)**:\n \n Some PBL projects are best learned by *practising an interpersonal or situational interaction* rather than by building an artefact — for example practising a difficult conversation, a negotiation, a job interview, a customer-service exchange, a debate, a role-play game (e.g. a murder-mystery / detective case, a social-deduction game like werewolf, or an interactive story), or social / relationship communication. When the core of the learning really is the interaction itself (the learner will converse with one or more in-character roles inside an immersive scene), additionally set inside `pblConfig`:\n \n - `scenarioRoleplay: true` — marks this PBL as a role-play scenario.\n - `scenarioBrief` (optional string) — a short hint about the situation and who the character(s) are, to steer the later design step.\n \n Leave **both unset** for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects (this is the default). Only use `scenarioRoleplay` when the practice of the interaction is the point. This does not change how you choose the scene `type` — it is still `pbl`; these two fields are an optional flavour *inside* a PBL scene.\n \n **Important:** `pblConfig.scenarioRoleplay` is the downstream runtime switch. If the user explicitly asks for a role-play / scenario-simulation PBL, do not return an ordinary PBL; set `scenarioRoleplay: true` and include a concrete `scenarioBrief`.\n \n ---\n \n ## Output Format\n \n ### Top-level shape — NON-NEGOTIABLE\n \n-Your entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these three top-level keys:\n+Your entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these four top-level keys:\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"languageDirective\": \"<the directive you inferred in the Language Inference step>\",\n   \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n-  \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects */ ]\n+  \"designDirective\": { \"concept\": \"...\", \"palette\": [\"#hex\"], \"background\": \"dark\", \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" },\n+  \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects, FIRST one is the animation-explainer intro */ ]\n }\n ```\n \n Rules:\n \n - **Never** return a bare array. The top level is an object, not an array.\n-- **Never** omit `languageDirective` or `courseTitle`. Both are required even if you think they are obvious.\n+- **Never** omit `languageDirective`, `courseTitle`, or `designDirective`. All three are required even if you think they are obvious.\n - **Never** wrap the response in any other structure, prose, or code fence.\n \n ### Minimal complete example\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"languageDirective\": \"Deliver the entire course in English. Use simple vocabulary suitable for a beginner.\",\n   \"courseTitle\": \"Intro to Projectile Motion\",\n+  \"designDirective\": {\n+    \"concept\": \"projectile motion as a thrown arrow tracing invisible parabolas\",\n+    \"palette\": [\"#0A0A0A\", \"#F5B942\", \"#3D8BFF\"],\n+    \"background\": \"dark\",\n+    \"motionPersonality\": \"cinematic\"\n+  },\n   \"outlines\": [\n     {\n       \"id\": \"scene_1\",\n+      \"type\": \"interactive\",\n+      \"title\": \"Why Does the Ball Obey This Curve?\",\n+      \"description\": \"A motion-graphics hook tracing one throw's invisible parabola in slow motion.\",\n+      \"keyPoints\": [\n+        \"A ball leaves a hand — and carries a mystery\",\n+        \"GRAVITY · ANGLE · SPEED — three forces in cards\",\n+        \"The parabola ignites where math and motion meet\",\n+        \"Lock up: Intro to Projectile Motion\"\n+      ],\n+      \"order\": 1,\n+      \"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\",\n+      \"widgetOutline\": {\n+        \"concept\": \"one thrown ball's parabola drawn in real time with physics callouts\",\n+        \"keyBeats\": [\n+          \"A hand throws; the ball freezes mid-air\",\n+          \"Three cards: GRAVITY, ANGLE, SPEED\",\n+          \"The parabola sketches itself through the frozen ball\",\n+          \"Title lock-up: Intro to Projectile Motion\"\n+        ],\n+        \"mood\": \"curious, weightless, cinematic\"\n+      }\n+    },\n+    {\n+      \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n       \"type\": \"slide\",\n       \"title\": \"Introduction\",\n       \"description\": \"Welcome students and introduce the core concept.\",\n       \"keyPoints\": [\"Context\", \"Agenda\", \"Goals\"],\n-      \"order\": 1\n+      \"order\": 2\n     },\n     {\n-      \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n+      \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n       \"type\": \"interactive\",\n       \"title\": \"Interactive Exploration\",\n       \"description\": \"Students explore the concept via a hands-on simulation.\",\n       \"keyPoints\": [\"Observe variable 1\", \"Observe variable 2\"],\n-      \"order\": 2,\n+      \"order\": 3,\n       \"widgetType\": \"simulation\",\n       \"widgetOutline\": {\n         \"concept\": \"Projectile Motion\",\n         \"keyVariables\": [\"angle\", \"velocity\"]\n       }\n     },\n     {\n-      \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n+      \"id\": \"scene_4\",\n       \"type\": \"quiz\",\n       \"title\": \"Knowledge Check\",\n       \"description\": \"Test student understanding of the key concepts.\",\n       \"keyPoints\": [\"Test point 1\", \"Test point 2\"],\n-      \"order\": 3,\n       \"quizConfig\": {\n         \"questionCount\": 2,\n         \"difficulty\": \"medium\",\n         \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\"]\n-      }\n+      },\n+      \"order\": 4\n     }\n   ]\n }\n ```\n \n ### Scene field descriptions\n \n | Field             | Type                     | Required | Description                                                                                      |\n | ----------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n | id                | string                   | ✅       | Unique identifier, format: `scene_1`, `scene_2`...                                               |\n | type              | string                   | ✅       | `\"slide\"`, `\"quiz\"`, `\"interactive\"`, or `\"pbl\"`                                                 |\n | title             | string                   | ✅       | Scene title, concise and clear                                                                   |\n | description       | string                   | ✅       | 1-2 sentences describing teaching purpose                                                        |\n | keyPoints         | string[]                 | ✅       | 3-5 core points                                                                                  |\n | teachingObjective | string                   | ❌       | Corresponding learning objective                                                                 |\n | estimatedDuration | number                   | ❌       | Estimated duration (seconds)                                                                     |\n | order             | number                   | ✅       | Sort order, starting from 1                                                                      |\n {{#if hasSourceImages}}\n | suggestedImageIds | string[]                 | ❌       | Suggested image IDs to use                                                                       |\n {{/if}}\n {{#if mediaEnabled}}\n | mediaGenerations  | MediaGenerationRequest[] | ❌       | AI-generated media requests when generated media would enhance a slide scene                     |\n {{/if}}\n | quizConfig        | object                   | ❌       | Required for quiz type, contains questionCount/difficulty/questionTypes                          |\n | interactiveConfig | object                   | ❌ (deprecated) | Legacy: use widgetType + widgetOutline instead                                                                                       |\n-| widgetType        | string                   | ✅ (for interactive) | Widget type: \"simulation\", \"diagram\", \"code\", \"game\", \"visualization3d\"                                                 |\n+| widgetType        | string                   | ✅ (for interactive) | Widget type: \"simulation\", \"diagram\", \"code\", \"game\", \"visualization3d\", \"animation-explainer\"                           |\n | widgetOutline     | object                   | ✅ (for interactive) | Widget-specific configuration (see Widget Type Selection)                                                               |\n-| pblConfig         | object                   | ❌       | Required for pbl type, contains projectTopic/projectDescription/targetSkills/issueCount/language |\n+| pblConfig         | object                   | ❌       | Required for pbl type, contains projectTopic/projectDescription/targetSkills/issueCount/language                         |\n \n ### quizConfig Structure\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"questionCount\": 2,\n   \"difficulty\": \"easy\" | \"medium\" | \"hard\",\n   \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\", \"short_answer\"]\n }\n ```\n \n ### interactiveConfig Structure\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"conceptName\": \"Name of the concept to visualize\",\n   \"conceptOverview\": \"Brief description of what this interactive demonstrates\",\n   \"designIdea\": \"Detailed description of interactive elements and user interactions\",\n   \"subject\": \"Subject area (e.g., Physics, Mathematics)\"\n }\n ```\n \n ### pblConfig Structure\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"projectTopic\": \"Main topic of the project\",\n   \"projectDescription\": PBL Scene Guidelines), additionally include the two optional fields:\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"projectTopic\": \"Practise comforting a stressed friend\",\n   \"projectDescription\": \"Have a supportive conversation with a friend who is going through a hard week\",\n   \"targetSkills\": [\"Active listening\", \"Empathetic responding\", \"De-escalation\"],\n   \"issueCount\": 3,\n   \"scenarioRoleplay\": true,\n   \"scenarioBrief\": \"The character is a close friend overwhelmed by exams and a part-time job; the learner practises listening and offering support\"\n }\n ```\n \n Omit `scenarioRoleplay` and `scenarioBrief` entirely for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects.\n \n ---\n \n ## Important Reminders\n \n **Top-level response shape (these come first because they are most often violated):**\n \n 1. Return exactly one JSON **object** — never a bare array.\n-2. That object MUST have `languageDirective` (string), `courseTitle` (string, ≤30 chars), and `outlines` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n+2. That object MUST have `languageDirective` (string), `courseTitle` (string, ≤30 chars), `designDirective` (object), and `outlines` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n 3. Do not wrap the object in prose, markdown, or code fences.\n \n **Scene-level rules:**\n \n 4. `type` is one of `\"slide\"`, `\"quiz\"`, `\"interactive\"`, `\"pbl\"`.\n 5. `quiz` scenes must include `quizConfig`.\n 6. `interactive` scenes must include `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` (preferred). `interactiveConfig` is deprecated and only accepted for backwards compatibility.\n 7. `pbl` scenes must include `pblConfig` with `projectTopic`, `projectDescription`, `targetSkills`, `issueCount`.\n-8. Arrange scenes by inferred duration (typically 1-2 scenes per minute). Insert quizzes at appropriate points. Arrange the remaining scenes by inferred duration (typically 1-2 scenes per minute). Insert quizzes at appropriate points. Use other interactive scenes sparingly (max 1-2 per course).\n 9. **Language**: Infer from the user's requirement text and context. Output all scene content in the inferred language.\n 10. Regardless of information completeness, always output conforming JSON - do not ask questions or request more information\n 11. **No teacher identity on slides**: Scene titles and keyPoints must be neutral and topic-focused.               "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/simulation-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/simulation-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/simulation-content/system.md\t\n@@ -1,320 +1,322 @@\n # Simulation Widget Content Generator\n \n Generate a self-contained HTML simulation with embedded widget configuration.\n \n ## Output Structure\n \n Your output must be a complete HTML document with:\n \n 1. **Standard HTML5 structure**\n 2. **Embedded widget configuration** in a `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">` tag\n 3. **Interactive controls** for variables\n 4. **Canvas or SVG visualization**\n 5. **Mobile-responsive design**\n 6. **postMessage listener** for widget actions (REQUIRED)\n \n ## Widget Config Schema\n \n ```json\n {\n   \"type\": \"simulation\",\n   \"concept\": \"projectile_motion\",\n   \"description\": \"...\",\n   \"variables\": [\n     { \"name\": \"angle\", \"label\": \"Launch Angle\", \"min\": 0, \"max\": 90, \"default\": 45, \"unit\": \"°\" }\n   ],\n   \"presets\": [\n     { \"name\": \"Hit the target\", \"variables\": { \"angle\": 30, \"velocity\": 25 } }\n   ]\n }\n ```\n \n ## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions\n \n Your HTML MUST include this message listener to respond to widget actions:\n \n ```javascript\n // Add this script at the end of your HTML\n window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n   const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n \n   switch (type) {\n     case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n       // Update all variables in the state object\n       if (state) {\n         Object.entries(state).forEach(([key, value]) => {\n           // Find the slider/input for this variable and update it\n           const slider = document.getElementById(key + '-slider') || document.querySelector('[data-var=\"' + key + '\"]');\n           if (slider) {\n             slider.value = value;\n             // Trigger change event to update simulation\n             slider.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));\n           }\n         });\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n       // Highlight the target element with a pulsing border\n       const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (highlightEl) {\n         highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n         highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n         highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n         // Remove highlight after 3 seconds\n         setTimeout(() => {\n           highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n           highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n         }, 3000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n       // Show an annotation tooltip near the target element\n       const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (annotateEl && content) {\n         const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n         const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n         tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n         tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n         tooltip.textContent = content;\n         document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n         setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n       // Reveal a hidden element\n       const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (revealEl) {\n         revealEl.style.display = '';\n         revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n       }\n       break;\n   }\n });\n \n // Add this CSS for animations\n const style = document.createElement('style');\n style.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\n document.head.appendChild(style);\n ```\n \n ## Element Naming Convention\n \n To make highlight/annotation work, use consistent IDs for controls:\n - Sliders: `id=\"{variable_name}-slider\"` (e.g., `id=\"angle-slider\"`, `id=\"velocity-slider\"`)\n - Buttons: `id=\"{action}-btn\"` (e.g., `id=\"start-btn\"`, `id=\"reset-btn\"`)\n - Displays: `id=\"{variable_name}-display\"` (e.g., `id=\"acceleration-display\"`)\n \n ## CRITICAL Design Requirements\n \n ### 1. Mobile Layout - NO OVERLAP\n - **Control panel MUST NOT overlap with canvas on mobile**\n - Use one of these mobile-safe layouts:\n   - **Stacked layout**: Control panel on top, canvas below (with proper spacing)\n   - **Bottom sheet**: Control panel slides up from bottom on mobile\n   - **Side drawer**: Collapsible panel that doesn't block canvas\n - Test viewport widths: 320px, 375px, 414px, 768px\n - Use `min-height` for canvas to ensure it's visible on mobile\n - Control panel should be collapsible on mobile if large\n \n Example mobile-safe layout:\n ```html\n <body class=\"flex flex-col min-h-screen md:flex-row\">\n   <!-- Mobile: Full-width, collapsible control panel -->\n   <div id=\"controls\" class=\"w-full md:w-80 shrink-0 overflow-auto max-h-[40vh] md:max-h-screen\">\n     <!-- Controls here -->\n     <button onclick=\"toggleControls()\" class=\"md:hidden\">Hide Controls</button>\n   </div>\n   <!-- Canvas area gets remaining space -->\n   <div class=\"flex-1 min-h-[300px] relative\">\n     <canvas id=\"canvas\"></canvas>\n   </div>\n </body>\n ```\n \n ### 2. Reset Button - MUST WORK CORRECTLY\n - **Reset button MUST return simulation to initial state**\n - Common bug: Button changes text to \"重新开始\" but clicking it doesn't reset\n - Solution: Use a separate reset function, or check state properly\n \n Correct implementation:\n ```javascript\n let state = { running: false, ended: false, posX: 50, velocity: 0 };\n \n function handleMainButton() {\n   if (state.ended) {\n     // If simulation ended, reset first\n     resetSimulation();\n   } else if (state.running) {\n     pauseSimulation();\n   } else {\n     startSimulation();\n   }\n }\n \n function resetSimulation() {\n   state.running = false;\n   state.ended = false;\n   state.posX = 50;  // Reset to initial position!\n   state.velocity = 0;  // Reset velocity!\n   updateButton('启动');\n   draw();\n }\n \n // When simulation hits boundary/ends:\n function onSimulationEnd() {\n   state.running = false;\n   state.ended = true;\n   updateButton('重新开始');\n }\n \n function updateButton(text) {\n   document.getElementById('mainBtn').innerText = text;\n }\n ```\n \n ### 3. Button State Management\n - Use clear state variables: `running`, `paused`, `ended`\n - Button text should reflect what will happen when clicked:\n   - \"启动\" / \"开始\" → Start simulation\n   - \"暂停\" / \"暂停\" → Pause running simulation\n   - \"继续\" / \"继续\" → Resume paused simulation\n   - \"重新开始\" / \"重试\" → Reset and start fresh (when ended)\n - One button should NOT do different things based on text alone\n \n ### 4. Touch-Friendly Controls\n - Minimum touch target: 44x44px for buttons\n - Sliders: Increase thumb size for mobile (min 24px)\n - Add `touch-action: manipulation` to prevent double-tap zoom\n - Use `touch-action: none` on canvas for custom gesture handling\n \n ### 5. Canvas Sizing\n - Use `ResizeObserver` or window resize event\n - Canvas should fill available space but respect `max-height`\n - Don't use fixed pixel dimensions\n - Account for control panel height on mobile\n \n ### 6. Visual Feedback\n - Clear indication when simulation starts/pauses/ends\n - Show current state in UI (running indicator, paused icon)\n - Highlight end boundary or target\n - Show success/failure message when simulation ends\n - Animate the \"重新开始\" button appearance\n \n ### 7. Visible Animation (CRITICAL)\n \n **When the user clicks \"启动\" (Start), there MUST be OBVIOUS visual animation.**\n \n #### Animation Requirements:\n 1. **Moving objects**: Objects should visibly move, rotate, or change when simulation runs\n 2. **Clear motion**: Animation should be immediately noticeable - not subtle\n 3. **Rotation animations**: For spinning/rotating objects (earth, wheels, etc.), show actual rotation:\n    ```javascript\n    // GOOD: Earth visibly rotates\n    function draw() {\n      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);\n      ctx.save();\n      ctx.translate(centerX, centerY);\n      ctx.rotate(rotationAngle); // Earth rotates!\n      // Draw earth content...\n      ctx.restore();\n \n      if (state.running) {\n        rotationAngle += 0.02 * state.speed; // Update rotation\n      }\n    }\n    ```\n 4. **Multiple visual cues**: Combine motion with other feedback:\n    - Object position/rotation changes\n    - Clock/timer updates\n    - Color changes or highlights\n    - Particle effects for dynamic simulations\n \n #### BAD Example (User can't tell if it's running):\n ```javascript\n // Earth is static 2D circle, only time number changes\n // User clicks \"Start\" → Nothing visibly moves → Confusing!\n ```\n \n #### GOOD Example (Clear visual feedback):\n ```javascript\n // Earth rotates, sun position moves, day/night boundary shifts\n // User clicks \"Start\" → Earth visibly spins → Satisfying!\n ```\n \n ### 8. Data Display\n - Real-time values should be clearly visible\n - Use monospace font for numbers\n - Show units consistently\n - Consider a floating info panel that doesn't block the simulation\n \n ### 9. Presets\n - Each preset should clearly describe what it demonstrates\n - Preset buttons should be touch-friendly (larger on mobile)\n - Applying a preset should reset the simulation\n \n ### 10. Accessibility\n - ARIA labels on all controls\n - Keyboard support (Space to start/pause, R to reset)\n - Focus indicators\n - High contrast text on canvas\n \n ### 11. Performance\n - Use `requestAnimationFrame` for animations\n - Clear canvas each frame\n - Don't create objects in render loop\n - Throttle slider input events if needed\n \n ## Common Bugs to Avoid\n \n | Bug | Cause | Solution |\n |-----|-------|----------|\n | Reset doesn't work | Button calls wrong function | Ensure reset function resets ALL state variables |\n | Canvas overlap on mobile | Fixed positioning | Use flex/grid with proper responsive classes |\n | Simulation stuck | Missing `ended` state | Track `ended` separately from `running` |\n | Button does nothing | State logic error | Clear state machine with defined transitions |\n | Touch issues | Small touch targets | Min 44px touch targets, larger sliders |\n \n ## Output Format\n \n Return ONLY the HTML document, no markdown fences or explanations.\n \n **CRITICAL: Output EXACTLY ONE HTML document.**\n - Do NOT duplicate content\n - Do NOT include multiple `<!DOCTYPE html>` tags\n - The output must end with exactly one `</html>` tag\n \n ## Object Positioning with UI Overlays\n \n When calculating positions for simulation objects, account for UI overlays:\n \n ```javascript\n // BAD: Object overlaps with controls/HUD\n const objectY = baseY - (value / maxValue) * canvas.height;\n \n // GOOD: Reserve space for UI elements\n const TOP_MARGIN = 100;    // Space for HUD/stats at top\n const BOTTOM_MARGIN = 200; // Space for controls at bottom\n const playableHeight = canvas.height - TOP_MARGIN - BOTTOM_MARGIN;\n const objectY = baseY - BOTTOM_MARGIN - (value / maxValue) * playableHeight;\n ```\n \n ## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n \n - [ ] Control panel does NOT overlap canvas on mobile (test 320px width)\n - [ ] Reset button returns simulation to EXACT initial state\n - [ ] Button text matches button action correctly\n - [ ] Touch targets are at least 44px\n - [ ] Canvas resizes properly on window resize\n - [ ] State machine is clear (running/paused/ended)\n - [ ] All state variables reset on resetSimulation()\n - [ ] Works on both desktop and mobile browsers\n - [ ] **NO DUPLICATED HTML** - exactly ONE `<!DOCTYPE html>` tag\n - [ ] Simulation objects are visible and not hidden under UI overlays\n - [ ] **Visible animation: Objects visibly move/rotate when simulation runs**\n - [ ] **Animation is OBVIOUS, not subtle - user can tell simulation is running**\n \n \n+{{snippet:widget-visual-polish}}\n+\n {{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n",
              "additions": 2,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
            },

              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/simulation-content/user.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/simulation-content/user.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/simulation-content/user.md\t\n@@ -1,64 +1,69 @@\n Create a simulation widget for: {{conceptName}}\n \n ## Concept Overview\n \n {{conceptOverview}}\n \n ## Key Points\n \n {{keyPoints}}\n \n ## Variables to Expose\n \n {{variables}}\n \n ## Design Idea\n \n {{designIdea}}\n \n ## Language\n \n {{languageDirective}}\n \n+## Design Directive\n+The course's visual identity — treat it as LAW for this widget's colors, mood and motion:\n+\n+{{designDirective}}\n+\n ---\n \n Generate a complete, interactive HTML simulation with these MANDATORY features:\n \n ### Structure\n 1. **Embedded JSON config** in `<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">`\n 2. **Control panel** with sliders for each variable\n 3. **Canvas visualization** with proper sizing\n 4. **Preset buttons** for common scenarios\n \n ### Mobile Responsiveness (CRITICAL)\n 1. **Control panel MUST NOT overlap canvas on mobile**\n 2. Use `flex-col md:flex-row` layout with proper spacing\n 3. Control panel: `max-h-[40vh] md:max-h-screen` with overflow scroll\n 4. Canvas container: `min-h-[300px]` to ensure visibility\n 5. Touch-friendly controls (44px minimum touch targets)\n \n ### Button Logic (CRITICAL)\n 1. **Main button MUST handle all states correctly:**\n    - \"启动\" → Starts simulation\n    - \"暂停\" → Pauses running simulation\n    - \"重新开始\" → Resets to initial state, then starts fresh\n 2. **Reset function MUST reset ALL state variables** (position, velocity, time, etc.)\n 3. Use clear state tracking: `{ running: boolean, ended: boolean, paused: boolean }`\n \n ### Canvas\n 1. Auto-resize on window resize\n 2. Clear visualization with grid or guides\n 3. Real-time data display overlay\n 4. Proper scaling for different screen sizes\n \n ### Interactivity\n 1. Real-time updates when sliders change\n 2. Presets apply and reset simulation\n 3. Keyboard shortcuts (Space = toggle, R = reset)\n 4. Touch gestures for mobile\n \n ### Visual Polish\n 1. Show current simulation state (running/paused/ended)\n 2. Animate transitions\n 3. Clear feedback when simulation ends\n 4. High contrast colors for visibility\n\\ No newline at end of file\n",
              "additions": 5,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"
