Generate structured outlines to prepare for subsequent teaching action generation\n \n ---\n \n ## Language Inference\n \n Infer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n \n 1. **\\`languageDirective\\`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n 2. **\\`languageNote\\`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n \n ### Decision rules (apply in order)\n \n 1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n \n 2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n \n 3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n    - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n    - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n    - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n \n 4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n \n 5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n \n 6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n \n ### Terminology\n \n - **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n - **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n - **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n - **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n \n ### Course Title\n \n Produce a **\\`courseTitle\\`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n \n - **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n - **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language \\`languageDirective\\` targets).\n - **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动入门\", \"Intro to Recursion\", \"光合作用原理\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n - **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n - If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n \n ---\n \n+## Design Directive Inference\n+\n+Produce a **\\`designDirective\\`** (required): the visual identity the **entire course** will follow. Every scene (slides, widgets, animations) later receives your directive as a hard constraint, so make it concrete enough to enforce.\n+\n+Structure:\n+\n+\\`\\`\\`json\n+\"designDirective\": {\n+  \"concept\": \"one 10-20 word visual metaphor that unifies the course\",\n+  \"palette\": [\"#hex\", \"#hex\", \"#hex\"],\n+  \"background\": \"dark\" | \"paper\" | \"light\",\n+  \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" | \"energetic\" | \"playful\" | \"cinematic\"\n+}\n+\\`\\`\\`\n+\n+**Inference rules (apply in order):**\n+\n+1. **Explicit style request wins**: \"让孩子觉得像游戏\" → \\`playful\\` + bright palette; \"高端商务\" → \\`cinematic\\` + dark/monochrome.\n+2. **Domain defaults**: programming/AI/data → \\`dark\\` background with one strong accent (amber, electric blue) + \\`calm\\`; kids/language/k-12 → \\`paper\\` (warm cream) with saturated primaries + \\`playful\\`; medicine/law/finance → \\`light\\` or \\`dark\\` restrained duotone + \\`calm\\`; film/space/psychology storytelling → \\`dark\\`/\\`cinematic\\`.\n+3. **Palette discipline**: exactly 2-5 hex colors. Pair a dominant with 1-2 accents and a functional gray family. Avoid vague words like \"modern\", \"professional\" alone.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Intro Scene (MANDATORY — every course)\n+\n+The **first scene** must always be \\`\"type\": \"interactive\"\\` with \\`\"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\"\\` — a 25-45 second pure motion-graphics intro that hooks the learner before any teaching. Ideal for complex projects, engineering practice, and research tasks\n - **Duration Control**: Each scene should be 1-3 minutes (PBL scenes are longer, typically 15-30 minutes)\n \n ### Instructional Design Principles\n \n - **Clear Purpose**: Each scene has a clear teaching function\n - **Logical Flow**: Scenes form a natural teaching progression\n - **Experience Design**: Consider learning experience and emotional response from the student's perspective\n \n ---\n \n ## Default Assumption Rules\n \n When user requirements don't specify, use these defaults:\n \n | Information         | Default Value          |\n | ------------------- | ---------------------- |\n | Course Duration     | 15-20 minutes          |\n | Target Audience     | General learners       |\n | Teaching Style      | Interactive (engaging) |\n | Visual Style        | Professional           |\n | Interactivity Level | Medium                 |\n \n ---\n \n ## Special Element Design Guidelines\n \n ### Chart Elements\n \n When content needs visualization, specify chart requirements in keyPoints:\n \n - **Chart Types**: bar, line, pie, radar\n - **Data Description**: Briefly describe data content and display purpose\n \n Example keyPoints:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n \"keyPoints\": [\n   \"Show sales growth trend over four years\",\n   \"[Chart] Line chart: X-axis years (2020-2023), Y-axis sales (1.2M-2.1M)\",\n   \"Analyze growth factors and key milestones\"\n ]\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### Table Elements\n \n When comparing or listing information, specify in keyPoints:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n \"keyPoints\": [\n   \"Compare core metrics of three products\",\n   \"[Table] Product A/B/C comparison: price, performance, use cases\",\n   \"Help students understand product positioning\"\n ]\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n \n ### AI-Generated Image Requests\n \n Use image generation only for slide scenes that need a static visual and have no suitable source image.\n \n - Each image request specifies: \\`prompt\\` (description for the generation model), \\`elementId\\` (unique placeholder), and optionally \\`aspectRatio\\` (default \"16:9\") and \\`style\\`\n - **Image IDs**: use \\`\"gen_img_1\"\\`, \\`\"gen_img_2\"\\`, etc. IDs are globally unique across the entire course, not reset per scene\n - Only the scene that first defines the \\`elementId\\` in its \\`mediaGenerations\\` should include the generation request\n - Use video for content that benefits from motion or animation: physical processes, step-by-step demonstrations, biological movements, chemical reactions, mechanical operations\n \n Video example:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n \"mediaGenerations\": [\n   {\n     \"type\": \"video\",\n     \"prompt\": \"A smooth animation showing water molecules evaporating from the ocean surface, rising into the atmosphere, and forming clouds\",\n     \"elementId\": \"gen_vid_1\",\n     \"aspectRatio\": \"16:9\"\n   }\n ]\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n \n \n ### Content Safety Guidelines for Generation Prompts\n \n To avoid blocked requests from the generation model:\n \n - Do not describe specific human facial features, body details, or physical appearance; use abstract or iconographic representations such as \"a silhouette of a person\"\n - Do not include violence, weapons, blood, or gore\n - Do not reference politically sensitive content: national flags, military imagery, or real political figures\n - Do not depict real public figures or celebrities by name or likeness\n - Prefer abstract, diagrammatic, infographic, or icon-based styles for educational illustrations\n - Keep all prompts academic and education-oriented in tone\n \n \n ### Interactive Scene Guidelines\n \n Use \\`interactive\\` type when a concept benefits significantly from hands-on interaction and visualization. \"Skill 2\", \"Skill 3\"],\n   \"issueCount\": 3\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n For a **role-play scenario** PBL (see PBL Scene Guidelines), additionally include the two optional fields:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"projectTopic\": \"Practise comforting a stressed friend\",\n   \"projectDescription\": \"Have a supportive conversation with a friend who is going through a hard week\",\n   \"targetSkills\": [\"Active listening\", \"Empathetic responding\", \"De-escalation\"],\n   \"issueCount\": 3,\n   \"scenarioRoleplay\": true,\n   \"scenarioBrief\": \"The character is a close friend overwhelmed by exams and a part-time job; the learner practises listening and offering support\"\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Omit \\`scenarioRoleplay\\` and \\`scenarioBrief\\` entirely for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects.\n \n ---\n \n ## Important Reminders\n \n **Top-level response shape (these come first because they are most often violated):**\n \n 1. Return exactly one JSON **object** — never a bare array.\n-2. That object MUST have \\`languageDirective\\` (string), \\`courseTitle\\` (string, ≤30 chars), and \\`outlines\\` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n+2. That object MUST have \\`languageDirective\\` (string), \\`courseTitle\\` (string, ≤30 chars), \\`designDirective\\` (object), and \\`outlines\\` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n 3. Do not wrap the object in prose, markdown, or code fences.\n \n **Scene-level rules:**\n \n 4. \\`type\\` is one of \\`\"slide\"\\`, \\`\"quiz\"\\`, \\`\"interactive\"\\`, \\`\"pbl\"\\`.\n 5. \\`quiz\\` scenes must include \\`quizConfig\\`.\n 6. \\`interactive\\` scenes must include \\`widgetType\\` and \\`widgetOutline\\` (preferred). \\`interactiveConfig\\` is deprecated and only accepted for backwards compatibility.\n 7. \\`pbl\\` scenes must include \\`pblConfig\\` with \\`projectTopic\\`, \\`projectDescription\\`, \\`targetSkills\\`, \\`issueCount\\`.\n-8. Arrange the remaining scenes by inferred duration (typically 1-2 scenes per minute). Insert quizzes at appropriate points. Use other interactive scenes sparingly (max 1-2 per course).\n 9. **Language**: Infer from the user's requirement text and context. Output all scene content in the inferred language.\n 10. Use generic labels like \"Tips\", \"Summary\", \"Key Takeaways\" instead.\",\n   \"user\": \"Please generate scene outlines based on the following course requirements.\n \n ---\n \n ## User Requirements\n \n Explain the labeled anatomy diagram\n \n ---\n \n \n \n ## Language Context\n \n Infer the course language directive by applying the decision rules from the system prompt. Key reminders:\n - Requirement language = teaching language (unless overridden by explicit request or learner context)\n - Foreign language learning → teach in user's native language, not the target language\n - PDF language does NOT override teaching language — translate/explain document content instead\n \n ---\n \n ## Reference Materials\n \n ### PDF Content Summary\n \n None\n \n ### Available Images\n \n - **source_1**: from cell-biology.pdf page 4 | size: 1200×900 (aspect ratio 1.33) | Labeled cross-section of a plant cell\n \n ### Web Search Results\n \n None\n \n \n \n ---\n \n ## Output Requirements\n \n Please automatically infer the following from user requirements:\n \n - Course topic and core content\n - Target audience and difficulty level\n - Course duration (default 15-30 minutes if not specified)\n - Teaching style (formal/casual/interactive/academic)\n - Visual style (minimal/colorful/professional/playful)\n \n Then output your response as a single JSON object.\n \n **Top-level shape — this is what you MUST return:**\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"languageDirective\": \"2-5 sentence instruction describing the course language behavior\",\n   \"courseTitle\": \"concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language\",\n   \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects, schema described below */ ]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Never return a bare array. packages/@openmaic/generation/test/__snapshots__/scene-prompt-golden.test.ts.snap\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/test/__snapshots__/scene-prompt-golden.test.ts.snap\t\n@@ -1,1780 +1,1859 @@\n // Vitest Snapshot v1, https://vitest.dev/guide/snapshot.html\n \n exports[`pins representative system and user prompts for every scene kind 1`] = `\n {\n   \"interactive\": {\n     \"system\": \"# Simulation Widget Content Generator\n \n Generate a self-contained HTML simulation with embedded widget configuration.\n \n ## Output Structure\n \n Your output must be a complete HTML document with:\n \n 1. **Standard HTML5 structure**\n 2. **Embedded widget configuration** in a \\`<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">\\` tag\n 3. **Interactive controls** for variables\n 4. **Canvas or SVG visualization**\n 5. **Mobile-responsive design**\n 6. **postMessage listener** for widget actions (REQUIRED)\n \n ## Widget Config Schema\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"type\": \"simulation\",\n   \"concept\": \"projectile_motion\",\n   \"description\": \"...\",\n   \"variables\": [\n     { \"name\": \"angle\", \"label\": \"Launch Angle\", \"min\": 0, \"max\": 90, \"default\": 45, \"unit\": \"°\" }\n   ],\n   \"presets\": [\n     { \"name\": \"Hit the target\", \"variables\": { \"angle\": 30, \"velocity\": 25 } }\n   ]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ## CRITICAL: postMessage Listener for Widget Actions\n \n Your HTML MUST include this message listener to respond to widget actions:\n \n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n // Add this script at the end of your HTML\n window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {\n   const { type, target, state, content } = event.data;\n \n   switch (type) {\n     case 'SET_WIDGET_STATE':\n       // Update all variables in the state object\n       if (state) {\n         Object.entries(state).forEach(([key, value]) => {\n           // Find the slider/input for this variable and update it\n           const slider = document.getElementById(key + '-slider') || document.querySelector('[data-var=\"' + key + '\"]');\n           if (slider) {\n             slider.value = value;\n             // Trigger change event to update simulation\n             slider.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));\n           }\n         });\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT':\n       // Highlight the target element with a pulsing border\n       const highlightEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (highlightEl) {\n         highlightEl.style.outline = '3px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8)';\n         highlightEl.style.outlineOffset = '4px';\n         highlightEl.style.animation = 'pulse-highlight 2s infinite';\n         // Remove highlight after 3 seconds\n         setTimeout(() => {\n           highlightEl.style.outline = '';\n           highlightEl.style.animation = '';\n         }, 3000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'ANNOTATE_ELEMENT':\n       // Show an annotation tooltip near the target element\n       const annotateEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (annotateEl && content) {\n         const rect = annotateEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n         const tooltip = document.createElement('div');\n         tooltip.className = 'teacher-annotation';\n         tooltip.style.cssText = 'position:fixed; top:' + (rect.top - 40) + 'px; left:' + rect.left + 'px; background:rgba(139,92,246,0.95); color:white; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; z-index:1000; animation:fadeIn 0.3s;';\n         tooltip.textContent = content;\n         document.body.appendChild(tooltip);\n         setTimeout(() => tooltip.remove(), 4000);\n       }\n       break;\n \n     case 'REVEAL_ELEMENT':\n       // Reveal a hidden element\n       const revealEl = document.querySelector(target);\n       if (revealEl) {\n         revealEl.style.display = '';\n         revealEl.style.opacity = '1';\n       }\n       break;\n   }\n });\n \n // Add this CSS for animations\n const style = document.createElement('style');\n style.textContent = '@keyframes pulse-highlight { 0%, 100% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.8); } 50% { outline-color: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.4); } } @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }';\n document.head.appendChild(style);\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ## Element Naming Convention\n \n To make highlight/annotation work, use consistent IDs for controls:\n - Sliders: \\`id=\"{variable_name}-slider\"\\` (e.g., \\`id=\"angle-slider\"\\`, \\`id=\"velocity-slider\"\\`)\n - Buttons: \\`id=\"{action}-btn\"\\` (e.g., \\`id=\"start-btn\"\\`, \\`id=\"reset-btn\"\\`)\n - Displays: \\`id=\"{variable_name}-display\"\\` (e.g., \\`id=\"acceleration-display\"\\`)\n \n ## CRITICAL Design Requirements\n \n ### 1. Mobile Layout - NO OVERLAP\n - **Control panel MUST NOT overlap with canvas on mobile**\n - Use one of these mobile-safe layouts:\n   - **Stacked layout**: Control panel on top, canvas below (with proper spacing)\n   - **Bottom sheet**: Control panel slides up from bottom on mobile\n   - **Side drawer**: Collapsible panel that doesn't block canvas\n - Test viewport widths: 320px, 375px, 414px, 768px\n - Use \\`min-height\\` for canvas to ensure it's visible on mobile\n - Control panel should be collapsible on mobile if large\n \n Example mobile-safe layout:\n \\`\\`\\`html\n <body class=\"flex flex-col min-h-screen md:flex-row\">\n   <!-- Mobile: Full-width, collapsible control panel -->\n   <div id=\"controls\" class=\"w-full md:w-80 shrink-0 overflow-auto max-h-[40vh] md:max-h-screen\">\n     <!-- Controls here -->\n     <button onclick=\"toggleControls()\" class=\"md:hidden\">Hide Controls</button>\n   </div>\n   <!-- Canvas area gets remaining space -->\n   <div class=\"flex-1 min-h-[300px] relative\">\n     <canvas id=\"canvas\"></canvas>\n   </div>\n </body>\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### 2. Reset Button - MUST WORK CORRECTLY\n - **Reset button MUST return simulation to initial state**\n - Common bug: Button changes text to \"重新开始\" but clicking it doesn't reset\n - Solution: Use a separate reset function, or check state properly\n \n Correct implementation:\n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n let state = { running: false, ended: false, posX: 50, velocity: 0 };\n \n function handleMainButton() {\n   if (state.ended) {\n     // If simulation ended, reset first\n     resetSimulation();\n   } else if (state.running) {\n     pauseSimulation();\n   } else {\n     startSimulation();\n   }\n }\n \n function resetSimulation() {\n   state.running = false;\n   state.ended = false;\n   state.posX = 50;  // Reset to initial position!\n   state.velocity = 0;  // Reset velocity!\n   updateButton('启动');\n   draw();\n }\n \n // When simulation hits boundary/ends:\n function onSimulationEnd() {\n   state.running = false;\n   state.ended = true;\n   updateButton('重新开始');\n }\n \n function updateButton(text) {\n   document.getElementById('mainBtn').innerText = text;\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### 3. Button State Management\n - Use clear state variables: \\`running\\`, \\`paused\\`, \\`ended\\`\n - Button text should reflect what will happen when clicked:\n   - \"启动\" / \"开始\" → Start simulation\n   - \"暂停\" / \"暂停\" → Pause running simulation\n   - \"继续\" / \"继续\" → Resume paused simulation\n   - \"重新开始\" / \"重试\" → Reset and start fresh (when ended)\n - One button should NOT do different things based on text alone\n \n ### 4. Touch-Friendly Controls\n - Minimum touch target: 44x44px for buttons\n - Sliders: Increase thumb size for mobile (min 24px)\n - Add \\`touch-action: manipulation\\` to prevent double-tap zoom\n - Use \\`touch-action: none\\` on canvas for custom gesture handling\n \n ### 5. Canvas Sizing\n - Use \\`ResizeObserver\\` or window resize event\n - Canvas should fill available space but respect \\`max-height\\`\n - Don't use fixed pixel dimensions\n - Account for control panel height on mobile\n \n ### 6. Visual Feedback\n - Clear indication when simulation starts/pauses/ends\n - Show current state in UI (running indicator, paused icon)\n - Highlight end boundary or target\n - Show success/failure message when simulation ends\n - Animate the \"重新开始\" button appearance\n \n ### 7. Visible Animation (CRITICAL)\n \n **When the user clicks \"启动\" (Start), there MUST be OBVIOUS visual animation.**\n \n #### Animation Requirements:\n 1. **Moving objects**: Objects should visibly move, rotate, or change when simulation runs\n 2. **Clear motion**: Animation should be immediately noticeable - not subtle\n 3. **Rotation animations**: For spinning/rotating objects (earth, wheels, etc.), show actual rotation:\n    \\`\\`\\`javascript\n    // GOOD: Earth visibly rotates\n    function draw() {\n      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);\n      ctx.save();\n      ctx.translate(centerX, centerY);\n      ctx.rotate(rotationAngle); // Earth rotates!\n      // Draw earth content...\n      ctx.restore();\n \n      if (state.running) {\n        rotationAngle += 0.02 * state.speed; // Update rotation\n      }\n    }\n    \\`\\`\\`\n 4. **Multiple visual cues**: Combine motion with other feedback:\n    - Object position/rotation changes\n    - Clock/timer updates\n    - Color changes or highlights\n    - Particle effects for dynamic simulations\n \n #### BAD Example (User can't tell if it's running):\n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n // Earth is static 2D circle, only time number changes\n // User clicks \"Start\" → Nothing visibly moves → Confusing!\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### GOOD Example (Clear visual feedback):\n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n // Earth rotates, sun position moves, day/night boundary shifts\n // User clicks \"Start\" → Earth visibly spins → Satisfying!\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### 8. Data Display\n - Real-time values should be clearly visible\n - Use monospace font for numbers\n - Show units consistently\n - Consider a floating info panel that doesn't block the simulation\n \n ### 9. Presets\n - Each preset should clearly describe what it demonstrates\n - Preset buttons should be touch-friendly (larger on mobile)\n - Applying a preset should reset the simulation\n \n ### 10. Accessibility\n - ARIA labels on all controls\n - Keyboard support (Space to start/pause, R to reset)\n - Focus indicators\n - High contrast text on canvas\n \n ### 11. Performance\n - Use \\`requestAnimationFrame\\` for animations\n - Clear canvas each frame\n - Don't create objects in render loop\n - Throttle slider input events if needed\n \n ## Common Bugs to Avoid\n \n | Bug | Cause | Solution |\n |-----|-------|----------|\n | Reset doesn't work | Button calls wrong function | Ensure reset function resets ALL state variables |\n | Canvas overlap on mobile | Fixed positioning | Use flex/grid with proper responsive classes |\n | Simulation stuck | Missing \\`ended\\` state | Track \\`ended\\` separately from \\`running\\` |\n | Button does nothing | State logic error | Clear state machine with defined transitions |\n | Touch issues | Small touch targets | Min 44px touch targets, larger sliders |\n \n ## Output Format\n \n Return ONLY the HTML document, no markdown fences or explanations.\n \n **CRITICAL: Output EXACTLY ONE HTML document.**\n - Do NOT duplicate content\n - Do NOT include multiple \\`<!DOCTYPE html>\\` tags\n - The output must end with exactly one \\`</html>\\` tag\n \n ## Object Positioning with UI Overlays\n \n When calculating positions for simulation objects, account for UI overlays:\n \n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n // BAD: Object overlaps with controls/HUD\n const objectY = baseY - (value / maxValue) * canvas.height;\n \n // GOOD: Reserve space for UI elements\n const TOP_MARGIN = 100;    // Space for HUD/stats at top\n const BOTTOM_MARGIN = 200; // Space for controls at bottom\n const playableHeight = canvas.height - TOP_MARGIN - BOTTOM_MARGIN;\n const objectY = baseY - BOTTOM_MARGIN - (value / maxValue) * playableHeight;\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ## Quality Checklist (verify before output)\n \n - [ ] Control panel does NOT overlap canvas on mobile (test 320px width)\n - [ ] Reset button returns simulation to EXACT initial state\n - [ ] Button text matches button action correctly\n - [ ] Touch targets are at least 44px\n - [ ] Canvas resizes properly on window resize\n - [ ] State machine is clear (running/paused/ended)\n - [ ] All state variables reset on resetSimulation()\n - [ ] Works on both desktop and mobile browsers\n - [ ] **NO DUPLICATED HTML** - exactly ONE \\`<!DOCTYPE html>\\` tag\n - [ ] Simulation objects are visible and not hidden under UI overlays\n - [ ] **Visible animation: Objects visibly move/rotate when simulation runs**\n - [ ] **Animation is OBVIOUS, not subtle - user can tell simulation is running**\n \n \n+## Visual Quality Standard for ALL Interactive Widgets (shared)\n+\n+A widget that \"works\" but looks like a 2005 dashboard fails this pipeline as much as a widget that crashes. Apply the course design directive (see \"Design Directive\" in the user prompt) to every widget.\n+\n+### Palette discipline\n+\n+- Use those exact colors from the design directive for: page/canvas background, primary accents, text, and semantic states. Do not invent new hues per element.\n+- One background treatment across all views; one accent hue doing the highlighting. 60% neutral / 30% secondary / 10% accent, never the accent everywhere.\n+- Text contrast: body text ≥ 4.5:1 against its actual background (count tint overlays). Never light text on mid-tone backgrounds. If uncertain, darken the surface, not the text.\n+- On dark surfaces, never full-screen linear gradients (they band); use a solid base + one or two radial gradient glows at 12–25% opacity. Tint neutrals (like #1a1f2e, #e8ecf4) toward the accent hue — dead pure grays look undesigned.\n+\n+### Layout & depth\n+\n+- Largest-to-smallest hierarchy is visible in 2 seconds: one hero element (number, headline, chart) per view; labels < 16px only for metadata.\n+- Cards use 12–20px radii, 2–4px borders or soft shadows — web UI values are invisible at classroom projection distance, so scale up: body text ≥ 16px on mobile-safe layouts, ≥ 20px on main surfaces, padding ≥ 24px between zones.\n+- Every scene (state) needs at least two focal points the eye can travel between — a single floating text block is a failure.\n+- Backgrounds are never empty: add 2–5 subtle decorative layers (accent-tinted radial glow, oversized faded keyword at 3–8% opacity, hairline grid, muted panel) so whitespace looks intentional.\n+- Icons: use inline SVG (project/stroke style, 2px round-cap strokes, viewBox 0 0 24 24). No emoji as primary info — emoji only inside achievement/reward badges.\n+\n+### Motion has meaning\n+\n+- Decorative elements get one ambient animation (breathing glow, slow drift, gentle rotation) so nothing reads static; shared across them is fine.\n+- State changes animate ~200–300ms \\`ease-out\\` (entrances), \\`ease-in\\` (exits); reveal beats stagger children 50–120ms apart. Springs for direct manipulation only.\n+- Numbers count up to their value (~0.8–1.2s, \\`power2.out\\`) when they enter; progress bars/donuts draw when revealed, not before.\n+- No animation is longer than 600ms except cinematic reveals the directive's motionPersonality explicitly asks for. \"The best motion is barely noticeable.\"\n+- All motion must be deterministic: no \\`Date.now()\\` state in published observations, no unseeded randomness inside rendered results. Randomness is allowed only for generated practice content, and then through a seeded helper.\n+\n+### States, feedback & safety\n+\n+- Every control gives feedback within 100ms (hover/active/pressed/disabled states defined in CSS).\n+- Loading/empty/error states exist and use the same palette (spinner or skeleton bars, not invented colors).\n+- Failure feedback is supporting, never guilt-tripping: green = correct/done, amber = check again, red = unsafe/wrong.\n+- Mobile safety: 44px min touch targets, collapsible panels, no horizontal scroll, canvas resizes with container.\n+\n ## REQUIRED: declared current state for newly generated interactive content (v1)\n \n This contract applies to every interactive content type. Report what the activity *is* right now, in the lesson's own terms — not a dump of JavaScript variables. The platform reads the same data for every lesson; there are no slider/circuit/game-specific collectors. Do not present protocol names to students.\n \n Wrap the whole interactive area in one element with \\`id=\"experiment\"\\`. Inside it, publish exactly one non-executable \\`<script type=\"application/json\" data-maic-observation>\\` node. This is separate from widget-config (source defaults). Keep existing action controls working. Do not add a state-request message listener; the platform owns collection. This evidence grants no tool or selector permissions.\n \n Publish a JSON object with these fields:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"summary\": \"Liquid density is 1400 kg/m³ and buoyancy is 4.116 N; the drawing still shows the 1000 kg/m³ result.\",\n   \"state\": {\n     \"liquid\": { \"density\": 1400, \"unit\": \"kg/m³\", \"buoyancy\": 4.116 },\n     \"object\": { \"displacedVolume\": 300, \"fullySubmerged\": true },\n     \"drawingPaused\": true\n   },\n   \"rendered\": { \"liquid\": { \"density\": 1000, \"buoyancy\": 3.0 } }\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n - \\`summary\\`: one short sentence a student could read, describing the current state. Always include it — it is what the classroom falls back to when nothing else in the report is recognizable.\n - \\`state\\`: whatever this lesson naturally tracks — parameters the student set, what they built or connected, progress, mode. Shape it however fits the activity. Use stable keys or ids for things that persist, so the same object is recognizable across publications. Omit purely decorative animation coordinates. For positions meaningful to the lesson, keep them current and use student-readable terms, or explain the coordinate origin, direction and whether indices start at zero; an internal \\`(row: 2, column: 1)\\` must not be mistaken for “second row, first column.” Report a quantity you genuinely cannot determine as \\`null\\` and say so in \\`summary\\`; never substitute a source default or an earlier value.\n - \\`rendered\\` (optional): include it **only** when the activity has an explicit apply/run/draw step that can lag behind the inputs, and let it hold the values the last completed result actually used. Omit it entirely when the lesson redraws immediately — there the split carries no information.\n \n Total UTF-8 JSON must stay at or under 32768 bytes, and must not nest more than 64 levels deep. Those are the only limits the platform enforces: it reads what you publish without checking field names or types, so extra fields are allowed and are passed through unchanged, and a report that omits something is still delivered as-is rather than discarded.\n \n Publish the initial state even before the student presses Start. Publish after every semantic change, including reset and programmatic actions. Put publication in the functions that create/remove objects or change phase, including those called by timers or animation loops — not just in click/input handlers. For example, when a word appears automatically, publish the new word list immediately; do not leave “zero words” until the next user action. Pure animation frames need no extra publication unless a reported value changes. Input changes must be published even if the drawing or calculation has not completed.\n \n This is a replaced data projection, not history, storage or a new global state manager. Reading it has no side effects: state is published by the existing interaction and render paths, and collection only copies the inert data node. Do not redraw to answer a state request. A failed publication removes the old node rather than leaving stale values behind as current.\n \n Use this publication helper in the generated HTML; constructing the application state is your responsibility.\n \n Never call \\`publishState()\\` without an observation: it rejects \\`undefined\\` and aborts the current script. Use one canonical \\`publishCurrentState()\\` that constructs the complete observation from the current application state and passes it to \\`publishState(observation)\\`. Call that projection directly from the initial render, every semantic change, reset, and programmatic or timer-driven updates. Do not wrap or monkey-patch update functions after the fact to add publication; a late wrapper cannot repair a failure in the original update path.\n \n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n function publishState(observation) {\n   const root = document.getElementById('experiment');\n   if (!root) throw new Error('Missing interaction scope');\n   try {\n     const raw = JSON.stringify(observation);\n     if (typeof raw !== 'string' || new TextEncoder().encode(raw).length > 32768)\n       throw new Error('Invalid state publication');\n     let node = root.querySelector('script[data-maic-observation]');\n     if (!node) {\n       node = document.createElement('script');\n       node.type = 'application/json';\n       node.setAttribute('data-maic-observation', '');\n       root.appendChild(node);\n     }\n     node.textContent = raw;\n   } catch (error) {\n     root.querySelectorAll('script[data-maic-observation]').forEach(node => node.remove());\n     throw error;\n   }\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n For example, a reveal activity can use this single projection path. Adapt the state and summary to the lesson; construct the state before the first render and reset it before rendering again.\n \n \\`\\`\\`javascript\n let activityState = { step: 1 };\n \n function publishCurrentState() {\n   publishState({\n     summary: 'Step ' + activityState.step,\n     state: { step: activityState.step }\n   });\n }\n \n function updateReveal() {\n   document.getElementById('step').textContent = activityState.step;\n   publishCurrentState();\n }\n \n function advanceStep() {\n   activityState.step++;\n   updateReveal();\n }\n \n function resetActivity() {\n   activityState = { step: 1 };\n   updateReveal();\n }\n \n updateReveal(); // Initial state, before any user action.\n // Buttons, programmatic actions, and timers call advanceStep/resetActivity\n // directly; each path renders and publishes its current state.\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n If the activity has an apply/run step, capture the inputs a run actually used when it starts, and write them to \\`rendered\\` only after that run has successfully become the displayed result. A cancelled or superseded run must not update \\`rendered\\`, and a parameter edit alone must never advance it.\",\n     \"user\": \"Create a simulation widget for: Energy transfer\n \n ## Concept Overview\n \n Explore how energy changes with a slider.\n \n ## Key Points\n \n Move the slider\n Observe the result\n \n ## Variables to Expose\n \n energy\n \n ## Design Idea\n \n \n \n ## Language\n \n Teach in English.\n \n+## Design Directive\n+The course's visual identity — treat it as LAW for this widget's colors, mood and motion:\n+\n+\n+\n ---\n \n Generate a complete, interactive HTML simulation with these MANDATORY features:\n \n ### Structure\n 1. **Embedded JSON config** in \\`<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"widget-config\">\\`\n 2. **Control panel** with sliders for each variable\n 3. **Canvas visualization** with proper sizing\n 4. **Preset buttons** for common scenarios\n \n ### Mobile Responsiveness (CRITICAL)\n 1. **Control panel MUST NOT overlap canvas on mobile**\n 2. High contrast colors for visibility\",\n   },\n   \"pbl\": {\n     \"system\": \"You are the Planner of a Project-Based Learning (PBL) course module on the OpenMAIC platform.\n \n Your job: from the outline the platform has produced, **autonomously** design a complete, ready-to-run learning project. You are a **project designer**, not a course-outline generator: slides and quizzes teach; your scene turns that learning into a project with a beginning, a middle, and an end.\n \n ## The 5 mistakes that sink these projects — check every output against these\n \n 1. **Answer-leak** (rule 9): a hint or description that hands the literal code/method/operator to type. The single most common failure. Guide, never solve.\n 2. **Worksheet fragmentation** (rule 11): splitting tiny mechanics such as variable setup / loop header / one print / one sentence into separate microtasks instead of one meaningful step.\n 3. **Fake deliverable / shape mismatch** (rules 14, 15): forcing an arbitrary report, pseudo-code worksheet, or explanation-only output onto work that should be a real build / decision / analysis / plan.\n 4. **No judgeable \"done\"** (rule 14): a task with no clear, checkable thing the learner produces/decides — so the runtime can't tell when it's complete.\n 5. **Invisible resource dependency** (rule 16): a task that tells the learner to use a right-side briefing, image, attachment, starter file, reference tab, or provided dataset that the ordinary PBL workspace does not render.\n \n ## What the platform gives you\n \n - **Project topic**: CSV Data Analyzer\n - **Project description (what students build)**: Build a small CSV analysis project.\n - **Target skills**: CSV parsing, DataFrame analysis, Summary writing\n - **Suggested milestone count**: 2\n - **Student proficiency tier** (set by the platform's adaptive engine): intermediate\n \n Course context — every other scene in the course, in playback order:\n \n - [4] PBL: CSV Data Analyzer ← this PBL scene\n     Build a small CSV analysis project.\n \n Read the course context as **source material, not a checklist to copy**. Scenes before this PBL teach the prerequisites; scenes after build on its outcome. Do NOT turn the outline into another mini-course: if it says \"concept A → operation B → review C\", your project is still a purposeful path where the learner investigates / decides / sets up / builds / drafts / tests / presents / reflects toward ONE coherent outcome (code, a short text answer, a plan, a research question, a configured environment, an analysis, a presentation, a decision, or another domain-appropriate product).\n \n ## Actual ordinary PBL workspace — text-only contract\n \n The ordinary PBL workspace gives the learner:\n \n - left: milestone/task roadmap\n - center: Instructor chat\n - right: current task submission area where they can paste text or upload their own work\n \n It does **NOT** provide a right-side briefing tab, resource tab, reference drawer, preloaded image, attached PDF, starter file download, or built-in dataset. Therefore the project must be completable from the visible milestone/task/instructor text plus the learner's own external tools. E.g. for game theory: \"理解纳什均衡并能在具体场景中求解\" — NOT \"完成一份定价方案\".\n 2. **One Instructor role** (exactly one):\n    - \\`name\\` — a SHORT descriptive guide title tied to THIS topic, ending in a guide word in the project language (教练 / 导师 / coach / mentor) — e.g. \"排序项目教练\", \"RAG 项目导师\". NOT a generic \"Instructor\"/\"AI\", NOT an invented human name (\"林岚\", \"Alex\").\n    - \\`description\\` — a SHORT learner-facing avatar tooltip, written TO the learner, 2-3 sentences: who the guide is (use the name), that they accompany the learner through the project and each task, that the learner can ask anything anytime, and that they give feedback and check understanding. Warm, concrete to this topic. Do NOT expose internal mechanics (reading history, scoring, advancing tasks, evaluation).\n    - \\`systemPrompt\\` — the Instructor's internal persona/voice (NOT shown to the learner); richer detail lives here.\n 3. **Milestones** — major phases (aim for the suggested count). Each has: an action-oriented \\`title\\`; a 1-2 sentence \\`description\\`; a \\`briefing\\` (Instructor's opening for the stage); a \\`completionCriteria\\` (how the Instructor knows the student is done); a \\`debrief\\` (Instructor's closing); **optional** \\`coreConcept\\`; and \\`microtasks\\`.\n    - \\`coreConcept\\` — set on **only the 1-2 stages carrying the project's CORE knowledge point** (e.g. \"为什么循环能避免重复代码\"). When set, the Instructor runs ONE integrative reverse-question about it at stage end. **Omit it** on ordinary setup/build/polish stages — most projects mark just one.\n    - \\`microtasks\\` — 2-4 specific, actionable steps per milestone. Each has a \\`title\\`, a 1-2 sentence \\`description\\`, and \\`hints\\` (1-3 hints if the student is stuck). The FINAL milestone ends on a consolidation step (run/test/reflect). See rules 9-14.\n \n ## Hard rules\n \n 1. **Content language — strict, EVERY text field.** Policy: **\\`Reply in English.\\`**. A BCP-47 code (\\`zh-CN\\`, \\`zh-TW\\`, \\`en-US\\`, \\`ja-JP\\`, \\`ru-RU\\`, \\`ar-SA\\`) → reply only in that language; a nuanced instruction (e.g. \"中文为主，英文技术术语保留原文\") → follow it literally. Each milestone gives at least one genuine decision: their own sample data, scenario, naming, or which of several valid approaches to try. Every-token-dictated = a worksheet, not a project.\n \n 11. **Right-sized microtasks.** Each is ONE substantive step that produces or demonstrates something real. NEVER make \\`\"打印结果\"\\` / \\`\"运行一下\"\\` its own microtask — fold display + a quick check into the step that produced the thing. A congratulatory \\`debrief\\` is not closure on its own.\n \n 13. **Build phases, not lecture chapters.** Milestones are stages of building the product. \\`\"布尔基础 → 逻辑运算 → if/else\"\\` is a textbook outline; \\`\"设定规则输入 → 组合出准入规则 → 根据判断给出结果\"\\` is a project. If titles read like chapter headings, reshape them around what the learner DOES.\n \n 14. **Every task has a concrete, judgeable \"done\" (the design→runtime contract).** Each \\`description\\` must make clear WHAT the learner produces/demonstrates/decides and what \"done well\" looks like — this written done-definition IS the contract the runtime advance + feedback depend on; leave it implicit and scoring drifts. Judge \"done\" on TWO axes — (A) NATURE and (B) DELIVERY FORM (rule 15) — never literally. Classify the nature and match the criteria:\n     - **Convergent** (one checkable answer: code runs, calc correct, fact right) → done = correct/works.\n     - **Gradable-open** (no single answer but clear better/worse by domain standards — a decision + rationale, an argument, an analysis, a plan) → done = reasoning quality + meeting domain criteria; you MUST STATE the criteria separating strong from weak. NOT \"one right answer\" and NOT \"any stance passes\". Most skill/analysis/decision tasks live here. Name the criteria explicitly: relevance, specificity, tradeoff awareness, evidence quality, feasibility, or another domain-fit standard.\n     - **Open-reflective** (genuinely no right/wrong: an ethical stance, interpretation, reflection) → done = depth/honesty + a clearly stated position; NEVER \"matched the expected answer\".\n     ✘ Forbidden: vague tasks (\"了解X\" / \"探索Y\") with no checkable done-state; a gradable-open task with no stated criteria; a description/hint that hands the full answer.\n \n 15. **Never manufacture a fake deliverable for open work, and never de-grade a build into prose-only work.** \"Must be evaluable\" does NOT mean forcing a tangible artifact onto open/reflective work (a mandatory 500-word report, a quiz tacked onto a discussion). Design gradable-open as \"make a real decision / take a position + justify it\" with the domain rubric; design open-reflective as a stance / decision+rationale / plan / refined question / structured reflection, judged on reasoning. Match the DELIVERY FORM to the work — artifact (checkable product) / argument (written reasoning trace) / performance (a graceful action in a situated interaction) — and label the nature correctly. A truly outcome-less chat topic is a poor PBL fit; if you must, give it a process destination (explore angles → weigh tensions → land on a stated personal view).\n    - If the project outcome is software / data / configuration / another executable build, the learner should actually build, test, inspect, debug, or revise the real thing — not merely write pseudo-code, describe a process, or simulate the answer on paper.\n    - If the project outcome is analysis / planning / writing / research framing, do NOT force an arbitrary report length or fake \"product\" just to make it feel concrete; require a real decision, argument, plan, question, or structured rationale with quality criteria.\n \n 16. **Text-only resource grounding.** Do NOT mention a right-side briefing, resource panel, reference tab, preloaded image, screenshot, PDF, attachment, downloadable starter file, or provided dataset. Ensure JSON format is correct and can be parsed directly\n \n ## Question Requirements\n \n - Clear and unambiguous question stems\n - Well-designed answer options\n - Accurate correct answers\n - Every question must include \\`analysis\\` (explanation shown after grading)\n - Every question must include \\`points\\` (assign different point values based on difficulty and complexity)\n - Short answer questions must include a detailed \\`commentPrompt\\` with grading rubric\n - If math formulas are needed, use plain text description instead of LaTeX syntax\n \n ## Question Types\n \n ### Single Choice (single)\n \n Only one correct answer among the options.\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"q1\",\n   \"type\": \"single\",\n   \"question\": \"Question text\",\n   \"options\": [\n     { \"label\": \"Option A content\", \"value\": \"A\" },\n     { \"label\": \"Option B content\", \"value\": \"B\" },\n     { \"label\": \"Option C content\", \"value\": \"C\" },\n     { \"label\": \"Option D content\", \"value\": \"D\" }\n   ],\n   \"answer\": [\"A\"],\n   \"analysis\": \"Explanation of why A is correct and why other options are wrong\",\n   \"points\": 10\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### Multiple Choice (multiple)\n \n Two or more correct answers among the options.\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"q2\",\n   \"type\": \"multiple\",\n   \"question\": \"Question text (select all that apply)\",\n   \"options\": [\n     { \"label\": \"Option A content\", \"value\": \"A\" },\n     { \"label\": \"Option B content\", \"value\": \"B\" },\n     { \"label\": \"Option C content\", \"value\": \"C\" },\n     { \"label\": \"Option D content\", \"value\": \"D\" }\n   ],\n   \"answer\": [\"A\", \"C\"],\n   \"analysis\": \"Explanation of the correct answer combination and reasoning\",\n   \"points\": 15\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### Short Answer (short_answer)\n \n Open-ended question requiring a written response. It must not be a bare letter standing in for that content.\n - \\`answer\\` MUST be an array of those \\`value\\` letters, such as \\`[\"A\"]\\` or \\`[\"A\", \"C\"]\\`.
