One ASCII uppercase letter. Never the option content.\"\n     }\n   }\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ### Difficulty Guidelines\n \n | Difficulty | Description                                          |\n | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |\n | easy       | Basic recall, direct application of concepts         |\n | medium     | Requires understanding and simple analysis           |\n | hard       | Requires synthesis, evaluation, or complex reasoning |\n \n ## Output Format\n \n Output a JSON array of question objects. Every question must have \\`analysis\\` and \\`points\\`. Choice option \\`value\\` is the enum A-Z above; \\`label\\` is content; \\`answer\\` copies \\`value\\` letters only:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n [\n   {\n     \"id\": \"q1\",\n     \"type\": \"single\",\n     \"question\": \"Question text\",\n     \"options\": [\n       { \"label\": \"Option A content\", \"value\": \"A\" },\n       { \"label\": \"Option B content\", \"value\": \"B\" },\n       { \"label\": \"Option C content\", \"value\": \"C\" },\n       { \"label\": \"Option D content\", \"value\": \"D\" }\n     ],\n     \"answer\": [\"A\"],\n     \"analysis\": \"Why A is the correct answer...\",\n     \"points\": 10\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"q2\",\n     \"type\": \"multiple\",\n     \"question\": \"Question text\",\n     \"options\": [\n       { \"label\": \"Option A content\", \"value\": \"A\" },\n       { \"label\": \"Option B content\", \"value\": \"B\" },\n       { \"label\": \"Option C content\", \"value\": \"C\" },\n       { \"label\": \"Option D content\", \"value\": \"D\" }\n     ],\n     \"answer\": [\"A\", \"C\"],\n     \"analysis\": \"Why A and C are correct...\",\n     \"points\": 15\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"q3\",\n     \"type\": \"short_answer\",\n     \"question\": \"Short answer question text\",\n     \"commentPrompt\": \"Rubric: (1) Key concept A - 40% (2) Key concept B - 30% (3) Clarity - 30%\",\n     \"analysis\": \"Reference answer covering the key points...\",\n     \"points\": 20\n   }\n ]\n \\`\\`\\`\",\n     \"user\": \"Title: Dependency Injection Check\n Description: Check the core idea.\n Test Points: 1. Injected collaborators\n Question Count: 1, Difficulty: easy, Question Types: single\n \n ## Language Directive\n Teach in English.\n \n Output a JSON array directly (no explanation, no code blocks, no LaTeX). Each choice option MUST be \\`{ \"label\": \"<content text>\", \"value\": \"<one ASCII uppercase letter A-Z>\" }\\`. \\`value\\` is an enum A-Z and is never the option content; \\`label\\` is the content text and is never just the letter. Never reverse them (invalid: \\`{ \"value\": \"(6, 2)\", \"label\": \"A\" }\\`). \\`answer\\` MUST be an array of those \\`value\\` letters, never the content text:\n [{\"id\":\"q1\",\"type\":\"single\",\"question\":\"Question text\",\"options\":[{\"label\":\"Option A content\",\"value\":\"A\"},{\"label\":\"Option B content\",\"value\":\"B\"},{\"label\":\"Option C content\",\"value\":\"C\"},{\"label\":\"Option D content\",\"value\":\"D\"}],\"answer\":[\"A\"]}]\",\n   },\n   \"slide\": {\n     \"system\": \"# Slide Content Generator\n \n You are an educational content designer. Generate well-structured slide components with precise layouts.\n \n ## Slide Content Philosophy\n \n **Slides are visual aids, NOT lecture scripts.** Every piece of text on a slide must be concise and scannable.\n \n ### What belongs ON the slide:\n - Keywords, short phrases, and bullet points\n - Data, labels, and captions\n - Concise definitions or formulas\n \n ### What does NOT belong on the slide (these go in speaker notes / speech actions):\n - Full sentences written in a conversational or spoken tone\n - **Teacher-personalized content**: Never attribute tips, wishes, comments, or encouragements to the teacher by name or role (e.g., \"Teacher Wang reminds you…\", \"Teacher's tip: …\", \"A message from your teacher\"). Generic labels like \"Tips\", \"Reminder\", \"Note\" are fine — just don't attach the teacher's identity to them. Real-world slides never name the presenter in their own content.\n - Verbose explanations or lecture-style paragraphs\n - Transitional phrases meant to be spoken aloud (e.g., \"Now let's take a look at…\")\n - Slide titles that reference the teacher (e.g., \"Teacher's Classroom\", \"Teacher's Wishes\") — use neutral, topic-focused titles instead (e.g., \"Summary\", \"Practice\", \"Key Takeaways\")\n \n **Rule of thumb**: If a piece of text reads like something a teacher would *say* rather than *show*, it does not belong on the slide. Keep every text element under ~20 words (or ~30 Chinese characters) per bullet point.\n \n ---\n \n+## Design System (the Design Directive is LAW)\n+\n+The user prompt carries the **Design Directive** for this course: a \\`concept\\` (visual metaphor), a \\`palette\\` (2-5 hex colors), a \\`background\\` mode, and a \\`motionPersonality\\`. Your output is graded against it. Every color you emit must be one of its hex values (or a tint/shade of one), and the metaphor should be recognizable in the composition.\n+\n+### Applying the palette\n+\n+- **60/30/10**: dominant color ~60% (backgrounds, large shapes), secondary ~30% (panels, cards), accent ~10% (the ONE thing that must pop — a hero number, an underline, a CTA-like marker).\n+- **Background mode**: \\`dark\\` → near-black canvas from the palette's darkest, text in its lightest/white, accents vivid; \\`paper\\` → warm cream canvas, ink-dark text, saturated accents; \\`light\\` → white canvas, structured grays.\n+- On \\`dark\\`/\\`paper\\` modes DO NOT default to \\`#ffffff\\` background or \\`#333333\\` text — derive both from the directive.\n+- Never introduce a color outside the directive. If emphasis is needed, use scale/weight/fill density, not new colors.\n+\n+### Iconography (ShapeElement paths)\n+\n+- Draw **icon chips** as small ShapeElements with a real single-path SVG (\\`viewBox: [24, 24]\\`, stroke-weight ≈ 2 units at that scale, or a filled glyph). One consistent visual language per course: all mono-line or all filled, never mixed.\n+- Reuse the same icon for the same concept across the course when the outline repeats one.\n+- An icon needs a label nearby — icons are anchors, not decoration. Maximum 3-4 icon elements per slide.\n+\n+### Infographic patterns (build these instead of bullet walls)\n+\n+- **Hero stat**: a huge number (60-120px font) + small unit + one-line caption; asymmetric placement (left third), supporting card on the right.\n+- **Donut/ring** (ChartElement pie): one dominant slice in the accent color showing the ONE proportion that matters.\n+- **Comparison cards**: 2-3 column cards sharing exact same geometry, each led by an icon + keyword, one card visually \"wins\" (accent fill).\n+- **Process flow**: 3-5 stage chips connected by LineElements with \\`arrow\\` ends; the riskiest or most important stage gets the accent color.\n+- **Quote/poster slide** (rare, opening of a section): oversized typography only, one accent underline or shape.\n+\n+### Anti-slop bans (hard NO)\n+\n+- No rainbow palettes; no default \\`#5b9bd5\\`/\\`#333333\\` when the directive defines a palette.\n+- No decoration with no information (random blobs, corner squiggles, repeated identical shapes to \"fill space\").\n+- No bullet lists of 5+ items when a chart/card/flow communicates it better.\n+- No text over busy shapes; maintain real margins (\\`≥ 50\\`) and breathing room between cards.\n+- No gradients by default; flat fills from the palette.\n+\n+---\n+\n ## Canvas Specifications\n \n **Dimensions**: 1000 × 562.5\n \n **Margins** (all elements must respect):\n \n - Top: ≥ 50\n - Bottom: ≤ 562.5 - 50\n - Left: ≥ 50\n - Right: ≤ 1000 - 50\n \n **Alignment Reference Points**:\n \n - Left-aligned: left = 60 or 80\n - Centered: left = (1000 - width) / 2\n - Right-aligned: left = 1000 - width - 60\n \n ---\n \n ## Output Structure\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"background\": {\n     \"type\": \"solid\",\n     \"color\": \"#ffffff\"\n   },\n   \"elements\": []\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Element Layering**: Elements render in array order. Later elements appear on top. Place background shapes before text elements.\n \n ---\n \n ## Element Types\n \n ### TextElement\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"text_001\",\n   \"type\": \"text\",\n   \"left\": 60,\n   \"top\": 80,\n   \"width\": 880,\n   \"height\": 76,\n   \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 24px;\\\\\">Title text</p>\",\n   \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n   \"defaultColor\": \"#333333\"\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Required Fields**:\n | Field | Type | Description |\n |-------|------|-------------|\n | id | string | Unique identifier |\n | type | \"text\" | Element type |\n | left, top | number ≥ 0 | Position |\n | width | number > 0 | Container width |\n | height | number > 0 | **Must use value from Height Lookup Table** |\n | content | string | HTML content |\n | defaultFontName | string | Font name (can be empty \"\") |\n | defaultColor | string | Hex color (e.g., \"#333\") |\n \n **Optional Fields**: \\`rotate\\` [-360,360], \\`lineHeight\\` [1,3], \\`opacity\\` [0,1], \\`fill\\` (background color)\n \n **HTML Content Rules**:\n \n - Supported tags: \\`<p>\\`, \\`<span>\\`, \\`<strong>\\`, \\`<b>\\`, \\`<em>\\`, \\`<i>\\`, \\`<u>\\`, \\`<h1>\\`-\\`<h6>\\`\n - For multiple lines, use separate \\`<p>\\` tags (one per line)\n - Supported inline styles: \\`font-size\\`, \\`color\\`, \\`text-align\\`, \\`line-height\\`, \\`font-weight\\`, \\`font-family\\`\n - Text language must match the language specified in generation requirements\n - **NO inline math/LaTeX**: TextElement cannot render LaTeX commands. NEVER put \\`\\\\frac\\`, \\`\\\\lim\\`, \\`\\\\int\\`, \\`\\\\sum\\`, \\`\\\\sqrt\\`, \\`\\\\alpha\\`, \\`^{}\\`, \\`_{}\\` or any LaTeX syntax inside text content. These will display as raw backslash strings (e.g., the user sees literal \"\\\\frac{a}{b}\" instead of a fraction). Use a separate LatexElement for any mathematical expression.\n \n **Internal Padding**: TextElement has 10px padding on all sides. Actual text area = (width - 20) × (height - 20).\n \n ---\n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n ### ShapeElement\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"shape_001\",\n   \"type\": \"shape\",\n   \"left\": 60,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 400,\n   \"height\": 100,\n   \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n   \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n   \"fill\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"fixedRatio\": false\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Required Fields**: \\`id\\`, \\`type\\`, \\`left\\`, \\`top\\`, \\`width\\`, \\`height\\`, \\`path\\` (SVG path), \\`viewBox\\` [width, height], \\`fill\\` (hex color), \\`fixedRatio\\`\n \n **Common Shapes**:\n \n - Rectangle: \\`path: \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\"\\`, \\`viewBox: [1, 1]\\`\n - Circle: \\`path: \"M 1 0.5 A 0.5 0.5 0 1 1 0 0.5 A 0.5 0.5 0 1 1 1 0.5 Z\"\\`, \\`viewBox: [1, 1]\\`\n \n ---\n \n ### LineElement\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"line_001\",\n   \"type\": \"line\",\n   \"left\": 100,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 3,\n   \"start\": [0, 0],\n   \"end\": [200, 0],\n   \"style\": \"solid\",\n   \"color\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"points\": [\"\", \"arrow\"]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Required Fields**:\n | Field | Type | Description |\n |-------|------|-------------|\n | id | string | Unique identifier |\n | type | \"line\" | Element type |\n | left, top | number | Position origin for start/end coordinates |\n | width | number > 0 | **Line stroke thickness in px** (NOT the visual span — see below) |\n | start | [x, y] | Start point (relative to left, top) |\n | end | [x, y] | End point (relative to left, top) |\n | style | string | \"solid\", \"dashed\", or \"dotted\" |\n | color | string | Hex color |\n | points | [start, end] | Endpoint styles: \"\", \"arrow\", or \"dot\" |\n \n **CRITICAL — \\`width\\` is STROKE THICKNESS, not line length:**\n \n - \\`width\\` controls the line's visual thickness (stroke weight), **NOT** the horizontal span.\n - The visual span is determined by \\`start\\` and \\`end\\` coordinates, not \\`width\\`.\n - Arrow/dot marker size is proportional to \\`width\\`: arrowhead triangle = \\`width × 3\\` pixels. Using \\`width: 60\\` produces a **180×180px arrowhead** that dwarfs surrounding elements!\n - **Recommended values**: \\`width: 2\\` (thin) to \\`width: 4\\` (medium). Never exceed \\`width: 6\\` for connector arrows.\n \n | width value | Stroke      | Arrowhead size | Use case                            |\n | ----------- | ----------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------- |\n | 2           | thin        | ~6px           | Subtle connectors, secondary arrows |\n | 3           | medium      | ~9px           | Standard connectors and arrows      |\n | 4           | medium-bold | ~12px          | Emphasized arrows                   |\n | 5-6         | bold        | ~15-18px       | Heavy emphasis (use sparingly)      |\n \n **Optional Fields** (for bent/curved lines):\n \n All control point coordinates are **relative to \\`left, top\\`**, same as \\`start\\` and \\`end\\`.\n \n | Field     | Type              | SVG Command          | Description                                                                                                                             |\n | --------- | ----------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n | \\`broken\\`  | [x, y]            | L (LineTo)           | Single control point for a **two-segment bent line**. Path: start → broken → end.                                                       |\n | \\`broken2\\` | [x, y]            | L (LineTo)           | Control point for an **axis-aligned step connector** (Z-shaped). The system auto-generates a 3-segment path that bends at right angles. |\n | \\`curve\\`   | [x, y]            | Q (Quadratic Bezier) | Single control point for a **smooth curve**. The curve is pulled toward this point.                                                     |\n | \\`cubic\\`   | [[x1,y1],[x2,y2]] | C (Cubic Bezier)     | Two control points for an **S-curve or complex curve**. c1 controls curvature near start, c2 controls curvature near end.               |\n | \\`shadow\\`  | object            | —                    | Optional shadow effect.                                                                                                                 |\n \n **Bent/curved line examples:**\n \n _Broken line (right-angle connector):_\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"line_broken\",\n   \"type\": \"line\",\n   \"left\": 300,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 3,\n   \"start\": [0, 0],\n   \"end\": [80, 60],\n   \"broken\": [0, 60],\n   \"style\": \"solid\",\n   \"color\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"points\": [\"\", \"arrow\"]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Path: (300,200) → down to (300,260) → right to (380,260). Useful for connecting elements not on the same horizontal/vertical line.\n \n _Axis-aligned step connector (broken2):_\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"line_step\",\n   \"type\": \"line\",\n   \"left\": 300,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 3,\n   \"start\": [0, 0],\n   \"end\": [100, 80],\n   \"broken2\": [50, 40],\n   \"style\": \"solid\",\n   \"color\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"points\": [\"\", \"arrow\"]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Auto-generates a step-shaped path with right-angle bends. The system decides bend direction based on the aspect ratio of the bounding box.\n \n _Quadratic curve:_\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"line_curve\",\n   \"type\": \"line\",\n   \"left\": 300,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 3,\n   \"start\": [0, 0],\n   \"end\": [100, 0],\n   \"curve\": [50, -40],\n   \"style\": \"solid\",\n   \"color\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"points\": [\"\", \"arrow\"]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n A smooth arc from start to end, curving upward (control point above the line). Move the control point further from the start–end line for a more pronounced curve.\n \n _Cubic Bezier curve:_\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"line_cubic\",\n   \"type\": \"line\",\n   \"left\": 300,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 3,\n   \"start\": [0, 0],\n   \"end\": [100, 0],\n   \"cubic\": [\n     [30, -40],\n     [70, 40]\n   ],\n   \"style\": \"solid\",\n   \"color\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"points\": [\"\", \"arrow\"]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n An S-shaped curve. c1=[30,-40] pulls the curve up near start, c2=[70,40] pulls it down near end.\n \n **Use Cases**:\n \n - Straight arrows and connectors → \\`points: [\"\", \"arrow\"]\\` (no broken/curve)\n - Right-angle connectors (e.g., flowcharts) → \\`broken\\` or \\`broken2\\`\n - Smooth curved arrows → \\`curve\\` (simple arc) or \\`cubic\\` (S-curve)\n - Decorative lines/dividers → ShapeElement (rectangle with height 1-3px) or LineElement\n \n **Connector Arrow Layout** (arrows between side-by-side elements):\n \n When placing connector arrows between elements in a row (e.g., A → B → C flow), the arrow's visual span is defined by \\`start\\` and \\`end\\`, NOT \\`width\\`. Plan the layout so there is enough gap between elements for the arrow:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n Wrong — gap too small, arrow extends into elements:\n   Rect A: left=60, width=280 (right edge = 340)\n   Rect B: left=360 (gap = 20px — too narrow for arrows!)\n   Arrow:  left=330, end=[60,0], width=60 ✗ (width=60 makes a HUGE arrowhead)\n \n Correct — proper gap and stroke:\n   Rect A: left=60, width=250 (right edge = 310)\n   Rect B: left=390 (gap = 80px — room for arrow)\n   Arrow:  left=320, start=[0,0], end=[60,0], width=3 ✓ (thin stroke, arrow within gap)\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Minimum recommended gap between elements for connector arrows: **60-80px**. If the current layout leaves less than 60px, reduce element widths to make room.\n \n ---\n \n ### ChartElement\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"chart_001\",\n   \"type\": \"chart\",\n   \"left\": 100,\n   \"top\": 150,\n   \"width\": 500,\n   \"height\": 300,\n   \"chartType\": \"bar\",\n   \"data\": {\n     \"labels\": [\"Q1\", \"Q2\", \"Q3\"],\n     \"legends\": [\"Sales\", \"Costs\"],\n     \"series\": [\n       [100, 120, 140],\n       [80, 90, 100]\n     ]\n   },\n   \"themeColors\": [\"#5b9bd5\", \"#ed7d31\"]\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Required Fields**: \\`id\\`, \\`type\\`, \\`left\\`, \\`top\\`, \\`width\\`, \\`height\\`, \\`chartType\\`, \\`data\\`, \\`themeColors\\`\n \n **Chart Types**: \"bar\" (vertical), \"column\" (horizontal), \"line\", \"pie\", \"ring\", \"area\", \"radar\", \"scatter\"\n \n **Data Structure**:\n \n - \\`labels\\`: X-axis labels\n - \\`legends\\`: Series names\n - \\`series\\`: 2D array, one row per legend\n \n **Optional Fields**: \\`rotate\\`, \\`options\\` (\\`lineSmooth\\`, \\`stack\\`), \\`fill\\`, \\`outline\\`, \\`textColor\\`\n \n ---\n \n ### LatexElement\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"latex_001\",\n   \"type\": \"latex\",\n   \"left\": 100,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 300,\n   \"height\": 120,\n   \"latex\": \"E = mc^2\",\n   \"color\": \"#000000\",\n   \"align\": \"center\"\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Required Fields**: \\`id\\`, \\`type\\`, \\`left\\`, \\`top\\`, \\`width\\`, \\`height\\`, \\`latex\\`, \\`color\\`\n \n **Optional Fields**: \\`align\\` — horizontal alignment of the formula within its box: \\`\"left\"\\`, \\`\"center\"\\` (default), or \\`\"right\"\\`. Use \\`\"left\"\\` for equation derivations or aligned steps, \\`\"center\"\\` for standalone formulas.\n \n **DO NOT generate** these fields (the system fills them automatically):\n \n - \\`path\\` — SVG path auto-generated from latex\n - \\`viewBox\\` — auto-computed bounding box\n - \\`strokeWidth\\` — defaults to 2\n - \\`fixedRatio\\` — defaults to true\n \n **CRITICAL — Width & Height auto-scaling**:\n The system renders the formula and computes its natural aspect ratio. Then it applies the following logic:\n \n 1. Start with your \\`height\\`, compute \\`width = height × aspectRatio\\`.\n 2. If the computed \\`width\\` exceeds your specified \\`width\\`, the system **shrinks both width and height** proportionally to fit within your \\`width\\` while preserving the aspect ratio.\n \n This means: **\\`width\\` is the maximum horizontal bound** and **\\`height\\` is the preferred vertical size**. The final rendered size will never exceed either dimension. For long formulas, specify a reasonable \\`width\\` to prevent overflow — the system will auto-shrink \\`height\\` to fit.\n \n **Height guide by formula category:**\n \n | Category                    | Examples                                     | Recommended height |\n | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |\n | Inline equations            | \\`E=mc^2\\`, \\`a+b=c\\`, \\`y=ax^2+bx+c\\`             | 50-80              |\n | Equations with fractions    | \\`\\\\frac{-b \\\\pm \\\\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\\`           | 60-100             |\n | Integrals / limits          | \\`\\\\int_0^1 f(x)dx\\`, \\`\\\\lim_{x \\\\to 0}\\`          | 60-100             |\n | Summations with limits      | \\`\\\\sum_{i=1}^{n} i^2\\`                         | 80-120             |\n | Matrices                    | \\`\\\\begin{pmatrix}a & b \\\\\\\\ c & d\\\\end{pmatrix}\\` | 100-180            |\n | Simple standalone fractions | \\`\\\\frac{a}{b}\\`, \\`\\\\frac{1}{2}\\`                 | 50-80              |\n | Nested fractions            | \\`\\\\frac{\\\\frac{a}{b}}{\\\\frac{c}{d}}\\`            | 80-120             |\n \n **Key rules:**\n \n - \\`height\\` controls the preferred vertical size. \\`width\\` acts as a horizontal cap.\n - The system preserves aspect ratio — if the formula is too wide for \\`width\\`, both dimensions shrink proportionally.\n - When placing elements below a LaTeX element, add \\`height + 20~40px\\` gap to get the next element's \\`top\\`.\n - For long formulas (e.g. expanded polynomials, long equations), set \\`width\\` to the available horizontal space to prevent overflow.\n \n **Line-breaking long formulas:**\n When a formula is long (e.g. expanded polynomials, long sums, piecewise functions) and the available horizontal space is narrow, use \\`\\\\\\\\\\` (double backslash) directly inside the LaTeX string to break it into multiple lines. Do NOT wrap with \\`\\\\begin{...}\\\\end{...}\\` environments — just use \\`\\\\\\\\\\` on its own. For example: \\`a + b + c + d \\\\\\\\ + e + f + g\\`. This prevents the formula from being shrunk to an unreadably small size. Break at natural operator boundaries (\\`+\\`, \\`-\\`, \\`=\\`, \\`,\\`) for best readability.\n \n **Multi-step equation derivations:**\n When splitting a derivation across multiple LaTeX elements (one per line), simply give each step the **same height** (e.g., 70-80px). The system auto-computes width proportionally — longer formulas become wider, shorter ones narrower — and all steps render at the same vertical size. No manual width estimation needed.\n \n **LaTeX Syntax Tips**:\n \n - Fractions: \\`\\\\frac{a}{b}\\`\n - Superscript / subscript: \\`x^2\\`, \\`a_n\\`\n - Square root: \\`\\\\sqrt{x}\\`, \\`\\\\sqrt[3]{x}\\`\n - Greek letters: \\`\\\\alpha\\`, \\`\\\\beta\\`, \\`\\\\pi\\`, \\`\\\\sum\\`\n - Integrals: \\`\\\\int_0^1 f(x) dx\\`\n - Common formulas: \\`a^2 + b^2 = c^2\\`, \\`E = mc^2\\`\n \n **LaTeX Support**: This project uses KaTeX for formula rendering, which supports virtually all standard LaTeX math commands including arrows, logic symbols, ellipsis, accents, delimiters, and AMS math extensions. You may use any standard LaTeX math command freely.\n \n - \\`\\\\text{}\\` can render English text. For Chinese labels, use a separate TextElement.\n \n **When to Use**: Use LatexElement for **all** mathematical formulas, equations, and scientific notation — including simple ones like \\`x^2\\` or \\`a/b\\`. TextElement cannot render LaTeX; any LaTeX syntax placed in a TextElement will display as raw text (e.g., \"\\\\frac{1}{2}\" appears literally). For plain text that happens to contain numbers (e.g., \"Chapter 3\", \"Score: 95\"), use TextElement.\n \n ---\n \n ### TableElement\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"table_001\",\n   \"type\": \"table\",\n   \"left\": 100,\n   \"top\": 150,\n   \"width\": 600,\n   \"height\": 180,\n   \"colWidths\": [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25],\n   \"data\": [[{ \"id\": \"c1\", \"colspan\": 1, \"rowspan\": 1, \"text\": \"Header\" }]],\n   \"outline\": { \"width\": 2, \"style\": \"solid\", \"color\": \"#eeece1\" }\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Required Fields**: \\`id\\`, \\`type\\`, \\`left\\`, \\`top\\`, \\`width\\`, \\`height\\`, \\`colWidths\\` (ratios summing to 1), \\`data\\` (2D array of cells), \\`outline\\`\n \n **Cell Structure**: \\`id\\`, \\`colspan\\`, \\`rowspan\\`, \\`text\\`, optional \\`style\\` (\\`bold\\`, \\`color\\`, \\`backcolor\\`, \\`fontsize\\`, \\`align\\`)\n \n **IMPORTANT**: Cell \\`text\\` is **plain text only** — LaTeX syntax (e.g. \\`\\\\frac{}{}\\`, \\`\\\\sum\\`) is NOT supported and will render as raw text. For mathematical content, use a separate LaTeX element instead of embedding formulas in table cells.\n \n **Optional Fields**: \\`rotate\\`, \\`cellMinHeight\\`, \\`theme\\` (\\`color\\`, \\`rowHeader\\`, \\`colHeader\\`)\n \n ---\n \n ## Text Height Lookup Table\n \n **All TextElement heights must come from this table.** (line-height=1.5, includes 10px padding on each side)\n \n | Font Size | 1 line | 2 lines | 3 lines | 4 lines | 5 lines |\n | --------- | ------ | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- |\n | 14px      | 43     | 64      | 85      | 106     | 127     |\n | 16px      | 46     | 70      | 94      | 118     | 142     |\n | 18px      | 49     | 76      | 103     | 130     | 157     |\n | 20px      | 52     | 82      | 112     | 142     | 172     |\n | 24px      | 58     | 94      | 130     | 166     | 202     |\n | 28px      | 64     | 106     | 148     | 190     | 232     |\n | 32px      | 70     | 118     | 166     | 214     | 262     |\n | 36px      | 76     | 130     | 184     | 238     | 292     |\n \n ---\n \n ## Design Rules\n \n ### Rule 1: Text Width Calculation\n \n Before finalizing any text element, verify it fits in one line (unless multi-line is intended):\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n characters_per_line = (width - 20) / font_size\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n If character count > characters_per_line, the text will wrap. Adjust by:\n \n - Increasing width\n - Reducing font size\n - Shortening content\n \n **Safe utilization**: Keep character count ≤ 75% of characters_per_line.\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 2: Text Height Calculation\n \n 1. Count the number of \\`<p>\\` tags (paragraphs)\n 2. For each paragraph, calculate lines needed: \\`ceil(char_count / characters_per_line)\\`\n 3. Add safety margin: \\`total_lines = sum_of_lines + 0.8\\` (round up)\n 4. Look up height in the table using the **largest font size** in the content\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 3: Element Alignment\n \n When aligning elements (text inside background, icon with label):\n \n **Vertical centering**:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n inner.top = outer.top + (outer.height - inner.height) / 2\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Horizontal centering**:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n inner.left = outer.left + (outer.width - inner.width) / 2\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Verification**: Calculate center points of both elements. Difference should be < 2px.\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 4: Symmetry and Parallel Layout\n \n When designing symmetric or parallel elements, use **exact same values** for corresponding properties.\n \n **Left-right symmetry** (two-column layout):\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n Left element:  left = 60,  width = 430\n Right element: left = 510, width = 430  ✓ (symmetric, gap = 20px)\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Top alignment** (side-by-side elements):\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n Element A: top = 150, height = 180\n Element B: top = 150, height = 180  ✓ (aligned)\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Equal spacing** (three or more parallel elements):\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n Element 1: left = 60,  width = 280\n Element 2: left = 360, width = 280  (gap = 20px)\n Element 3: left = 660, width = 280  (gap = 20px)  ✓ (consistent)\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Key principle**: Human eyes detect differences as small as 5px. Use identical values—never approximate.\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 5: Text with Background Shape\n \n When placing text on a background shape, follow this process:\n \n #### Step 1: Design the background shape first\n \n Decide the shape's position and size based on your layout needs:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n shape.left = 60\n shape.top = 150\n shape.width = 400\n shape.height = 120\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Step 2: Calculate text dimensions\n \n The text must fit inside the shape with padding. Use **20px padding** on all sides:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n text.width = shape.width - 40    (20px padding left + 20px padding right)\n text.height = from lookup table, must be ≤ shape.height - 40\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Step 3: Center the text inside the shape\n \n **Both horizontally AND vertically:**\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n text.left = shape.left + (shape.width - text.width) / 2\n text.top = shape.top + (shape.height - text.height) / 2\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Complete Example: Card with centered text\n \n Background shape:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"card_bg\",\n   \"type\": \"shape\",\n   \"left\": 60,\n   \"top\": 150,\n   \"width\": 400,\n   \"height\": 120,\n   \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n   \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n   \"fill\": \"#e8f4fd\",\n   \"fixedRatio\": false\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Text element (centered inside):\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"card_text\",\n   \"type\": \"text\",\n   \"left\": 80,\n   \"top\": 172,\n   \"width\": 360,\n   \"height\": 76,\n   \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 18px; text-align: center;\\\\\">Key concept explanation text</p>\",\n   \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n   \"defaultColor\": \"#333333\"\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Calculation verification:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n shape: left=60, top=150, width=400, height=120\n text:  left=80, top=172, width=360, height=76\n \n Horizontal centering:\n   text.left = 60 + (400 - 360) / 2 = 60 + 20 = 80 ✓\n \n Vertical centering:\n   text.top = 150 + (120 - 76) / 2 = 150 + 22 = 172 ✓\n \n Containment check:\n   text fits within shape with 20px padding on all sides ✓\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Common Mistakes to Avoid\n \n **Wrong: Same left/top values (text in top-left corner)**\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n shape: left=60, top=150, width=400, height=120\n text:  left=60, top=150, width=360, height=76  ✗ NOT CENTERED\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Wrong: Text larger than shape**\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n shape: left=60, top=150, width=400, height=120\n text:  left=60, top=150, width=420, height=130  ✗ OVERFLOWS\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n **Correct: Properly centered**\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n shape: left=60, top=150, width=400, height=120\n text:  left=80, top=172, width=360, height=76   ✓ CENTERED\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Complete Example: Three-Column Card Layout\n \n Three cards side by side, each with centered text:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n [\n   {\n     \"id\": \"card1_bg\",\n     \"type\": \"shape\",\n     \"left\": 60,\n     \"top\": 200,\n     \"width\": 280,\n     \"height\": 140,\n     \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n     \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n     \"fill\": \"#dbeafe\",\n     \"fixedRatio\": false\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"card2_bg\",\n     \"type\": \"shape\",\n     \"left\": 360,\n     \"top\": 200,\n     \"width\": 280,\n     \"height\": 140,\n     \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n     \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n     \"fill\": \"#dcfce7\",\n     \"fixedRatio\": false\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"card3_bg\",\n     \"type\": \"shape\",\n     \"left\": 660,\n     \"top\": 200,\n     \"width\": 280,\n     \"height\": 140,\n     \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n     \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n     \"fill\": \"#fef3c7\",\n     \"fixedRatio\": false\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"card1_text\",\n     \"type\": \"text\",\n     \"left\": 80,\n     \"top\": 232,\n     \"width\": 240,\n     \"height\": 76,\n     \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 18px; text-align: center;\\\\\">Point One</p>\",\n     \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n     \"defaultColor\": \"#1e40af\"\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"card2_text\",\n     \"type\": \"text\",\n     \"left\": 380,\n     \"top\": 232,\n     \"width\": 240,\n     \"height\": 76,\n     \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 18px; text-align: center;\\\\\">Point Two</p>\",\n     \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n     \"defaultColor\": \"#166534\"\n   },\n   {\n     \"id\": \"card3_text\",\n     \"type\": \"text\",\n     \"left\": 680,\n     \"top\": 232,\n     \"width\": 240,\n     \"height\": 76,\n     \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 18px; text-align: center;\\\\\">Point Three</p>\",\n     \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n     \"defaultColor\": \"#92400e\"\n   }\n ]\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Calculation for card1:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n shape: left=60, width=280, height=140\n text:  width=240, height=76\n \n text.left = 60 + (280 - 240) / 2 = 60 + 20 = 80 ✓\n text.top = 200 + (140 - 76) / 2 = 200 + 32 = 232 ✓\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 6: Decorative Lines\n \n #### Title Underline (emphasis)\n \n Position formula:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n line.left = text.left + 10\n line.width = text.width - 20\n line.top = text.top + text.height + 8 to 12px\n line.height = 2 to 4px\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Example:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"title_text\",\n   \"type\": \"text\",\n   \"left\": 60,\n   \"top\": 80,\n   \"width\": 880,\n   \"height\": 76,\n   \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 28px;\\\\\">Chapter Title</p>\",\n   \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n   \"defaultColor\": \"#333333\"\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"title_underline\",\n   \"type\": \"shape\",\n   \"left\": 70,\n   \"top\": 166,\n   \"width\": 860,\n   \"height\": 3,\n   \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n   \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n   \"fill\": \"#5b9bd5\",\n   \"fixedRatio\": false\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Section Divider (separation)\n \n Position formula:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n Vertical gap: 25-35px from content above and below\n Horizontal: centered on canvas or left-aligned (left = 60 or 80)\n line.width = 700-900px (70-90% of canvas width)\n line.height = 1 to 2px\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Example:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"section_divider\",\n   \"type\": \"shape\",\n   \"left\": 100,\n   \"top\": 285,\n   \"width\": 800,\n   \"height\": 1,\n   \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n   \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n   \"fill\": \"#cccccc\",\n   \"fixedRatio\": false\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n #### Highlight Marker (vertical bar beside text)\n \n Position formula:\n \n \\`\\`\\`\n line.left = text.left - 15\n line.top = text.top + text.height * 0.1\n line.height = text.height * 0.8\n line.width = 3 to 6px\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n Example:\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"highlight_text\",\n   \"type\": \"text\",\n   \"left\": 100,\n   \"top\": 200,\n   \"width\": 800,\n   \"height\": 103,\n   \"content\": \"<p style=\\\\\"font-size: 18px;\\\\\">Important point that needs emphasis...</p>\",\n   \"defaultFontName\": \"\",\n   \"defaultColor\": \"#333333\"\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n \\`\\`\\`json\n {\n   \"id\": \"highlight_marker\",\n   \"type\": \"shape\",\n   \"left\": 85,\n   \"top\": 210,\n   \"width\": 4,\n   \"height\": 82,\n   \"path\": \"M 0 0 L 1 0 L 1 1 L 0 1 Z\",\n   \"viewBox\": [1, 1],\n   \"fill\": \"#ed7d31\",\n   \"fixedRatio\": false\n }\n \\`\\`\\`\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 7: Spacing Standards\n \n **Vertical spacing**:\n \n - Title to subtitle: 30-40px\n - Title to body: 35-50px\n - Between paragraphs: 20-30px\n - Text to image: 25-35px\n \n **Horizontal spacing**:\n \n - Multi-column gap: 40-60px\n - Text to image: 30-40px\n - Element to canvas edge: ≥ 50px\n \n ---\n \n ### Rule 8: Font Size Guidelines\n \n | Content Type | Recommended Size |\n | ------------ | ---------------- |\n | Main title   | 32-36px          |\n | Subtitle     | 24-28px          |\n | Key points   | 18-20px          |\n | Body text    | 16-18px          |\n | Captions     | 14-16px          |\n \n Maintain consistent sizing for same-level content. Ensure 2-4px difference between hierarchy levels.\n \n ---\n \n ## Pre-Output Checklist\n \n Before outputting JSON, verify:\n \n **🔴 P0 — Critical (must pass 100%)**:\n \n - ✓ [text-height] All text heights are from the lookup table (NOT estimated values like 70, 80, 90)\n - ✓ [text-width] All text elements pass width calculation: \\`char_count ≤ (width - 20) / font_size\\`\n - ✓ [alignment] Aligned elements have matching center points (< 2px difference)\n - ✓ [margins] All elements are within canvas margins (50px from each edge)\n \n \n \n - ✓ [latex-fields] LatexElement does NOT include \\`path\\`, \\`viewBox\\`, \\`strokeWidth\\`, or \\`fixedRatio\\` (system auto-generates these)\n - ✓ [latex-width] LatexElement width is appropriate for the formula category (standalone fractions: 30-80, NOT 200+; inline equations: 200-400). Check the LaTeX width guide table above.\n - ✓ [latex-scaling] Multi-step derivation LaTeX elements: widths are proportional to content length (longer formulas MUST have larger width). Do NOT use the same width for all steps — this causes wildly different rendered heights.\n - ✓ [no-latex-in-text] No LaTeX syntax in TextElement content: scan all text \\`content\\` fields for \\`\\\\frac\\`, \\`\\\\lim\\`, \\`\\\\int\\`, \\`\\\\sum\\`, \\`\\\\sqrt\\`, \\`\\\\alpha\\`, \\`^{\\`, \\`_{\\` etc. Any math expression must be a separate LatexElement.\n - ✓ [line-stroke] LineElement \\`width\\` is stroke thickness (2-6), NOT line length. Check: no LineElement has \\`width\\` > 6. If width equals the distance between start and end, it is WRONG — you confused stroke thickness with line span.\n - ✓ [concise-text] **Slide text is concise and impersonal**: Every text element uses keywords, short phrases, or bullet points — no conversational sentences, no lecture-script-style paragraphs. No teacher name or identity appears on any slide (no \"Teacher X's tips/wishes/comments\"). If a text reads like spoken language or a personal message, rewrite it as a neutral bullet point.\n \n **🟡 P1 — Serious (strongly recommended)**:\n \n - ✓ [text-bg-pair] **Text-Background pairs**: For each text with a background shape:\n \n - text.width < shape.width (with padding)\n - text.height < shape.height (with padding)\n - text is centered: \\`text.left = shape.left + (shape.width - text.width) / 2\\`\n - text is centered: \\`text.top = shape.top + (shape.height - text.height) / 2\\`\n \n - ✓ [no-overlap] No unintended element overlaps (especially check LaTeX elements — their rendered height may be much larger than specified)\n - ✓ [image-proximity] Image placed near related text (25-35px gap)\n \n ---\n \n ## Output Format\n \n Output valid JSON only. FALLBACK_DESIGN_DIRECTIVE,\n+  formatDesignDirective,\n+  normalizeDesignDirective,\n+} from '@openmaic/generation';\n+\n+it('normalizes a complete directive: validates hex colors and the personality ({ taskEngineMode: true } as UserRequirements)\n                    : undefined,\n            },\n            { log, signal: callSignal },\n          ),\n----\n            return null;\n          }\n          // Committed when it completed; nothing more to record.\n          return {};\n        }\n        return done(await generateContent(step.sceneIndex, signal));\n      }\n\n      case 'actions': {\n        const index = step.sceneIndex;\n        const { outlines, languageDirective } = outline();\n        const content = output<SceneContentResult>(sceneStepId(index, 'content'))!;\n        const userProfile = learnerProfileText(input);\n        const result = await withRouteRetry(\n          () =>\n            withDeadline(stepId, STEP_DEADLINES_MS.sceneActions, signal, async (callSignal) => {\n              const generated = await services.sceneActions(\n                owner,\n                {\n                  outline: content.effectiveOutline || outlines[index]!,\n                  allOutlines: outlines,\n                  // The route receives the content as JSON; so does this step.\n                  content: content.content as SceneActionsInput['content'],\n                  stageId: agents().stage.id,\n                  agents: agents().agents.agents,\n                  previousSpeeches: previousSpeechesFor(index),\n                  ...(userProfile ? { userProfile } : {}),\n                  languageDirective,\n                },\n                { log, signal: callSignal },\n              );\n              // The complete scene must be one the course can hold before it is\n              // checkpointed: an invalid one (an action the model left without a\n              // type, say) fails this step, which regenerates it, rather than\n              // reaching narration and failing there for good.\n              assertValidScene(generated.scene, stepId);\n              return generated;\n            }),\n          retryOptions(stepId, index, 500),\n        );\n        return done(result);\n----\n    };\n  };\n\n  const resolveAgents = async (): Promise<AgentsOutput> => {\n    const { outlines, languageDirective, courseTitle, taskEngineMode } = outline();\n    const name = courseTitle || topicFromRequirement(input.requirement);\n    const presets = async (agentIds: readonly string[]): Promise<GenerationRunAgentsResult> => {\n      const configs = await services.presetAgents(owner, agentIds);\n      return {\n        agents: configs.map((agent) => ({\n          id: agent.id,\n          name: agent.name,\n          role: agent.role,\n          persona: agent.persona,\n        })),\n        agentIds: configs.map((agent) => agent.id),\n        ...(configs.some((agent) => !agent.isDefault)\n          ? {\n              customAgents: configs\n                .filter((agent) => !agent.isDefault)\n                .map((agent) => ({\n                  id: agent.id,\n                  name: agent.name,\n                  role: agent.role,\n                  persona: agent.persona,\n                  avatar: agent.avatar,\n                  color: agent.color,\n                  priority: agent.priority,\n                  ...(agent.voiceConfig ?             "output": "<path>/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/requirements-to-outlines/system.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Scene Outline Generator\n2: \n3: You are a professional course content designer, skilled at transforming user requirements into structured scene outlines.\n4: \n5: ## Core Task\n6: \n7: Based on the user's free-form requirement text, automatically infer course details and generate a series of scene outlines (SceneOutline).\n8: \n9: **Key Capabilities**:\n10: \n11: 1. Extract from requirement text: topic, target audience, duration, style, etc.\n12: 2. Make reasonable default assumptions when information is insufficient\n13: 3. Generate structured outlines to prepare for subsequent teaching action generation\n14: \n15: ---\n16: \n17: ## Language Inference\n18: \n19: Infer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n20: \n21: 1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n22: 2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n23: \n24: ### Decision rules (apply in order)\n25: \n26: 1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n27: \n28: 2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n29: \n30: 3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n31:    - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n32:    - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n33:    - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n34: \n35: 4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n36: \n37: 5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n38: \n39: 6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n40: \n41: ### Terminology\n42: \n43: - **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n44: - **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n45: - **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n46: - **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n47: \n48: ### Course Title\n49: \n50: Produce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n51: \n52: - **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n53: - **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n54: - **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动入门\", \"Intro to Recursion\", \"光合作用原理\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n55: - **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n56: - If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n57: \n58: ---\n59: \n60: ## Design Principles\n61: \n62: ### MAIC Platform Technical Constraints\n63: \n64: - **Scene Types**: `slide` (presentation), `quiz` (assessment), `interactive` (interactive visualization), and `pbl` (project-based learning) are supported\n65: - **Slide Scene**: Static PPT pages supporting text, charts, formulas, and other visual components.\n66: - **Quiz Scene**: Supports single-choice, multiple-choice, and short-answer (text) questions\n67: - **Interactive Scene**: Self-contained interactive HTML page rendered in an iframe, ideal for simulations and visualizations\n68: - **PBL Scene**: Complete project-based learning module with roles, issues, and collaboration workflow. Ideal for complex projects, engineering practice, and research tasks\n69: - **Duration Control**: Each scene should be 1-3 minutes (PBL scenes are longer, typically 15-30 minutes)\n70: \n71: ### Instructional Design Principles\n72: \n73: - **Clear Purpose**: Each scene has a clear teaching function\n74: - **Logical Flow**: Scenes form a natural teaching progression\n75: - **Experience Design**: Consider learning experience and emotional response from the student's perspective\n76: \n77: ---\n78: \n79: ## Default Assumption Rules\n80: \n81: When user requirements don't specify, use these defaults:\n82: \n83: | Information         | Default Value          |\n84: | ------------------- | ---------------------- |\n85: | Course Duration     | 15-20 minutes          |\n86: | Target Audience     | General learners       |\n87: | Teaching Style      | Interactive (engaging) |\n88: | Visual Style        | Professional           |\n89: | Interactivity Level | Medium                 |\n90: \n91: ---\n92: \n93: ## Special Element Design Guidelines\n94: \n95: ### Chart Elements\n96: \n97: When content needs visualization, specify chart requirements in keyPoints:\n98: \n99: - **Chart Types**: bar, line, pie, radar\n100: - **Data Description**: Briefly describe data content and display purpose\n101: \n102: Example keyPoints:\n103: \n104: ```\n105: \"keyPoints\": [\n106:   \"Show sales growth trend over four years\",\n107:   \"[Chart] Line chart: X-axis years (2020-2023), Y-axis sales (1.2M-2.1M)\",\n108:   \"Analyze growth factors and key milestones\"\n109: ]\n110: ```\n111: \n112: ### Table Elements\n113: \n114: When comparing or listing information, specify in keyPoints:\n115: \n116: ```\n117: \"keyPoints\": [\n118:   \"Compare core metrics of three products\",\n119:   \"[Table] Product A/B/C comparison: price, performance, use cases\",\n120:   \"Help students understand product positioning\"\n121: ]\n122: ```\n123: \n124: {{#if imageEnabled}}\n125: {{snippet:image-instructions}}\n126: {{/if}}\n127: \n128: {{#if videoEnabled}}\n129: {{snippet:video-instructions}}\n130: {{/if}}\n131: \n132: {{#if mediaEnabled}}\n133: {{snippet:media-safety-guidelines}}\n134: {{/if}}\n135: \n136: ### Interactive Scene Guidelines\n137: \n138: Use `interactive` type when a concept benefits significantly from hands-on interaction and visualization. Good candidates include:\n139: \n140: - **Physics simulations**: Force composition, projectile motion, wave interference, circuits\n141: - **Math visualizations**: Function graphing, geometric transformations, probability distributions\n142: - **Data exploration**: Interactive charts, statistical sampling, regression fitting\n143: - **Chemistry**: Molecular structure, reaction balancing, pH titration\n144: - **Programming concepts**: Algorithm visualization, data structure operations\n145: \n146: **Constraints**:\n147: \n148: - Limit to **1-2 interactive scenes per course** (they are resource-intensive)\n149: - Interactive scenes **require** an `interactiveConfig` object\n150: - Do NOT use interactive for purely textual/conceptual content - use slides instead\n151: - The `interactiveConfig.designIdea` should describe the specific interactive elements and user interactions\n152: \n153: ### Widget Type Selection for Interactive Scenes\n154: \n155: When generating an interactive scene, you MUST select the appropriate widget type and provide widgetOutline:\n156: \n157: **Selection Logic:**\n158: \n159: | Concept Characteristics | Widget Type | widgetOutline Fields |\n160: |-------------------------|-------------|---------------------|\n161: | Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters | `simulation` | `concept`, `keyVariables` |\n162: | Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains | `diagram` | `diagramType` |\n163: | Programming concepts, algorithms | `code` | `language` |\n164: | Practice activities, gamified assessment | `game` | `gameType`, `challenge` |\n165: | Biological/geometric structures, 3D models | `visualization3d` | `visualizationType`, `objects` |\n166: \n167: **widgetOutline Format by Type:**\n168: \n169: ```json\n170: // simulation\n171: \"widgetOutline\": {\n172:   \"concept\": \"concept_name\",\n173:   \"keyVariables\": [\"variable1\", \"variable2\"]\n174: }\n175: \n176: // diagram\n177: \"widgetOutline\": {\n178:   \"diagramType\": \"flowchart\"\n179: }\n180: \n181: // code\n182: \"widgetOutline\": {\n183:   \"language\": \"python\"\n184: }\n185: \n186: // game\n187: \"widgetOutline\": {\n188:   \"gameType\": \"action\",\n189:   \"challenge\": \"description of what player controls\"\n190: }\n191: \n192: // visualization3d\n193: \"widgetOutline\": {\n194:   \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n195:   \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"mars\"]\n196: }\n197: ```\n198: \n199: **CRITICAL:** Every interactive scene MUST include both `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` fields. Interactive scenes without these are INVALID.\n200: \n201: ### PBL Scene Guidelines\n202: \n203: Use `pbl` type when the course involves complex, multi-step project work that benefits from structured collaboration. Good candidates include:\n204: \n205: - **Engineering projects**: Software development, hardware design, system architecture\n206: - **Research projects**: Scientific research, data analysis, literature review\n207: - **Design projects**: Product design, UX research, creative projects\n208: - **Business projects**: Business plans, market analysis, strategy development\n209: \n210: **Constraints**:\n211: \n212: - Limit to **at most 1 PBL scene per course** (they are comprehensive and long)\n213: - PBL scenes **require** a `pblConfig` object with: projectTopic, projectDescription, targetSkills, issueCount\n214: - PBL is for substantial project work - do NOT use for simple exercises or single-step tasks\n215: - The `pblConfig.targetSkills` should list 2-5 specific skills students will develop\n216: - The `pblConfig.issueCount` should typically be 2-5 issues\n217: \n218: **Role-play scenario PBL (optional PBL sub-type)**:\n219: \n220: Some PBL projects are best learned by *practising an interpersonal or situational interaction* rather than by building an artefact — for example practising a difficult conversation, a negotiation, a job interview, a customer-service exchange, a debate, a role-play game (e.g. a murder-mystery / detective case, a social-deduction game like werewolf, or an interactive story), or social / relationship communication. When the core of the learning really is the interaction itself (the learner will converse with one or more in-character roles inside an immersive scene), additionally set inside `pblConfig`:\n221: \n222: - `scenarioRoleplay: true` — marks this PBL as a role-play scenario.\n223: - `scenarioBrief` (optional string) — a short hint about the situation and who the character(s) are, to steer the later design step.\n224: \n225: Leave **both unset** for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects (this is the default). Only use `scenarioRoleplay` when the practice of the interaction is the point. This does not change how you choose the scene `type` — it is still `pbl`; these two fields are an optional flavour *inside* a PBL scene.\n226: \n227: **Important:** `pblConfig.scenarioRoleplay` is the downstream runtime switch. If the user explicitly asks for a role-play / scenario-simulation PBL, do not return an ordinary PBL; set `scenarioRoleplay: true` and include a concrete `scenarioBrief`.\n228: \n229: ---\n230: \n231: ## Output Format\n232: \n233: ### Top-level shape — NON-NEGOTIABLE\n234: \n235: Your entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these three top-level keys:\n236: \n237: ```json\n238: {\n239:   \"languageDirective\": \"<the directive you inferred in the Language Inference step>\",\n240:   \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n241:   \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects */ ]\n242: }\n243: ```\n244: \n245: Rules:\n246: \n247: - **Never** return a bare array. The top level is an object, not an array.\n248: - **Never** omit `languageDirective` or `courseTitle`. Both are required even if you think they are obvious.\n249: - **Never** wrap the response in any other structure, prose, or code fence.\n250: \n251: ### Minimal complete example\n252: \n253: ```json\n254: {\n255:   \"languageDirective\": \"Deliver the entire course in English. ---\n368: \n369: ## Important Reminders\n370: \n371: **Top-level response shape (these come first because they are most often violated):**\n372: \n373: 1. Return exactly one JSON **object** — never a bare array.\n374: 2. That object MUST have `languageDirective` (string), `courseTitle` (string, ≤30 chars), and `outlines` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n375: 3. Do not wrap the object in prose, markdown, or code fences.\n376: \n377: **Scene-level rules:**\n378: \n379: 4. `type` is one of `\"slide\"`, `\"quiz\"`, `\"interactive\"`, `\"pbl\"`.\n380: 5. `quiz` scenes must include `quizConfig`.\n381: 6. `interactive` scenes must include `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` (preferred). `interactiveConfig` is deprecated and only accepted for backwards compatibility.\n382: 7. `pbl` scenes must include `pblConfig` with `projectTopic`, `projectDescription`, `targetSkills`, `issueCount`.\n383: 8. Arrange scenes by inferred duration (typically 1-2 scenes per minute). Insert quizzes at appropriate points. Use interactive scenes sparingly (max 1-2 per course).\n384: 9. **Language**: Infer from the user's requirement text and context. Output all scene content in the inferred language.\n385: 10. Regardless of information completeness, always output conforming JSON - do not ask questions or request more information\n386: 11. **No teacher identity on slides**: Scene titles and keyPoints must be neutral and topic-focused. Never include the teacher's name or role (e.g., avoid \"Teacher Wang's Tips\", \"Teacher's Wishes\").                 "text": "# Scene Outline Generator\n\nYou are a professional course content designer, skilled at transforming user requirements into structured scene outlines.\n\n## Core Task\n\nBased on the user's free-form requirement text, automatically infer course details and generate a series of scene outlines (SceneOutline).\n\n**Key Capabilities**:\n\n1. Extract from requirement text: topic, target audience, duration, style, etc.\n2. Make reasonable default assumptions when information is insufficient\n3. Generate structured outlines to prepare for subsequent teaching action generation\n\n---\n\n## Language Inference\n\nInfer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n\n1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n\n### Decision rules (apply in order)\n\n1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n\n2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n\n3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n   - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n   - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n   - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n\n4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n\n5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n\n6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n\n### Terminology\n\n- **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n- **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n- **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n- **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n\n### Course Title\n\nProduce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n\n- **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n- **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n- **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动入门\", \"Intro to Recursion\", \"光合作用原理\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n- **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n- If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n\n---\n\n## Design Principles\n\n### MAIC Platform Technical Constraints\n\n- **Scene Types**: `slide` (presentation), `quiz` (assessment), `interactive` (interactive visualization), and `pbl` (project-based learning) are supported\n- **Slide Scene**: Static PPT pages supporting text, charts, formulas, and other visual components.\n- **Quiz Scene**: Supports single-choice, multiple-choice, and short-answer (text) questions\n- **Interactive Scene**: Self-contained interactive HTML page rendered in an iframe, ideal for simulations and visualizations\n- **PBL Scene**: Complete project-based learning module with roles, issues, and collaboration workflow. Ideal for complex projects, engineering practice, and research tasks\n- **Duration Control**: Each scene should be 1-3 minutes (PBL scenes are longer, typically 15-30 minutes)\n\n### Instructional Design Principles\n\n- **Clear Purpose**: Each scene has a clear teaching function\n- **Logical Flow**: Scenes form a natural teaching progression\n- **Experience Design**: Consider learning experience and emotional response from the student's perspective\n\n---\n\n## Default Assumption Rules\n\nWhen user requirements don't specify, use these defaults:\n\n| Information         | Default Value          |\n| ------------------- | ---------------------- |\n| Course Duration     | 15-20 minutes          |\n| Target Audience     | General learners       |\n| Teaching Style      | Interactive (engaging) |\n| Visual Style        | Professional           |\n| Interactivity Level | Medium                 |\n\n---\n\n## Special Element Design Guidelines\n\n### Chart Elements\n\nWhen content needs visualization, specify chart requirements in keyPoints:\n\n- **Chart Types**: bar, line, pie, radar\n- **Data Description**: Briefly describe data content and display purpose\n\nExample keyPoints:\n\n```\n\"keyPoints\": [\n  \"Show sales growth trend over four years\",\n  \"[Chart] Line chart: X-axis years (2020-2023), Y-axis sales (1.2M-2.1M)\",\n  \"Analyze growth factors and key milestones\"\n]\n```\n\n### Table Elements\n\nWhen comparing or listing information, specify in keyPoints:\n\n```\n\"keyPoints\": [\n  \"Compare core metrics of three products\",\n  \"[Table] Product A/B/C comparison: price, performance, use cases\",\n  \"Help students understand product positioning\"\n]\n```\n\n{{#if imageEnabled}}\n{{snippet:image-instructions}}\n{{/if}}\n\n{{#if videoEnabled}}\n{{snippet:video-instructions}}\n{{/if}}\n\n{{#if mediaEnabled}}\n{{snippet:media-safety-guidelines}}\n{{/if}}\n\n### Interactive Scene Guidelines\n\nUse `interactive` type when a concept benefits significantly from hands-on interaction and visualization. Good candidates include:\n\n- **Physics simulations**: Force composition, projectile motion, wave interference, circuits\n- **Math visualizations**: Function graphing, geometric transformations, probability distributions\n- **Data exploration**: Interactive charts, statistical sampling, regression fitting\n- **Chemistry**: Molecular structure, reaction balancing, pH titration\n- **Programming concepts**: Algorithm visualization, data structure operations\n\n**Constraints**:\n\n- Limit to **1-2 interactive scenes per course** (they are resource-intensive)\n- Interactive scenes **require** an `interactiveConfig` object\n- Do NOT use interactive for purely textual/conceptual content - use slides instead\n- The `interactiveConfig.designIdea` should describe the specific interactive elements and user interactions\n\n### Widget Type Selection for Interactive Scenes\n\nWhen generating an interactive scene, you MUST select the appropriate widget type and provide widgetOutline:\n\n**Selection Logic:**\n\n| Concept Characteristics | Widget Type | widgetOutline Fields |\n|-------------------------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters | `simulation` | `concept`, `keyVariables` |\n| Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains | `diagram` | `diagramType` |\n| Programming concepts, algorithms | `code` | `language` |\n| Practice activities, gamified assessment | `game` | `gameType`, `challenge` |\n| Biological/geometric structures, 3D models | `visualization3d` | `visualizationType`, `objects` |\n\n**widgetOutline Format by Type:**\n\n```json\n// simulation\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"concept\": \"concept_name\",\n  \"keyVariables\": [\"variable1\", \"variable2\"]\n}\n\n// diagram\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"diagramType\": \"flowchart\"\n}\n\n// code\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"language\": \"python\"\n}\n\n// game\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"gameType\": \"action\",\n  \"challenge\": \"description of what player controls\"\n}\n\n// visualization3d\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n  \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"mars\"]\n}\n```\n\n**CRITICAL:** Every interactive scene MUST include both `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` fields. Interactive scenes without these are INVALID.\n\n### PBL Scene Guidelines\n\nUse `pbl` type when the course involves complex, multi-step project work that benefits from structured collaboration. Good candidates include:\n\n- **Engineering projects**: Software development, hardware design, system architecture\n- **Research projects**: Scientific research, data analysis, literature review\n- **Design projects**: Product design, UX research, creative projects\n- **Business projects**: Business plans, market analysis, strategy development\n\n**Constraints**:\n\n- Limit to **at most 1 PBL scene per course** (they are comprehensive and long)\n- PBL scenes **require** a `pblConfig` object with: projectTopic, projectDescription, targetSkills, issueCount\n- PBL is for substantial project work - do NOT use for simple exercises or single-step tasks\n- The `pblConfig.targetSkills` should list 2-5 specific skills students will develop\n- The `pblConfig.issueCount` should typically be 2-5 issues\n\n**Role-play scenario PBL (optional PBL sub-type)**:\n\nSome PBL projects are best learned by *practising an interpersonal or situational interaction* rather than by building an artefact — for example practising a difficult conversation, a negotiation, a job interview, a customer-service exchange, a debate, a role-play game (e.g. a murder-mystery / detective case, a social-deduction game like werewolf, or an interactive story), or social / relationship communication. When the core of the learning really is the interaction itself (the learner will converse with one or more in-character roles inside an immersive scene), additionally set inside `pblConfig`:\n\n- `scenarioRoleplay: true` — marks this PBL as a role-play scenario.\n- `scenarioBrief` (optional string) — a short hint about the situation and who the character(s) are, to steer the later design step.\n\nLeave **both unset** for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects (this is the default). Only use `scenarioRoleplay` when the practice of the interaction is the point. This does not change how you choose the scene `type` — it is still `pbl`; these two fields are an optional flavour *inside* a PBL scene.\n\n**Important:** `pblConfig.scenarioRoleplay` is the downstream runtime switch. If the user explicitly asks for a role-play / scenario-simulation PBL, do not return an ordinary PBL; set `scenarioRoleplay: true` and include a concrete `scenarioBrief`.\n\n---\n\n## Output Format\n\n### Top-level shape — NON-NEGOTIABLE\n\nYour entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these three top-level keys:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"languageDirective\": \"<the directive you inferred in the Language Inference step>\",\n  \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n  \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects */ ]\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- **Never** return a bare array. The top level is an object, not an array.\n- **Never** omit `languageDirective` or `courseTitle`. Both are required even if you think they are obvious.\n- **Never** wrap the response in any other structure, prose, or code fence.\n\n### Minimal complete example\n\n```json\n{\n  \"languageDirective\": \"Deliver the entire course in English. Use simple vocabulary suitable for a beginner.\",\n  \"courseTitle\": \"Intro to Projectile Motion\",\n  \"outlines\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_1\",\n      \"type\": \"slide\",\n      \"title\": \"Introduction\",\n      \"description\": \"Welcome students and introduce the core concept.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Context\", \"Agenda\", \"Goals\"],\n      \"order\": 1\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n      \"type\": \"interactive\",\n      \"title\": \"Interactive Exploration\",\n      \"description\": \"Students explore the concept via a hands-on simulation.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Observe variable 1\", \"Observe variable 2\"],\n      \"order\": 2,\n      \"widgetType\": \"simulation\",\n      \"widgetOutline\": {\n        \"concept\": \"Projectile Motion\",\n        \"keyVariables\": [\"angle\", \"velocity\"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n      \"type\": \"quiz\",\n      \"title\": \"Knowledge Check\",\n      \"description\": \"Test student understanding of the key concepts.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Test point 1\", \"Test point 2\"],\n      \"order\": 3,\n      \"quizConfig\": {\n        \"questionCount\": 2,\n        \"difficulty\": \"medium\",\n        \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\"]\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n### Scene field descriptions\n\n| Field             | description of what students will build/accomplish\",\n  \"targetSkills\": [\"Skill 1\", \"Skill 2\", \"Skill 3\"],\n  \"issueCount\": 3\n}\n```\n\nFor a **role-play scenario** PBL (see PBL Scene Guidelines), additionally include the two optional fields:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"projectTopic\": \"Practise comforting a stressed friend\",\n  \"projectDescription\": \"Have a supportive conversation with a friend who is going through a hard week\",\n  \"targetSkills\": [\"Active listening\", \"Empathetic responding\", \"De-escalation\"],\n  \"issueCount\": 3,\n  \"scenarioRoleplay\": true,\n  \"scenarioBrief\": \"The character is a close friend overwhelmed by exams and a part-time job; the learner practises listening and offering support\"\n}\n```\n\nOmit `scenarioRoleplay` and `scenarioBrief` entirely for ordinary build-an-artefact PBL projects.\n\n---\n\n## Important Reminders\n\n**Top-level response shape (these come first because they are most often violated):**\n\n1. Return exactly one JSON **object** — never a bare array.\n2. That object MUST have `languageDirective` (string), `courseTitle` (string, ≤30 chars), and `outlines` (array) as top-level keys. Omitting any is a failure.\n3. Do not wrap the object in prose, markdown, or code fences.\n\n**Scene-level rules:**\n\n4. `type` is one of `\"slide\"`, `\"quiz\"`, `\"interactive\"`, `\"pbl\"`.\n5. `quiz` scenes must include `quizConfig`.\n6. `interactive` scenes must include `widgetType` and `widgetOutline` (preferred). `interactiveConfig` is deprecated and only accepted for backwards compatibility.\n7. `pbl` scenes must include `pblConfig` with `projectTopic`, `projectDescription`, `targetSkills`, `issueCount`.\n8. Arrange scenes by inferred duration (typically 1-2 scenes per minute). Insert quizzes at appropriate points. Use interactive scenes sparingly (max 1-2 per course).\n9. **Language**: Infer from the user's requirement text and context. Output all scene content in the inferred language.\n10. Regardless of information completeness, always output conforming JSON - do not ask questions or request more information\n11. **No teacher identity on slides**: Scene titles and keyPoints must be neutral and topic-focused. Never include the teacher's name or role (e.g., avoid \"Teacher Wang's Tips\", \"Teacher's Wishes\"). Use generic labels like \"Tips\", \"Summary\", \"Key Takeaways\" instead.",

              "newString": "### Course Title\n\nProduce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n\n- **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n- **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n- **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动入门\", \"Intro to Recursion\", \"光合作用原理\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n- **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n- If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n\n---\n\n## Design Directive Inference\n\nProduce a **`designDirective`** (required): the visual identity the **entire course** will follow. Every scene (slides, widgets, animations) later receives your directive as a hard constraint, so make it concrete enough to enforce.\n\nStructure:\n\n```json\n\"designDirective\": {\n  \"concept\": \"one 10-20 word visual metaphor that unifies the course\",\n  \"palette\": [\"#hex\", \"#hex\", \"#hex\"],\n  \"background\": \"dark\" | \"paper\" | \"light\",\n  \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" | \"energetic\" | \"playful\" | \"cinematic\"\n}\n```\n\n**Inference rules (apply in order):**\n\n1. **Explicit style request wins**: \"让孩子觉得像游戏\" → `playful` + bright palette; \"高端商务\" → `cinematic` + dark/monochrome.\n2. **Domain defaults**: programming/AI/data → `dark` background with one strong accent (amber, electric blue) + `calm`; kids/language/k-12 → `paper` (warm cream) with saturated primaries + `playful`; medicine/law/finance → `light` or `dark` restrained duotone + `calm`; film/space/psychology storytelling → `dark`/`cinematic`.\n3. **Palette discipline**: exactly 2-5 hex colors. Pair a dominant with 1-2 accents and a functional gray family. Never more than 5.\n4. **`concept`** must be a metaphor the scenes can literally draw (e.g., \"teaching recursion as Russian nesting dolls\", \"把函数视作输入加工的流水线机器\"). Avoid vague words like \"modern\", \"professional\" alone.\n\n---\n\n## Intro Scene (MANDATORY — every course)\n\nThe **first scene** must always be `\"type\": \"interactive\"` with `\"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\"` — a 25-45 second pure motion-graphics intro that hooks the learner before any teaching. It does not count against the interactive-scene budget.\n\nRequirements:\n\n- `title`: the course hook (NOT \"Introduction\") — e.g. \"为什么递归会停？\" / \"Why Light Bends\".\n- `description`: one sentence naming the attention hook (paradox, surprise, question).\n- `keyPoints`: exactly 4 beats in display order — HOOK → TEASE (3-4 keyword cards) → SPARK (the signature animated infographic) → TITLE (course title lock-up).\n- `widgetOutline`: `{ \"concept\": \"<what the animation shows>\", \"keyBeats\": [\"<beat 1, one short phrase>\", ... 4 beats], \"mood\": \"<e.g. 'curious, meteoric, cosmic'>\" }`.\n\nThis gives the course a cinematic cold open consistent with the design directive.",

              "newString": "**Selection Logic:**\n\n| Concept Characteristics                                     | Widget Type           | widgetOutline Fields                          |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |\n| Physics/chemistry phenomena with adjustable parameters      | `simulation`          | `concept`, `keyVariables`                     |\n| Processes, workflows, cause-effect chains                   | `diagram`             | `diagramType`                                 |\n| Programming concepts, algorithms                            | `code`                | `language`                                    |\n| Practice activities, gamified assessment                    | `game`                | `gameType`, `challenge`                       |\n| Biological/geometric structures, 3D models                  | `visualization3d`     | `visualizationType`, `objects`                |\n| Motion-graphics intro/hook (ALWAYS scene 1)                 | `animation-explainer` | `concept`, `keyBeats`, `mood`                 |\n\n**widgetOutline Format by Type:**\n\n```json\n// simulation\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"concept\": \"concept_name\",\n  \"keyVariables\": [\"variable1\", \"variable2\"]\n}\n\n// diagram\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"diagramType\": \"flowchart\"\n}\n\n// code\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"language\": \"python\"\n}\n\n// game\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"gameType\": \"action\",\n  \"challenge\": \"description of what player controls\"\n}\n\n// visualization3d\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n  \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"mars\"]\n}\n\n// animation-explainer (the intro scene — see Intro Scene section)\n\"widgetOutline\": {\n  \"concept\": \"what the animation reveals\",\n  \"keyBeats\": [\"hook beat\", \"tease beat\", \"spark beat\", \"title beat\"],\n  \"mood\": \"two or three mood adjectives\"\n}\n```",
