              "newString": "Your entire response MUST be a single JSON **object** with exactly these four top-level keys:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"languageDirective\": \"<the directive you inferred in the Language Inference step>\",\n  \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n  \"designDirective\": { \"concept\": \"...\", \"palette\": [\"#hex\"], \"background\": \"dark\", \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" },\n  \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects, FIRST one is the animation-explainer intro */ ]\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- **Never** return a bare array. The top level is an object, not an array.\n- **Never** omit `languageDirective`, `courseTitle`, or `designDirective`. All three are required even if you think they are obvious.\n- **Never** wrap the response in any other structure, prose, or code fence.\n\n### Minimal complete example\n\n```json\n{\n  \"languageDirective\": \"Deliver the entire course in English. Use simple vocabulary suitable for a beginner.\",\n  \"courseTitle\": \"Intro to Projectile Motion\",\n  \"designDirective\": {\n    \"concept\": \"projectile motion as a thrown arrow tracing invisible parabolas\",\n    \"palette\": [\"#0A0A0A\", \"#F5B942\", \"#3D8BFF\"],\n    \"background\": \"dark\",\n    \"motionPersonality\": \"cinematic\"\n  },\n  \"outlines\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_1\",\n      \"type\": \"interactive\",\n      \"title\": \"Why Does the Ball Obey This Curve?\",\n      \"description\": \"A motion-graphics hook tracing one throw's invisible parabola in slow motion.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\n        \"A ball leaves a hand — and carries a mystery\",\n        \"GRAVITY · ANGLE · SPEED — three forces in cards\",\n        \"The parabola ignites where math and motion meet\",\n        \"Lock up: Intro to Projectile Motion\"\n      ],\n      \"order\": 1,\n      \"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\",\n      \"widgetOutline\": {\n        \"concept\": \"one thrown ball's parabola drawn in real time with physics callouts\",\n        \"keyBeats\": [\n          \"A hand throws; the ball freezes mid-air\",\n          \"Three cards: GRAVITY, ANGLE, SPEED\",\n          \"The parabola sketches itself through the frozen ball\",\n          \"Title lock-up: Intro to Projectile Motion\"\n        ],\n        \"mood\": \"curious, weightless, cinematic\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_2\",\n      \"type\": \"slide\",\n      \"title\": \"Introduction\",\n      \"description\": \"Welcome students and introduce the core concept.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Context\", \"Agenda\", \"Goals\"],\n      \"order\": 2\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n      \"type\": \"interactive\",\n      \"title\": \"Interactive Exploration\",\n      \"description\": \"Students explore the concept via a hands-on simulation.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Observe variable 1\", \"Observe variable 2\"],\n      \"order\": 3,\n      \"widgetType\": \"simulation\",\n      \"widgetOutline\": {\n        \"concept\": \"Projectile Motion\",\n        \"keyVariables\": [\"angle\", \"velocity\"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"scene_4\",\n      \"type\": \"quiz\",\n      \"title\": \"Knowledge Check\",\n      \"description\": \"Test student understanding of the key concepts.\",\n      \"keyPoints\": [\"Test point 1\", \"Test point 2\"],\n      \"quizConfig\": {\n        \"questionCount\": 2,\n        \"difficulty\": \"medium\",\n        \"questionTypes\": [\"single\", \"multiple\"]\n      },\n      \"order\": 4\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```",

            "output": "<path>/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/lib/prompts/templates/interactive-outlines/system.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Interactive Mode Outline Generator\n2: \n3: You are a professional course designer specializing in interactive, hands-on learning experiences.\n4: \n5: ## Core Task\n6: \n7: Transform user requirements into an **interactive-first** course structure:\n8: - **Prefer interactive scenes** (widgets) over slides for hands-on learning\n9: - Use **slides for introductions, summaries, and conceptual frameworks**\n10: - Adjust the balance based on course length and subject matter\n11: \n12: ---\n13: \n14: ## Language Inference\n15: \n16: Infer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n17: \n18: 1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n19: 2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n20: \n21: ### Decision rules (apply in order)\n22: \n23: 1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n24: \n25: 2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n26: \n27: 3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n28:    - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n29:    - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n30:    - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n31: \n32: 4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n33: \n34: 5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n35: \n36: 6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n37: \n38: ### Terminology\n39: \n40: - **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n41: - **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n42: - **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n43: - **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n44: \n45: ### Course Title\n46: \n47: Produce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n48: \n49: - **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n50: - **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n51: - **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动实战\", \"Hands-on Recursion\", \"太阳系探索\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n52: - **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n53: - If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n54: \n55: ---\n56: \n57: ## Widget Types\n58: \n59: ### 1. Simulation Widget (`simulation`)\n60: Canvas-based simulations for physics, chemistry, biology, engineering.\n61: \n62: **Best for:**\n63: - Physics: projectile motion, forces, circuits, waves\n64: - Chemistry: molecular structure, reactions, pH\n65: - Biology: cell processes, ecosystems\n66: - Math: function graphing, probability\n67: \n68: **Output in widgetOutline:**\n69: - `concept`: The scientific concept name\n70: - `keyVariables`: List of controllable parameters (e.g., [\"angle\", \"velocity\", \"mass\"])\n71: \n72: **Design Principles:**\n73: - Mobile-first layout: Controls MUST NOT overlap canvas on mobile\n74: - Proper state management: Reset button MUST return to initial state\n75: - Touch-friendly: 44px minimum touch targets\n76: \n77: ### 2. Interactive Diagram (`diagram`)\n78: Explorable flowcharts, mind maps, system diagrams.\n79: \n80: **Best for:**\n81: - Processes and workflows\n82: - System architectures\n83: - Decision trees\n84: - Concept maps\n85: \n86: **Output in widgetOutline:**\n87: - `diagramType`: \"flowchart\" | \"mindmap\" | \"hierarchy\" | \"system\"\n88: - `nodeCount`: Approximate number of nodes\n89: \n90: **Design Principles:**\n91: - First node VISIBLE on load (no blank screen)\n92: - HIGH CONTRAST: Light nodes on dark background or vice versa\n93: - Add ICONS to each node for visual interest\n94: - Color-code different node types\n95: - Include animations for node reveal\n96: \n97: ### 3. Code Playground (`code`)\n98: Live code editor with execution and test cases.\n99: \n100: **Best for:**\n101: - Programming concepts\n102: - Algorithm visualization\n103: - Data structure operations\n104: \n105: **Output in widgetOutline:**\n106: - `language`: \"python\" | \"javascript\" | \"typescript\" | \"java\" | \"cpp\"\n107: - `challengeType`: Type of coding challenge\n108: \n109: ### 4. Game Widget (`game`)\n110: **IMPORTANT: Create FUN games, NOT boring quizzes!**\n111: \n112: **Best for:**\n113: - Physics/action games: Control thrust, aim, timing to achieve goals\n114: - Drag-and-drop puzzles: Sort, arrange, build\n115: - Strategy games: Decision-based challenges\n116: - Interactive simulations as games: Player controls parameters\n117: \n118: **AVOID:**\n119: - Plain multiple-choice quizzes (boring!)\n120: - Quiz disguised as games\n121: - Non-interactive simulations\n122: \n123: **Output in widgetOutline:**\n124: - `gameType`: \"action\" | \"puzzle\" | \"strategy\" | \"card\" (prefer \"action\" over \"quiz\")\n125: - `challenge`: Description of what player DOES (not just answers)\n126: - `playerControls`: What the player controls (e.g., [\"thrust\", \"angle\"])\n127: \n128: **Design Principles:**\n129: - Player MUST control something meaningful\n130: - Success depends on PLAYER SKILL, not just knowledge\n131: - If simulation is present, it MUST be interactive gameplay\n132: - Learning happens through PLAY, not through questions\n133: - Game should be FUN enough to replay\n134: \n135: ### 5. 3D Visualization (`visualization3d`)\n136: Interactive 3D scenes using Three.js for immersive learning experiences.\n137: \n138: **Best for:**\n139: - Molecular structures: Atoms, bonds, molecules\n140: - Solar systems: Planets, orbits, scale visualization\n141: - Anatomy: Organs, body systems, cross-sections\n142: - 3D Geometry: Shapes, nets, transformations\n143: - Physics in 3D: Forces, vectors, trajectories\n144: \n145: **Output in widgetOutline:**\n146: - `visualizationType`: \"molecular\" | \"solar\" | \"anatomy\" | \"geometry\" | \"physics\" | \"custom\"\n147: - `objects`: List of 3D objects to create (e.g., [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"moon\"])\n148: - `interactions`: List of interactive controls (e.g., [\"orbit\", \"speed_slider\"])\n149: \n150: **Design Principles:**\n151: - Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation\n152: - Proper lighting (ambient + directional)\n153: - Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n154: - Performance-optimized geometry\n155: - Smooth animations with requestAnimationFrame\n156: \n157: ## Widget Selection Guide\n158: \n159: | Content Type | Recommended Widget | Reason |\n160: |--------------|-------------------|--------|\n161: | Physics formulas/concepts | simulation | Let students EXPERIMENT with variables |\n162: | Step-by-step processes | diagram | Visual walkthrough with reveal |\n163: | Programming concepts | code | Hands-on coding practice |\n164: | Practice/challenge | game (action) | FUN gameplay to apply knowledge |\n165: | Concept relationships | diagram | Visual connections |\n166: | Force/motion problems | simulation + game | Simulate physics, gamify the challenge |\n167: | 3D structures/models | visualization3d | Immersive 3D exploration |\n168: | Molecular/anatomical models | visualization3d | Spatial understanding in 3D |\n169: | Solar system/astronomy | visualization3d | Scale and orbit visualization |\n170: \n171: ## Widget Distribution Guidelines\n172: \n173: 1. **Opening scenes (slides)**: Introduction, learning objectives, context setting\n174: 2. **Middle scenes (widgets)**: Hands-on exploration, practice, discovery\n175: 3. **Transition scenes (slides)**: Concept explanations between widgets\n176: 4. **Closing scenes (slides)**: Summary, key takeaways, next steps\n177: \n178: ## Widget Type Preferences (Adjust Based on Course Length)\n179: \n180: For **longer courses (10+ scenes)**, consider:\n181: - Multiple simulations for varied experiments\n182: - At least one game for fun practice\n183: - Use diagrams sparingly (prefer interactive diagrams)\n184: \n185: For **shorter courses (<10 scenes)**:\n186: - Focus on quality over quantity\n187: - One well-designed widget may be sufficient\n188: - Slides can provide context when widget variety is limited\n189: \n190: **Example distribution for 10 scenes:**\n191: - 2 simulations\n192: - 1-2 games\n193: - 1 diagram (if relevant)\n194: - code/visualization3d as needed\n195: \n196: **Flexibility is encouraged**                 "text": "# Interactive Mode Outline Generator\n\nYou are a professional course designer specializing in interactive, hands-on learning experiences.\n\n## Core Task\n\nTransform user requirements into an **interactive-first** course structure:\n- **Prefer interactive scenes** (widgets) over slides for hands-on learning\n- Use **slides for introductions, summaries, and conceptual frameworks**\n- Adjust the balance based on course length and subject matter\n\n---\n\n## Language Inference\n\nInfer the course language from all available signals and produce:\n\n1. **`languageDirective`** (required): A 2-5 sentence instruction covering teaching language, terminology handling, and cross-language situations.\n2. **`languageNote`** (optional, per scene): Only when a scene's language handling differs from the course-level directive.\n\n### Decision rules (apply in order)\n\n1. **Explicit language request wins**: \"请用英文教我\", \"teach me in Chinese\", \"用中英双语\" → follow directly.\n\n2. **Requirement language = teaching language** (default): The language the user writes in is the strongest implicit signal.\n\n3. **Foreign language learning → teach in the user's native language, NOT the target language**:\n   - \"I want to learn Chinese\" → teach in **English**\n   - \"我想学日语\" → teach in **Chinese**\n   - Exception: advanced learners (TEM-8/专八, DALF C1, JLPT N1) aiming for native-level fluency → teach in the **target language** for immersion.\n\n4. **Cross-language PDF → requirement language wins**: Translate/explain document content in the teaching language. Never let the PDF language override the requirement language.\n\n5. **Proxy requests (parent/teacher/tutor) → consider the learner's context**: A parent writing in Chinese for a child in IB/AP → teach in **English**. A Chinese teacher designing a Japanese reading lesson → teach in **Chinese** with Japanese as learning material.\n\n6. **Audience-appropriate language**: For children or beginners, explicitly specify simple vocabulary and supportive scaffolding in the directive.\n\n### Terminology\n\n- **Programming / product names** (Python, Docker, ComfyUI): keep in English.\n- **Science / academic terms** with standard translations: use the teaching language's translation.\n- **Emerging tech terms** (AI/ML): show bilingually.\n- **User's explicit request** about terminology overrides the above defaults.\n\n### Course Title\n\nProduce a **`courseTitle`** (required): a concise, human-readable name for the **entire course**. This becomes the course's display name, so it must be short and scannable — never the raw requirement text.\n\n- **Length**: ≤ 30 characters (roughly one short phrase). Hard cap; if the concept is long, compress it.\n- **Language**: write it in the **inferred teaching language** (same language `languageDirective` targets).\n- **Style**: a noun phrase summarizing the topic — e.g. \"抛体运动实战\", \"Hands-on Recursion\", \"太阳系探索\". Not a sentence, not a question.\n- **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n- If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n\n---\n\n## Widget Types\n\n### 1. Simulation Widget (`simulation`)\nCanvas-based simulations for physics, chemistry, biology, engineering.\n\n**Best for:**\n- Physics: projectile motion, forces, circuits, waves\n- Chemistry: molecular structure, reactions, pH\n- Biology: cell processes, ecosystems\n- Math: function graphing, probability\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `concept`: The scientific concept name\n- `keyVariables`: List of controllable parameters (e.g., [\"angle\", \"velocity\", \"mass\"])\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- Mobile-first layout: Controls MUST NOT overlap canvas on mobile\n- Proper state management: Reset button MUST return to initial state\n- Touch-friendly: 44px minimum touch targets\n\n### 2. Interactive Diagram (`diagram`)\nExplorable flowcharts, mind maps, system diagrams.\n\n**Best for:**\n- Processes and workflows\n- System architectures\n- Decision trees\n- Concept maps\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `diagramType`: \"flowchart\" | \"mindmap\" | \"hierarchy\" | \"system\"\n- `nodeCount`: Approximate number of nodes\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- First node VISIBLE on load (no blank screen)\n- HIGH CONTRAST: Light nodes on dark background or vice versa\n- Add ICONS to each node for visual interest\n- Color-code different node types\n- Include animations for node reveal\n\n### 3. Code Playground (`code`)\nLive code editor with execution and test cases.\n\n**Best for:**\n- Programming concepts\n- Algorithm visualization\n- Data structure operations\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `language`: \"python\" | \"javascript\" | \"typescript\" | \"java\" | \"cpp\"\n- `challengeType`: Type of coding challenge\n\n### 4. Game Widget (`game`)\n**IMPORTANT: Create FUN games, NOT boring quizzes!**\n\n**Best for:**\n- Physics/action games: Control thrust, aim, timing to achieve goals\n- Drag-and-drop puzzles: Sort, arrange, build\n- Strategy games: Decision-based challenges\n- Interactive simulations as games: Player controls parameters\n\n**AVOID:**\n- Plain multiple-choice quizzes (boring!)\n- Quiz disguised as games\n- Non-interactive simulations\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `gameType`: \"action\" | \"puzzle\" | \"strategy\" | \"card\" (prefer \"action\" over \"quiz\")\n- `challenge`: Description of what player DOES (not just answers)\n- `playerControls`: What the player controls (e.g., [\"thrust\", \"angle\"])\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- Player MUST control something meaningful\n- Success depends on PLAYER SKILL, not just knowledge\n- If simulation is present, it MUST be interactive gameplay\n- Learning happens through PLAY, not through questions\n- Game should be FUN enough to replay\n\n### 5. 3D Visualization (`visualization3d`)\nInteractive 3D scenes using Three.js for immersive learning experiences.\n\n**Best for:**\n- Molecular structures: Atoms, bonds, molecules\n- Solar systems: Planets, orbits, scale visualization\n- Anatomy: Organs, body systems, cross-sections\n- 3D Geometry: Shapes, nets, transformations\n- Physics in 3D: Forces, vectors, trajectories\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `visualizationType`: \"molecular\" | \"solar\" | \"anatomy\" | \"geometry\" | \"physics\" | \"custom\"\n- `objects`: List of 3D objects to create (e.g., [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"moon\"])\n- `interactions`: List of interactive controls (e.g., [\"orbit\", \"speed_slider\"])\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation\n- Proper lighting (ambient + directional)\n- Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n- Performance-optimized geometry\n- Smooth animations with requestAnimationFrame\n\n## Widget Selection Guide\n\n| Content Type | Recommended Widget | Reason |\n|--------------|-------------------|--------|\n| Physics formulas/concepts | simulation | Let students EXPERIMENT with variables |\n| Step-by-step processes | diagram | Visual walkthrough with reveal |\n| Programming concepts | code | Hands-on coding practice |\n| Practice/challenge | game (action) | FUN gameplay to apply knowledge |\n| Concept relationships | diagram | Visual connections |\n| Force/motion problems | simulation + game | Simulate physics, gamify the challenge |\n| 3D structures/models | visualization3d | Immersive 3D exploration |\n| Molecular/anatomical models | visualization3d | Spatial understanding in 3D |\n| Solar system/astronomy | visualization3d | Scale and orbit visualization |\n\n## Widget Distribution Guidelines\n\n1. **Opening scenes (slides)**: Introduction, learning objectives, context setting\n2. **Middle scenes (widgets)**: Hands-on exploration, practice, discovery\n3. **Transition scenes (slides)**: Concept explanations between widgets\n4. **Closing scenes (slides)**: Summary, key takeaways, next steps\n\n## Widget Type Preferences (Adjust Based on Course Length)\n\nFor **longer courses (10+ scenes)**, consider:\n- Multiple simulations for varied experiments\n- At least one game for fun practice\n- Use diagrams sparingly (prefer interactive diagrams)\n\nFor **shorter courses (<10 scenes)**:\n- Focus on quality over quantity\n- One well-designed widget may be sufficient\n- Slides can provide context when widget variety is limited\n\n**Example distribution for 10 scenes:**\n- 2 simulations\n- 1-2 games\n- 1 diagram (if relevant)\n- code/visualization3d as needed\n\n**Flexibility is encouraged** — match widgets to content needs, not rigid formulas.\n\n## Example Outline with Good Game Design\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n  \"type\": \"interactive\",\n  \"title\": \"精准着陆挑战\",\n  \"description\": \"控制飞船推力，安全着陆到目标区域\",\n  \"keyPoints\": [\"调节推力大小\", \"观察速度变化\", \"实现软着陆\"],\n  \"order\": 3,\n  \"widgetType\": \"game\",\n  \"widgetOutline\": {\n    \"gameType\": \"action\",\n    \"challenge\": \"控制推力使飞船以低于5m/s的速度着陆\",\n    \"playerControls\": [\"thrust_slider\"],\n    \"physicsConcept\": \"F=ma, thrust counteracts gravity\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Note:** This is a REAL game where player controls thrust, not a quiz asking \"What thrust is needed?\"\n\n## Example: 3D Visualization Outline\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"scene_3\",\n  \"type\": \"interactive\",\n  \"title\": \"太阳系探索\",\n  \"description\": \"交互式3D太阳系模型，探索行星轨道和相对大小\",\n  \"keyPoints\": [\"行星轨道运动\", \"行星相对大小\", \"太阳系结构\"],\n  \"order\": 3,\n  \"widgetType\": \"visualization3d\",\n  \"widgetOutline\": {\n    \"visualizationType\": \"solar\",\n    \"objects\": [\"sun\", \"mercury\", \"venus\", \"earth\", \"mars\", \"jupiter\"],\n    \"interactions\": [\"orbit\", \"speed_slider\", \"planet_selector\"]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n{{#if imageEnabled}}\n{{snippet:image-instructions}}\n{{/if}}\n\n{{#if \"courseTitle\": \"<concise course name, ≤30 chars, in the teaching language>\",\n  \"outlines\": [ /* array of scene objects */ ]\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- **Never** return a bare array.               "newString": "- **Do NOT** include: quotes, numbering, leading emojis, the teacher's name/role, or words like \"Course\"/\"课程\"/\"A course about\".\n- If the requirement is already a crisp title, you may reuse it (trimmed to the limit). If it is a long prompt, distill it to its essence.\n\n---\n\n## Design Directive Inference\n\nProduce a **`designDirective`** (required): the visual identity the **entire course** will follow. Every scene (slides, widgets, animations) later receives your directive as a hard constraint, so make it concrete enough to enforce.\n\nStructure:\n\n```json\n\"designDirective\": {\n  \"concept\": \"one 10-20 word visual metaphor that unifies the course\",\n  \"palette\": [\"#hex\", \"#hex\", \"#hex\"],\n  \"background\": \"dark\" | \"paper\" | \"light\",\n  \"motionPersonality\": \"calm\" | \"energetic\" | \"playful\" | \"cinematic\"\n}\n```\n\n**Inference rules (apply in order):**\n\n1. **Explicit style request wins**: \"让孩子觉得像游戏\" → `playful` + bright palette; \"高端商务\" → `cinematic` + dark/monochrome.\n2. **Domain defaults**: programming/AI/data → `dark` background with one strong accent (amber, electric blue) + `calm`; kids/language/k-12 → `paper` (warm cream) with saturated primaries + `playful`; medicine/law/finance → `light` or `dark` restrained duotone + `calm`; film/space/psychology storytelling → `dark`/`cinematic`.\n3. **Palette discipline**: exactly 2-5 hex colors. Pair a dominant with 1-2 accents and a functional gray family. Never more than 5.\n4. **`concept`** must be a metaphor the scenes can literally draw (e.g., \"teaching recursion as Russian nesting dolls\", \"把函数视作输入加工的流水线机器\"). Avoid vague words like \"modern\", \"professional\" alone.\n\n---\n\n## Intro Scene (MANDATORY — every course)\n\nThe **first scene** must always be `\"type\": \"interactive\"` with `\"widgetType\": \"animation-explainer\"` — a 25-45 second pure motion-graphics intro that hooks the learner before any teaching. It does not count against the widget quota.\n\nRequirements:\n\n- `title`: the course hook (NOT \"Introduction\") — e.g. \"为什么递归会停？\" / \"Why Light Bends\".\n- `description`: one sentence naming the attention hook (paradox, surprise, question).\n- `keyPoints`: exactly 4 beats in display order — HOOK → TEASE (3-4 keyword cards) → SPARK (the signature animated infographic) → TITLE (course title lock-up).\n- `widgetOutline`: `{ \"concept\": \"<what the animation shows>\", \"keyBeats\": [\"<beat 1, one short phrase>\", ... 4 beats], \"mood\": \"<e.g. 'curious, meteoric, cosmic'>\" }`.\n\nThis gives the course a cinematic cold open consistent with the design directive.",

              "newString": "### 5. 3D Visualization (`visualization3d`)\nInteractive 3D scenes using Three.js for immersive learning experiences.\n\n**Best for:**\n- Molecular structures: Atoms, bonds, molecules\n- Solar systems: Planets, orbits, scale visualization\n- Anatomy: Organs, body systems, cross-sections\n- 3D Geometry: Shapes, nets, transformations\n- Physics in 3D: Forces, vectors, trajectories\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `visualizationType`: \"molecular\" | \"solar\" | \"anatomy\" | \"geometry\" | \"physics\" | \"custom\"\n- `objects`: List of 3D objects to create (e.g., [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"moon\"])\n- `interactions`: List of interactive controls (e.g., [\"orbit\", \"speed_slider\"])\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation\n- Proper lighting (ambient + directional)\n- Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n- Performance-optimized geometry\n- Smooth animations with requestAnimationFrame\n\n### 6. Motion-Graphics Explainer (`animation-explainer`)\nA pure motion-graphics page that HOOKS the learner with animated typography, iconography, and a signature animated infographic — exactly the mandatory intro scene of every course. GSAP-driven phases (HOOK → TEASE → SPARK → TITLE), no narration narrator, no interactive controls beyond play/replay.\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `concept`: What the animation reveals (the hook payload)\n- `keyBeats`: The 4 beats in display order (one short phrase each)\n- `mood`: 2-3 mood adjectives that tune pacing, easing and composition\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- Deterministic timeline, not random: exact easing, phase labels, replay button\n- FIRST frame must be a composed poster frame, not a blank canvas\n- Honor the course design directive: its palette is the ONLY palette\n- Typography is a character: scale contrast, letter-spacing play, masked reveals",
              "oldString": "### 5. 3D Visualization (`visualization3d`)\nInteractive 3D scenes using Three.js for immersive learning experiences.\n\n**Best for:**\n- Molecular structures: Atoms, bonds, molecules\n- Solar systems: Planets, orbits, scale visualization\n- Anatomy: Organs, body systems, cross-sections\n- 3D Geometry: Shapes, nets, transformations\n- Physics in 3D: Forces, vectors, trajectories\n\n**Output in widgetOutline:**\n- `visualizationType`: \"molecular\" | \"solar\" | \"anatomy\" | \"geometry\" | \"physics\" | \"custom\"\n- `objects`: List of 3D objects to create (e.g., [\"sun\", \"earth\", \"moon\"])\n- `interactions`: List of interactive controls (e.g., [\"orbit\", \"speed_slider\"])\n\n**Design Principles:**\n- Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation\n- Proper lighting (ambient + directional)\n- Touch-friendly controls for mobile\n- Performance-optimized geometry\n- Smooth animations with requestAnimationFrame"

Infer it from the task domain (training/industrial safety → restrained high-contrast duotone, `calm`; the `concept` should be a literal workshop-control-room metaphor the scenes can draw). Keep the palette to 2-5 hex colors.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, produce 10-14 scenes.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, prefer 10-12 scenes by default.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, generate at least 10 scenes.\n - For suitable vocational tasks, generate no more than 14 scenes.\n",

                "text": "/**\n * Audio Provider Type Definitions\n *\n * Unified types for TTS (Text-to-Speech) and ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition)\n * with extensible architecture to support multiple providers.\n *\n * Currently Supported TTS Providers:\n * - OpenAI Whisper (https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/speech-to-text)\n * - Browser Native (Web Speech API, client-side only)\n * - Qwen ASR (DashScope API)\n * - Azure STT (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/speech-service/fast-transcription-create)\n *\n * Future Provider Support (extensible):\n * - Deepgram ASR (https://developers.deepgram.com/docs)\n *\n * HOW TO ADD A NEW PROVIDER:\n *\n * Step 1: Add provider ID to the union type\n *   - For TTS: Add to TTSProviderId below\n *   - For ASR: Add to ASRProviderId below\n *\n * Step 2: Add provider configuration to constants.ts\n *   - Define provider metadata (name, icon, voices, formats, etc.)\n *   - Add to TTS_PROVIDERS or ASR_PROVIDERS registry\n *\n * Step 3: Implement provider logic in tts-providers.ts or asr-providers.ts\n *   - Add 'elevenlabs-tts' to TTSProviderId union type\n * 2. In constants.ts:\n *    TTS_PROVIDERS['elevenlabs-tts'] = {\n *      id: 'elevenlabs-tts',\n *      name: 'ElevenLabs',\n *      requiresApiKey: true,\n *      defaultBaseUrl: 'https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1',\n *      icon: '/elevenlabs.svg',\n *      voices: [...],\n *      supportedFormats: ['mp3', 'pcm'],\n *      speedRange: { min: 0.5, max: 2.0, default: 1.0 }\n *    }\n * 3. In i18n.ts:\n *    providerElevenLabsTTS: 'ElevenLabs TTS' / 'ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech'\n */\n\n// ============================================================================\n// TTS (Text-to-Speech) Types\n// ============================================================================\n\n/**\n * TTS Provider IDs\n *\n * Add new TTS providers here as union members.\n * Keep in sync with TTS_PROVIDERS registry in constants.ts\n */\nexport type BuiltInTTSProviderId =\n  | 'openai-tts'\n  | 'azure-tts'\n  | 'glm-tts'\n  | 'qwen-tts'\n  | 'voxcpm-tts'\n  | 'doubao-tts'\n  | 'elevenlabs-tts'\n  | 'minimax-tts'\n  | 'google-tts'\n  | 'lemonade-tts'\n  | 'browser-native-tts';\n\nexport type TTSProviderId = BuiltInTTSProviderId | `custom-tts-${string}`;\n\n/**\n * Voice information for TTS\n */\nexport interface TTSVoiceInfo {\n  id: string;\n  name: string;\n  language: string;\n  localeName?: string; // Language name in its native script (e.g., \"中文（简体，中国）\", \"日本語\")\n  gender?: 'male' | 'female' | 'neutral';\n  description?: string;\n  /** Model IDs this voice is compatible with. Undefined = all models. */\n  compatibleModels?: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * TTS Provider Configuration\n */\nexport interface TTSProviderConfig {\n  id: TTSProviderId;\n  name: string;\n  requiresApiKey: boolean;\n  defaultBaseUrl?: string;\n  icon?: string;\n  /**\n   * Declared exclusion from the agent-facing voice catalog. A provider flagged\n   * here (e.g. a paid showcase whose presets must never be offered to the\n   * agent) is dropped from `list_voices` / `set_roster` binding validation\n   * even when it is served and keyed — an explicit mechanism, not \"no env so\n   * absent\". Session-registered clones of the provider remain bindable when a\n   * registration adapter is configured (see the agent catalog assembly).\n   */\n  excludeFromAgentVoiceCatalog?: boolean;\n  /**\n   * True when the provider has NO deployment default voice: its only\n   * synthesizable voices are the ones registered at runtime. Such a provider's\n   * registered voices stay in the catalog regardless of clone-synthesis\n   * capability, because they are the only voices that provider can produce.\n   */\n  requiresRegisteredVoice?: boolean;\n  /** Available models. Empty array means provider has no model concept (e.g. Azure, Browser Native). */\n  models: Array<{ id: string; name: string }>;\n  /** Default model ID used when user hasn't selected one. Empty string if no models. */\n  defaultModelId: string;\n  voices: TTSVoiceInfo[];\n  supportedFormats: string[]; // ['mp3', 'wav', 'opus', etc.]\n  speedRange?: {\n    min: number;\n    max: number;\n    default: number;\n  };\n  /**\n   * `false` when the provider ignores the requested speed, which locks the speed\n   * control in settings. Omitted means speed is supported; a missing\n   * `speedRange` does not imply the opposite.\n   */\n  supportsSpeed?: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * TTS Model Configuration for API calls\n */\nexport interface TTSModelConfig {\n  providerId: TTSProviderId;\n  modelId?: string;\n  apiKey?: string;\n  baseUrl?: string;\n  voice: string;\n  speed?: number;\n  format?: string;\n  providerOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  /**\n   * Cancel the provider request(s) when this signal aborts. The agent runtime\n   * threads the session cancel signal here so an in-flight synthesis fetch is\n   * aborted within seconds of a cancel, instead of wedging the session until a\n   * restart repairs it.\n   */\n  signal?: AbortSignal;\n  /**\n   * Server-side outbound address policy for this provider call. `true` marks a\n   * client-supplied BYOK `baseUrl`: the request is pinned to the strict public\n   * policy, so metadata, private, loopback and CGNAT targets are refused even\n   * when the operator enabled local networks. When unset (a server-managed or\n   * built-in default target) the adapter falls back to the process-wide\n   * `ALLOW_LOCAL_NETWORKS` behavior.\n   */\n  publicOnly?: boolean;\n  /**\n   * `true` when the provider is server-configured: its endpoint is operator\n   * configuration and may be on a local network without ALLOW_LOCAL_NETWORKS\n   * (cloud metadata stays refused). Set by the server, never from request\n   * input; an unmanaged provider's catalog default leaves it unset.\n   */\n  managed?: boolean;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) Types\n// ============================================================================\n\n/**\n * ASR Provider IDs\n *\n * Add new ASR providers here as union members.\n * Keep in sync with ASR_PROVIDERS registry in constants.ts\n */\nexport type BuiltInASRProviderId =\n  | 'openai-whisper'\n  | 'browser-native'\n  | 'qwen-asr'\n  | 'funasr-asr'\n  | 'lemonade-asr'\n  | 'azure-asr';\n\nexport type ASRProviderId = BuiltInASRProviderId | `custom-asr-${string}`;\n\n/**\n * ASR Provider Configuration\n */\nexport interface ASRProviderConfig {\n  id: ASRProviderId;\n  name: string;\n  requiresApiKey: boolean;\n  defaultBaseUrl?: string;\n  icon?: string;\n  models: Array<{ id: string; name: string }>;\n  defaultModelId: string;\n  supportedLanguages: string[];\n  supportedFormats: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * ASR Model Configuration for API calls\n */\nexport interface ASRModelConfig {\n  providerId: ASRProviderId;\n  modelId?: string;\n  apiKey?: string;\n  baseUrl?: string;\n  language?: string;\n  /**\n   * Server-side outbound address policy (see {@link TTSModelConfig.publicOnly}).\n   * A client-supplied BYOK `baseUrl` sets this so the strict public policy wins.\n   */\n  publicOnly?: boolean;\n  /** Server-configured provider (see {@link TTSModelConfig.managed}). */\n  managed?: boolean;\n}\n\n/** Returns true if the provider ID is a user-defined custom TTS provider. */\nexport function isCustomTTSProvider(id: string): boolean {\n  return typeof id === 'string' && id.startsWith('custom-tts-');\n}\n\n/** Returns true if the provider ID is a user-defined custom ASR provider. */\nexport function isCustomASRProvider(id: string): boolean {\n  return typeof id === 'string' && id.startsWith('custom-asr-');\n}",

Add the provider ID to TTSProviderId or ASRProviderId in types.ts\n * 2. Add provider configuration to TTS_PROVIDERS or ASR_PROVIDERS below\n * 3. Implement provider logic in tts-providers.ts or asr-providers.ts\n * 4. Add i18n translations in lib/i18n.ts\n *\n * Provider configuration should include:\n * - id: Unique identifier matching the type definition\n * - name: Display name for the provider\n * - requiresApiKey: Whether the provider needs an API key\n * - defaultBaseUrl: Default API endpoint (optional)",

                "text": "/**\n * Audio Provider Constants\n *\n * Registry of all TTS and ASR providers with their metadata.\n * Separated from tts-providers.ts and asr-providers.ts to avoid importing\n * Node.js libraries (like sharp, buffer) in client components.\n *\n * This file is client-safe and can be imported in both client and server components.\n *\n * To add a new provider:\n * 1. Add the provider ID to TTSProviderId or ASRProviderId in types.ts\n * 2. Add provider configuration to TTS_PROVIDERS or ASR_PROVIDERS below\n * 3. Implement provider logic in tts-providers.ts or asr-providers.ts\n * 4. Add i18n translations in lib/i18n.ts\n *\n * Provider configuration should include:\n * - id: Unique identifier matching the type definition\n * - name: Display name for the provider\n * - requiresApiKey: Whether the provider needs an API key\n * - defaultBaseUrl: Default API endpoint (optional)\n * - icon: Path to provider icon (optional)\n * - models: Available model choices (empty array if no model concept)\n * - defaultModelId: Default model ID (empty string if no models)\n * - voices: Array of available voices (TTS only)\n * - supportedFormats: Audio formats supported by the provider\n * - speedRange: Min/max/default speed settings (TTS only)\n * - supportedLanguages: Languages supported by the provider (ASR only)\n */\n\nimport type {\n  BuiltInTTSProviderId,\n  TTSProviderId,\n  TTSProviderConfig,\n  TTSVoiceInfo,\n  BuiltInASRProviderId,\n  ASRProviderId,\n  ASRProviderConfig,\n} from './types';\nimport { isCustomTTSProvider } from './types';\nimport {\n  VOXCPM_AUTO_VOICE,\n  VOXCPM_AUTO_VOICE_ID,\n  VOXCPM_TTS_PROVIDER_ID,\n  VOXCPM_VLLM_MODEL_ID,\n} from './voxcpm';\n\n/**\n * Default supported languages for custom OpenAI-compatible ASR providers.\n * A practical subset of commonly used languages + auto-detect.\n */\nexport const CUSTOM_ASR_DEFAULT_LANGUAGES = [\n  'auto',\n  'zh',\n  'en',\n  'ja',\n  'ko',\n  'es',\n  'fr',\n  'de',\n  'ru',\n  'ar',\n  'pt',\n  'it',\n  'hi',\n];\n\n/**\n * TTS Provider Registry\n *\n * Central registry for all TTS providers.\n * Keep in sync with TTSProviderId type definition.\n */\nexport const MINIMAX_TTS_MODELS = [\n  { id: 'speech-2.8-hd', name: 'Speech 2.8 HD' },\n  { id: 'speech-2.8-turbo', name: 'Speech 2.8 Turbo' },\n  { id: 'speech-2.6-hd', name: 'Speech 2.6 HD' },\n  { id: 'speech-2.6-turbo', name: 'Speech 2.6 Turbo' },\n  { id: 'speech-02-hd', name: 'Speech 02 HD' },\n  { id: 'speech-02-turbo', name: 'Speech 02 Turbo' },\n] as const;\n\nexport const DEFAULT_QWEN_TTS_VOICE_CLONE_MODEL = 'qwen3-tts-vc-2026-01-22';\n/** Client-visible VC model. Server-only overrides are resolved in provider-config. */\nexport const QWEN_TTS_VOICE_CLONE_MODEL = DEFAULT_QWEN_TTS_VOICE_CLONE_MODEL;\n\nexport function isQwenVoiceCloneModel(modelId?: string, configuredModelId?: string): boolean {\n  return (\n    !!modelId &&\n    (/-tts-vc(?:-|$)/iu.test(modelId) || (!!configuredModelId && modelId === configuredModelId))\n  );\n}\n\n/** A Qwen catalog voice is provider-owned and must never use the clone model. */\nexport function isQwenCatalogVoice(voiceId?: string): boolean {\n  return !!voiceId && TTS_PROVIDERS['qwen-tts'].voices.some((voice) => voice.id === voiceId);\n}\n\n/** A non-catalog Qwen voice ID is an enrolled clone; local profile storage is not authoritative. */\nexport function isQwenCloneVoice(voiceId?: string): boolean {\n  return !!voiceId && !isQwenCatalogVoice(voiceId);\n}\n\n/**\n * Enforce the client-side half of the model-follows-voice invariant. The server\n * maps the VC sentinel to its operator-resolved model and applies model pins.\n */\nexport function resolveTTSModelForVoice(\n  providerId: TTSProviderId,\n  voiceId: string,\n  requestedModelId?: string,\n): string | undefined {\n  if (providerId !== 'qwen-tts') return requestedModelId;\n  if (isQwenCloneVoice(voiceId)) return QWEN_TTS_VOICE_CLONE_MODEL;\n  return requestedModelId && !isQwenVoiceCloneModel(requestedModelId)\n    ? requestedModelId\n    : TTS_PROVIDERS['qwen-tts'].defaultModelId;\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a model can speak a voice: a catalogue voice that lists compatible\n * models (OpenAI's Marin and Cedar need gpt-4o-mini-tts) only on those; any\n * other voice (no such list, a clone, a user voice) on any model. Without a\n * model the provider's default model is meant.\n */\nexport function voiceServesModel(providerId: string, voiceId: string, modelId?: string): boolean {\n  const provider = TTS_PROVIDERS[providerId as BuiltInTTSProviderId];\n  const voice = provider?.voices.find((entry) => entry.id === voiceId);\n  if (!voice?.compatibleModels) return true;\n  const model = modelId || Object.values(customProviders) : [];\n  return [...builtIn, ...custom];\n}\n\n/**\n * Narrow an arbitrary string (e.g. from a persisted document or an imported\n * manifest, where the contract keeps providerId an open string) to a known\n * TTS provider id: a registered built-in provider or the user-defined\n * custom-provider namespace. Anything else must be treated as \"no voice\".\n */\nexport function isKnownTTSProviderId(id: string): id is TTSProviderId {\n  // Object.hasOwn, not `in`: prototype-chain keys ('toString', 'constructor',\n  // …) must not pass a whitelist built from an object literal.\n  return Object.hasOwn(TTS_PROVIDERS, id) || isCustomTTSProvider(id);\n}\n\n/**\n * Get TTS provider by ID (checks built-in first, then custom)\n */\nexport function getTTSProvider(\n  providerId: TTSProviderId,\n  customProviders?: Record<string, TTSProviderConfig>,\n): TTSProviderConfig | undefined {\n  if (Object.hasOwn(TTS_PROVIDERS, providerId)) {\n    return TTS_PROVIDERS[providerId as BuiltInTTSProviderId];\n  }\n  return customProviders?.[providerId];\n}\n\n/**\n * Models a user may pick manually in the UI. The Qwen voice-clone model is\n * excluded: it is never chosen by hand, only resolved implicitly from a picked\n * clone voice (model-follows-voice), so it must not appear in manual model\n * pickers while staying in the provider registry for voice-driven dispatch.\n */\nexport function getManuallySelectableTTSModels(\n  providerId: TTSProviderId,\n  customProviders?: Record<string, TTSProviderConfig>,\n): TTSProviderConfig['models'] {\n  const provider = getTTSProvider(providerId, customProviders);\n  return (provider?.models || []).filter((model) => !isQwenVoiceCloneModel(model.id));\n}\n\n/**\n * Get voices for a specific TTS provider\n */\nexport function getTTSVoices(\n  providerId: TTSProviderId,\n  customProviders?: Record<string, TTSProviderConfig>,\n): TTSVoiceInfo[] {\n  return getTTSProvider(providerId, customProviders)?.voices || [];\n}\n\n/**\n * Get all available ASR providers (built-in + custom)\n */\nexport function getAllASRProviders(\n  customProviders?: Record<string, ASRProviderConfig>,\n): ASRProviderConfig[] {\n  const builtIn = Object.values(ASR_PROVIDERS);\n  const custom = customProviders ? Object.values(customProviders) : [];\n  return [...builtIn, ...custom];\n}\n\n/**\n * Get ASR provider by ID (checks built-in first, then custom)\n */\nexport function getASRProvider(\n  providerId: ASRProviderId,\n  customProviders?: Record<string, ASRProviderConfig>,\n): ASRProviderConfig | undefined {\n  if (Object.hasOwn(ASR_PROVIDERS, providerId)) {\n    return ASR_PROVIDERS[providerId as BuiltInASRProviderId];\n  }\n  return customProviders?.[providerId];\n}\n\n/**\n * Get supported languages for a specific ASR provider\n */\nexport function getASRSupportedLanguages(\n  providerId: ASRProviderId,\n  customProviders?: Record<string, ASRProviderConfig>,\n): string[] {\n  return getASRProvider(providerId, customProviders)?.supportedLanguages || [];\n}",

                "text": "/**\n * TTS (Text-to-Speech) Provider Implementation\n *\n * Factory pattern for routing TTS requests to appropriate provider implementations.\n * Follows the same architecture as lib/ai/providers.ts for consistency.\n *\n * Currently Supported Providers:\n * - OpenAI TTS: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/text-to-speech\n * - Azure TTS: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/text-to-speech\n * - GLM TTS: https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/models/sound-and-video/glm-tts\n * - Qwen TTS: https://bailian.console.aliyun.com/\n * - MiniMax TTS: https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/speech-t2a-http\n * - Doubao TTS: https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6561/1257543\n * - ElevenLabs TTS: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert\n * - Google Gemini TTS: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation\n * - Browser Native: Web Speech API (client-side only)\n *\n * HOW TO ADD A NEW PROVIDER:\n *\n * 1. Add provider ID to TTSProviderId in lib/audio/types.ts\n *    Example: | 'elevenlabs-tts'\n *\n * 2. Add provider configuration to lib/audio/constants.ts\n *    Example:\n *    'elevenlabs-tts': {\n *      id: 'elevenlabs-tts',\n *      name: 'ElevenLabs',\n *      requiresApiKey: true,\n *      defaultBaseUrl: 'https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1',\n *      icon: '/logos/elevenlabs.svg',\n *      voices: [...],\n *      supportedFormats: ['mp3', 'pcm'],\n *      speedRange: { min: 0.5, max: 2.0, default: 1.0 }\n *    }\n *\n * 3. Implement provider function in this file\n *    Pattern: async function generateXxxTTS(config, text): Promise<TTSGenerationResult>\n *    - Validate config and build API request\n *    - Handle API authentication (apiKey, headers)\n *    - Convert provider-specific parameters (voice, speed, format)\n *    - Return { audio: Uint8Array, format: string }\n *\n *    Example:\n *    async function generateElevenLabsTTS(\n *      config: TTSModelConfig,\n *      text: string\n *    ): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n *      const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['elevenlabs-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n *\n *      const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/text-to-speech/${config.voice}`, {\n *        method: 'POST',\n *        headers: {\n *          'xi-api-key': config.apiKey!,\n *          'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n *        },\n *        body: JSON.stringify({\n *          text,\n *          model_id: 'eleven_multilingual_v2',\n *          voice_settings: {\n *            stability: 0.5,\n *            similarity_boost: 0.75,\n *          }\n *        }),\n *      });\n *\n *      if (!response.ok) {\n *        throw new Error(`ElevenLabs TTS API error: ${response.statusText}`);\n *      }\n *\n *      const arrayBuffer = await response.arrayBuffer();\n *      return {\n *        audio: new Uint8Array(arrayBuffer),\n *        format: 'mp3',\n *      };\n *    }\n *\n * 4. Add case to generateTTS() switch statement\n *    case 'elevenlabs-tts':\n *      return await generateElevenLabsTTS(config, text);\n *\n * 5. Add i18n translations in lib/i18n.ts\n *    providerElevenLabsTTS: { zh: 'ElevenLabs TTS', en: 'ElevenLabs TTS' }\n *\n * Error Handling Patterns:\n * - Always validate API key if requiresApiKey is true\n * - Throw descriptive errors for API failures\n * - Include response.statusText or error messages from API\n * - For client-only providers (browser-native), throw error directing to client-side usage\n *\n * API Call Patterns:\n * - Direct API: Use fetch with appropriate headers and body format (recommended for better encoding support)\n * - SSML: For Azure-like providers requiring SSML markup\n * - URL-based: For providers returning audio URL (download in second step)\n */\n\nimport type { TTSModelConfig } from './types';\nimport { isCustomTTSProvider } from './types';\nimport {\n  isQwenCloneVoice,\n  resolveTTSModelForVoice,\n  TTS_PROVIDERS,\n  DEFAULT_TTS_VOICES,\n} from './constants';\nimport { downloadAudio, QwenVoiceCloneError, synthesizeQwenVoiceClone } from './qwen-voice-clone';\nimport { evictQwenVoiceRegistrationMemo } from './qwen-voice-clone-registration';\nimport { splitConcatenatedJsonObjects } from './json-stream';\nimport {\n  VOXCPM_VLLM_MODEL_ID,\n  VOXCPM_AUTO_VOICE_ID,\n  normalizeVoxCPMBackend,\n  type VoxCPMProviderOptions,\n} from './voxcpm';\nimport { createLogger } from '@/lib/logger';\nimport {\n  audioEndpointPolicy,\n  audioProviderFetch,\n  type AudioEndpointTarget,\n} from '@/lib/server/audio-provider-fetch';\nimport { ProviderQuotaExhaustedError } from '@/lib/server/provider-quota';\nimport { appAttributionHeaders } from '@/lib/config/app-attribution';",

charset=utf-8',\n      },\n      body: JSON.stringify({\n        text,\n        model_id: config.modelId || 'eleven_multilingual_v2',\n        voice_settings: {\n          stability: 0.5,\n          similarity_boost: 0.75,\n          speed: clampedSpeed,\n        },\n      }),\n      signal,\n    },\n  );\n\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    throwIfTtsRateLimited('ElevenLabs', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n    throw new Error(`ElevenLabs TTS API error: ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n  }\n\n  return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'ElevenLabs', requestedFormat);\n}\n\n// Re-export from constants for convenience\nexport { getAllTTSProviders, getTTSProvider, getTTSVoices } from './constants';\n\n/**\n * Doubao TTS 2.0 implementation (Volcengine Seed-TTS 2.0).\n *\n * Two auth modes, distinguished by the API key shape — Volcengine exposes\n * Seed-TTS as two separate products that do NOT share credentials or endpoints\n * (verified: a plan key 401s on the normal endpoint, and the plan endpoint\n * rejects Bearer auth):\n *  - Standalone speech console: `appId:accessKey` → normal endpoint\n *    (.../api/v3/tts/unidirectional) with `X-Api-App-Id` + `X-Api-Access-Key`.\n *  - Ark Agent Plan: a single `ark-...` plan key → plan endpoint\n *    (.../api/plan/tts/unidirectional, carried in config.baseUrl) with\n *    `X-Api-Key`.             "metadata": {
              "preview": "/**\n * Localized display names for the built-in audio providers.\n *\n * The `name` field in `ASR_PROVIDERS` / `TTS_PROVIDERS` is a registry label, not\n * a UI string: several are written in Chinese (`浏览器原生 ASR (Web Speech API)`,\n * `Qwen ASR (阿里云百炼)`). Rendering it directly leaks Chinese into every other\n * locale, so any surface that shows a provider to the user must resolve the\n * name through i18n instead.\n *\n * Kept here rather than in a component so the settings dialog and the\n * generation toolbar cannot drift apart on what a provider is called.\n */\n\nimport type { ASRProviderId, TTSProviderId } from './types';\n\nconst ASR_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS: Record<string, string> = {\n  'openai-whisper': 'settings.providerOpenAIWhisper',\n  'browser-native': 'settings.providerBrowserNative',\n  'qwen-asr': 'settings.providerQwenASR',\n  'azure-asr': 'settings.providerAzureASR',",
              "truncated": false,
              "loaded": [],
              "display": {
                "type": "file",
                "path": "/Volumes/Kingston/Development/Dev_Projects/alostad-creator/OpenMAIC/lib/audio/provider-display.ts",
                "text": "/**\n * Localized display names for the built-in audio providers.\n *\n * The `name` field in `ASR_PROVIDERS` / `TTS_PROVIDERS` is a registry label, not\n * a UI string: several are written in Chinese (`浏览器原生 ASR (Web Speech API)`,\n * `Qwen ASR (阿里云百炼)`). Rendering it directly leaks Chinese into every other\n * locale, so any surface that shows a provider to the user must resolve the\n * name through i18n instead.\n *\n * Kept here rather than in a component so the settings dialog and the\n * generation toolbar cannot drift apart on what a provider is called.\n */\n\nimport type { ASRProviderId, TTSProviderId } from './types';\n\nconst ASR_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS: Record<string, string> = {\n  'openai-whisper': 'settings.providerOpenAIWhisper',\n  'browser-native': 'settings.providerBrowserNative',\n  'qwen-asr': 'settings.providerQwenASR',\n  'azure-asr': 'settings.providerAzureASR',\n  'funasr-asr': 'settings.providerFunASRASR',\n  'lemonade-asr': 'settings.providerLemonadeASR',\n};\n\nconst TTS_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS: Record<string, string> = {\n  'openai-tts': 'settings.providerOpenAITTS',\n  'azure-tts': 'settings.providerAzureTTS',\n  'glm-tts': 'settings.providerGLMTTS',\n  'qwen-tts': 'settings.providerQwenTTS',\n  'voxcpm-tts': 'settings.providerVoxCPMTTS',\n  'doubao-tts': 'settings.providerDoubaoTTS',\n  'elevenlabs-tts': 'settings.providerElevenLabsTTS',\n  'minimax-tts': 'settings.providerMiniMaxTTS',\n  'google-tts': 'settings.providerGoogleTTS',\n  'lemonade-tts': 'settings.providerLemonadeTTS',\n  'browser-native-tts': 'settings.providerBrowserNativeTTS',\n};\n\n/**\n * Translate a built-in ASR provider's name. Unknown ids (custom providers,\n * which carry their own user-supplied name) fall back to `fallback`, then to\n * the id, so a caller never renders an empty label.\n */\nexport function resolveASRProviderName(\n  providerId: ASRProviderId | string,\n  t: (key: string) => string,\n  fallback?: string,\n): string {\n  const key = ASR_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS[providerId];\n  return key ? t(key) : fallback || providerId;\n}\n\n/** TTS counterpart of {@link resolveASRProviderName}. */\nexport function resolveTTSProviderName(\n  providerId: TTSProviderId | string,\n  t: (key: string) => string,\n  fallback?: string,\n): string {\n  const key = TTS_PROVIDER_NAME_KEYS[providerId];\n  return key ? t(key) : fallback || providerId;\n}",
                "lineStart": 1,
                "lineEnd": 61,

              }

              "newString": "// Re-export from constants for convenience\nexport { getAllTTSProviders, getTTSProvider, getTTSVoices } from './constants';\n\n/**\n * Fish Audio TTS implementation (https://docs.fish.audio/text-to-speech/api).\n *\n * - `POST {baseUrl}/tts` (default baseUrl `https://api.fish.audio/v1`), Bearer\n *   auth, and the model is carried in a `model` HEADER (s2.1-pro default;\n *   s2.1-pro-free, s2-pro, drama-3, s1 are the other routes).\n * - `reference_id` is the voice-model ID from a fish.audio voice page URL.\n *   The `default` registry voice is the sentinel for the service default\n *   voice (verified: the official quickstart omits `reference_id` entirely).\n * - Binary audio response (mp3/wav/opus/pcm).\n */\nasync function generateFishAudioTTS(\n  config: TTSModelConfig,\n  text: string,\n  signal: AbortSignal,\n): Promise<TTSGenerationResult> {\n  const baseUrl = config.baseUrl || TTS_PROVIDERS['fish-tts'].defaultBaseUrl;\n  const requestedFormat = config.format || 'mp3';\n  const format = ['mp3', 'wav', 'opus', 'pcm'].includes(requestedFormat) ? requestedFormat : 'mp3';\n\n  const body: Record<string, unknown> = { text, format };\n  if (config.voice && config.voice !== 'default') {\n    body.reference_id = config.voice;\n  }\n  const speed = config.speed && config.speed > 0 ? Math.min(2.0, Math.max(0.5, config.speed)) : 1.0;\n  if (speed !== 1.0) {\n    body.prosody = { speed };\n  }\n\n  const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/tts`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: {\n      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey!}`,\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n      // Fish routes the backend model through a plain `model` header, not the body.\n      model: config.modelId || TTS_PROVIDERS['fish-tts'].defaultModelId,\n    },\n    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n    signal,\n  });\n\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    throwIfTtsRateLimited('Fish Audio', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n    throw new Error(`Fish Audio TTS API error (${response.status}): ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n  }\n\n  return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'Fish Audio', requestedFormat);\n}",

Math.min(2.0, Math.max(0.5, config.speed)) : 1.0;\n+  if (speed !== 1.0) {\n+    body.prosody = { speed };\n+  }\n+\n+  const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/tts`, {\n+    method: 'POST',\n+    headers: {\n+      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey!}`,\n+      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n+      // Fish routes the backend model through a plain `model` header, not the body.\n+      model: config.modelId || TTS_PROVIDERS['fish-tts'].defaultModelId,\n+    },\n+    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n+    signal,\n+  });\n+\n+  if (!response.ok) {\n+    throwIfTtsRateLimited('Fish Audio', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n+    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n+    throw new Error(`Fish Audio TTS API error (${response.status}): ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n+  }\n+\n+  return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'Fish Audio', requestedFormat);\n+}\n+\n+/**\n  * Doubao TTS 2.0 implementation (Volcengine Seed-TTS 2.0).\n  *\n  * Two auth modes, distinguished by the API key shape — Volcengine exposes\n  * Seed-TTS as two separate products that do NOT share credentials or endpoints\n",

Math.min(2.0, Math.max(0.5, config.speed)) : 1.0;\n+  if (speed !== 1.0) {\n+    body.prosody = { speed };\n+  }\n+\n+  const response = await ttsFetch(config, `${baseUrl}/tts`, {\n+    method: 'POST',\n+    headers: {\n+      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey!}`,\n+      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n+      // Fish routes the backend model through a plain `model` header, not the body.\n+      model: config.modelId || TTS_PROVIDERS['fish-tts'].defaultModelId,\n+    },\n+    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n+    signal,\n+  });\n+\n+  if (!response.ok) {\n+    throwIfTtsRateLimited('Fish Audio', response.status, response.headers?.get('retry-after'));\n+    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => response.statusText);\n+    throw new Error(`Fish Audio TTS API error (${response.status}): ${errorText || response.statusText}`);\n+  }\n+\n+  return await validateTTSAudioResponse(response, 'Fish Audio', requestedFormat);\n+}\n+\n+/**\n  * Doubao TTS 2.0 implementation (Volcengine Seed-TTS 2.0).\n  *\n  * Two auth modes, distinguished by the API key shape — Volcengine exposes\n  * Seed-TTS as two separate products that do NOT share credentials or endpoints\n",

                "text": "import { appAttributionHeaders } from '@/lib/config/app-attribution';\nimport { pcmS16leMonoToWav } from './pcm-wav';\n\nconst log = createLogger('TTSProviders');\n\n/**\n * for a server-configured\n * provider, the operator policy for an unmanaged provider's default endpoint.\n */\nfunction ttsFetch(\n  target: AudioEndpointTarget | undefined,\n  url: string,\n  init: Uint8Array;\n  format: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Thrown when a TTS provider returns a rate-limit / concurrency-quota error.\n * Allows downstream consumers to distinguish rate-limit errors from other TTS failures.\n *\n * TODO: The API route currently catches all errors uniformly as GENERATION_FAILED.\n * This class enables future retry/backoff logic without changing the throw sites.\n */\nexport class TTSRateLimitError extends Error {\n  /** Milliseconds from a `Retry-After` header, when the provider sent one. */\n  readonly retryAfterMs?: number;\n\n  constructor(\n    public readonly provider: string,\n    message: string,\n    retryAfterMs?: number,\n    options?: ErrorOptions,\n  ) {\n    super(message, options);\n    this.name = 'TTSRateLimitError';\n    if (retryAfterMs !== undefined && Number.isFinite(retryAfterMs) && retryAfterMs > 0) {\n      this.retryAfterMs = retryAfterMs;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/** Neutral identity for ordinary Qwen TTS failures (never VC-branded). => void, name: string) => (\n    <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n      <Label className=\"text-sm\">{label}</Label>\n      <div className=\"relative\">\n        <Input\n          name={name}\n          aria-label={name}\n          type={show ? 'text' : 'password'}\n          autoComplete=\"new-password\"\n          autoCapitalize=\"none\"\n          autoCorrect=\"off\"\n          spellCheck={false}\n          placeholder={t('settings.enterApiKey')}\n          value={value}\n          onChange={(e) => set(e.target.value)}\n          onBlur={() => void commit()}\n          className=\"font-mono text-sm pr-10\"\n        />\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={() => setShow(!show)}\n          className=\"absolute right-2 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground\"\n        >\n          {show ? <EyeOff className=\"h-4 w-4\" /> : <Eye className=\"h-4 w-4\" />}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n  return (\n    <>\n      {field(t('settings.doubaoAppId'), appId, setAppId, 'tts-app-id-doubao-tts')}\n      {field(t('settings.doubaoAccessKey'), accessKey, setAccessKey, 'tts-access-key-doubao-tts')}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * A text-to-speech service: its key (write-only), the user's narration speed,\n * a spoken test on the server with the saved configuration, its models, and\n * the voices a user makes for voice-design providers.\n */\n/** Path each built-in TTS service calls under its base URL, for the request URL hint. */\nexport function ttsEndpointPath(providerId: string): string {\n  switch (providerId) {\n    case 'openai-tts':\n    case 'glm-tts':\n    case 'lemonade-tts':\n      return '/audio/speech';\n    case 'azure-tts':\n      return '/cognitiveservices/v1';\n    case 'qwen-tts':\n      return '/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation';\n    case 'elevenlabs-tts':\n      return '/text-to-speech';\n    case 'doubao-tts':\n      return '/unidirectional';\n    case 'google-tts':\n      return '/interactions';\n    default:\n      return '';\n  }\n}\n\nexport function TTSSettings({ view, apply, entry }: ServicePanelProps) {\n  const { t, locale } = useI18n();\n\n  const ttsSpeed = useSettingsStore((state) => state.ttsSpeed);\n  const setTTSSpeed = useSettingsStore((state) => state.setTTSSpeed);\n  const ttsVoice = useSettingsStore((state) => state.ttsVoice);\n  const ttsVoiceProviderId = useSettingsStore((state) => state.ttsVoiceProviderId);\n\n  const providerId = entry.registryId;\n  const ttsProvider = TTS_PROVIDERS[providerId as BuiltInTTSProviderId];\n  const isBrowser = providerId === 'browser-native-tts';\n  const isVoxCPM = providerId === VOXCPM_TTS_PROVIDER_ID;\n  const isDoubao = providerId === 'doubao-tts';\n  const editable =\n    (entry.state === 'workspace' || entry.state === 'available') &&\n    !isBrowser &&\n    !!ttsProvider?.requiresApiKey;\n  const use = rootUse(view, 'tts', entry.id);\n  const manuallySelectableModels = getManuallySelectableTTSModels(\n    providerId as BuiltInTTSProviderId,\n  );\n\n  // The voice the test speaks with: the user's while this service is the\n  // workspace's narration, else the service's own default.\n  const capabilities = useMemo(() => modelCapabilities(view), [view]);\n  const selection = useMemo(\n    () =>\n      ttsSelection(capabilities, {\n        voice: ttsVoice,\n        providerId: ttsVoiceProviderId,\n        speed: ttsSpeed,\n      }),\n    [capabilities, ttsVoice, ttsVoiceProviderId, ttsSpeed],\n  );\n  const effectiveVoice =\n    use.inUse && selection ? selection.voice : defaultVoiceFor(providerId, use.modelId);\n  const cloneSpeedDisabled = providerId === 'qwen-tts' && isQwenCloneVoice(effectiveVoice);\n  const configured = entry.state === 'deployment' || entry.state === 'workspace' || isBrowser;\n  // A service that needs no key (the browser's own speech) can be made the\n  // workspace's narration here: it is added first when it is not saved yet.\n  const keyless = !ttsProvider?.requiresApiKey && entry.state !== 'server-only';\n  const [assigning, setAssigning] = useState(false);\n  const makeNarration = async () => {\n    setAssigning(true);\n    try {\n      reportApply(await assignService(apply, view, entry, 'tts'), t);\n    } finally {\n      setAssigning(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const [testText, setTestText] = useState(t('settings.ttsTestTextDefault'));\n  const [testStatus, setTestStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'testing' | 'success' | 'error'>('idle');\n  const [testMessage, setTestMessage] = useState('');\n  const { previewing: testingTTS, startPreview, stopPreview } = useTTSPreview();\n\n  // Keep the sample text in sync with locale changes.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    setTestText(t('settings.ttsTestTextDefault'));\n  }, [t]);\n\n  // Stop a preview when the panel goes away.\n  useEffect(() => stopPreview, [stopPreview]);\n\n  const save = (apiKey: string) => saveServiceProvider(view, apply, entry, { apiKey }, t);\n  // Azure Speech takes its official endpoint for the region the key belongs to.\n  const regionalEndpoint = regionalEndpointTemplate('tts', providerId);\n\n  const handleTestTTS = async () => {\n    if (!testText.trim()) return;\n    setTestStatus('testing');\n    setTestMessage('');\n    try {\n      const providerOptions = isVoxCPM\n        ? await getVoxCPMProviderOptions(effectiveVoice, {\n            role: 'teacher',\n            locale,\n            backend: slotVoxCPMBackend(capabilities.tts),\n          })\n        : undefined;\n      await startPreview({\n        text: testText,\n        providerId,\n        voice: effectiveVoice,\n        speed: ttsSpeed,\n        providerOptions,\n        // The service as the server saved it, not necessarily the one in use.\n        ...(isBrowser\n          ? {}\n          : { previewProvider: entry.id, ...(use.modelId ? { previewModel: use.modelId } : {}) }),\n      });\n      setTestStatus('success');\n      setTestMessage(t('settings.ttsTestSuccess'));\n    } catch (error) {\n      log.error('TTS test failed:', error);\n      setTestStatus('error');\n      setTestMessage(\n        error instanceof Error && error.message\n          ? `${t('settings.ttsTestFailed')}: ${error.message}`\n          : t('settings.ttsTestFailed'),\n      );\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <div className={cn('space-y-6', isVoxCPM ? 'max-w-5xl' : 'max-w-3xl')}>\n      {/* Browser-native TTS can't produce managed audio files, so the Pro-mode\n          timeline's per-line audio (preview / regenerate / bulk voiceover) is\n          unavailable on it — surface that when this provider is selected. */}\n      {isBrowser && (\n        <div className=\"rounded-lg border border-amber-200 bg-amber-50 p-3 text-sm text-amber-700 dark:border-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-950/30 dark:text-amber-300\">\n          {t('settings.ttsBrowserNativeTimelineNotice')}\n        </div>\n      )}\n\n      {entry.state === 'deployment' && <ServerConfiguredNotice view={view} capability=\"tts\" />}\n      {entry.state === 'server-only' && <ServerOnlyNotice noUserKeys={!view.allowUserKeys} />}\n\n      {/* API Key & Base URL — the server's services are the operator's. */}\n      {editable && (\n        <>\n          <div className={cn('grid gap-4', isDoubao ? (\n              <DoubaoKeyFields onSave={save} />\n            ) : (\n              <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n                <Label className=\"text-sm\">{t('settings.ttsApiKey')}</Label>\n                <ApiKeyField\n                  name={`tts-api-key-${entry.id}`}\n                  provider={entry.provider}\n                  inputClassName=\"font-mono text-sm\"\n                  onSave={save}\n                  onRemove={() => save('')}\n                />\n              </div>\n            )}\n            <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n              <Label className=\"text-sm\">{t('settings.ttsBaseUrl')}</Label>\n              {regionalEndpoint ? (\n                <RegionalEndpointField\n                  name={`tts-endpoint-${entry.id}`}\n                  provider={entry.provider}\n                  template={regionalEndpoint}\n                  onSave={(baseUrl) => saveServiceProvider(view, apply, entry, { baseUrl }, t)}\n                />\n              ) : (\n                <>\n                  {ttsProvider?.defaultBaseUrl && (\n                    <p className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground break-all\">\n                      {t('settings.requestUrl')}: {ttsProvider.defaultBaseUrl}\n                      {ttsEndpointPath(providerId)}\n                    </p>\n                  )}\n                  <EndpointServerOnlyHint />\n                </>\n              )}\n            </div>\n          </div>\n          {isDoubao && entry.provider?.key?.set && (\n            <p className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground\">\n              {t('settings.serverConfig.keyStored', { mask: entry.provider.key.mask ?? '' })}\n            </p>\n          )}\n        </>\n      )}\n\n      {entry.state !== 'server-only' && (\n        <>\n          <TTSSpeedField\n            provider={ttsProvider}\n            speed={ttsSpeed}\n            cloneVoiceLocked={cloneSpeedDisabled}\n            onSpeedChange={setTTSSpeed}\n          />\n\n          {keyless && !use.inUse && (\n            <div className=\"flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2 rounded-lg border border-border/60 bg-muted/30 px-3 py-2 text-sm\">\n              <span className=\"min-w-0 text-muted-foreground\">\n                {t('settings.serverConfig.notNarration')}\n              </span>\n              <Button\n                variant=\"outline\"\n                size=\"sm\"\n                disabled={assigning || !use.slot || use.slot.locked}\n                onClick={() => void makeNarration()}\n              >\n                {t('settings.serverConfig.useForNarration')}\n              </Button>\n            </div>\n          )}\n\n          {/* Test TTS */}\n          <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n            <Label className=\"text-sm\">{t('settings.testTTS')}</Label>\n            <div className=\"flex gap-2\">\n              <Input\n                placeholder={t('settings.ttsTestTextPlaceholder')}\n                value={testText}\n                onChange={(e) => setTestText(e.target.value)}\n                className=\"flex-1\"\n              />\n              <Button\n                onClick={() => void handleTestTTS()}\n                disabled={testingTTS || !testText.trim() || !configured}\n                size=\"default\"\n                className=\"gap-2 w-32\"\n              >\n                {testingTTS ? (\n                  <Loader2 className=\"h-4 w-4 animate-spin\" />\n                ) : (\n                  <Volume2 className=\"h-4 w-4\" />\n                )}\n                {t('settings.testTTS')}\n              </Button>\n            </div>\n          </div>\n        </>\n      )}\n\n      {testMessage && (\n        <div\n          className={cn(\n            'rounded-lg p-3 text-sm overflow-hidden',\n            testStatus === 'success' &&\n              'bg-green-50 text-green-700 border border-green-200 dark:bg-green-950/50 dark:text-green-400 dark:border-green-800',\n            testStatus === 'error' &&\n              'bg-red-50 text-red-700 border border-red-200 dark:bg-red-950/50 dark:text-red-400 dark:border-red-800',\n          )}\n        >\n          <div className=\"flex items-start gap-2 min-w-0\">\n            {testStatus === 'success' && <CheckCircle2 className=\"h-4 w-4 mt-0.5 shrink-0\" />}\n            {testStatus ===         key={model.id}\n                className=\"inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2.5 py-1 rounded-md bg-muted/50 border border-border/40 text-xs font-mono text-muted-foreground\"\n              >\n                <span className=\"size-1.5 rounded-full bg-emerald-500/70\" />\n                {model.name}\n              </div>\n            ))}\n          </div>\n          <p               "newString": "/**\n * A Fish Audio voice reference: accept either the raw voice-model ID or the\n * voice page URL (`https://fish.audio/m/<id>…`) and take the ID from it.\n * Returns `undefined` when nothing usable was typed.\n */\nexport function fishVoiceIdFromInput(input: string): string | undefined {\n  const trimmed = input.trim();\n  if (!trimmed) return undefined;\n  const match = trimmed.match(\n    /(?:fish\\.audio\\/(?:m|voice)\\/)?([0-9a-fA-F]{16,64})(?:[/?#]|$)/,\n  );\n  const id = match?.[1] ?? trimmed;\n  const cleaned = id.trim();\n  return /^[0-9a-fA-F]{16,64}$/.test(cleaned) ? cleaned.toLowerCase() : trimmed || undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fish Audio voices are community/custom voice models identified by an opaque\n * model ID, so the pickers add a free-text row for pasting that ID (or the\n * voice page URL). `onPick` receives the resolved voice ID.\n */\nfunction FishVoiceIdRow({\n  onPick,\n  active,\n}: {\n  onPick: (voiceId: string) => void;\n  active: boolean;\n}) {\n  const { t } = useI18n();\n  const [customVoiceInput, setCustomVoiceInput] = useState('');\n  const commit = () => {\n    const voiceId = fishVoiceIdFromInput(customVoiceInput);\n    if (!voiceId) return;\n    setCustomVoiceInput('');\n    onPick(voiceId);\n  };\n  return (\n    <div className=\"px-2 py-1.5 space-y-1\">\n      <div className=\"flex items-center gap-1.5\">\n        <input\n          value={customVoiceInput}\n          onChange={(e) => setCustomVoiceInput(e.target.value)}\n          onBlur={() => {\n            if (customVoiceInput.trim()) commit();\n          }}\n          onKeyDown={(e) => {\n            e.stopPropagation();\n            if (e.key === 'Enter') {\n              e.preventDefault();\n              commit();\n            }\n          }}\n          aria-label={t('agentBar.fishVoiceIdPlaceholder')}\n          placeholder={t('agentBar.fishVoiceIdPlaceholder')}\n          className={cn(\n            'h-7 min-w-0 flex-1 rounded-sm border border-input bg-background px-2 text-[12px]',\n            'outline-none transition-colors placeholder:text-muted-foreground/50',\n            active ? 'border-primary/50 text-primary' : 'focus:border-primary/50',\n          )}\n        />\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={commit}\n          disabled={!customVoiceInput.trim()}\n          className={cn(\n            'shrink-0 rounded-sm border border-border/60 px-2 py-1 text-[11px] font-medium',\n            'text-muted-foreground hover:border-border hover:text-foreground disabled:opacity-40',\n          )}\n        >\n          {t('agentBar.fishVoiceIdApply')}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      <p className=\"px-0.5 text-[10px] leading-tight text-muted-foreground/60\">\n        {t('agentBar.fishVoiceIdHint')}\n      </p>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction AgentBar() {",

              "patch": "Index: CHANGELOG.md\n===================================================================\n--- CHANGELOG.md\t\n+++ CHANGELOG.md\t\n@@ -1,815 +1,818 @@\n # Changelog\n \n All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.\n \n The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).\n \n ## [Unreleased]\n \n ### Added\n \n+- Motion-graphic course intros. Generated courses open with an `animation-explainer` scene: a deterministic GSAP timeline (HOOK → TEASE → SPARK → TITLE, ~30s) grounded in the course topic, king-of-the-trailer kinetic typography distilled into a new `animation-explainer-content` prompt template. The teacher can nudge it phase-by-phase through narration (`{\"phase\": …}`) and replay it; it publishes its phase via the standard observation contract and does not consume the interactive-scene budget.\n+- Per-course design directives. The outline stage now also infers a `designDirective` (visual concept, 2–5 hex palette, background mode `dark|paper|light`, motion personality `playful|energetic|calm|cinematic`) from the requirement and materials, emits it live through the run stream, stores it on the confirmed outline and the Stage document, and threads it through every slide, quiz and widget prompt — the single root-cause fix for \"every course generates the same PowerPoint blue\". Slide generation additionally learns a design system (60/30/10 palette discipline, background-mode derivation, SVG icon chips, infographic patterns, anti-slop bans), and every interactive widget prompt gains a shared visual-polish contract.\n+- Fish Audio narration. A new built-in TTS provider calls `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts` (backend models `s2.1-pro`/`s2.1-pro-free`/`s2-pro`/`drama-3`/`s1`, mp3/wav/opus output, `prosody.speed` 0.5–2.0). Voices are user-owned Fish voice models: the narrator and agent voice popovers accept a pasted voice ID or `fish.audio/m/<id>` URL in a free-text field, and the provider is configurable through `TTS_FISH_*` env vars. Disabled until a Fish API key is configured.\n - PDF page selection in the classic composer. A PDF is uploaded with `POST /api/materials?extract=false`, `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages` reports `{ pageCount }`, and `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages?page=N` returns that page as a PNG thumbnail. `POST /api/materials/<id>/extraction` with `{ \"pages\": [1, 3, 8] }` or `{ \"pages\": \"all\" }` validates the selection against the document, stores it on the extraction, slices the PDF to those pages, and then runs the extractor. Extraction reads report `selectedPages` and `sourcePageCount`; existing materials need no migration.\n - Course-design skills in the classic composer. `GET /api/generation/skills` lists the built-in skills that shape a classroom (the twelve outline skills), and a generation run accepts up to five `skillIds`, resolved for the owner and passed to the outline step. Unknown or non-outline skill ids are refused before the run starts.\n \n ### Changed\n \n - The twelve outline skills speak Arabic. Their SKILL.md frontmatter titles and descriptions — what the skill picker shows — are Arabic now; the English `/handle` stays the machine contract. Arabic display names for the workbench were already in the ar-SA overlay.\n - Mobile classrooms play like a video player: the live scene is the main element, the roundtable shrinks to a 56px controls bar in both orientations, and the plan / chat panels open as fixed overlay drawers from the dock toggles. Drawer surfaces are solid (`--aurora-drawer-solid`) so a white slide can't wash the text out. The dock's controls keep a compact row (scenes · prev play next · tray · chat) with volume, speed, autoplay, whiteboard, quote and fullscreen in an expandable tray sheet; 40px+ touch targets throughout. The old mobile reel cards (`MobileSceneReels`) are removed.\n - Phone fullscreen is layout-only video playback now.
