Implied by\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_PRO_WORKBENCH_ENABLED; set it alone to enable the classroom\n# editor on a deployment without the workbench.\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIC_EDITOR_ENABLED=true\n\n# Select @openmaic/editor inside Pro mode. Set this build-time flag to\n# false or 0 and rebuild to roll back to the legacy classroom chat runtime.\n# Pi requires model/provider tool (function) calling support.\n# Docker Compose's env_file loads .env.local at runtime, not into build args.\n# To rebuild with legacy chat: NEXT_PUBLIC_PI_CHAT_ENABLED=false docker compose up -d --build openmaic\n# Runtime-only changes leave the built client/server choice unchanged.\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_PI_CHAT_ENABLED=false\n\n# Enable the unified PPT/Interactive courseware-reference entry in Pi playback.\n# Pi chat and editor element references remain independent from this default-off build-time gate.\n# Changing a NEXT_PUBLIC_* value requires rebuilding the application.\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_COURSEWARE_REFERENCE_ENABLED=true\n\n# Enable the server-side vocational task-engine generation path.\n# OPENMAIC_ENABLE_VOCATIONAL=true\n\n# Show the experimental vocational task-engine control in the client.\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_VOCATIONAL_TEST_UI=true\n\n# Show the video export and PPTX import entry points.\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_VIDEO_EXPORT=true\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_PPTX_IMPORT=true\n\n# Informational destination shown on exported Quiz/PBL cover cards. Unset or\n# blank defaults to open.maic.chat; set to \"off\" to omit it.\n# NEXT_PUBLIC_VIDEO_EXPORT_CTA_DESTINATION=open.maic.chat\n\n# --- Agent Runtime (experimental) ---------------------------------------------\n\n# Server-only gate for durable background agent sessions: the /api/agent\n# session and owner-event control-plane routes plus the in-process session\n# runner. Default OFF — while disabled, every /api/agent/sessions* and\n# /api/agent/owner-events route answers 404. Truthy values are \"true\" or \"1\";\n# anything else (including unset) is treated as disabled.\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_ENABLED=true\n\n# The runtime uses the PostgreSQL connection (DATABASE_URL) from the\n# \"Persistence\" section below, which every deployment configures.\n\n# The agent runs on the `agent` slot of the model configuration (openmaic.yml,\n# or the model settings): a model that supports tool calling. Optional fields\n# on the slot: api (\"openai-completions\", the default, or \"openai-responses\"),\n# contextWindow (pins the window compaction assumes below the catalogue value),\n# and thinking, which must never set effort (the tool-using driver cannot\n# combine reasoning_effort with function tools on this transport). A\n# deployment configured only through DEFAULT_MODEL has the agent turned off.\n\n# Runner tuning. Defaults are shown; only relevant once the runtime is enabled.\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS=1000\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_HEARTBEAT_MS=2000\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_LEASE_TTL_MS=10000\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_MAX_CONCURRENT=2\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5\n\n# Global per-tool-call execution bound for every agent run (ms). A tool call\n# that neither resolves nor rejects within the budget is aborted and settles as\n# an error tool-result the agent can retry or proceed from; the session does\n# not die. Default 600000 (10 minutes). Tools with known longer budgets (media\n# synthesis, material extraction) carry their own explicit bounds in code.\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS=600000\n\n# Conversation compaction is reserved and OFF by default. The reusable\n# compaction runtime is not implemented yet — it lands in a later slice of\n# work — and until then the runner runs without context transformation, so\n# these knobs are inert placeholders.\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_COMPACTION_ENABLED=true\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_COMPACTION_RESERVE_TOKENS=0\n# OPENMAIC_AGENT_COMPACTION_KEEP_RECENT_TOKENS=0\n\n# Session prompts and follow-up messages are capped server-side at a fixed\n# 100,000 characters; this limit is a constant and is not configurable.\n\n# --- Generation runs ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Course generation runs on the server: a run is a PostgreSQL record that a\n# worker in every server process executes, step by step, and another process\n# takes over from its last checkpoint if one dies. The worker always runs (it\n# does not depend on OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_ENABLED) and needs a process that\n# outlives requests, so serverless hosts are not supported. It shares the lease\n# timing of the agent runtime (OPENMAIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS,\n# _HEARTBEAT_MS, _LEASE_TTL_MS and _MAX_ATTEMPTS above). Defaults are shown;\n# values must be positive integers.\n#\n# Runs one owner may have in progress at once (a run waiting for its outline to\n# be confirmed, or paused at a failed step, does not count). Over the limit,\n# starting, confirming or retrying a run answers 429 ACTIVE_RUN_LIMIT.\n# OPENMAIC_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS_PER_OWNER=2\n# Runs one owner may have waiting for outline confirmation at once.\n# OPENMAIC_MAX_WAITING_RUNS_PER_OWNER=10\n# Runs one server process executes at once.\n# OPENMAIC_GENERATION_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT=4\n# Uploaded materials one server process extracts at once in the background\n# (each is parsed or transcribed right after its upload, before generation).\n# OPENMAIC_MATERIAL_EXTRACTION_CONCURRENCY=2\n# One owner's extractions running at once across every server process, so one\n# owner's uploads cannot hold every worker while others wait.\n# OPENMAIC_MATERIAL_EXTRACTION_PER_OWNER=2\n# The largest stored extraction result (text and images) of one material, in\n# MB; a larger one fails with EXTRACTION_RESULT_TOO_LARGE. Results count\n# against the owner's material byte quota.\n# OPENMAIC_MATERIAL_EXTRACTION_MAX_RESULT_MB=100\n# Hours an uploaded material that no generation run or agent session uses is\n# kept after it was last read (an open composer reads its materials back) before\n# it is deleted.\n# OPENMAIC_UNUSED_MATERIAL_TTL_HOURS=24\n# Run event streams (one run's events, or the owner's run changes) one owner may\n# hold open on one process.\n# OPENMAIC_GENERATION_RUN_STREAMS_PER_OWNER=16\n# Hours a finished run keeps its full event log before it is compacted to its\n# final snapshot.\n# OPENMAIC_GENERATION_RUN_RETENTION_HOURS=24\n\n# --- Proxy (optional) --------------------------------------------------------\n\n# HTTP_PROXY=\n# HTTPS_PROXY=\n# Comma-separated hosts that bypass the proxy. Without openmaic.yml it\n# becomes the default of every chat slot (the `llm` root), below the models a\n# workspace picks in the settings; the agent stays off. There is no hardcoded\n# vendor fallback: a call with no model configured fails.\n# Example: openai:gpt-5.5, minimax:MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed,\n# bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5\nDEFAULT_MODEL=\n\n# Per-stage models are slots in openmaic.yml (course.outline,\n# course.content.slide, classroom, agent, ...). Per owner, not per deployment: with anonymous-cookie owners a cleared\n# cookie is a new owner with a fresh quota.\n# ASSET_QUOTA_BYTES=\n\n# The anonymous owner cookie and the ACCESS_CODE cookie carry the `Secure` flag\n# in production builds. Setting\n# this without an access code fails startup. Everyone holding the access code\n# then sees, edits and can publish the same courses, with no per-person\n# attribution — which is what SECURITY.md already says ACCESS_CODE is, and not\n# user authentication. 1-128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-]; the reserved `anon:`\n# prefix is rejected, and a malformed value fails startup rather than being\n# ignored.\n# PERSISTENCE_SHARED_OWNER_ID=\n\n# Personal installations: resolve every request to one fixed owner for a\n# single person, who may publish. Unset or \"direct\" keeps direct egress (the safe default). Requires\n# the object store's CORS to admit this app's origin and expose Content-Type, and\n# the signing identity to hold s3:ListBucket on the bucket so a missing key\n# answers 404 NoSuchKey rather than 403.\n# ASSET_BYTE_EGRESS=redirect\n\n# Claiming anonymous work on sign-in (see README \"Claiming anonymous work\").\n# explicit (default): the app calls POST /api/identity/claim; auto: the first\n# request that carries both an account and an anonymous owner claims it.\n# OWNER_CLAIM_TRIGGER=explicit\n\n# The page response of a browser's first load mints the anonymous owner cookie\n# (default on), so the page's first API requests do not each mint an owner.\n# Set it to false only when registered owner auth methods set\n# anonymousFallback: false (startup warns when they do and this is on); hosts\n# that keep anonymous visitors need it, and skip it per request in\n# middleware.ts for requests their methods authenticate.\n# \"true\", \"1\", \"false\" or \"0\"; anything else fails startup.\n# OWNER_ANONYMOUS_PREMINT=true\n\n# How long an owner-scoped write (default 30000) and a claim (default 5000) wait\n# for the owner's identity lock before answering 503 OWNER_BUSY with\n# Retry-After.             "output": "lesson-visual-upgrade.md\n# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.\n\nThe format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- PDF page selection in the classic composer. A PDF is uploaded with `POST /api/materials?extract=false`, `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages` reports `{ pageCount }`, and `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages?page=N` returns that page as a PNG thumbnail. `POST /api/materials/<id>/extraction` with `{ \"pages\": [1, 3, 8] }` or `{ \"pages\": \"all\" }` validates the selection against the document, stores it on the extraction, slices the PDF to those pages, and then runs the extractor. Extraction reads report `selectedPages` and `sourcePageCount`; existing materials need no migration.\n- Course-design skills in the classic composer. `GET /api/generation/skills` lists the built-in skills that shape a classroom (the twelve outline skills), and a generation run accepts up to five `skillIds`, resolved for the owner and passed to the outline step. Unknown or non-outline skill ids are refused before the run starts.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The twelve outline skills speak Arabic. Their SKILL.md frontmatter titles and descriptions — what the skill picker shows — are Arabic now; the English `/handle` stays the machine contract. Arabic display names for the workbench were already in the ar-SA overlay.\n- Mobile classrooms play like a video player: the live scene is the main element, the roundtable shrinks to a 56px controls bar in both orientations, and the plan / chat panels open as fixed overlay drawers from the dock toggles. Drawer surfaces are solid (`--aurora-drawer-solid`) so a white slide can't wash the text out. The dock's controls keep a compact row (scenes · prev play next · tray · chat) with volume, speed, autoplay, whiteboard, quote and fullscreen in an expandable tray sheet; 40px+ touch targets throughout. The old mobile reel cards (`MobileSceneReels`) are removed.\n- Phone fullscreen is layout-only video playback now. The browser Fullscreen API squeezed the lesson card inside the classroom chrome on phones, so `togglePresentation` flips `isPresenting` without it on phones: header and dock hide, the canvas fills the page letterboxed on black, and the fullscreen bar carries previous · play/pause · next · autoplay · exit plus the tray — users never leave the fullscreen view to control it. The tray drops the items that moved onto the bar.\n- Fullscreen controls always worked again on every screen: `.aurora-roundtable > div` docked-skin styling (backdrop-filter + overflow hidden) turned the presenting phase's zero-height wrapper into a containing block that clipped the entire fixed controls pill out of existence — the bar rendered in the DOM but painted nowhere. The wrapper now carries a semantic class and an explicit override.\n- Home popovers fit the phone now: the agent-bar panel spans its composer row with a 384px cap (was a fixed-width panel hanging off the screen edge) and the skills popover keeps a 12px collision margin with a hard cap.\n- The lesson prompt box no longer carries a model pill. The course model is configured in workspace settings; the toolbar keeps only the no-provider set-up CTA (#580) so a fresh homepage still dead-ends somewhere instead of nowhere.\n\n\n## [1.2.0-rc.2] - 2026-10-11\n\n### Security\n\n- Enforce model authorization for server-managed providers across chat, media, speech, model-based web search and workspace model assignments. Unauthorized and unknown model ids return the same HTTP 403 response before provider access. Users' own credentials continue to work. [#1879](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/pull/1879) (with @13ob0)\n- Render jobs are bound to the requesting owner. The render-service and app must be upgraded together; upgrade every service instance (or drain old instances) together with or before the app. Old/new version mixes fail closed through a dedicated owner-bound job namespace. [#1884](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/pull/1884) (by @Duang777)\n- Deleted courses no longer serve their legacy classroom media: `/api/classroom-media/<id>/...` checks the course lifecycle before touching the filesystem and answers a tombstoned course with the same 404 as a missing file. Successful responses are `private, max-age=300, must-revalidate` instead of `public, immutable`. [#1883](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/pull/1883) (by @Duang777)\n\n### Breaking change: server-managed model authorization\n\n- Set `*_MODELS` for every provider with server-managed credentials, or set `models` under each provider in `openmaic.yml` / `server-providers.yml`. Without a list, only deployment default/fallback and capability slot references authorize models; preset catalogues and workspace assignments do not. Provider-only media slots authorize a single adapter default. Services without model ids need no list. Providers configured without credentials (local Ollama, Lemonade) are not restricted; a keyless gateway that adds its own upstream credential should be given a key and a model list.\n- Migration: list the model ids users should be able to select (including voice compatibility models), restart the server, then update workspace selections that are no longer authorized. A startup warning names the configuration setting for each provider with credentials but no explicit list.\n\n### Bug Fixes\n\n- S3 asset storage: `@openmaic/storage` 0.37.3 supports path-style addressing for S3-compatible object stores such as MinIO and Ceph. Set `AWS_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true` (or `1`) together with `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` so objects are addressed as `endpoint/bucket/key`; leaving it unset keeps the existing behaviour for Amazon S3 (#1686).\n- Server persistence: `@openmaic/storage` 0.37.2 bounds `HttpDocumentStore` requests with a deadline (`requestTimeoutMs`, default 30s, `<= 0` disables) covering the request round trip — sending the body and receiving the response headers — so a persistence endpoint that stops answering fails like any other transport error instead of holding its caller forever. The stage autosave keeps at most one save in flight and starts the next only once that promise settles, so a request that never settled silently stranded every later save for the life of the page while the editor went on rendering the in-memory document; the reload showed what had actually reached the server. A request aborted at the deadline rejects with `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, which the autosave's existing backoff retries. The budget is the floor plus an allowance proportional to the request body (sized at a fixed 100 KiB/s) and is capped at 10 minutes, so a large document on a slow link is not mistaken for a stall; reading the response body stays outside the bound. This mirrors the budget `HttpAssetStore` already applies through `probeTimeoutMs` / `startBoundedOperation`.\n",

A PDF is uploaded with `POST /api/materials?extract=false`, `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages` reports `{ pageCount }`, and `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages?page=N` returns that page as a PNG thumbnail. `POST /api/materials/<id>/extraction` with `{ \"pages\": [1, 3, 8] }` or `{ \"pages\": \"all\" }` validates the selection against the document, stores it on the extraction, slices the PDF to those pages, and then runs the extractor. Extraction reads report `selectedPages` and `sourcePageCount`; existing materials need no migration.\n- Course-design skills in the classic composer. `GET /api/generation/skills` lists the built-in skills that shape a classroom (the twelve outline skills), and a generation run accepts up to five `skillIds`, resolved for the owner and passed to the outline step. Unknown or non-outline skill ids are refused before the run starts.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The twelve outline skills speak Arabic. Their SKILL.md frontmatter titles and descriptions — what the skill picker shows — are Arabic now; the English `/handle` stays the machine contract. Arabic display names for the workbench were already in the ar-SA overlay.\n- Mobile classrooms play like a video player: the live scene is the main element, the roundtable shrinks to a 56px controls bar in both orientations, and the plan / chat panels open as fixed overlay drawers from the dock toggles. Drawer surfaces are solid (`--aurora-drawer-solid`) so a white slide can't wash the text out. The dock's controls keep a compact row (scenes · prev play next · tray · chat) with volume, speed, autoplay, whiteboard, quote and fullscreen in an expandable tray sheet; 40px+ touch targets throughout. The old mobile reel cards (`MobileSceneReels`) are removed.\n- Phone fullscreen is layout-only video playback now. The browser Fullscreen API squeezed the lesson card inside the classroom chrome on phones, so `togglePresentation` flips `isPresenting` without it on phones: header and dock hide, the canvas fills the page letterboxed on black, and the fullscreen bar carries previous · play/pause · next · autoplay · exit plus the tray — users never leave the fullscreen view to control it. [#1884](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/pull/1884) (by @Duang777)\n- Deleted courses no longer serve their legacy classroom media: `/api/classroom-media/<id>/...` checks the course lifecycle before touching the filesystem and answers a tombstoned course with the same 404 as a missing file. Successful responses are `private, max-age=300, must-revalidate` instead of `public, immutable`. [#1883](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC/pull/1883) (by @Duang777)\n\n### Breaking change: server-managed model authorization\n\n- Set `*_MODELS` for every provider with server-managed credentials, or set `models` under each provider in `openmaic.yml` / `server-providers.yml`. Design directive (D2) — final vocabulary\n\n`packages/@openmaic/generation/src/design-directive.ts`:\n\n- `DesignDirective {concept, palette (2–5 hex, lower-cased, deduped), background: dark|paper|light,\n  motionPersonality: playful|energetic|calm|cinematic}`.\n- `normalizeDesignDirective` validates/normalizes model output; aliases accepted\n  (`black/night→dark`, `cream/warm→paper`, `white/bright→light`, `premium/storytelling→calm`,\n  `bouncy→playful`, `dramatic→cinematic`; case-insensitive). Returns `null` when the value is\n  absent or wholly unusable (default-only) so prompts fall back to self-selection instead of\n  asserting an empty directive.\n- `formatDesignDirective(null)` returns non-empty guidance text; with a directive it renders the\n  block `- Visual concept / - Palette (use ONLY these hexes) / - Background mode / - Motion\n  personality` every scene prompt receives.\n- `FALLBACK_DESIGN_DIRECTIVE` (dark/calm, no concept/palette) is used by placeholders when the\n  outline produced nothing.\n- Unit tests: `packages/@openmaic/generation/test/design-directive.test.ts`.\n\n## 2. Threading map (design directive)\n\n| Touch point | What flows |\n| --- | --- |\n| Outline stream, per chunk | `extractDesignDirective(buffer)` in `lib/server/generation/steps/outline.ts` (balanced-brace scan, 16 KB head) emits `OutlineEvent {type:'designDirective'}` → run event `outline_design_directive` (UI sees the directive while streaming) |\n| Outline result | `outline-generator.ts` parses + normalizes; `OutlineResult.designDirective?` |\n| Confirm | `engine.ts` stores `GenerationRunOutline.designDirective`; `availableAgents`/Stage build carry it onto `Stage` (`packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/stage.ts`) |\n| Scene content | `SceneContentInput.designDirective` (`scene-content.ts`) → `generateSceneContent(designDirectiveText)` → **all** widget cases + `generateSlideContent` receive `designDirective` in template variables |\n| Classroom regeneration | `generation-tools.ts` reads `doc.stage.designDirective ?? ''` |\n\nStream retry resets the directive state between attempts so a half-extracted directive from a\nfailed chunk never leaks.\n\n## 3. Animation explainer (D1)\n\n- Prompt: `templates/animation-explainer-content/{system,user}.md` (distilled\n  hyperframes/OpenDesign/LottieFiles doctrine; deterministic GSAP timeline; p0 HOOK → p1 TEASE →\n  p2 SPARK → p3 TITLE + ambient loop; `data-maic-observation` `{summary, state:{phase, phaseIndex},\n  beats}`; `#phase-dots`, `#replay-btn`; `no-anim` static fallback).\n- Outline prompts (`requirements-to-outlines`, app `interactive-outlines`): scene 1 is the intro\n  explainer (does not consume the interactive budget); `widgetOutline {concept, keyBeats, mood}`;\n  widget table + JSON shape + rule numbering updated.\n- Task-engine outlines: `designDirective` only (briefing slide stays first — no intro scene).\n- Narration (`interactive-actions/system.md`): teacher talks one beat per phase\n  (`{\"phase\": \"p1\"}` alignment only, `{\"replay\": true}` reserved; never\n  highlight/annotate/reveal this widget type).\n- Editor: `outlines-editor.tsx` WIDGET_KINDS gains `animation-explainer`; i18n label\n  `generation.widgetAnimationExplainer` in all 12 locales.\n- `scene-generator.ts`: defaults for missing `keyBeats`/`mood` are derived from the title and the\n  directive's motion personality (`Motion personality: (\\w+)` match).\n\n## 4. Visual design prompts (D3)\n\n- `slide-content/system.md` + `## Design System (the Design Directive is LAW)` section:\n  60/30/10 palette discipline, background-mode derivation, ShapeElement SVG-path icon chips\n  (viewBox [24,24], 2-unit stroke), one pattern per slide among hero-stat / donut /\n  comparison-cards / process-flow / poster, anti-slop bans.\n- `slide-content/user.md` + every widget `user.md`: `## Design Directive … {{designDirective}}`.\n- Every interactive widget `system.md` gains `{{snippet:widget-visual-polish}}`\n  (surface/depth/elevation, states, focus discipline, SVG icon chips at 2-unit stroke, mobile gap\n  ≥8, 48px touch targets, theme-variable contract).\n\n## 5.               "preview": "# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.\n\nThe format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- PDF page selection in the classic composer. A PDF is uploaded with `POST /api/materials?extract=false`, `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages` reports `{ pageCount }`, and `GET /api/materials/<id>/pages?page=N` returns that page as a PNG thumbnail. `POST /api/materials/<id>/extraction` with `{ \"pages\": [1, 3, 8] }` or `{ \"pages\": \"all\" }` validates the selection against the document, stores it on the extraction, slices the PDF to those pages, and then runs the extractor. Extraction reads report `selectedPages` and `sourcePageCount`; existing materials need no migration.\n- Course-design skills in the classic composer. `GET /api/generation/skills` lists the built-in skills that shape a classroom (the twelve outline skills), and a generation run accepts up to five `skillIds`, resolved for the owner and passed to the outline step. Unknown or non-outline skill ids are refused before the run starts.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The twelve outline skills speak Arabic. Their SKILL.md frontmatter titles and descriptions — what the skill picker shows — are Arabic now; the English `/handle` stays the machine contract. Arabic display names for the workbench were already in the ar-SA overlay.\n- Mobile classrooms play like a video player: the live scene is the main element, the roundtable shrinks to a 56px controls bar in both orientations, and the plan / chat panels open as fixed overlay drawers from the dock toggles. Drawer surfaces are solid (`--aurora-drawer-solid`) so a white slide can't wash the text out. The dock's controls keep a compact row (scenes · prev play next · tray · chat) with volume, speed, autoplay, whiteboard, quote and fullscreen in an expandable tray sheet; 40px+ touch targets throughout. The old mobile reel cards (`MobileSceneReels`) are removed.\n- Phone fullscreen is layout-only video playback now. The browser Fullscreen API squeezed the lesson card inside the classroom chrome on phones, so `togglePresentation` flips `isPresenting` without it on phones: header and dock hide, the canvas fills the page letterboxed on black, and the fullscreen bar carries previous · play/pause · next · autoplay · exit plus the tray — users never leave the fullscreen view to control it. The tray drops the items that moved onto the bar.\n- Fullscreen controls always worked again on every screen: `.aurora-roundtable > div` docked-skin styling (backdrop-filter + overflow hidden) turned the presenting phase's zero-height wrapper into a containing block that clipped the entire fixed controls pill out of existence — the bar rendered in the DOM but painted nowhere. The wrapper now carries a semantic class and an explicit override.\n- Home popovers fit the phone now: the agent-bar panel spans its composer row with a 384px cap (was a fixed-width panel hanging off the screen edge) and the skills popover keeps a 12px collision margin with a hard cap.",

                "text": "# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.\n\nThe format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- PDF page selection in the classic composer. Extraction reads report `selectedPages` and `sourcePageCount`; existing materials need no migration.\n- Course-design skills in the classic composer. `GET /api/generation/skills` lists the built-in skills that shape a classroom (the twelve outline skills), and a generation run accepts up to five `skillIds`, resolved for the owner and passed to the outline step.               "newString": "### Added\n\n- Motion-graphic course intros. Generated courses open with an `animation-explainer` scene: a deterministic GSAP timeline (HOOK → TEASE → SPARK → TITLE, ~30s) grounded in the course topic, king-of-the-trailer kinetic typography distilled into a new `animation-explainer-content` prompt template. The teacher can nudge it phase-by-phase through narration (`{\"phase\": …}`) and replay it; it publishes its phase via the standard observation contract and does not consume the interactive-scene budget.\n- Per-course design directives. The outline stage now also infers a `designDirective` (visual concept, 2–5 hex palette, background mode `dark|paper|light`, motion personality `playful|energetic|calm|cinematic`) from the requirement and materials, emits it live through the run stream, stores it on the confirmed outline and the Stage document, and threads it through every slide, quiz and widget prompt — the single root-cause fix for \"every course generates the same PowerPoint blue\". Slide generation additionally learns a design system (60/30/10 palette discipline, background-mode derivation, SVG icon chips, infographic patterns, anti-slop bans), and every interactive widget prompt gains a shared visual-polish contract.\n- Fish Audio narration. A new built-in TTS provider calls `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts` (backend models `s2.1-pro`/`s2.1-pro-free`/`s2-pro`/`drama-3`/`s1`, mp3/wav/opus output, `prosody.speed` 0.5–2.0). Voices are user-owned Fish voice models: the narrator and agent voice popovers accept a pasted voice ID or `fish.audio/m/<id>` URL in a free-text field, and the provider is configurable through `TTS_FISH_*` envistry. Disabled until a Fish API key is configured.\n- PDF page selection in the classic composer.               "file": "packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md",
              "patch": "Index: packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md\n===================================================================\n--- packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md\t\n+++ packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/animation-explainer-content/system.md\t\n@@ -1,165 +1,198 @@\n # Motion-Graphic Explainer Generator (Course Intro \"Trailer\")\n \n Generate a self-contained HTML motion-graphic explainer — a cinematic, animated opening scene for an online course, in the style of premium product-launch motion graphics (kinetic typography, hero stats, icon choreography, SVG path draws).\n \n **This is the FIRST scene of the course: its job is to HOOK the learner in 20–45 seconds and make them want to continue.** Motion is the message; there is no narrator audio inside the widget — the teacher (outside the iframe) narrates over it.\n \n ## Story Shape (4 phases — follow exactly)\n \n Build ONE master timeline with 4 labeled phases. Each phase is one idea. Total on-screen duration 25–45 s:\n \n | Phase | Label | Duration | Job |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | 1. HOOK | `p0` | 6–10 s | Open with the question, paradox, or stakes of the topic. A *wait, what?* moment — never \"Welcome to course X\". One bold statement, a moving visual, an intriguing number. |\n | 2. TEASE | `p1` | 7–12 s | Sketch the territory the course covers: 3–4 keyword cards or icons snap/chase in, a comparison or a map of the problem space. Sets expectation, not detail. |\n | 3. SPARK | `p2` | 8–14 s | The signature visual moment: one idea animated beautifully — the concept as a moving infographic (orbit, build-up, transformation, count-up, path draw). Sine for ambient loops. **Linear only for rotation, ticks, progress** — never for spatial movement.\n - Durations: micro (0.15–0.3s) = energy; standard (0.3–0.5s) = professional; slow (0.5–0.8s) = gravity; very slow (0.8–1.6s) = cinematic.             "input": {
              "content": "const path = require('path');\nconst fs = require('fs');\nconst { chromium } = require('playwright');\n\nconst OUT_DIR = process.env.OUT_DIR || '.';\nconst HTML = path.join(OUT_DIR, 'intro-widget.html');\n\nconst STOPS = [\n  [2000, 't2s-hook'],\n  [8000, 't8s-hook2'],\n  [14000, 't14s-tease'],\n  [20000, 't20s-spark'],\n  [26000, 't26s'],\n  [34000, 't34s-title'],\n  [42000, 't42s-ambient'],\n];\n\n(async () => {\n  const browser = await chromium.launch();\n  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } });\n  await page.goto('file://' + HTML);\n  const start = Date.now();\n  for (const [ms, label] of STOPS) {\n    const wait = ms - (Date.now() - start);\n    if (wait > 0) await page.waitForTimeout(wait);\n    // publish the observation payload alongside each frame\n    const obs = await page.evaluate(() => {\n      const el = document.querySelector('[data-maic-observation]');\n      if (!el) return null;\n      return JSON.parse(el.getAttribute('data-maic-observation') || 'null');\n    });\n    await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(OUT_DIR, `frame-${label}.png`) });\n    console.log(label, 'phase=', obs && JSON.stringify(obs.state));\n  }\n  await browser.close();\n})();\n",

              "newString": "### 2. Phase control API (REQUIRED)\n\nSingle-script discipline: declare `tl`, `ambientTl`, `currentPhase` and the publish helper in ONE\ntop-level `<script>` (NOT inside a DOMContentLoaded closure or a second block) — the phase API\nruns in that same scope. `setExplainerPhase` must never throw on any of `'p0'..'p3'`, `undefined`\nor a number, and must always update `currentState` and re-publish even when a seek is a no-op.\n\nExpose a global so the platform and the phase dots can drive the story:\n\n```javascript\nwindow.setExplainerPhase = function (phase) {\n  // phase is 'p0'..'p3' (or number index)\n  ambientTl.pause();\n  tl.seek(phase, false);\n  tl.play();\n};\nwindow.explainerGetState = function () {\n  return { phase: currentPhase(), progress: tl.totalProgress() };\n};\n```\n\n- On `message` events, honor `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with `state.phase` → `window.setExplainerPhase(state.phase)`. Also accept `{ state: { replay: true } }` → restart (`tl.restart()`).\n- In-iframe controls (always visible, small, bottom-center): phase dots `#phase-dots` (button per phase, `id=\"phase-dot-p0\"` etc., current highlighted) + a replay button `id=\"replay-btn\"`. Clicking → `setExplainerPhase` / restart. 44px touch targets.\n\n### 3. Observation contract\n\n{{snippet:interactive-observation}}\n\nFor this widget publish:\n```json\n{ \"summary\": \"Phase 2 (Spark): the solar system race is animating\", \"state\": { \"phase\": \"p2\", \"phaseIndex\": 2 }, \"beats\": [ {\"id\":\"p0\",\"label\":\"Hook\"}, ... ] }\n```\nPublish on load, on every phase change (`tl.call(publishCurrentState, [], tl, 'p1')` at each label) and after any seek. Include the phase label list once in `state.beats`.\n\n### 4. widget-config (widget-config REQUIRED)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"animation-explainer\",\n  \"concept\": \"<topic concept>\",\n",

              "newString": "Single-script discipline: ALL widget JavaScript lives in exactly ONE top-level `<script>` —\ntimelines (`tl`, `ambientTl`), phase state (e.g. `phaseIndex`), the publish helper, the phase API\nand the message router. No second block, no DOMContentLoaded closure, no cross-block references\n(a variable used by one block must be declared in that same block — cross-block and closure\nreferences throw `X is not defined` and brick the phase loop). `setExplainerPhase` must never\nthrow for `'p0'..'p3'`, a number or `undefined`, and must always update state + re-publish even\nwhen a seek is a no-op.\n\nSkeleton — keep this structure in one script:\n\n```javascript\n<script>\n  const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: false });            // labels p0..p3\n  const ambientTl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true, repeat: -1 });\n  let phaseIndex = 0;                                       // one source of truth\n\n  function publishCurrentState() {\n    publish({ summary: `Phase ${phaseIndex + 1}`, state: { phase: 'p' + phaseIndex, phaseIndex } });\n  }\n\n  window.setExplainerPhase = function (phase) {           // never throws\n    const p = typeof phase === 'number' ? 'p' + phase\n            : ['p0', 'p1', 'p2', 'p3'].includes(String(phase)) ? String(phase) : null;\n    if (!p) { tl.restart(); return publishCurrentState(); }\n    ambientTl.pause();\n    tl.seek(p, false); tl.play();\n    phaseIndex = Number(p.slice(1));\n    document.querySelectorAll('.phase-dot').forEach(function (d, i) {\n      d.classList.toggle('active', i === phaseIndex);\n    });\n    publishCurrentState();\n  };\n\n  window.explainerGetState = function () {\n    return { phase: 'p' + phaseIndex, progress: tl.totalProgress() };\n  };\n\n  window.addEventListener('message', function (event) {    // same block\n    var st = event.data && event.data.type === 'SET_WIDGET_STATE' ? event.data.state : null;\n    if (!st) return;\n    if (st.replay) tl.restart();\n    else if (st.phase !== undefined) window.setExplainerPhase(st.phase);\n  });\n</script>\n```\n\n- On `message` events, honor `SET_WIDGET_STATE` with `state.phase` → `window.setExplainerPhase(state.phase)`. listFiles(directory: string): string[] {\n   return readdirSync(directory)\n+    .filter((name) => !name.startsWith('.'))\n     .flatMap((name) => {\n       const entry = join(directory, name);\n       return statSync(entry).isDirectory() ? listFiles(entry) : [entry];\n     })\n     .sort();\n }\n \n describe('packaged prompt assets', () => {\n   const expectedTemplateFiles = PROMPT_IDS.flatMap((promptId) => [\n     `templates/${promptId}/system.md`,\n     `templates/${promptId}/user.md`,\n   ]).sort();\n   const expectedSnippetFiles = SNIPPET_IDS.map((snippetId) => snippets', () => {\n     const actualFiles = [\n       ...listFiles(join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'templates')),\n       ...listFiles(join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'snippets')),\n     ]\n       .map((file) => /await pyodide\\.loadPackage\\(\\s*(?:['\"]micropip['\"]|\\[[^\\]]*['\"]micropip['\"][^\\]]*\\])\\s*\\)/,\n     );\n     const firstImportIndex = source.indexOf('import micropip');\n     const expect(loadIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);\n     expect(firstImportIndex).toBeGreaterThan(loadIndex);\n     expect(source).toMatch(orderedExample);\n   });\n \n   test.each(PBL_PROMPT_FILES)('ships prompts-pbl/%s', (filename) => {\n     expect(\n       readFileSync(join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'prompts-pbl', filename), 'utf8').length,\n     ).toBeGreaterThan(100);\n   });\n \n   test('every referenced snippet is packaged and represented by SnippetId', () => {\n     const references = new Set<string>();\n     for (const templateFile of expectedTemplateFiles) {\n       const source = readFileSync(join(PACKAGE_ROOT, templateFile), 'utf8');\n       for (const match of source.matchAll(/\\{\\{snippet:(\\w[\\w-]*)\\}\\}/g)) {\n         references.add(match[1]);\n       }\n     }\n \n     expect([...references].sort()).toEqual([...SNIPPET_IDS].sort());\n     for (const snippetId of SNIPPET_IDS) {\n       expect(loadSnippet(snippetId, PACKAGE_ROOT).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n     }\n   });\n \n   // The loader only interpolates `\\w+` names. Pin the app's grandfathered\n   // slide dimensions exactly, while preventing any new non-camelCase names.\n   test('templates use the supported placeholder naming convention', () => {\n     const offenders: string[] = [];\n     for (const promptId of PROMPT_IDS) {\n       for (const filename of ['system.md', 'user.md']) {\n         const source = readFileSync(join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'templates', promptId, filename), 'utf8');\n         const matches = source.match(/\\{\\{(?!snippet:|#if |\\/if)([^}]+)\\}\\}/g) ?? [];\n         for (const placeholder of matches) {\n           const name = placeholder.slice(2, -2);\n           if (!/^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/.test(name)) {\n             offenders.push(`${promptId}/${filename}: ${placeholder}`);\n           }\n         }\n       }\n     }\n \n     expect(offenders.sort()).toEqual(GRANDFATHERED_NON_CAMEL_CASE_PLACEHOLDERS);\n   });\n });\n",
